No overlap with rounds 1–12 findings.

### 74. Golden-set construction spec + contamination controls as CI gates (ChatGPT, R13) — HIGH
LoCoMo (10 conversations, 1,986 QAs) and LongMemEval (500 questions) describe construction but report no inter-annotator κ, no QA rejection/correction rates, no paired control deltas — "a benchmark having answers" is not verified gold. Memory eval has a contamination path static QA lacks: eval questions/answers leaking into the store under test. Fix: golden-set construction spec — every item carries question + answer + evidence span + unanswerability flag; category tags mirroring LongMemEval's abilities (extraction, multi-session, temporal, knowledge-update, abstention); dual independent annotation on a stratified sample with κ reported; rejected-item counts and generation error rates logged as harness metadata; contamination controls as CI gates — question-blind ingestion mandatory, one-way data flow (evaluator-only query/gold mounts), query-exclusion hash scans over ingested docs/summaries/caches, canary sentinel facts in held-out histories, leakage-sensitivity audit (blind-vs-exposed runs; large delta = protocol failure); ranking-stability reporting — bootstrap CIs, sub-2-point deltas treated as noise, golden set versioned like data (Idea 68). Caveat: LoCoMo/LongMemEval counts partner-recalled 2024 snapshots — verify before quoting; all gold reliability figures measured on our own harness.

### 75. Epistemic-status marking spec for memory records (ChatGPT, R13) — HIGH
No shipped product marks the epistemic status of a claim — Google AI Overviews, Copilot, Perplexity, ChatGPT Search, Gemini Double-check, Glean all expose *sources*, not whether a sentence is verbatim retrieval, paraphrase, synthesis, or inference; retrieval scores describe query-passage match, not answer correctness. ALCE/RAGTruth measure citation-support behavior, but no public controlled study shows marking UIs reduce user error or appropriately calibrate trust. Fix: `epistemic_status` field on the record envelope — observed / extracted-verbatim / inferred / derived-summary / corrected (binds to Idea 47's assertion envelope; Idea 69's inferred-never-observed rule); retrieval/similarity scores never surface as answer confidence; claim-level confidence displayed only when calibrated against a measured error rate; memory-derived claims surfaced to users cite originating records via Idea 46's lineage; "citation present" treated as weaker than "claim supported," unsupported-claim rate measured in the write-path harness. Caveat: the no-shipped-epistemic-labeling and no-measured-UI-effects absence claims are partner-recalled — cite as such; ALCE/RAGTruth verify before quoting.

### 76. Negative-trajectory store + adaptation-before-execution (Grok, R13) — HIGH
Failure memory is measured in adjacent fields: FAR (Failure-Aware Retry) lifts RoboMimic success (Square 100: 63.3% vs 48.0% base; average 70.9% vs 52.2%) by steering retries from failures; MATE shows previously *successful* trajectories mislead embodied agents when context changed — 81.3%/93.3% on ALFWorld with ~1/10 tokens via a deterministic post-retrieval adaptation stage; a memory-surrogate agent tracking "failed commands to avoid repeating" lifts Terminal-Bench 2.0 (45.9% vs 37.6%) and τ2-Bench (61.8% vs 55.0%); OpenAmer's public outcome ledger records all 1,701 runs (31.9% pass) with a `why` field per failure. Fix: negative-trajectory store with (state, attempted-action, observation, failure-mode, why) schema serving avoidance constraints; **adaptation-before-execution** — retrieved sequences (positive AND negative) validated against the current tool surface before binding (operationalizes Idea 71's stale-sequence defense; a non-validating sequence is quarantined, not executed — Idea 33 scenario); failure-aware retry re-queries the negative store with the failure signature. Caveat: FAR/MATE numbers are robotics-benchmark results, not agent-memory production telemetry; AgentCore "significant improvements" vendor-reported without numbers.

### 77. User-profile tier: episodic→semantic preference induction + preference half-life (Grok, R13) — MEDIUM-HIGH
PersonaAgent (ICLR 2025): episodic interaction buffer + semantic consolidated user profile; RealPref benchmark (100 profiles, 1,300 preferences): preference-following drops with context length and implicit expression; LLM-persona live experiment: +0.04% engaged topics / +0.03% users with lasting topics (p<0.05) — honest small lifts; BLMRec: per-event learned decay + stagnation-risk down-weighting of misleading stale signals. Fix: per-user profile as a third memory object — episodic interaction buffer + consolidated semantic profile (Idea 70's two-tier applied to the user); every induced preference carries provenance (Idea 46), confidence, and consent scope (Idea 73), correctable/deletable like any memory; preference half-life via Idea 72's decay machinery (stagnant signals down-weighted, not accumulated); personalization KPIs — repeated-user-correction rate, RealPref-style held-out preference-following accuracy. Caveat: PersonaAgent under review; recommender lifts are not agent-memory constants; BLMRec details via secondary report.

### 78. Known-answer canary suite + threshold-calibration runbook (Fo, R13) — HIGH
Calibrates Idea 67 (which specified the five live panels but left threshold-setting open). Established in adjacent ops: Teradata canary queries every 20–60 min; tiered LLM-pipeline canary gates (Baseline/Stress/Incident/Held-out); CloudWatch Synthetics expected-latency-from-history. The calibration rule: baseline each canary over N clean runs, set thresholds above measured normal variation, re-baseline after every index rebuild/re-embedding. What probes catch that dashboards miss: silent correctness failures (filtered queries returning short, recall drift under churn). Fix: known-answer canary suite per Idea 57's query-class matrix — (query, expected-doc-set, expected-rank-floor) triples run on schedule, incl. tenant-scoped silent-drop canaries; threshold-calibration runbook — deviation bands (e.g., >2σ or >3× baseline delta), versioned threshold config; incident→canary promotion — every retrieval-quality incident grows the suite (informational → blocking once expected behavior confirmed); canary reports are diagnostic (stage/stratum/expected/observed), never just "quality regression detected." Caveat: practitioner-grade/adjacent evidence — no shipped agent-memory canary suite to copy; all thresholds locally baselined (Idea 56's rule extended to alert thresholds).

### 79. Autonomy telemetry spec + degradation-signature alerts (Fo, R13) — MEDIUM-HIGH
First public deployment numbers: Anthropic's 10M+ interaction analysis — ~73% of tool calls include human verification, 0.8% irreversible; experienced users intervene in ~9% of turns vs 5% for new users (vigilance, not complacency). Salt Security survey: 12.5% can track all agent execution stages; 49.8% confirmed/suspected unauthorized actions; 17.5% can stop agents. Oversight Game: ask/oversee rates 99.4%/99.8% at risky states vs 3.9%/2.7% at safe — selective deference is the quantity to track. Fix: autonomy telemetry spec — per action: origin (agent-initiated vs human-instructed), verification state, reversibility class, overrides (rejected/modified/asked-first); reported ratios — verification coverage, override/intervention rate stratified by user experience, irreversible-action share, risk-stratified ask rate (extends Idea 73's agency-of-write instrumentation from memory entries to agent actions); degradation signatures as Idea 67-panel alerts — declining override rate, falling review duration with flat approvals, evidence-seeking decay (acquiescence masquerading as quality); approval gates on irreversible/high-consequence actions only, with a working mid-run stop (binds to Idea 66). Caveat: Anthropic figures via secondary report — re-verify against primary; Salt figures vendor-sampled (49.8% includes *suspected*); Oversight Game is lab results, not deployment telemetry.

## Ideas 80–85 — Partner watch pipeline (round 14, 6 analyses, 2026-10-16)

Fold-in done 2026-10-16 ~20:20 IST. Ranked by build relevance. Sources: `hidden_files/research/watch-log/082-*.md` through `087-*.md` + ROUND-14-SYNTHESIS.md. ChatGPT ×2 consulted directly via omniroute (codex, --stream --stdin); Grok-lens ×2 and Fo-lens ×2 research-derived — direct Grok consultation unavailable this run (OpenRouter x-ai route flapped 500/429 for ~6 min, second consecutive round), direct Fo consultation still needs a live browser session — both flagged, not blocking. No overlap with rounds 1–13 findings.

### 80. Optimistic concurrency + conflict telemetry on the write path (ChatGPT, R14) — HIGH
Three conflict classes when writers share one memory store: write-write, lost update (write computed from a stale read), derived-summary race (agent + consolidation job summarizing different snapshots). No published measurement of lost-update rates or concurrency incidents in AI-agent memory exists anywhere — our hazardous writer sets (runtime agents, consolidation job, human editors) make this our telemetry to build. Fix: per-record version stamps with optimistic concurrency on every write — a write presents the version it read, a mismatch fails loudly returning the current version (runtime-write version counter kept distinct from Idea 68's schema/migration dimensions); conflict telemetry as a first-class metric — every version-mismatch rejection, LWW resolution, and merge-race detection logged as structured events, with a concurrency chaos fixture (agent writes + consolidation job + simulated human edit on the same records) feeding Idea 23's regression loop; consolidation writes go through the same version-checked path as agent writes — summaries merge against current versions and carry source-snapshot version ranges in lineage (Idea 46), staged in a separate tier first (Idea 70). Caveat: mechanisms and "no one has measured" claims are partner-recalled from storage/database literature — verify DeCandia/Shapiro citations before quoting; all conflict rates measured on our own harness.

### 81. Explicit context↔memory paging layer + the missing controlled comparison (ChatGPT, R14) — HIGH
MemGPT/Letta is the clearest explicit-paging architecture (bounded in-context main area + external archival, model-called memory functions) but uses weak FIFO eviction; no controlled paging-vs-context-stuffing evaluation (task success + token cost, varying policies) exists in the literature. Fix: Idea 70's two tiers become exactly the paging design — bounded working context with a defined token-budget eviction trigger and a retrieval-on-demand promotion API, as a named configurable component; eviction importance-scored, never FIFO — evicted items carry version metadata (Idea 68) and lineage links (Idea 46), so eviction is a reversible move, never deletion; every promoted item tagged with source record versions + eviction timestamp (reinstated evictee, not fresh evidence); run the missing comparison on our golden set — paging agent vs otherwise-identical context-stuffing agent, varying eviction (FIFO vs recency vs importance) and promotion policies, measuring task success AND token cost together (Idea 65's Pareto harness question stated operationally). Caveat: MemGPT details partner-recalled from the 2023 arXiv snapshot — verify before quoting; paging numbers measured on our harness, the first such comparison.

### 82. Retrieval-time ACL enforcement: pre-retrieval hard gate + ACL canary suite (Grok, R14) — HIGH
2025–26 doctrine has converged: filter inside the search query (pre-retrieval), never in application code afterward — post-retrieval filtering silently degrades recall (result counts become an inference channel) and fails open on filter bugs, and unauthorized docs leak via caches, streaming buffers, and observability traces. Agent-Memory-OS (7 stars) ships the pattern: IDs-only candidates re-read behind an ACL hard gate before ranking, `requester_agent_id` on every call. Real incidents: Copilot oversharing (Gartner: 40% delayed rollouts; 2026 governance report: 93% of orgs in production, >75% with governance incidents) and retrieval-layer CVEs (SearchLeak CVE-2026-42824, EchoLeak CVE-2025-32711). No published A/B on recall loss from post-filtering or isolated enforcement overhead — our harness is the first measurement. Fix: hard pre-retrieval gate (requester identity from the authenticated session, never the prompt); single `secure_retrieve` chokepoint with tenant/ACL/expiry filters pushed into the index query; ACL-sync freshness (stale-ACL retrieval = named incident class in Idea 33's suite; known-answer ACL canary per deployment — user A must never retrieve user B's records, Idea 23); append-only retrieval audit log (what retrieved, whose ACL, what schema version — Ideas 60/63/66/67). Caveat: Agent-Memory-OS figures are the author's own; Copilot figures secondary/vendor-reported; filtered-latency numbers are benchmark-blog figures, not controlled studies.

### 83. Version-aware consolidation contract + mixed-version ablation suite (Grok, R14) — HIGH
No published system handles consolidation against a mixed-version store and no measured merge/conflict error rates exist; Mem0's LLM-judged update phase (ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP, misclassification rates unpublished) could freely merge v1 and v2 records; same-field-changed-meaning (semantic field drift) is handled nowhere in agent memory — exactly Idea 68's core insight (a payload can deserialize while its meaning changed). Fix: consolidation declared as a writer class in Idea 68's expand–migrate–contract doctrine — the consolidator declares understood schema versions and quarantines (never best-effort merges) unknown/future ones; every output stamped with input record-schema versions + consolidation rule version + Idea 46 lineage; mixed-version ablation suite in Idea 69 — v1+v2 same-entity merge scenarios (must quarantine or version-stamp, never silently fuse) plus semantic-drift injection (e.g. `confidence` redefined from retrieval-score to calibration-bucket); non-destructive default (superseded nodes excluded from retrieval, retained with `supersedes` edges — MindMemOS over Mem0's default; Idea 76's negative store exempt from consolidation-driven deletion); inferred-never-observed guard on synthesized concept memories (Idea 69). Caveat: absence claims research-derived from one search pass — stated as such; all merge/conflict rates measured on our own suite.

### 84. Incident-review doctrine: freshness SLI, loud-degradation rule, deterministic write gate, bounded-retrieval invariants (Fo, R14) — HIGH
Four 2026 postmortems converge on one incident class: "silent quality loss, never an error" — embedding endpoint died while `/health` stayed green (ai-inference-platform SEV-2, 1h47m); invalid API key 401'd every embedding forever, buried in logs (GAIA v3→v4, earned rule "degradation must be loud", incident encoded as regression eval #1); LLM extractor hallucinated a fiscal year and a validator LLM rubber-stamped it — shipped fix was deterministic Python (Pydantic grounding + entity allow-list + quarantine-by-default; validator removal cut API costs ~50%, Akita postmortem); unbounded retrieval materialized 578 MiB/search × fan-out (lexora-ai; measured −99.5% bytes, −78.2% RSS, −95.3% latency after database-side Top-K). Fix: freshness SLI + ingestion-lag alerting as Idea 67 panels (`ingestion_oldest_pending_seconds`, `embedding_request_failures_total`, fresh-record searchability probe — freshness ≠ serving availability); loud-degradation rule + embedding-provider validation probe (silent semantic death = Idea 33 scenario + Idea 78 canary); deterministic write-path gate — "probabilistic proposes; deterministic commits" (LLM-as-judge measures offline, never the inline integrity gate); bounded-retrieval invariants as architecture constraints (no unbounded materialization, database-side candidate limits, documented fan-out maxima — violations need design review + measured peak-memory test, Idea 65); incident→regression-eval promotion doctrine (every incident ends as a reproduced regression eval + new canary). Caveat: practitioner-grade single-deployment evidence — Akita via secondary write-up; no published managed-vector-DB-outage or HNSW-corruption postmortem found (absence stated, not evidence of absence).

### 85. Bounded-execution envelopes + pre-flight cost enforcement on memory ops (Fo, R14) — MEDIUM-HIGH
LangSmith/Langfuse are recording systems — cost computed after generation, "a record of money that is gone"; no budget mechanism. Enforcement taxonomy: provider-key caps (coarse, shared), orchestration-layer per-agent pre-call counters (best granularity/latency), post-hoc alerts (reactive, hours lag), per-tool circuit breakers. The "bound outside the loop" doctrine: the LLM can't judge its own runaway — the bound lives in wiring code (calibrated p99 × 1.5–2×, warn at 80%, checkpoint before trip, per-task profiles; kill-switches must not corrupt state mid-workflow). Measured runaway data: one $50K runaway agent (via Mandiant report — unbounded retries + no enforcement + delayed observability); Composio-via-V9: cost overruns the top production-incident category, 88% of pilots never reach production. Zero published memory-op-specific runaway data — per-embed/retrieve/consolidation burn is unmeasured. Fix: V9-style five-dimension bounded-execution envelopes (iterations/tool-calls/tokens/wall-clock/cost) on every memory path (embed, retrieve, rerank, consolidate, backfill) — code, calibrated, pre-flight; observability (Idea 67) and enforcement as separate components (never present an alert as a cap); per-tenant/per-agent spend metering with attribution from day one (LiteLLM virtual keys + per-key budgets as backstop); memory-path cost-amplification red-teaming ("can a small memory write cause large memory activity?" — Idea 33 scenarios with measured worst-case cost bounds); deviation-from-baseline cost alerts alongside hard caps (R13 calibration rule). Caveat: runaway figures via secondary reports; calibration numbers are single-team recommendations, not cross-deployment constants; all memory-path caps locally measured (Idea 56's rule extended to cost budgets).

## Ideas 86–91 — Partner watch pipeline (round 15, 6 analyses, 2026-10-16)

Fold-in done 2026-10-16 ~19:45 IST. Ranked by build relevance. Sources: `hidden_files/research/watch-log/088-*.md` through `093-*.md` + ROUND-15-QUESTIONS.md. ChatGPT ×2 consulted directly via omniroute (codex, --stream --stdin); Grok-lens ×2 and Fo-lens ×2 research-derived — direct Grok consultation unavailable this run (empty result → 429 "all credentials cooling down" → empty result over ~4 min, third consecutive round; stopped per the 5-minute rule), direct Fo consultation still needs a live browser session — both flagged, not blocking. No overlap with rounds 1–14 findings (verified per-question in ROUND-15-QUESTIONS.md).

### 86. Concurrency chaos fixture spec: deterministic barriers, separated counters, retry-with-reread (ChatGPT, R15) — HIGH
Executes Idea 80's doctrine. Five-case scenario matrix run against isolated seeded records with deterministic barriers (not timing sleeps): write-write agent-vs-human, write-write agent-vs-consolidation, lost update (two agents, different fields — second must be rejected, not merged over), summary race (consolidation's input versions stale → publication rejected), semantic conflict (allowed by version checks, flagged by validation — never mislabeled as a version rejection). Telemetry schema separates `version_mismatch_rejections_total` from `semantic_conflicts_detected_total` and `stale_derivation_rejections_total`, partitioned by writer pair/record type/conflict class; every rejection event carries run/attempt/idempotency key/record/writer/expected+observed versions/retry number/outcome. Retry policy: never replay a stale payload — retry with the same idempotency key only after rereading and recomputing (bounded attempts + jitter, dedupe repeated keys); escalate to human when intent can't be preserved or retries exhaust. Fixture fails on: any stale write that commits, duplicate application, misclassified telemetry, summary published from stale inputs, or a retry that drops a concurrent change. Failures feed Idea 23's regression loop (seed/schedule preserved as regression cases) and block gate-(d). Caveat: pure fixture contract — no external-system behavior asserted; all conflict rates measured on our own harness.

### 87. Eviction importance-score function + paging-vs-stuffing harness (ChatGPT, R15) — HIGH
Executes Idea 81's doctrine. Importance score I_i = w_r·R + w_f·F + w_u·U + w_p·P + w_d·D (all signals normalized 0–1): recency with decay, frequency with diminishing returns, retrieval utility (measured contribution to task success), provenance value (source authority, primary vs derived), re-derivation cost (effort or impossibility of reconstruction). Weights calibrated on training traces by fitting to pairwise retention judgments derived from held-out task impact, regularized, frozen before final evaluation — never tuned on the test golden set; component ablations reported. Harness arms: paging policy × promotion policy (calibrated composite vs recency-only comparator; promote-on-successful-use vs task-relevance threshold) + importance-paging × no-promotion arm to isolate promotion's effect + context-stuffing baseline (same token budget, declared fixed truncation rule — a bounded comparator, not an unlimited-stuffing assumption). Golden-set measurement splits **retention test** (oracle checks whether needed info survived eviction — coverage and regret vs oracle eviction, reported separately) from **end-to-end test** (real retrieval/promotion policy, task outcomes) — identifying whether a miss came from eviction or retrieval. Pareto report: held-out task success/correctness, total tokens (incl. retrieval + promotion), latency (incl. paging), storage growth, with CIs across seeds. Caveat: no external paging figures asserted; no controlled paging-vs-stuffing evaluation exists in the literature — our harness is the first measurement.

### 88. ACL canary as a honeytoken transplant + deny-column audit (Grok, R15) — HIGH
Executes Idea 82's doctrine. Borrows Thinkst Canarytokens' core property: decoys with no legitimate operational use, so any interaction is a high-fidelity signal; "token accessed = burned" rotation. Per tenant, plant positive canaries (decoy-principal records no real session should retrieve) and negative canaries (user-A-only record probed as user B must return nothing) in the *same* index/namespace as real records, behind the *same* ACL gate — a bypass caught at a second read-time spot check localizes the failure to the gate vs the post-gate path. Rotation on every deployment and after any trigger (burned = replaced), with known-answer probes ("zero results" for unauthorized principal) re-run pre-deploy, post-deploy, and on schedule — kept separate from R6/R13 contamination canaries so one suite's pass never masks the other's failure. Audit log (append-only): per `secure_retrieve` call — requester id from the authenticated session (never the prompt), tenant, query hash (not raw query, so the audit log isn't itself a data leak), candidate IDs pre- and post-gate, per-candidate gate decisions, ranking model version, returned IDs, latency, canary flags. Denied-access attempts are first-class events: oversharing incidents are discovered in the deny column, not the allow column. Canary failure = Idea 33 silent-security-failure incident: deny-by-default freeze on the namespace (R1 kill-switch doctrine, halting the dangerous direction), replay pre/post-gate columns to localize, promote to regression eval (Q5 pipeline). Caveat: Thinkst doctrine transfers, its numbers don't; no measured enforcement-overhead or recall-loss figures exist (R14 caveat).

### 89. Mixed-version ablation suite: four hard criteria + per-release compatibility matrix (Grok, R15) — HIGH
Executes Idea 83's doctrine. Schema registries (Confluent: BACKWARD default, FULL/FORWARD/TRANSITIVE levels; automatic writer/reader resolution) prove the mechanism for *structural* compatibility — but semantic drift (same field, changed meaning) passes every compatibility check and is handled nowhere; that gap is exactly what this suite tests. Three fixture classes: v1+v2 same-entity merge (assert both input versions carried, nothing silently dropped, rule version stamped, cross-version value disagreement fires the conflict monitor); semantic-drift injection (`confidence` retrieval-score → calibration-bucket — must flag or quarantine, never numerically merge); unknown/future-version quarantine (require quarantine with reason code, never best-effort merge or silent skip — negative test: v1-only corpus on a v2-only consolidator must quarantine everything). Four hard criteria: no silent merge (any output from a non-declared input version = fail), no silent drop (any input with no output trace — merge, quarantine, or explicit skip reason = fail; quarantine is visible, not a black hole), stamping completeness (random-sample audit: zero unstamped outputs), drift detection (the canonical failure is merging 0.83-a-score with "high"-a-bucket). Each run publishes a compatibility matrix (consolidator version × record schema versions → merge/quarantine/skip counts); release candidates pass gate-(d) only on a clean matrix. Drift fixtures become permanent Idea 23 regression cases — semantic drift is the likeliest silent recurrence. Caveat: "no published system handles consolidation against mixed-version stores" is research-derived from one R14 pass + this round's schema-registry reading; all merge rates measured on our own suite.

### 90. Incident→regression promotion pipeline: capture schema + four-criteria gate (Fo, R15) — HIGH
Executes Idea 84's doctrine. Google's SRE postmortem template (sre.google: written record of incident, impact, actions, root cause(s), follow-up actions with owners and deadlines; blameless; broadly distributed so cross-team trends surface) gets three memory-system additions at capture time: the trigger artifact (exact query/record set/config that produced the failure — without it the postmortem is a story, not a repro), the oracle (correct behavior as assertions, not prose: "freshness probe failed → alert within 60s"), and the detection gap (which monitor/canary should have caught it — this field *generates* the new canary). Promotion gate — an incident becomes a regression eval only if: reproducible (trigger artifact replays deterministically, seeds/snapshots pinned — R8 restore doctrine), assertion-able (pass/fail against golden set or canary probe, not human judgment), class-membered (instantiates an Idea 33 class or names a new one), fix-verifiable (fails pre-fix, passes post-fix — otherwise it's testing the fixture, not the fix). Below the line: stays a postmortem (written, distributed, trended — the SRE aggregation value), not a regression eval. Replay harness format per promoted incident: `incident.yaml` (class, trigger artifact, oracle assertions, detection-gap note), `repro/` (pinned fixtures), `assertions.py`, `canary/` (new probe from the detection gap, wired into the scheduled suite). Promotion is review-gated like a PR. Idea 23's loop consumes the corpus; trend metric: incident-class recurrence rate — a class firing twice is the pipeline's own failure signal. Caveat: no controlled study found verifying postmortems causally reduce recurrence — the pipeline is a design bet, stated as such; the four criteria are our procedural decision, not an industry standard.

### 91. Per-memory-op cost instrumentation at the chokepoints + pre-flight estimators (Fo, R15) — MEDIUM-HIGH
Executes Idea 85's doctrine. Substrate: OTel GenAI semantic conventions (OTel GenAI SIG, active since 2024 — `gen_ai.operation.name`, `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens/output_tokens`, `gen_ai.request.model`, `gen_ai.provider.name`) confirmed across LiteLLM docs, Envoy AI Gateway, and practitioner write-ups; LiteLLM additionally emits `litellm.cost.total` and ships virtual keys (Org→Team→User→Key) with per-key/team USD budgets. Two honest gaps designed around: conventions standardize tokens/latency, **not cost** (cost is an extension attribute, `memory.cost.usd`, computed from a price table — our design, flagged as such); cost/latency correlate with token counts, not request counts (50K-token op where 3K is normal = the canonical misbehavior signal). Every memory op emits a span: `memory.op` (embed/retrieve/rerank/consolidate/backfill), `memory.tenant`, `memory.agent`, `memory.request_id` (fan-out attribution — one retrieval fans out to N embed calls), token counts, cost extension; non-LLM costs (vector DB compute, storage) get the same span shape with `memory.cost.source=db` so the bill is complete. Measurement points at R14's chokepoints: `secure_retrieve`, the embed batcher, consolidation job entry, backfill scheduler. Pre-flight estimators predict cost from (op type, input size, fan-out, model price); over-estimate → refuse or degrade before spending (clamp Top-K, skip rerank) — and the estimator's own error is a tracked metric (systematic under-estimation = an Idea 33-class silent failure of the enforcement layer itself). Cost-amplification red-teaming (scheduled, adversarial-but-legitimate: namespace-wide re-embed trigger, Top-K-clamp defeat, consolidation explosion): measure worst-case per-op cost, set hard caps from measured maxima not guesses; unbound amplification paths become Q5 incident-corpus entries. Deviation-from-baseline alerts (per tenant×op tokens/cost) catch what caps miss — R14's $50K runaway would have tripped deviation long before the cap; warn at 80% of envelope, checkpoint before trip so killed consolidations resume. Caveat: no memory-op runaway dataset exists; calibration figures remain single-team recommendations; LiteLLM budget fit against our latency budget is our own measurement to make.

### 92. Fixture mutation-testing + gate-(d) wiring: kill/survivor report, adversarial writers, seed discipline (ChatGPT, R16) — HIGH
Validates Idea 86. The chaos fixture is test infrastructure and must itself be tested: four controlled bug-injections each mapped to the assertion that must kill it (removed version predicate → write-write case must see a lost update; stale-payload retry → assert no stale commit; version-less summary publish → summary-race case must fail with correct stale_derivation counter; version-without-semantic-validation → semantic case must flag independently). A surviving mutant is a coverage gap, not a pass. Adversarial writers beyond the five-case matrix: clock-skewed writers (ordering by version, never timestamp), idempotency-key reuse with different payloads (reject/distinguish, never wrong result), version-check bypass (DB constraint or audit must expose it), consolidation racing human edits on the same entities incl. multi-record derivations, duplicate delivery + restart at commit boundaries. CI wiring: deterministic cases per PR, seeded schedules + full mutation suite nightly, stress pre-release; gate-(d) blocks on any invariant violation, counter mismatch, surviving mutant, or flake. Seed discipline: stable corpus, add seeds never replace, rotate randomized seeds periodically; every fixture failure minimized into a named deterministic regression case before fixing (feeds Idea 23). Thresholds: barrier timeouts are deadlock guards only (timeout = failure), 3–5 bounded retries then escalate, zero stale commits, latency limits from measured CI baselines. Caveat: threshold numbers are ChatGPT-recommended example gates — calibrate on our own harness; Jepsen/Elle/Kung-Robinson grounding is methodological, not measured.

### 93. Eviction weight validation protocol: cross-dataset stability, adversarial scorer suites, example gates (ChatGPT, R16) — HIGH
Validates Idea 87. Grouped nested splits: fit weights on some trace distributions, test on held-out domains/periods/users/systems; never split near-duplicates across train/test; bootstrap by task/trace for uncertainty intervals; compare coefficient sign consistency and rank correlation across folds — but judge generalization by held-out retention/regret, not coefficient identity. Sensitivity analysis: ablate each signal and perturb weights within a predeclared range, re-run end-to-end arms, report which perturbations move task success/cost/Pareto membership. Four labeled adversarial suites: frequency gaming (diminishing-returns must stop boilerplate crowding out unique facts), slow-burn facts (recency decay must not evict stable constraints), provenance spoofing (provenance from trusted lineage, never record text), utility gaming (retrieval-utility attributable, capped, robust to correlated events). Example gates (calibrate to product risk): ≥98% oracle coverage overall / ≥95% per critical slice; regret ≤2pp overall / ≤5pp per slice; non-inferior end-to-end within a predeclared margin; Pareto regions defined before testing; CIs across seeds, never a bare mean. Re-fit rule: only on new quality-controlled judgments or demonstrated distribution shift — never to fix a failing gate; weights/features/data/thresholds versioned together. Caveat: gates are example thresholds, not measured constants; TinyLFU (Einziger et al.) is a methodological baseline reference, not a result.

### 94. ACL-canary red-team: distinguishability attacks, canary-aware adversaries, rotation-safe regression (Grok, R16) — HIGH
Hardens Idea 88. The canary system is itself an attack surface. Distinguishability protocol: train a decoy-vs-real classifier — if it beats chance, decoys are fingerprintable (embedding anomalies, metadata cohorts like shared creation batches, access-pattern asymmetries); negative canaries must be indistinguishable from genuinely-empty results (identical latency and response shape). Canary-aware adversaries: the AHA honeytoken framework's own caveat transfers — "insider threats with prior canary schema knowledge could bypass this" — so deploy decoy diversity (multiple independently-rotated schemas), rotate decoy principals, and treat canary schemas as secrets; touched canaries capture the requester's tool/agent signature from the audit log (counter-fingerprinting). Failure modes of the canary system itself: canary fatigue (every false positive trains operators to ignore the next burn — near-zero false positives is a design requirement, per honeytoken practice), false-positive deny storms from bad ACL pushes (audit gate-decision column is the discriminator), rotation breaking regression history (assert on canary-class behavior, never decoy identities). Thresholds: probes off the hot path capped at a fixed latency-budget fraction; burned canaries rotated immediately, unburned on a weeks-scale schedule. Passing run: all known-answer probes correct, distinguisher at chance, zero false positives in window, complete deny-column coverage, rotation within SLA. Caveat: honeytoken doctrine is transferred from intrusion-security practice — no retrieval-layer canary deployment numbers exist; all thresholds measured on our own harness.

### 95. Drift-sensitivity grade ladder + consumer-contract fixtures + release-matrix artifact (Grok, R16) — HIGH
Validates Idea 89. Five-grade drift-injection ladder with recall reported per grade: G1 trivial renames/type flips (table stakes — schema registries catch these), G2 unit/range shifts, G3 semantic redefinition (`confidence` retrieval-score → calibration-bucket), G4 population redefinition ("active customer" now includes trials), G5 gradual cross-version drift. Headline metric is G3+ recall, not overall pass rate. False-quarantine rate measured on legitimate evolutions, with the behavioral binding constraint: engineers must not be incentivized to bypass the suite; every quarantine carries a human-readable reason + audited one-command override. Evasion-designed drift: below-threshold gradualism → cumulative v1-vs-vN check; unfixtured fields → fixture corpus generated from the actual schema with coverage reported; split-version drift → cross-version semantic assertions. Consumer-driven contract tests close the structural/semantic gap ("schema registries catch structural breakage, not semantic breakage" — dev.to): consumers publish dependent assertions, producer CI runs them, and the ablation suite consumes those contracts as fixture sources. The compatibility matrix publishes as a versioned release artifact on every consolidator release; gate-(d) reads it — no matrix, no release. Fixtures model the dual-write migration window explicitly. Caveat: industry drift examples are documented incidents, not agent-memory measurements; the ladder and recall targets are our design decisions — the "first measurement" claim holds only after our harness runs.

### 96. Promotion-pipeline hardening: recurrence-slope metric, suite prioritization, schema stress drills (Fo, R16) — HIGH
Hardens Idea 90. The trend metric made falsifiable: per-class incidents per rolling window normalized by deployment activity; positive recurrence slope triggers a pipeline review (fix didn't fix, oracle wrong, or canary gap); below-the-line incidents tracked in the same taxonomy or the metric is gameable by selective promotion; a class counts as evidence only after two clean windows with the code path still exercised. Suite-growth management: hybrid selection + prioritization (documented practical answer for tight CI budgets) — selection on changed modules per PR, risk-prioritized remainder, full suite on schedule; diversity-and-novelty prioritization signals (which beat composite risk scores in a leakage-safe study); fixed runtime budgets per cadence tier with visible dropped-because-of-budget accounting; retirement rule (clean classes graduate to lower cadence, recurrence re-promotes instantly). Capture-schema stress drills (quarterly game-days): inject a novel failure class, require a complete incident.yaml from the schema alone, second engineer replays from it — failure to replay means the schema gets fixed, and the drill becomes a schema-regression case. Thresholds: review-gate SLA (e.g. 5 business days), below-the-line postmortems retained ≥1 year class-tagged, every promotion ships a canary (new or reused). Passing run = weekly trend report: per-class slope, eval pass rates, canary coverage, capture→review→promote conversion, SLA compliance, suite runtime vs budget. Caveat: selection/prioritization literature is general software-engineering CI practice transferred to incident evals; the recurrence-slope metric is our design — "promotion prevents repeats" stays a falsifiable bet until our own trend data exists.

### 97. Cost-enforcement validation: shadow reconciliation, estimator MAPE bands, cap-defeat red-team (Fo, R16) — MEDIUM-HIGH
Validates Idea 91. Shadow accounting: sum of `memory.cost.usd` per tenant per day must reconcile against provider bills + vector-DB compute within a declared tolerance — the gap is the unattributed-cost metric, and unattributed cost is where runaways hide (FinOps reconciliation controls: allocated/total-eligible ratio, source-bill-vs-allocated difference). Reconcile per layer (token cost vs vector-DB compute vs embedding cost), not one blended number. Missing-cost hunt list: retries/regenerations (~10% broken responses in production LLM workloads), hidden/structured request fields, uninstrumented fan-out, idle capacity (utilization assumptions carry 2.5–24× error — arXiv 2606.11690). Showback before chargeback: publish the attribution model for dispute before caps trip on it. Estimator discipline from PreflightLLMCost (≤25% MAPE standard / ≤15% enhanced, bootstrap CIs, μ+2σ worst case, CI exits 1 on budget breach): declared MAPE bands per (op, model, size class); signed-bias alerts (systematic under-estimation = Idea 33-class silent enforcement failure); (predicted, actual) pairs recalibrated on schedule, versioned. Cap-defeat red-team from the Token Budgets 63-incident catalog: call-count caps are not dollar caps (overshoot up to 1395% — find and convert them); post-call checks admit one overshooting call (giant-call adversary → pre-call refusal, zero overshoot in the study); coarse estimators under-reserve 168%/153% (adversarial inputs: max-length contexts, tool-augmented prompts, dense multi-byte text); slow-drip below thresholds (caught by baseline-deviation alerts); cross-tenant attribution confusion (caught as unattributed cost). Thresholds: caps from measured maxima (p99 × 1.5–2×), warn 80% → checkpoint → trip with hysteresis against flapping. Caveat: Token Budgets figures are LLM-agent measurements transferred to memory ops; "no memory-op runaway dataset exists" still holds — our shadow ledger is the first measurement.

## Ideas 98–103 — Partner watch pipeline (round 17, 6 analyses, 2026-10-16)

Fold-in done 2026-10-16 ~21:10 IST. Round 17 is the production-operations layer: how the R14 doctrines / R15 specs / R16 validations actually run live. Ranked by build relevance. Sources: `hidden_files/research/watch-log/100-*.md` through `105-*.md` + ROUND-17-QUESTIONS.md. ChatGPT ×2 consulted directly via omniroute (codex, --stream --stdin); Grok-lens ×2 and Fo-lens ×2 research-derived — direct Grok consultation unavailable a fifth consecutive round (OpenRouter 402 insufficient credits, stopped per the 5-minute rule), direct Fo consultation still needs a live browser session — both flagged, not blocking. No overlap with rounds 1–16 (verified per-question in ROUND-17-QUESTIONS.md).

### 98. Sequenced release-gate battery + deploy-to-halt runbook: no override for corruption, leak, or failed rollback (ChatGPT, R17) — HIGH
Operates Ideas 92/95. Six gates in fixed order — change review (name the rollback owner, test the rollback plan) → drift/compat suite vs the matrix → chaos fixture → ACL canaries (any unauthorized read/write = hard block) → cost budget verification → release readiness (dashboards, alerts, rollback controls, named sign-off) — results recorded against the release + compatibility matrix. Gate-(d) override owned by the release authority with explicit concurrence from the memory-service owner (+ security owner for ACL risk); no override ever for confirmed data corruption, unauthorized access, or a failed rollback path. Consolidation changes deploy via shadow mode → isolated cohort → staged expansion with observation holds, prior job kept runnable. Freeze triggers enumerated; halt procedure preserves logs/IDs, assesses data+access impact, then rolls back; resume only on validated remediation + recorded approval. Caveat: gate ordering and budgets are ChatGPT's design recommendation — calibrate on live data.

### 99. Live multi-writer coordination: OCC by default, fenced leases only where exclusive ownership is needed (ChatGPT, R17) — HIGH
Production complement to Idea 92's fixture. Writers register tenant + workload class + operation ID with bounded concurrency quotas; jobs claim records/namespace partitions with leases (owner, expiry, monotonically-increasing fencing token — storage rejects old-token commits, so a paused worker can't overwrite its successor); record version/ETag on every update, narrow transactions. Deadlock/livelock policy: single-record atomic commits, globally-consistent claim ordering, bounded retries with randomized backoff then dead-letter — never infinite — plus an operator-visible cancellation path. Priority: human corrections outrank consolidation/backfill (reject or rebase the job's stale write, never silently overwrite a human edit); tenant fairness via weighted fair queuing, separate interactive/bulk queues, reserved interactive capacity, per-tenant rate limits. Coordination-health monitoring (lease age/takeover, conflict/retry rates, human-edit collisions, cross-tenant skew); degradation response throttles bulk first and fails closed when correctness is uncertain. Caveat: priority order and queueing discipline are ChatGPT's design recommendation; quotas and thresholds calibrate on live contention data.

### 100. Canary on-call runbook: page on burn, ticket on tooling, freeze by procedure (Grok, R17) — HIGH
Operationalizes Ideas 88/94. Positive-canary burn pages security on-call immediately (Thinkst doctrine: decoy interaction = high-fidelity compromise signal); negative-canary anomaly pages the service on-call as a gate failure; canary-tooling signals go to a low-severity ticket queue — never a page (the anti-fatigue design). SEV-1/2/3 ladder with first-response SLAs; deny-by-default freeze procedure that preserves the audit slice and keeps canary schemas secret from tenants; false-positive triage tree keyed on the audit gate-decision column (allow-where-deny = real gate failure; burn cluster after an ACL push = bad push → rollback); escalation to security co-ownership at SEV-2, incident commander + war room at SEV-1; every declared incident closes with a postmortem whose detection-gap field generates the next canary — a burn with no new canary is an incomplete review. Caveat: Grok-lens synthesis of SRE/PagerDuty/Thinkst sources, not a partner answer; minute-budgets are design recommendations.

### 101. Cost attribution as organizational operations: showback before chargeback, gap on the platform's books (Grok, R17) — MEDIUM-HIGH
Operationalizes Ideas 91/97. Daily showback per tenant×agent×op plus the unattributed-cost line published visibly (FinOps: unallocated cost is never absorbed silently); chargeback on attributed cost only, with the reconciliation gap kept on the platform as the incentive to shrink it; disputes adjudicated against estimator (predicted, actual) pairs and declared MAPE bands, not vibes; trip overrides and cap raises owned jointly by tenant budget owner + service owner — on-call cannot unilaterally raise a cap; trip resumption requires root cause + re-estimated cap + two-owner sign-off; security freeze overrides cost operations; monthly reconciliation close as a release artifact that gate-(d) may read as a block signal. Caveat: Grok-lens synthesis of FinOps sources transferred to memory-op attribution; ownership rules and cadences are design recommendations — no memory-op chargeback case study exists.

### 102. Rollback decision tree + honest semantics for non-invertible memory: freeze is the default (Fo, R17) — HIGH
Reverse side of Ideas 89/95's forward doctrine. Roll back on matrix regression with growing blast radius; roll forward when the fix is smaller than a rollback and rollback would re-introduce worse; freeze (stop rollout, halt the path) when evidence isn't in — freeze is the default, not the failure; decision SLA 30–60 min for SEV-2+, else the safer branch wins automatically. Three declared rollback operations for non-invertible memory — restore-to-snapshot, quarantine-forward, replay-from-source — and the release must declare which applies per changed path *before* shipping (undeclared rollback plan = gate-(d) block). Schema rollback keeps the old reader/writer path warm through the dual-write window in reverse; never roll back data and code independently without a reverse compatibility-matrix check; rollback verification re-runs the full gate battery and records the rollback as an R15-format incident. Caveat: Fo-lens synthesis of K8s/Argo progressive delivery and expand/contract migration practice; SLA windows and operation definitions are design decisions.

### 103. Memory-ops human cadence: weekly reviews, quarterly drills, annual silent-quality game day (Fo, R17) — HIGH
Closes the loop on Idea 96's measurement. 45-minute weekly incident review consuming the R16Q5 trend report: new incidents + promotion decisions, recurrence-slope review with named owners, stale-action-item escalation (2 cycles → service owner, 4 cycles → release authority), below-the-line taxonomy scan. Quarterly schema stress drills with mandatory on-call-lead attendance; annual full-loop game day; at least one silent-quality game day per year (the incident class paging can't see — R14's defining class). Blameless reviews where "which monitor should have caught this" is a mandatory question and a new canary/SLI is the mandatory output when the answer is "none." Ops calendar composes reviews, monthly reconciliation close, drills, and release freezes (published a quarter ahead); a review that promotes nothing and questions nothing is itself a signal. Caveat: Fo-lens synthesis of Google SRE postmortem/game-day practice; timeboxes and escalation thresholds are design recommendations calibrated to single-service scope.

## Ideas 104–109 — Partner watch pipeline (round 18, 6 analyses, 2026-10-16)

Ranked by build relevance. Sources: `hidden_files/research/watch-log/106-*.md` through `111-*.md` + ROUND-18-SYNTHESIS.md. ChatGPT consulted directly; Grok/Fo analyses research-derived (OpenRouter credits exhausted; no live browser in coordinator scope).

### 104. Embedding-inversion threat model: stored vectors ARE sensitive text (Grok, R18) — VERY HIGH
Vec2Text: 92% exact recovery of 32-token inputs (BLEU ~97); ZSInvert: >80% sensitive-info leakage on Enron for all encoders, survives σ=0.01 DP noise; Zero2Text: black-box cross-domain. Any vector-DB leak is a document leak. Fix: encrypt vectors of sensitive content pre-storage, or explicitly null them on erasure — load-bearing constraint on Idea 105's crypto design.

### 105. Crypto-shredding spec: per-subject DEKs + KMS KEK, erasure = key destruction (ChatGPT, R18) — VERY HIGH
AES-256-GCM per-record/subject DEKs wrapped by KMS-held KEK; deletion = destroy DEK + tombstone + hash-chained audit entry + signed erasure certificate. Honest limits: proof attests "key no longer exists," not that every copy is gone; backups become unrecoverable without rewriting (decisive vs logical delete); derived copies need lineage-tracked keys (Idea 46); model weights aspirational. Operationalizes Idea 50. Start at the PII tier. Fix: erasure mechanism.

### 106. Bitemporal query layer: add the transaction-time axis (ChatGPT, R18) — HIGH
Valid time (when fact is true) vs transaction time (when store learned it) as first-class query layer; corrections close transaction intervals, never overwrite; retrieval must persist time policy + record IDs per decision or replay silently changes. Full XTDB adoption heavier than needed — layer semantics onto the existing assertion model. Fix: assertion record schema + replay tooling.

### 107. Conflict adjudication workflow: flag → triage → adjudicate → close (Fo, R18) — HIGH
Structured conflict tickets in severity-routed queues; steward adjudicates in evidence-panel UI (keep-A/keep-B/merge/quarantine) with mandatory reason codes; never silent age-out (aging auto-escalates or quarantines); severity SLAs, two-eyes escalation. The missing human half of the monitor runbook. Builds on Ideas 89/90. Fix: monitor runbook.

### 108. Cold-start bootstrap: five production moves (Grok, R18) — MEDIUM-HIGH
Popularity defaults, signup elicitation (dense preference signal), contextual-bandit exploration, content-embedding bootstrap for cold items (9.2× better than random documented), import paths; evaluated by A/B holdouts. Maps to new-tenant memory-store bootstrap: defaults + elicitation + import + progressive enrichment. Fix: onboarding design.

### 109. Multi-region write ownership: home-region convention, adopt early (Fo, R18) — MEDIUM
Most real "active-active" is home-region partitioning (one writer per entity, nothing to merge); freshness via replication-lag SLO (p99 < 1s) + vector/HLC clocks. Single-region fine now, but adopt the convention early — retrofitting later is a migration. Fix: write-path convention.

### 116. TEE deployment pattern against embedding inversion: never persist full transcripts as raw vectors in a shared index (ChatGPT, R20) — MEDIUM
R18 showed embeddings recover ~92% of stored text; no mainstream vector DB ships HE/ORAM. Track 3-bit-quantized private retrieval (arXiv 2609.36376: 1–3 min/query) for Phase-3's private-recall lane. Treat the conflict monitor's inputs as inversion targets. Fix: store threat model + TEE deployment pattern.

### 117. Synthetic memory-store recipe for conflict-density eval: event graphs, seeded contradictions with resolution policies, IFCMemoryBench replay-restriction (ChatGPT, R20) — HIGH
Persona-grounded histories with validity intervals + provenance; deliberate contradictions with recorded policies (recency / explicit correction / authority / ask); realism = dirtiness (40/30/20/10 entity-detail split collapses Hit@1 27–32%→5.6%); LoCoMo/LongMemEval baselines to borrow. Score the monitor on detection AND action-correctness, with unanswerable cases. Fix: Phase-3 synthetic-store eval harness.

### 118. Conflict-detector red-team battery: paraphrase laundering, drift trajectories, Kerckhoffs threat model, Explanation-before-label (Grok, R20) — HIGH
RL-tuned paraphrasers drop detector AUC 0.789→0.147 (TPR@1%FPR→0.000), transfer across families; drift attacks (pairwise-clean, endpoints-contradict) are unmeasured by every published benchmark; NLI hedges to "neutral" under pressure (+20.8% robustness gap); adaptive attacks cost ~1000x the attacker — that cost multiplier is the security margin. Measure at fixed-threshold TPR@FPR, never accuracy. Fix: Phase-3 adversarial battery.

### 119. Write-amplification metric for the memory store: fan-out factor per logical write, in bytes and dollars (Grok, R20) — HIGH
One write → re-embed k chunks → HNSW delete+insert tombstones → metadata indexes → summary invalidation ($0.005–$0.030 per consolidation call, exceeds the write's whole embed+index cost) → LSM compaction (WAF 2.8–14.2×). Full re-index calibration: 50K docs on 3-large ≈ $4K and 4–6h; chunking/model change = full reindex (schema, not config). R19 backpressure must threshold on fan-out-adjusted cost, not logical writes. Fix: per-stage write counters from day one.

### 120. Degraded-mode ladder for the monitor: sparse-only fallback with explicit `degraded` field, circuit breaker, log-vs-index reconciler (Fo, R20) — HIGH
Breaker trips after 3 consecutive timeouts → fail fast 60s; rerank dies first (99.96% of retrieval latency), then dense leg, then BM25 (local, survives); `degraded: "sparse_only"` contract — never present a reduced answer as normal; admission control 429+Retry-After, agents shed first; recovery reconciles log-vs-index before traffic returns (stale vectors worse than a down store). A false-negative "no conflicts" in degraded mode is worse than a slow one. Fix: monitor runbook + degraded signal.

### 121. Cross-lingual store design: shared multilingual index, language as first-class record field, per-language monitor thresholds (Fo, R20) — HIGH
Shared aligned index (BGE-M3 class) — not translation-on-write (×N storage), not translation-on-read (3–6s/query, fails on short queries), not per-language indexes (mixed queries fall through); 3-large scores 0.0056 vs gemini-embedding-001 0.7049 on en-ta STS; English-only encoders shred Devanagari/Tamil into UNKs while returning plausible vectors (silent garbage); single global cosine threshold provably unworkable (~10× across models). A Hindi-remembered/English-contradicted pair must collide. Fix: encoder one-way-door decision + cross-lingual conflict suite for Phase-3.

### 122. Retrieval-layer injection defense: unforgeable boundaries + retrieval-time inspection for the controller (Grok, R21) — HIGH
Indirect prompt injection via retrieved memories is a distinct attack phase (AgentPoison 63% end-to-end ASR with one poisoned record; InjecMEM 76.6%, PMPA 81.7% cross-session; prompt-level defenses fail post-poisoning). Textual delimiters are security theater (83% ASR) — StruQ's unforgeable reserved-token delimiters hit ~0%; behavioral instruction-detection from model internals hits 99.6% in-domain, ASR 0.12% on BIPIA. Render every retrieved memory behind structural boundaries, scan at retrieval (not just write), flag memories prescribing future writes (worming), gate shared-memory promotion. Fix: retrieval-pipeline injection ASR eval for Phase-3.

### 123. Dedup pipeline order: exact-hash → flag near-dups → conflict detection, never merge-before-monitor (Grok, R21) — HIGH
Negation and small fact-differences are similarity-invisible ("out" vs "not out" merges at 0.9 token overlap); aggressive dedup eats the contradictions the monitor exists to find. Deployed cosine thresholds span 0.90–0.98 and are embedder-dependent — tune via SemDeDup's 10%-sample protocol on our corpus, document ε and retained fraction. Flag-don't-drop for near-dups; demote-don't-delete for versions; MMR/group-by-document fix crowding at selection time. Fix: dedup policy in the design doc, monitor downstream of dedup.

### 124. Context packer as a named pipeline stage: retrieve wide → rerank 3–4 → dedup → edge-place → budget → cite (ChatGPT, R21) — HIGH
20+ point positional accuracy swings (worst case below closed-book 56.1%); every model degrades with input length; a focused ~300-token prompt beats ~113k history; even one distractor hurts. Defaults: best evidence first, second-best last; budget the whole request with the real tokenizer + explicit output allowance; stable `[S1]`-style source IDs for the monitor's audit trail. Validate position sweeps on the deployed model before defaults become law. Fix: packer owned by the controller at the retrieval→generation boundary.

### 125. Hybrid multimodal store: modality-specialized encoders + shared-space cross-modal search, transcription as backbone (ChatGPT, R21) — MEDIUM
Most "multimodal memory" products actually search transcripts/captions/OCR (Limitless, TwelveLabs pattern); ImageBind-style joint spaces stay research-only. Contradictions can span modalities (photo vs text note — Phase-3 frontier, no shipped tooling); cross-modal dedup is harder (voice note + photo of the same event). EmbeddingGemma 2 (Oct 2026, Apache 2.0, 191MB text-only / 567MB all-modality on Pixel) makes on-device multimodal viable. Fix: hybrid architecture decision for Phase-3 multimodal intake.

### 126. On-device memory as filtered CRDT replica: contradiction pass runs after merge, not only at write (Fo, R21) — MEDIUM
Shipped pattern: filtered replica on device (shape subscriptions), CRDT delta queues, vector-clock convergence with cloud as merge authority — but CRDTs guarantee byte convergence, not semantic correctness; contradictory facts recorded on two devices survive "automatic" resolution (NodeDB dead-letter queue + CompensationHint is the honest pattern). Budgets are physical (~1.0–1.1 GB RAM for 3B quantized); split is stable: recall+embed+offline-write on device, validation+consolidation+analytics in cloud. Fix: sync-completion contradiction hook for any future local-first track.

Production ε sits 1–2 orders of magnitude above theory (Census 2020 shipped ε=19.61; Apple iOS ε=14/day; Chrome ε=2, lifetime cap 8–9). ### 128. Three-clock per-assertion validity record: truth, check, retention as separate fields (ChatGPT, R22) — HIGH
Per-assertion `valid_from/valid_until` (half-open truth interval, NULL = currently valid), `observed_at`, `review_after` (freshness deadline), `record_until` (retention), `status ∈ {current, superseded, disputed, unverified}`. Hard rule: "not recently verified" ≠ "false" — never close a validity interval on review-deadline expiry. Invalidation by supersession: temporally overlapping contradiction on the same entity pair closes the old edge's `valid_until` at the new edge's `valid_from`; never overwrite in place. Retire ≠ delete (retired claims keep provenance for historical "why did we believe X?" queries). Retrieval filters on the validity window and surfaces ranges into the context template. Turns R1/R2/R8's ad-hoc decay/tombstone logic into one schema. Fix: assertion schema for Phase-3.

### 129. Cross-agent sharing architecture: five-family taxonomy, identity-bound namespaces, write arbitration (ChatGPT, R22) — HIGH
Blackboard / partitioned namespaces / scoped capabilities / governed promotion / separate-stores-with-broker — name the family for every sharing decision. Namespace bound to *authenticated identity at the service boundary*, never caller-supplied text ("isolation as an application bug waiting to happen"). Separate read/write capabilities with expiry. MCP/A2A give transport/auth, not memory authorization — the memory server enforces its own ACLs. Load-bearing failure: concurrent writes silently overwrite ("shared memory turns into a source of misinformation"); write arbitration (version checks/transactions) on every shared-write path. Governed Memory paper as best quantitative anchor (99.6% recall, zero leakage in adversarial tests — paper result, not production replication); no public shared-memory postmortem exists. Fix: sharing architecture section of the Phase-3 design doc.

### 130. Per-stage latency SLOs with p99-as-leading-churn-indicator (Grok, R22) — HIGH
Read path is solved at agent-memory scale (mesa kNN P50 3.9/P99 ~4.8 ms; Pinecone S1 28 ms p95 @10M) — the binding cost is everything around ANN (hybrid +6 ms p50; consolidation LLM round-trips 200–2000 ms dominate storage ~100x). Churn degrades tails, not medians, architecture-specifically (Chroma p99 8 ms @500k → 800 ms+ @50M on SQLite lock contention; Weaviate holds). No managed vendor publishes write-path p99 — write→findable lag is unmeasured everywhere; instrument it explicitly. SLOs per stage: ANN with production filters attached (filtering wall > vector scan as tail risk), write→findable lag, end-to-end incl. embedding + LLM on a separate budget. p99 alert from day one (~100 ms) fires on churn before vector-count thresholds do. Fix: latency SLO spec + p99 churn alerts.

### 131. Per-op cost ladder: consolidation token budgets first, rerank measured, 17x tier spread (Grok, R22) — HIGH
At 1M queries/month (Oct 2026): LLM tokens ~75–80% of usage, reranking ~15% ("the line item people forget," an order of magnitude above the vector DB), observability 5–20%, vector DB ~1%, embeddings ~$1. Model-tier choice alone = ~17x spread per 1K queries — routing is the biggest lever (−72%). Consolidation LLM calls ($0.005–$0.030 each) can exceed the write's whole embed+index cost → per-cycle token budgets. Index builds are compute-hours (100K chunks: 16h CPU vs 28 min GPU) — borrow-a-GPU-per-reindex. Below ~100K queries/month, 0.5 FTE maintenance dwarfs usage. Sampled tracing from day one (10–20% full + 100% token logging). Fix: per-op cost counters pre-call with warn-at-80%/trip caps (calibrates R14's enforcement doctrine).

### 132. Four-level consistency vocabulary with write-token propagation and measured staleness SLO (Fo, R22) — HIGH
Strong / Bounded (default, ~5s in one deployment) / Session (read-your-writes via the client's own last-write timestamp as GuaranteeTs) / Eventually — promise stated per-read-call, not per-store. Neo4j bookmarks = same idea for graphs (causal consistency without global strong consistency). Write-token propagation: controller stamps reads with its last-write ts for session RYW without paying Strong everywhere. Failure class named: **phantom missing memories** (Pinecone: 200-OK ≠ queryable; Weaviate: read level below write level silently skips repair; vector-query UUID lists ignore read consistency) — looks like a contradiction bug, is a consistency bug; the conflict monitor must be consistency-aware. Default reads Bounded/QUORUM; escalate to Strong for conflict-monitor and write-verification reads. Write→poll-until-visible probes in the harness publish p50/p99 visibility lag as the staleness SLO. Fix: consistency section of the store ops spec.

### 133. Semantic cache dual layer: exact-match first, calibrated thresholds, write-path invalidation (Fo, R22) — MEDIUM
Measured numbers are all FAQ/chatbot traffic (61.6–68.8% hit rates, ~65% latency improvement at 67% hit rate) — treat as upper bound, not plan, for memory traffic. Threshold is the pivotal control: 0.99→0.75 raised savings 15.8%→86.3% with <1pp accuracy drop on chatbot traffic, but loose thresholds serve confidently-wrong answers fast ("amplifies correctness and incorrectness equally") — calibrate per query class from a held-out precision/recall curve. Invalidation three-pronged: per-type TTL + write-path invalidation events + staleness-detection re-runs (the write that lands in the vector store must invalidate the cache entry — ties to Idea 132). Cache-bypass for correctness-critical reads (conflict-monitor verification). Tenant-scoped keys mandatory (R10). Fix: retrieval-path cache spec for Phase-3.

### 134. Bounded retention blend + intervention tier: MadCat formula as default, silence-policed re-injection (ChatGPT, R23) — HIGH
No production retention-decay curve exists anywhere — every decay parameter must be locally measured (licenses R12's retention-curve harness as required). Starting parameterization: `finalScore = vectorScore × (0.5 + recency×0.3 + priority×0.2)` — bounded (never below 0.5× base), priority as the survival channel for old-but-important facts; evaluate decay-inside-the-HNSW-walk. "Remember When It Matters": behavioral state decay means the design target is influence decay, not deletion — add an intervention tier (memory sidekick / scheduled re-injection) with an explicit silence policy (over-reminding wastes tokens and distracts; +8.3pp Terminal-Bench / +6.8pp τ²-Bench evidence). AgentMemBench's horizon collapse (EKV 0.573 vs ≤0.005) as calibration anchors. Keep ranking and retention separate; retention class-specific. Fix: retrieval ranking function + intervention path + retention harness.

### 135. Correction routing: store-first, weights-exception; editing metrics as acceptance tests (ChatGPT, R23) — HIGH
Corrections land in the explicit memory store (reversibility, provenance, expiry, per-user scoping); parametric editing is NOT in the Phase-3 update path — ROME/MEMIT evidence is offline/benchmark-bound, and cumulative edits erode locality (an edit pile is a regression time-bomb). Adopt efficacy / generalization / specificity / portability as acceptance-test categories for memory updates generally; source-of-truth-first discipline (correct upstream, cite with timestamp). Parametric erasure is unreliable — sensitive removal stays key destruction (R18). Fix: correction routing rule + acceptance-test suite.

### 136. Retrieval/generation split monitoring with FP1–FP7 failure tags and the three ingestion alerts (Grok, R23) — HIGH
Barnett et al.'s seven failure points, split by the retrieval/generation line: FP4 (correct context, wrong answer) is indistinguishable from FP2 (missing context) from output alone — log what was retrieved before any tuning decision. Index gaps are the catastrophic silent tail (HelpBot: 5-week stale index, exit code zero, traces green). Filter brittleness measured: a 31-day-old top article deleted by a 30-day window. Dense retrieval structurally blind to exact tokens → hybrid + RRF; gap vs ordering = different layers, different fixes. Three LLMOps alerts from day one: per-source document counts, index freshness, per-source failure rate; ingestion partial failures never exit zero silently. No hard recency/namespace filters by default; text+vectors stored separately with model labels; threshold drift tracked per space. Fix: retrieval monitoring spec + ingestion alert battery.

### 137. Key rotation runbook: epochs, dual-read, add-before-replace; shredding/rotation interplay (Grok, R23) — HIGH
DEK rotation re-encrypts rows (expensive, rare — compromise/classification change); KEK rotation re-wraps 32-byte DEKs (minutes, cheap — annual/compliance cadence; routine DEK rotation often not audit-required). Generation epochs in every envelope from day one; lazy rollover (rewrap-on-read, dual-read during transition); add-before-replace (old generations never deleted first — the crash-safety rule); never single-transaction full-store re-encryption (40TB war story: WAL ballooned, 14h replication lag). One key-op at a time; re-seal key material after every rotation; restore drills cover mixed-generation stores. Shredding/rotation interplay: erasure during dual-read = "pending destruction after grace window" — certificate names generations destroyed, attests cache invalidation (DEK cache TTL = propagation bound), covers lineage-tracked derived keys; every rotation a hash-chained provenance event ("what key generation protected this record at decision time"). Fix: rotation runbook + erasure-certificate v2.

### 138. Three-layer chaos program: CI fixture, quarterly catalogue, game days — with indeterminate-timeout checker rule (Fo, R23) — MEDIUM
Evidence basis for R8/R14–R17's specified fixtures: industry fault menu (pod failures, partitions, packet corruption, bandwidth restriction, time faults) as pre-release hardening; Jepsen-style checkers catch silent consistency violations (VoltDB 6.3) — with the rules "demonstrates faults, not absence" and "timed-out = indeterminate, not failed" (checker explores both branches). New faults for R8's menu: time faults (clock skew vs version stamps) and bandwidth restriction (grey failures evading lag monitors). Ops discipline: steady state first, falsifiable hypotheses, abort conditions pre-written, quarterly 5-experiment catalogue; game days validate *response* (least-confident scenario, real runbooks, no hints, debrief → action items), fixtures validate *mechanisms* — one never substitutes for the other. Fix: resilience chapter of the Phase-3 ops spec.

### 139. Failover ops contract: agent-seat RTO, single-writer fence + quiescence, drill ladder (Fo, R23) — MEDIUM
Database-internal RTO is a fiction: 60–120s advertised failover left apps dark up to 6 minutes (DNS caching, dead-socket pools, unbounded statements) — define and measure RTO as "first successful retrieval at the agent's seat," with client-side killers named in the spec. Cutover contract: single-writer fence (CAS control row naming the active region) + quiescence ≥ max in-flight write + consolidation pass + clock skew; region-local replay state purged, never replicated; split-brain (writes from both regions at same revision) = drill invalidated, fail closed on ambiguity. Per-record version stamps give provable split-brain detection. Drill ladder quarterly: planned switchover (RPO 0) → residency-verified → partition-injected → region-loss; RTO budgets shrink with practice (30–60 min realistic day one, 15 min aspirational post-4-drills); no surprise drills. Precondition: standby holds KEK material before cutover (ties to Idea 137). Fix: failover chapter of the Phase-3 ops spec.

### 140. ErasureCase DSR workflow: state machine, server-side checklist, O(keys) erasure via DEK+map destruction (Fo, R24) — VERY HIGH
Deletion is a state machine (requested/validated/blocked/in-progress/needs-attention/completed/failed); checklist seeded server-side from R19's inventory, recorded per case; completion = every step acknowledged. Delete the random subject_ref mapping AND destroy the subject's DEK — erasure becomes destroying keys, not hunting copies. Required step: re-run or invalidate consolidation output derived from erased records. Backups: deferred tombstone + restore drill proving erased data doesn't resurrect. WORM proof-of-erasure ledger; intake routed by strictest jurisdiction; deletion vs suppression as disjoint paths (suppression down the irreversible shred path is data loss). Fix: DSR chapter of the Phase-3 ops spec.

### 141. Paired memory-on/off ablation as the milestone's evidence standard (ChatGPT, R24) — VERY HIGH
WorldModelMCP preregistered paired benchmark (fixed agent, 49 paired SWE-bench Verified instances): 67.3% → 77.6% (+10.2pp), zero baseline regressions — strongest causal design in 24 rounds of survey. Operationalizes R19's attribution battery: same controller, same tasks, fixed budget; report success delta + retrieval hits + regressions + tokens. Headline cross-model scores are explicitly not memory evidence. Fix: required evidence bar for every Phase-3 memory claim.

### 142. Two-loop reflection (hot bounded + cold deep) with provenance links and raw-episode fallback (ChatGPT, R24) — HIGH
Hot loop: replay last ~3 verbal lessons into the prompt (no context bloat); cold loop: importance-triggered or scheduled deep reflection writing higher-order insights back into the stream, sleep-time consolidation. Every derived fact carries a provenance link; retrieve the raw episode when fact confidence is low — the LoCoMo datum demands it (summaries: 84.7% recall but 32.0 vs 43.3 F1, ~10pt FactScore drop). Write-path selectivity before abstraction; contradiction/supersede policy for structured facts (temporal-KG extraction turns errors into durable false facts otherwise). Fix: controller reflection + provenance design.

### 143. Embedding strategy: tiered index/query pair, batch consolidation, dims-as-dominant-cost (Grok, R24) — HIGH
Three-term cost: token price × dimension × format, set once at index creation (100M chunks: 819 GB at 2048-f32 → 3.2 GB at 256-binary). Shared-space tiered pairs (Cohere Embed 5 Pro→Fast $0.12→$0.08 at 98.4 vs 100 quality; Voyage 4 same pattern) break the price/quality tradeoff; batch APIs halve consolidation cost. Self-host breakeven ~300K queries/month or ~20M sentences/month (+10–15% ops tax). Selection order: compliance → language share → cost-of-wrong-answer → engineering capacity. Fix: embedding strategy section of the Phase-3 design doc.

### 144. Index-build discipline: flat below 50k, IVFFlat-family, signal-triggered scheduled rebuilds (Grok, R24) — HIGH
Measured 13x build-time spread at 2.25M (LanceDB/Milvus 7–8 min vs pgvector 92 min); HNSW 15–45 min/1M, 2–6h/10M, superlinear. Below ~50k entries the index is negative value — stay on exact/flat search, persist graph snapshots, never rebuild on restart. Triggers = embedding-model changes / churn degradation / centroid drift, not calendar. Codastra's rule: peak load = query + indexing load — builds run CONCURRENTLY on separate capacity with 1%→5%→20% shadow-then-ramp. Geometric recall holds at scale; nDCG collapses for all engines (embedding ceiling, not index defect). Fix: index lifecycle spec for Phase-3.

### 145. Staged dual-write upgrade template with named commit point: blue-green for embedding swaps (Fo, R24) — MEDIUM-HIGH
Upgrade = code version + embedding/schema version (separable). Staged recipe: read v1/write both → re-embed with read-both/log-diffs verification → read v2/write both → cut → drop v1. Rollback dies when old code can't read new data — the dual-write IS the rollback plan; name the commit point explicitly. Per-step checkpoints (version + config diff + snapshot); old index warm as parachute; drain in-flight consolidation before cutover; change-freeze + baseline/1.5×-alert monitoring. Rolling for code, blue-green for embedding/schema. Fix: upgrade chapter of the Phase-3 ops spec.
