## Ideas 146–151 — Partner watch pipeline (round 25, 6 analyses, 2026-10-17)

Ranked by build relevance. Sources: `hidden_files/research/watch-log/148-*.md` through `153-*.md` + ROUND-25-SYNTHESIS.md. ChatGPT consulted directly; Grok/Fo analyses research-derived (OpenRouter credits exhausted; no live browser in scope).

### 146. Plan memory as typed artifacts + subgoal ledger: CORPGEN's four failure modes as the design checklist (ChatGPT, R25) — HIGH
No clean evidence that persisting a plan tree improves web-benchmark completion — measured deltas support skill memory (Voyager 3.3× items) and feedback memory (Reflexion 97% vs 75% ALFWorld) instead. CORPGEN (Microsoft): baseline CUAs collapse 16.7%→8.7% under interleaved load; tiered memory + hierarchical planning + experiential trajectory retrieval recovers 15.2% vs 4.3% (3.5×, load-degraded baseline). Four failure modes = design checklist: context saturation O(N), cross-task interference (→ sub-agent isolation), dependency-DAG complexity, reprioritization overhead. Eval warning: artifact-based judgment agreed with humans 90% vs 40% for trace-based. Fix: typed versioned plan artifacts + subgoal ledger + checkpoint resume; experiential-trajectory retrieval at plan time; true memory ablation per Idea 141.

### 147. Claim-level faithfulness verifier as read-path gate: decompose → entailment-check → per-claim verdicts (ChatGPT, R25) — HIGH
Operational pattern converged (RAGAS Faithfulness, Lynx, Azure Groundedness): atomic-claim decomposition → entailment check against retrieved memory records with provenance/freshness → per-claim verdicts retained. Never gate on aggregate scores (~92% aggregate can hide ~18% per-claim hallucination; FActScore's only hard number: 58.0% factual precision +~6pp with retrieval, setup-specific). Inverts R21: the retrieved store is the verifier's evidence base — the verifier must sit downstream of provenance/freshness or it certifies consistency with a poisoned store, not truth. Citation correctness ≠ completeness; refusal/abstention is part of the defense. Fix: read-path verifier with purpose-built entailment classifier, calibrated on human-labeled evidence from our own store.

### 148. Graph-when-it-earns-it: vector+keyword baseline, graph expansion on four named failure conditions (Grok, R25) — HIGH
Zep/Graphiti: +18.5% LongMemEval at ~90% lower latency; temporal tasks 63.8% vs 49.0% vector-only; multi-hop +20–30pp (MOSAIC, HippoRAG). But no substrate dominates: vector net-negative on ALFWorld (−0.5 vs no-memory); BM25 beat graph on BigCodeBench at 1/6 latency; one KG lost to flat RAG (0.417 vs 0.468 F1). Hybrid entry-plus-expansion = measured sweet spot (+25pp at ~16× latency). Real bill: ~400× embedding cost per turn at write time, durable extraction errors, cold start, single-session recall regression (94.6%→80.4%). Fix: start vector+keyword over self-contained statements; add graph expansion only on multi-hop-through-entity / identity fragmentation / stale-vs-current / provenance evidence; bitemporal invalidation semantics for time even without a graph.

### 149. Retrieval-first investment order + numeric sidecar: 20pp retrieval vs 3–8pp write; numbers die first (Grok, R25) — HIGH
3×3 factorial (write strategy × retrieval method, LoCoMo): accuracy varies 20pp across retrieval methods, 3–8pp across write strategies; raw chunks with zero LLM calls matched the expensive pipelines; precision@5 vs accuracy r=0.98. Loss profile: JSON→columnar 56% saved/100% retained and code strip 63%/100% are free; prose summarization saves 65% but keeps 32% of numeric facts (9/28). Safe band ~4–5× at parity (LLMLingua-2 3.1× −0.8pp; HORMA 22% tokens at parity); 30–98× costs 7–12pp. Fix: retrieval/ranking before summarization; lossless lane + numeric sidecar (dates, IDs, amounts verbatim); tiered storage with reversible originals + numeric-consistency monitoring; report accuracy/tokens/latency together on every compression claim.

### 150. ACL-change operations contract: two-clock propagation, filter-first, six-layer detection (Fo, R25) — MEDIUM-HIGH
Baked-in metadata ACLs = inherent stale-permission window (permissions baked at ingestion; source revocation doesn't reach the index). Two clocks: document-ACL sync + group-membership refresh (DataRobot: 30-min principals cron) — the slower defines the effective window; fail-closed on revoke path. Enforcement must be filter-first inside the vector query on every query path (Milvus #50398: hybrid_search bypassed partition-key isolation). Detection contract: egress re-checks, canary documents/tenants, data-plane logging, continuous ACL reconciliation with drift alert, per-path CI conformance, re-tests after every change. Isolation failures are silent — dashboards green, first alarm is a customer email. Rollback = reconciliation (revert delta → drift 0 → canaries clean), not a 36h re-index. Fix: ACL-change chapter of the Phase-3 ops spec.

### 151. Capacity formula: static index + peak working set + fragmentation margin; serialize background jobs (Fo, R25) — MEDIUM-HIGH
Instructive incident: 15M-doc store at 75% RAM died in an oom-killer storm when a 4× QPS surge added ~28GB of query working buffers on top of the static index — size the peak working set, not the index. Adopted constants: ≤70% utilization, 3–5× growth provision, 6–12-month window, 20–30% compute buffer, 30% indexing headroom (verify your own multiplier — pgvector vs PRISM at 100M vectors: 180GB/42h vs 25GB/49min). Rebuild storms are a scheduling problem: cap concurrent background jobs (HNSW optimize, rebalance, compaction), rebalance off-peak, load-before-index for bulk loads. Shard on memory exhaustion (arrives before QPS limits); shard-level utilization alerting; top-K aggregation load-tested at 2–3× with real topology. Quantization = relief valve with recall-verification contract; rebuild time is a budgeted capacity item. Fix: capacity chapter of the Phase-3 ops spec, beside R22's cost modeling.

### 152. Tool Memory tier + selective-reminder policy: reliability stats, failed-call records, versioned schema memory (ChatGPT, R26) — HIGH
Meta's Proactive Memory Agent: separate memory agent tracking failed commands/tool state, reminding selectively — Terminal-Bench 2.0 37.6%→45.9% (+8.3pp), τ2-Bench 55.0%→61.8%; selective reminding beats every-step reminding. Three contents: per-tool reliability stats (success/failure, latency, error types) feeding per-turn filtering; failed-call records retrievable at selection time ("don't repeat this"); schema memory versioned with changed-schema invalidation. Keep both mechanisms: fast decision-model filter shrinks the candidate set cheaply; memory adds learned reliability. Honest bar: no clean isolation of tool-memory benefit on general benchmarks yet — run our own tool-memory on/off ablation on BFCL-style suites first. Fix: Tool Memory tier + reminder-hook design.

### 153. Three-layer conflict resolution: convergence / adjudication / audit, never conflated (ChatGPT, R26) — HIGH
CRDTs prove convergence, not factual correctness — no benchmark compares resolution strategies on memory-truth accuracy anywhere. Convergence layer: CRDT discipline or SERIALIZABLE isolation (Recall demo: SERIALIZABLE aborts the racing agent; READ COMMITTED silently double-commits). Adjudication layer: provenance write-gate ("no source, no write" — FleetMemory: 30/30 adversarial writes blocked at 293ms; unsourced claims slip 6/6 without the rule), contradiction flagging not silent overwrite, precedence rules (user correction > inference; sourced > unsourced; current-scoped > stale-general), adversarial verifier defaulting to reject, every verdict journaled. Audit layer: never destroy overwritten facts (mark invalid, link to replacement); decision journal supporting point-in-time replay. Semantic merges only as derived claims with both sources + rationale. Fix: three-layer update-path spec.

### 154. Retrieval-first escalation ladder for long-context: query-type routing + uncertainty-gated LC (Grok, R26) — HIGH
EDAR (controlled, bootstrap CIs): long-context beats naive RAG ~15.7pp at ~40× latency, but entropy-routed hybrid ties LC (56.9%, CI overlap) at −70.7% tokens, escalating 18.2% of queries — the frontier question is routing policy, not RAG-vs-LC. SurfSense: full-context 58.5–59.6% vs agentic RAG 53.2% at 2–4× the money, 12/15 comparisons not significant. Exchange rate: ~6pp recall for 15× tokens and 12× p95 (R25 mem0 datum). Crossover ~100k tokens, moves with prompt caching (cached LC is RAG-competitive when prefix stable + >20k tokens + reuse >3×/5min TTL). Failure modes structural and complementary (lost-in-the-middle U-curve vs chunking losses). Fix: escalation ladder — point-extraction → retrieval; uncertainty-gated → full-document context; global-synthesis → long-context; full-context baseline with paired bootstrap CIs in every eval.

### 155. Three-tier write pipeline: sync lightweight ack → async seal → async index; consolidation out of the loop (Grok, R26) — MEDIUM-HIGH
VDBBench 1.0 (first streaming vector benchmark): Pinecone held QPS/recall throughout ingestion; Elasticsearch won only after a lengthy optimization phase — elapsed time, not peak throughput, is the metric. Production two-tier visibility: interim index (Milvus temp IVF_FLAT above ~5k-row segments) gives seconds-scale approximate visibility; full-index recall arrives asynchronously on seal. Gap: no agent-memory layer publishes write-to-query latency — all benchmarks query-side only. Backpressure already lives in stores (Milvus 0.85/0.95 water levels); the agent layer ignores it. Fix: (1) sync lightweight write ack into interim-indexed tier, (2) async durable sealing, (3) async index/compaction — consolidation in tier 2/3 never the sync loop; VDBBench-style streaming evaluation (P99 + recall during ingestion); wire store write-protection signals into R19's backpressure contracts; no-interim-index control in eval.

### 156. Backup operations: coordinated snapshots, per-layer RPO tiers, embedding-identity preflight (Fo, R26) — MEDIUM-HIGH
Only coordinated recovery points are valid — object storage + metadata + blob store captured together (Milvus/etcd rule); partial restores are unusable. Streaming memory: coordinated snapshot (30s ingestion pause) + stream replay from checkpoint marker; PITR depth = stream retention. Verification is the real product: fingerprint-verified restores to isolated destinations, dry-run PITR checks, quarterly drills where a failed drill is a P1. Transfers: RPO tiered per memory layer (working checkpoint-only, long-term deep); embedding identity pinned as restore preflight (model change ⇒ explicit re-embed, never silent reuse); backup buckets as exfiltration surface (separate IAM, object lock, access logging). Fix: backup chapter of the Phase-3 ops spec — complements R7's restore-drill validation.

### 157. Network security: private-everything posture; exposed vector endpoint = P1 with unknowable exfiltration (Fo, R26) — MEDIUM
Measured pattern: internet-exposed search ports with no auth — one scan found ~30 open vector DBs with PII/medical data. Worse for vectors: silent tampering (planted content the LLM ingests) + embedding inversion (R18/R25) — leaked embeddings are as readable as source text; "no evidence of misuse" is not evidence. Posture: private subnets; VPC endpoints/PrivateLink/Private Service Connect for managed memory and embedding calls; TLS 1.2+ at edge with service-mesh mTLS on sensitive scopes; rotation calendar (certs, KMS keys, secrets); exposure-detection fixtures (external surface scans, CI config assertions, data-plane connection logging). Fix: network-security chapter of the Phase-3 ops spec — extends R25's access-control chapter with the network layer.

### 158. Deep-research memory: planner-prior routing, process memory, token-budgeted handoffs (Grok, R27) — HIGH
MIA: memory as planner prior gains +4.15pp text-only; the same memory fed to the executor hurts (−0.4pp) — memory consumption is a routing decision. Buffer holds compressed workflow summaries (trajectories, failed attempts, plans), hybrid scoring (semantic + value + frequency); ablation ladder 11.7 → 31.1 GAIA; 7B executor with MIA beat its 32B counterpart ~18%. LongMemEval-V2: whole-file runbooks + coding agent 74.9%/108s beat chunked RAG 51.0%/0.2s (~350–600× latency); naive retrieval memory can be net-negative. Provenance schema-mandatory (SOURCED_FROM edges, confirmation counts, exponential decay, scheduled prune()). Cost bound: token budgets at every boundary (6000-token scratchpad, 800-token handoff, artifact-store-by-handle) with observable compression events. Negative result: ranked recall won, the oracle didn't saturate (use, not retrieval, is the binding constraint); memory is pure cost when the task fits in context. Fix: Manager-Planner-Executor split; planner-prior routing; accuracy–latency frontier as the reporting discipline.

### 159. Federated memory: local-first + signed-edge consent; three architectures, phase-transition economics (ChatGPT, R27) — HIGH
Three tiers: local-first with selective replication (most practical), P2P/append-only substrates, federated protocols with independent operators; DID/UCAN layered orthogonally. Consent as signed revocable edges (Hive demo: revoke effective on next read, audit trail) — revocation is best-effort (cannot erase retained plaintext). Stigmergy paper: +68.7% individual-memory gain; shared traces beat private memory only above critical density ρ≈0.20 — shared infrastructure pays only above a participation threshold. "Decentralized" ≠ "private" (Deep Leakage from Gradients): embeddings, metadata, retained copies leak even when raw records stay local. Fix: local-first encrypted store + UCAN-style scoped capabilities; revocation honored on next read, communicated as best-effort; collective-memory investment gated on interaction density; explicit threat model per design.

### 160. Tiering with measured demotion: multiplicative gates, query-time decay, probe-verified warm→cold (Grok, R27) — HIGH
Score = access-frequency EMA × Ebbinghaus decay (computed at query time — demotion never writes) × recency boost × impact score; impact orthogonal to recency (200-day-old impact-0.9 stays warm; 30-day-old impact-0.2 is cold). mak372's probe-verified demotion: answer probe question with/without the chunk, similarity ≥ threshold → demote — 84.7% token savings at 100% recall. Measured payoff is token-cost (60–80% context reduction at 0.25–0.35×), not latency. MemGPT failure modes: premature eviction (latent constraint loss), failed recall (silent degradation), per-agent divergence. Cold-tier surprise: plain files beat specialized libraries on LoCoMo (74.0%, second-hand) — cold design variable is chunk index vs files+manifest. Fix: multiplicative gates; probe-test for high-stakes demotions; cold queryable, never deleted; track tier hit rate + demotion-regret rate; tiering goal 60–80% reduction at ~0.3× cost with a regret budget.

### 161. Voice memory: three lifetimes + speech presentation layer (ChatGPT, R27) — MEDIUM-HIGH
Three functions: turn-taking state (streaming, ~200ms regime), conversation memory (facts/summaries across sessions), paralinguistic memory (prosody — unverified). Practitioner pattern: separate retrieval logic per memory type (JARVIS's three ChromaDB collections: knowledge vs conversation history vs documents). Voice-specific surface: presentation policy at the output boundary — retrieved memory must be condensed for speech (HF support agent's voice-summary layer; voicebot's "answer the way a voice should sound"). Token-budgeted history with summarization/compaction as eviction (FastRTC). Honest gaps: no end-to-end spoken-agent benchmark; latency figures measure timing, not memory quality; prosody/disfluency-repair persistence are research hypotheses, not design choices. Fix: three-lifetime model; per-type retrieval policies; speech presentation layer; prosody claims gated behind dedicated studies.

### 162. Change-management chapter: parallel-generation release, per-type review gates, back-out on every RFC (Fo, R27) — MEDIUM-HIGH
Production pattern: build candidate generation from source checkpoint while current serves → reconcile deletions in both → version the query path (encoder + preprocessing + metric) as one release → switch → retain old generation for rollback window. Four operation types with different review gates: index rebuild / embedding migration / chunking migration / permission update. Embedding changes promote only on held-out eval deltas (silent relevance collapse is the failure mode). Rollback eligibility is a fresh decision — gated on authorization-freshness, defaulting to retrieval-disabled. Incident law: skip pre-deploy checks and the migration becomes the incident. Change-freeze needs named window + owner + exception criteria (freeze ≠ resilience). Fix: change-management chapter of the Phase-3 ops spec — complements R24's upgrade-operations contract.

### 163. API evolution chapter: machine-readable deprecation timeline; retrieval behavior is breaking (Fo, R27) — MEDIUM
Deprecation for agent clients (never read changelogs) must be machine-readable: Deprecation/Sunset/Link headers + OpenAPI deprecated flags. Lifecycle: instrument callers → announce → telemetry-driven holdout outreach (exit criterion is usage, not calendar) → brownout/soft-shutdown ramp → 410 Gone with successor link. Windows: 4–8 weeks internal, 6–12 months partners, 12+ months public/embedded. Breaking-change taxonomies must cover retrieval behavior (chunking, scoring, defaults) — Weaviate v3→v4 incompatibility, Pinecone's date-versioned 2026-07 index-model break, pinecone-client rename. Strategy: never break a published version; parallel versions behind adapters; version the contract, not the implementation. Fix: API-evolution chapter of the Phase-3 ops spec.

## Ideas 164–169 — Partner watch pipeline (round 28, 6 analyses, 2026-10-17)

Ranked by build relevance. Sources: `hidden_files/research/watch-log/166-*.md` through `171-*.md` + ROUND-28-SYNTHESIS.md. ChatGPT consulted directly; Grok/Fo analyses research-derived (OpenRouter credits exhausted; no live browser in scope).

### 164. Memory distillation pipeline: episodic store → rehearsal-generated consolidation → FFN channels; sequential-edit acceptance (Grok, R28) — HIGH
Cortex: prospective rehearsal (model distills its own context-conditioned outputs) + FFN-only updates — 88.9% of context-induced gains recovered after 50 sequential factual edits on 14B, 99.8% non-target performance retained; Doc2LoRA collapsed to 24% on batch consolidation. Three flavors: structural distillation (11× token reduction, 96.8% query vocabulary retained — but only 27% of high-IDF rarities: query-serving, never evidence of record), hierarchical teacher-memory for small agents (AppWorld 16.07%→41.07%), PMD procedural self-distillation (+3.8–13.6%; co-evolution required — memory that never lands in weights is weaker). Boundary: ephemeral state → flat files/KV (zero compute); durable capabilities → weights (re-reading 50KB prompts every call is "a dead end"). Converges with R27's MIA +TTL. Fix: consolidation pipeline with sequential-edit consolidation rate as the acceptance metric; lossless evidence tier stays mandatory.

### 165. Eval composition for the controller: no single benchmark suffices — MAB + oracle diagnostics + MemBench + priced operating points (Grok, R28) — HIGH
LoCoMo is in crisis: Penfield audit found ~99 wrong answers (100% mathematically impossible), the LLM judge scores up to 63% of intentionally wrong answers correct, cross-paper scores mutually disputed — any claim grounded only in LoCoMo QA accuracy is not evidence; prefer session-level R@K or MAB exact-match/F1. Landscape: MemBench (read/write, capacity cliffs), MemoryAgentBench (734 questions, four competencies; multi-hop 28.0%→10.0% as context 6K→32K — a composition failure), EverMemBench oracle-evidence (retrieval-vs-reading attribution), STALE (forgetting — perpetually neglected), AMB meta-benchmark. Cost/latency rarely reported with accuracy (LME-V2's priced table is the exception). Fix: compose — MAB competencies + oracle diagnostics + MemBench efficiency + LME-V2 accuracy–latency operating points + cost axis on every measurement; synthetic suites labeled diagnostic until transfer measured (Idea 167).

### 166. Consent as a versioned state machine: pause-creation / stop-use / delete-item / delete-all as four intents (ChatGPT, R28) — HIGH
Claude + ChatGPT controls converge: "off" ≠ "deleted"; chat-deletion ≠ memory-deletion; pause vs reset (only one reversible). Readable, editable memory lists are the trust surface — reading is where users catch wrong items shaping outputs. Re-creation loop: "forget this" needs a suppression marker (remember-not-to-forget), disclosed as stored data. Deletion is distributed: copies in embeddings, caches, backups, derived summaries, downstream agents — per-store receipts, retry on failure, stated retention exceptions; a single success toast is the dishonest pattern. Honest ceiling: no public measurements of control usage or trust effects exist — measure discovery, correction success, deletion latency, failed downstream deletions, comprehension ourselves. Fix: five-operation consent API (inspect / correct-verified / delete with receipts / pause creation-vs-use / withdraw) + suppression markers.

### 167. Synthetic benchmark validity: structure-first recipe + transfer gate before deployment claims (ChatGPT, R28) — HIGH
Canonical recipe: event graph → sessionized dialogue with indirect evidence revelation → QA → human verification (LongMemEval: all 500 seed questions manually rewritten; ~30% commercial-assistant accuracy decay as conversations stretch). Honest headline: no published study shows synthetic memory-benchmark scores predict real-user performance — leaderboard percentages are capability figures, not validity scores. Coverage ≠ representativeness: LoCoMo's 1,986 questions rest on ~10 conversations — report independent histories, grouped by history. Locomo-Plus gap: factual-recall corpora miss the behavioral-constraint channel (implicit information, inferred goals). Fix: hybrid corpus (synthetic breadth + private consented never-trained-on real set); transfer check as a gate (synthetic-vs-real side by side; non-transferring suite labeled diagnostic); behavioral-constraint items beyond factual QA.

### 168. Compliance chapter: audit-log-as-artifact from day one; deletion SLA + copy inventory as ship gates (Fo, R28) — MEDIUM-HIGH
Auditors map memory stores to SOC 2 CC6/CC7/CC8 + Privacy: access-review sign-offs, alert response records, vuln scans with remediation tracking, change tickets, DSR logs. Type II evidence must be contemporaneous/attributable/continuous — cannot be reconstructed at period end. Vector-specific ops: CDC-driven tombstoning + source-doc→chunk lineage registry for GDPR erasure; reconciliation scope includes dormant tenants. Procurement blockers: published deletion SLA (days) + copy inventory with stated boundaries. Remediated exceptions are expected artifacts, not failures — log with retro-attestation. Fix: compliance chapter of the Phase-3 ops spec — feeds R24's ErasureCase workflow with the evidence pipeline.

### 169. Secrets chapter: full-surface register, dual-key rotation, ordered leak runbook (Fo, R28) — MEDIUM-HIGH
Secrets register wider than the DB key: embedding-provider keys (highest cost-risk surface), vector-DB credentials, KMS handles, third-party API keys. Cadence: 30-day API keys / 90-day standing credentials / master keys under supervised ceremony only. Zero-downtime rotation: dual-key acceptance, ~7-day overlap, dynamic secret reads, per-consumer restart map. Leak runbook ordering (non-negotiable): revoke at issuer → invalidate caches → rotate entire leaked surface → forensics by key_id → written notifiability decision (30-min containment target). Traps: rotating an encryption key before disconnecting dependents destroys revocation capability; agent-generated diffs are the new leak front door (pre-commit scanning as a control); prefer managed identity over long-lived secrets. Fix: secrets chapter of the Phase-3 ops spec — complements R23's DEK/KEK rotation.

## Ideas 170–175 — Partner watch pipeline (round 29, 6 analyses, 2026-10-17)

Ranked by build relevance. Sources: `hidden_files/research/watch-log/172-*.md` through `177-*.md` + ROUND-29-SYNTHESIS.md. ChatGPT consulted directly; Grok/Fo analyses research-derived (OpenRouter credits exhausted; no live browser in scope).

### 170. Injection defense at the request boundary: retrieval-time scanning + provenance tags + policy-evaluated tool calls (ChatGPT, R29) — HIGH
The model cannot structurally separate trusted instructions from retrieved content — the defense lives upstream of the model: scan recalled memories at retrieval time (block/strip/warn + decision logged); tag every recalled memory (source, id, timestamp, trust tier) and carry provenance into generation and the policy layer; evaluate tool proposals against provenance (block calls from untrusted-tagged content); response scanning before delivery. Closest measured mechanism: KFS-RAG's sanitized-evidence substitution (keyword-grounded facts replacing raw retrieved text via causal keyword validation). Load-bearing layers: code-enforced authorization + human gate on irreversible actions — filters/prompts alone never hold. Honest ceiling: no apples-to-apples residual ASRs exist for retrieved-memory injection; any ASR quoted must name benchmark, model, attack set, config. Fix: retrieval-path defense design + audit record schema (source, signature, decision, outcome).

### 171. Temporal reasoning layer: write-time enrichment + additive rerank + tri-temporal supersession (ChatGPT, R29) — HIGH
Mem0's shipped pattern: time signatures at write time (separate enrichment pass; event date, status, precision, type), query-time temporal-intent classification with no read-path LLM call, temporal scoring layered additively (imprecise dates never silently dropped) — LoCoMo 86.1%→92.5%, LongMemEval 90.4%→94.4% at top_200, multi-session +11.2pts, ~+1ms median (vendor figures — replicate before claiming). Storage: tri-temporal model (valid/known/system time) with supersession chains — retiring a belief sets valid_until with provenance, never overwritten; was_valid_at(t)/as_of as mechanical primitives. Retrieval alone fails temporal selection (GPT-4o 60.2% full history vs 40.1% basic retrieval); summaries silently discard temporal facts (84.7% recall but 32.0 vs 43.3 F1). Fix: three-piece temporal layer (enrichment with state keys → intent classification + additive rerank → time-travel primitives); evaluate via Mem0's open framework.

### 172. Late-interaction retrieval stack: single-vector recall → MaxSim rerank with hard latency budget (Grok, R29) — HIGH
ColBERT re-ranking matches cross-encoder MRR@10 (34.9 vs 34.7) at 61ms vs 10,700ms (~175×). Honest comparator: TCT-ColBERT distilled bi-encoder + BM25 hybrid reaches 0.364 MRR@10 at 106ms end-to-end, beating multi-stage ColBERT's 0.360 at 458ms in-domain. PLAID makes late interaction CPU-viable (6.8× GPU / 45× CPU at parity, 38ms GPU); MUVERA reduces multi-vector to single-vector MIPS (10% better recall, 90% lower latency than PLAID on BEIR); 2026 fused kernels 18–51× over fast-plaid. Fix: retrieval stack = single-vector recall → MaxSim rerank under a hard latency budget; distill the fast path from the precise path's judgments; PLAID-class indexing for CPU-served deployments.

### 173. Encryption-at-rest posture: delegate to storage; field-level client-side for evidentiary content (Grok, R29) — MEDIUM-HIGH
No vector DB encrypts at the application level — Weaviate's checklist delegates to encrypted storage (EBS/S3 + KMS). Measured overhead: 2–5% sequential I/O with AES-NI (~4.7 GB/s Xeon); 20–30% only without hardware acceleration. SSD gotcha: dm-crypt workqueues (persistent no_read/write_workqueue flags, measured 2× throughput). Production pattern: AES-256-GCM on content payloads client-side (<1ms per retrieval, zero search overhead), vectors/metadata in clear — encryption on the searchable substrate buys nothing and costs query capability. Fix: provider-encrypted disks + customer-held key for evidentiary fields; searchable substrate in clear.

### 174. Audit-logging operations: three-layer schema, tamper-evidence pipeline, reconstruction set (Fo, R29) — MEDIUM-HIGH
Three layers: API ops (allow/deny), retrieval forensics (vector IDs, similarity scores, chunk extraction, memory snapshots), LLM-gateway query/response hash pairs — vendors sell layer 1; layers 2–3 are your own code. Tamper-evidence: write-only off-host streaming + chain-hashed, rotation-frozen records with flooding protections. Retention constants: ≥90 days hot searchable, 1-year warm, 7-year cold WORM. SIEM = real-time streaming with ingest verification, not batch upload. Investigations need the reconstruction set (prompts, chunks, config, tool calls, permissions, before/after snapshots, synced clocks) — with the honest limit that logs can't guarantee replay of stochastic LLM behavior. Fix: audit-logging chapter of the Phase-3 ops spec; consumes R26's decision-journal pattern.

### 175. Performance-tuning runbook: measurement procedure, one-way build params, filtered-search hazard (Fo, R29) — MEDIUM
Procedure not constants: exact-scan ground truth on real queries → single-variable ef_search/nprobe sweeps → recall@k-vs-p95 elbow → declared recall target (≥0.95) → quarterly re-measurement. Build params (M, ef_construction, distance metric) are one-way doors (rebuild required); ef_search is the live lever. Measured: ef 10→100 takes recall@10 ~85%→98+%; int8 ≈ 4× memory, ~2% recall loss, ~1.5× faster; hybrid +13–17pt recall@10 for single-digit ms; one IVF-PQ migration: 96GB→3.8GB, P99 3.4ms at 98.9% recall. Filtered search needs its own runbook (partition → iterative scan → filter-aware planning → beam scaled by selectivity) — post-filtering silently destroys per-tenant recall. Quantization + over-fetch/rerank usually beats knob-turning. Fix: tuning chapter of the Phase-3 ops spec; quarterly re-tuning on the R17 ops calendar.

## Ideas 176–181 — Partner watch pipeline (round 30, 6 analyses, 2026-10-17)

Ranked by build relevance. Sources: `hidden_files/research/watch-log/178-*.md` through `183-*.md` + ROUND-30-SYNTHESIS.md. ChatGPT consulted directly; Grok/Fo analyses research-derived (OpenRouter credits exhausted; no live browser in scope).

### 176. Read-path salience: multiplicative fusion + dumb write path + abstention SLO (Grok, R30) — HIGH
Retrieval method is worth ~20 points of LoCoMo accuracy (57.1%→77.2%), write-time importance pipelines only 3–8; raw chunks (zero LLM calls) match or beat expensive write-time extraction/summarization. Multiplicative fusion of global salience × contextual consistency beats additive (Chain-of-Memory: 76.40 vs 72.55 on LongMemEval). Recency handles ~96% of real queries (RealCompanion: 3.4% of real messages need out-of-thread memory) — salience scoring is optimized for distant probes only, where recency collapses (2.2%) and BM25 (24.8%) beats it. The abstention half: 10 injected unselected messages push misfire rate 0%→60.8% — the measurable win is *withholding* low-confidence retrievals. GA's α=β=γ=1.0 was a guess, never tuned. Fix: write path stores raw chunks (0 LLM calls); retrieval = multiplicative recency-decayed-importance × relevance; misfire-rate SLO on no-need probes.

### 177. Append-only continual learner: frozen weights + validity windows + per-lane decay (Grok, R30) — HIGH
System-level forgetting is retrieval degradation, not weight drift: GPT-4o drops 30.3% (0.870 oracle → 0.606 full history) on LongMemEval-S. Parametric lifelong learning is a negative result — ROME collapses from n=32 edits, MEMIT caps at thousands, FT-W at 10k edits causes complete generation failure. Design law: frozen base + append-only evidence store = zero forgetting by construction; three accumulation lanes (episodic facts with validity windows + contradiction detection; procedural skills — multi-model traces hit 73.1% cross-model accuracy, refinement rounds +3.7–6.7 pts; beliefs mutable only via supersession-with-audit-trail). Practitioner half-lives: 72h episodic / 30d semantic. ARC-AGI-3 isolation rule: discard beliefs, never evidence. Fix: three-lane store + per-lane decay + five LongMemEval-ability breakdown per release, with misfire number.

### 178. Utility-weighted pruning as audited operations: TTL tiers + recall-driven eviction + contradiction reconciliation (ChatGPT, R30) — HIGH
No controlled pruning-vs-accuracy curve exists — so pruning is deliberate, reversible, audited, not ambient decay. Policy menu: (a) TTL expiration tiers for transient state; (b) utility-weighted eviction — track recalls per memory, score by recall frequency × verification status decaying with disuse, soft-archive the useless tail (reversible, git-audited), human review for borderline cases; never auto-delete verified or user-scoped memories; (c) contradiction reconciliation — new conflicting fact deprecates the old record with an audit delta (belief coherence, not space saving); (d) atomic right-to-be-forgotten across document store, relational DB, and vector index. Summaries are lossy pruning of provenance — keep the raw record retrievable. Vendor headline figures (Mem0 LOCOMO, disputed by Letta/Zep) compare architectures, not pruning rules — quote with both sides. Fix: explicit pruning subsystem in the Phase-3 controller with accuracy-vs-memory-budget reporting.

### 179. Two-pool experience store: bounded inference-time lessons + tagged trajectory pool for train-time (ChatGPT, R30) — MEDIUM-HIGH
Two kinds of replay with different evidence. Inference-time lesson retrieval: Reflexion (episodic +6%, verbal reflection +8% more; CoT 33%→53%, ReAct 39%→58% on HotPotQA) — bounded replay of distilled lessons (last-3 pattern) beats raw-trajectory storage; ExpeL's ablation proves insight extraction × similarity retrieval are individually necessary and synergistic, with cross-task transfer. Train-time trajectory reuse: STaR (GSM8K 5.5%→72.5%), Agent Q (booking success 18.6%→81.7%) — full-pipeline results, not replay-buffer ablations. LoCoMo warns: summaries keep 84.7% recall but drop 43.3→32.0 F1 — distillation must preserve reasoning-needed facts. **Gap flag:** prioritized replay has zero credible language-agent measurement — tag episodes with outcome, verifier signal, and surprise/error magnitude so we can evaluate prioritized vs uniform sampling ourselves. Fix: lesson pool (distilled, similarity-retrievable, bounded) + trajectory pool (full episodes, quality-filtered, for later fine-tuning).

### 180. Vendor-exit runbook: two primitives, parallel-run validation, re-embed fork decided at selection (Fo, R30) — MEDIUM-HIGH
Only two real exit primitives: vendor snapshots (recovery-within-vendor, not portable) and the (id, vector, payload) paginated scroll (Pinecone has no export — ~3h for 52M vectors; vec2pg reference rates 700–1100/s Pinecone, 900–2500/s Qdrant). Three failure modes: no vector export (Dust case — rebuild from scratch), metadata loss (scroll must fetch with_vectors + with_payload), metric/index drift (HNSW→PRISM changes recall — re-validate golden-set recall at parity). Five phases: export → load → parallel run → three-phase output-parity validation (path alignment, output cosine similarity vs production logs, latency within SLA) → cutover with rollback; the parallel window is sized by query-volume coverage, not the calendar. Re-embed vs carry-vectors fork decided at selection time — the re-embed path requires keeping the source corpus as a first-class artifact (feeds R24). Lock-in screen at selection: "can I export my embeddings?" Contract at the verbs level (insert/update/delete, filtered k-NN with recall contract, snapshot/export) + per-vendor behavior config — not a thin API adapter. pgvector-shaped tiers get portability free (pg_dump/PITR). Fix: exit chapter of the Phase-3 ops spec; exercise the exit path before production load.

### 181. Six-scenario load-test production gate + recall golden-set monitor (Fo, R30) — MEDIUM
Vendor benchmarks cover at most two scenarios; the production gate runs six: (a) concurrent filtered search at peak (50–100 clients, P95/P99 — 3× P50→P99 degradation rule signals concurrency failure; Reddit's 340M-vector case showed 10× P99 spikes single-client tests missed); (b) write+read simultaneity (read-latency spikes proportional to write volume catch re-index contention); (c) recall at actual data scale; (d) 2× data oversize failure-mode characterization; (e) cold-start (first 1,000 queries — index-load 1.2–2.3s on Milvus/Weaviate); (f) binary-search breaking point at ≤1% error rate (Locust + Little's Law). Workload from production retrieval logs (1,000+ queries, 80/15/5 distribution, drift-refreshed) with the caching trap guarded by measured cache-miss rate. Cost-per-billion-queries at fixed recall ($84–$7,088, 84× spread) is the capacity-planning metric. Recall gets a production monitor: golden set of 100–500 queries per tenant, approximate-vs-brute-force recall@k on schedule, re-run after every reindex/model-change/parameter-edit (also the migration-validation gate). Cadence: smoke per deploy, nightly baseline, weekly 2× stress, monthly soak, quarterly chaos; 5-min minimum per reported metric. Fix: load-testing chapter of the Phase-3 ops spec; index-lifecycle SLOs (build time, cold start, sustained writes) on the ops dashboard.

## Ideas 182–187 — Partner watch pipeline (round 31, 6 analyses, 2026-10-17)

Ranked by build relevance. Sources: `hidden_files/research/watch-log/184-*.md` through `189-*.md` + ROUND-31-SYNTHESIS.md. ChatGPT consulted directly; Grok/Fo analyses research-derived (OpenRouter credits exhausted; no live browser in scope).

### 182. Continuity-impact measurement doctrine: presence >> design; sequence-level metrics + random/recency controls (Grok, R31) — HIGH
The cleanest ladder (MemDelta, paired n=500): No-Memory 2.2% vs RAG 47.2% (+45pp, p<.001) vs full context 49.8% — memory's presence dwarfs its design (~2.6pp between RAG and full-context). Beyond presence, the real levers are *which* memories (task-similarity +16.5pp over random, ExpeL) and *breadth* (cross-task vs single-task; MemRL gains vanish when intra-dataset similarity is low). Per-task metrics under-measure memory: altk-evolve scenario-goal +14.3pp vs task-goal +3.6pp, Hard tier more than doubled; memory's payoff compounds. Anchor: WorldModelMCP +10.2pp (67.3%→77.6%, +15.0pp within-domain, +6.9pp cross-domain, zero regressions, preregistered). Cognaptus latest-only ablation: recency-only looks fine on current reads (96/96 tie) and collapses post-reveal (32/96 vs 96/96). Fix: W7 gate suite includes scenario/episode-level success metrics, random-retrieval and recency-only controls, MemDelta statistics (paired, bootstrap CIs, McNemar), retrieval-density logging for the inverted-U test.

### 183. Vendor-telemetry discount rule: LoCoMo key ~6.4% wrong; no 2026 headline independently replicated (Grok, R31) — HIGH
Every 2026 vendor headline is vendor-claimed, disputed, or audit-discounted. Mem0 V3 (LoCoMo 92.5, LongMemEval 94.4, −90% tokens/−91% latency) carries its README's own caveat: scores reflect the managed platform, not OSS; the graph variant was removed from OSS (~4k lines). Zep↔Mem0 LoCoMo dispute (84% / 58.44% / 75.14%) unresolved; 2026 Zep rows self-reported. Letta's strongest data point (74% LoCoMo-with-grep, third-party-cited) cuts *against* extraction memory. Penfield Labs Apr 2026 audit (non-peer-reviewed, unrefuted): 6.4% of LoCoMo's key is wrong, LLM judge accepts ~63% of intentionally wrong answers. New entrants (Hindsight 91.4%, MemMachine 93%, Honcho 90.4%) are single-vendor claims. Fix: no vendor number adopted as a target — independent harness with fixed answer model/judge/retrieval budget, W7 paired-bootstrap reporting, 6.4% LoCoMo key-error discount; construction cost ($/kJ/wall-clock) reported alongside retrieval latency (arXiv 2606.06448: construction dominates energy, 26.7× spread).

### 184. Record schema as governance contract: status lifecycle + filter-before-rank (ChatGPT, R31) — HIGH
No standard schema exists; no ablation isolates any single field's retrieval effect. Every practitioner schema converges on the same governance core: scope/owner, source/provenance, status (candidate | active | superseded | quarantined | deleted), sensitivity, validity timestamps, correction path. Temporal fields are the only choice with credible evidence nearby: Graphiti's bi-temporal model (~18.5% temporal-retrieval gains — whole-architecture result). Confidence/importance are application-specific hypotheses, not standards — store only with a defined consumer. Fix: controller record = id; scope; kind (preference | fact | procedure | episode | pointer); content; source; status; sensitivity + allowed_for (consumption gates); temporal quartet (event_at, recorded_at, valid_until, last_verified_at); supersedes (never overwrite); retrieval filters by scope/kind/status/validity before semantic ranking; memory never grants permissions; new extractions land as `candidate`.

### 185. Three-mode curation subsystem: in/on/out-of-loop per action + measured review KPIs (ChatGPT, R31) — MEDIUM-HIGH
Review UIs exist everywhere (ChatGPT/Gemini/Claude panels, LangGraph write gates, grudge's human-gated lesson queue, openmallab's confidence-gated review) — but no published controlled result shows human curation improves memory quality; that gap is the finding. Design: per-action oversight modes — synchronous approval for high-risk writes (identity, scope, permissions, contradiction of verified facts), async on-the-loop sampling + alerts for routine, out-of-the-loop for deterministic sweeps; evidence-forward review UI (claim next to source, verifier uncertainty highlighted); seeded known-errors to catch rubber-stamping; random sample of auto-approved items kept in the review stream; promote recurring corrections to conventions only after recurrence (3×). Fix: curation subsystem in the Phase-3 controller with escape rate, seeded-error catch rate, and routing accuracy tracked from launch — first-party evidence nobody else has; human verdicts stored as labeled data for the write-confidence model.

### 186. Resharding runbook: online double-write + checksum gate + per-shard coverage metric (Fo, R31) — MEDIUM
Shard-key choice dominates operability: tenant-key custom sharding (Qdrant shard keys, Weaviate tenant shards, Pinecone namespaces) buys routing precision + compliance isolation at the cost of accepting skew. Two hot-shard kinds, two responses: monotonic-key hotspots (fix via hash distribution/key design) vs single-hot-key skew (no redistribution fixes it — empirical 14.6%→8.3% via bucketing `key % 16` at scatter-read cost). Resharding is the highest-risk operation: clone → double-write → checksum gate → gradual read migration (1%→100%) → cutover with stated cutover criterion and abort path. The vector-specific hazard: a fan-out query missing a migrating shard returns a wrong top-k, not an error — track "all shards answered" as a recall health metric. Escalation ladder: rebalance → dedicated shard → key bucketing. Fix: sharding-operations chapter of the Phase-3 ops spec; default shard-count policy at collection creation (retrofitting costs a reshard); per-shard rate-limited bulk ops (Slack-2022 OOM pattern).

### 187. Analytics-export pipeline: CDC on the write path; stream metadata, batch embeddings (Fo, R31) — MEDIUM
Dedicated vector DBs expose no CDC feed — export attaches to the authoritative write path/source of truth, never scrapes the vector store (or deletes/corrections vanish silently). pgvector CDC is production-feasible: Postgres logical replication + Debezium (Confluent V2 connector supports pgVector columns). Two patterns: streaming CDC (Debezium→Kafka→warehouse) for metadata/change events — what was forgotten/edited, when; scheduled batch (Airbyte-style) for embeddings. PII control = Postgres 16+ filtered publications (column/row exclusion, reviewed like access policy); embedding-model version + dims as first-class export columns with a backfill procedure on model change; page before `max_slot_wal_keep_size` forces re-snapshot; idempotent sinks + hard-delete capture + delete-heavy acceptance test; append-only raw staging doubles as the memory-audit trail; heavy analytics (drift, quality audits) runs offline against the export copy, outside serving SLOs. Fix: analytics-export chapter of the Phase-3 ops spec.

## Ideas 188–193 — Partner watch pipeline (round 32, 6 analyses, 2026-10-17)

Ranked by build relevance. Sources: `hidden_files/research/watch-log/190-*.md` through `195-*.md` + ROUND-32-SYNTHESIS.md. ChatGPT consulted directly; Grok/Fo analyses research-derived (OpenRouter credits exhausted; no live browser in scope).

### 188. Inversion-grade threat model: plaintext embeddings = plaintext documents (Grok, R32) — HIGH
Measured attacks: Vec2Text ~92% exact reconstruction of 32-token inputs; ZSInvert (2025) ~50–62% token F1 zero-shot across encoders, surviving σ=0.01 DP noise (only utility-destroying σ=0.1 stops it — noise is not a practical defense); Zero2Text (2026) attacks black-box embedding APIs at 1.8× ROUGE-L / 6.4× BLEU-2 over prior SOTA. Backdoored RAG fine-tuning: 79.7–94.1% verbatim extraction of stored documents. PrivacyBench: ~15.8% average secret leakage (up to 26.6%), retrieval surfacing secret docs 62.8% of the time — the burden falls on the generator. Fix: encrypt embeddings at rest and during serving; engine-level row security *before* retrieval (never post-retrieval filtering); frozen generator with explicit retrieval context; vector backups classified at source-document sensitivity; encoder rotation retired as a control against zero-shot inversion; vector-store reads logged and rate-limited like database reads.

### 189. Calibrated abstention gate: multi-signal + conformal thresholds + reader-level eval (Grok, R32) — HIGH
Single retrieval-confidence scores cannot separate answerable from unanswerable: measured overlap band 0.31–0.59; τ=0.35 lets 17/35 unanswerable through, τ=0.50 hands off half of answerable questions. On identical retrieval, readers ranged 93.3% vs 56.7% correct abstention (LongMemEval) — abstention is a reader property, evaluated separately. Eye-balled thresholds miss their promised error rate in 34–54% of data splits; RC-RAG measures the price: ~15% risk costs 25–45% abstention coverage. A calibrated multi-signal gate cuts confident-wrong 42.3%→17.6% (ECE 0.033). Statistical and verbalized uncertainty are poorly correlated — never gate on stated confidence. Fix: learn g(x) from pipeline signals, set τ by conformal selective prediction, track misfire and miss separately, report risk–coverage curves; plan for the coverage cost as the price of reliability, not a tuning failure.

### 190. Access-first interop: stable MCP tool contract + versioned behavior-preserving export (ChatGPT, R32) — HIGH
MCP standardizes the wire (tools/resources/prompts discovery), not the memory — "MCP-compatible tells you the transport, not the memory format." Six open gaps: record schema, retrieval semantics, conflict resolution, provenance/identity, lifecycle/deletion policy, export/migration. Implementations (official server-memory, OpenMemory, Zep/Graphiti, Supermemory, SuperLocalMemory, mcp-memory-service) are all MCP-callable and mutually non-portable; LangGraph Store/checkpoints are within-framework persistence, not interchange; A2A/Agent Protocol don't cover memory either. Fix: ship a stable MCP tool contract (write/read/search/update/delete with tenant+provenance fields) with documented semantics on all six gaps; define a versioned export format (records + activation history + conflict policy) — no product currently does behavior-preserving export, a genuine contribution; adopt the one-memory-many-clients deployment pattern.

### 191. Activation-triad scoring + three-store split + soft-forget (ChatGPT, R32) — MEDIUM-HIGH
Cognitive-architecture transfer, licensed not literal: ACT-R's retrieval-score formula (base-level recency×frequency + spreading context activation + threshold) as the controller's scoring function; Soar's working/semantic/episodic split with episodic snapshots as compact state→action→outcome traces; Soar's forgetting experiments (Derbinsky AGI talk): principled forgetting beat no-forgetting (latency budget blown within an hour) and hand-tuned cleanup. Forgetting = loss of accessibility, not deletion — soft-forget drops low-activation memories from the retrieval pool but keeps them recoverable. CLARION adds the metacognitive watchdog (escalate on retrieval failure or repeated mistakes) and impasse→chunking maps to the failure→procedure-cache loop. Caveat: reconstruction fallback is harder for LLMs than for Soar — provenance-backed soft-delete, not true forgetting; ACT-R decay parameters are human-fit priors, validate empirically. Fix: activation scoring + retrieval threshold + three-store schema + metacognitive watchdog in the Phase-3 controller.

### 192. Tenant-offboarding runbook: inventory-first, verified-zero, tombstoned namespace (Fo, R32) — MEDIUM
Offboarding fails at the deletion inventory, not execution: relational rows (incl. soft-deletes), vector embeddings + snapshots, object versions/backups, embedding-keyed semantic caches (invisible to tenant_id scans), logs/traces, eval sets, fine-tuned adapters (cannot be partially deleted — retire or retrain), warehouse copies. Derived data is the dominant resurrection risk. Runbook: freeze + revoke credentials first → delete per store → handle derived copies → verification battery (zero row counts, orphan-embedding index scan, cache-miss probes, negative read probes, sample restore test, vendor destruction reports reconciled) → certificate with stated scope *and* exceptions. A later restore must not resurrect the tenant — tombstone the namespace and make every restore pipeline check it. Fix: tenant-offboarding chapter of the Phase-3 ops spec with the canonical copy-inventory template.

### 193. Cold-archive operations: design around the restore (Fo, R32) — MEDIUM
Expedited restore (1–5 min) costs an order of magnitude more than Bulk (5–12h; Deep Archive up to 48h); restores incur dual storage charges during the window — tier-approval matrix (Bulk default, data-owner approval for Standard) with bounded windows and automatic re-cooling. Verification = fixity: golden hashes in an immutable log + scheduled checksum scrubbing + manifest reconciliation + quarterly restore drills into isolated namespaces. Lifecycle policies fail most often on prefix mismatch; expiration forbidden on regulated data (Object Lock). Memory-specific failure: archived embeddings tied to a retired model are unreadable-in-effect — archive the model version and migration plan with the data. Fix: cold-archive chapter of the Phase-3 ops spec; per-tier retrieval latency vs SLA, scrubber mismatch rate, and restore-drill pass rate as the metrics.

## Ideas 194–199 — Partner watch pipeline (round 33, 6 analyses, 2026-10-17)

Ranked by build relevance. Sources: `hidden_files/research/watch-log/196-*.md` through `201-*.md` + ROUND-33-SYNTHESIS.md. ChatGPT consulted directly; Grok/Fo analyses research-derived (OpenRouter credits exhausted; no live browser in scope).

### 194. Prospective-memory subsystem: durable intention store + scheduler/event-monitor + learned silence (ChatGPT, R33) — HIGH
A memory store is not a scheduler — intentions need durable state plus a separate execution path. Two trigger families, both deployed in OSS agents: time-based (cron/scheduler) and event-based (condition monitoring; brain-mem's trigger_type + repeat counts; agentcontext's task-matched triggers auto-expiring after ~3 fires). *Remember When It Matters*: a proactive memory sidekick learns when to intervene vs stay silent — +8.3pp Terminal-Bench 2.0, +6.8pp τ²-Bench, the first measured lift from *timed* delivery; silence is first-class (unnecessary reminders distract and corrupt reasoning). No independent benchmark of missed-trigger/duplicate-firing rates exists for any product (Gemini Scheduled Actions, ChatGPT scheduled tasks are feature-level only). Fix: intention records (action + owner + trigger + timezone/ambiguity + status pending/fired/completed/cancelled/snoozed + dedup identity + retry policy); scheduler + event monitor with time-based fallbacks; visible/snoozeable/cancellable intentions; missed-trigger and duplicate-fire rates instrumented from day one.

### 195. Gated query rewriting: time-aware expansion first-class; never stack on calibrated encoders (Grok, R33) — HIGH
HyDE: +14–17pp nDCG@10 over Contriever zero-shot, but hurts where lexical match already works. Time-aware query expansion: +7–11% on temporal reasoning in LongMemEval — the only rewrite measured on agent-memory corpora. Step-Back: TimeQA 41.5%→66% while introducing 11.9% new errors. Decomposition: marginal alone, strong with reranking (HotpotQA EM 25.4→28.1). Critical negatives: stacking HyDE on a query-calibrated encoder loses 10.8pp (CoHyDE); rewriting on saturated corpora is net-negative at 2.2× latency; never equal-weight-fuse original + rewrite rankings. Fix: gate rewriting on measured headroom (question-type classifier + retrieval confidence), never global; decomposition only for multi-hop/temporal with reranking; time-aware expansion as a first-class primitive; HyDE only for vague queries against document-calibrated encoders; single-call cost-efficient forms (ToR-Lite ~1.9× gain per ms).

### 196. Consumer-memory UX law: provenance on every surfaced memory; deletion cascades; no verbatim claims (ChatGPT, R33) — MEDIUM-HIGH
The #1 confusion across ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini: saved memory ≠ chat history — deleting a chat does not delete the memory derived from it (OpenAI documents this explicitly). All three are selective/summarized/relevance-gated over finite context; a saved fact is never guaranteed to be retrieved and applied. Patterns to copy: ChatGPT's per-response "View sources" attribution (inspect, trace to archived conversation, mark relevant/not-relevant, correct); Claude's explicit scoping (the convenience-vs-predictability axis). Gemini's fragmented controls (saved info / past-chat personalization / Activity / Gems) are the anti-pattern. No independent head-to-head reliability study exists. Fix: every surfaced memory shows provenance + edit affordances; memories carry visible scope; deletion is one action cascading across store and source chats; surface which memories were considered/retrieved and why; instrument save/update/retrieve/delete correctness internally — first-mover measurement is a differentiator.

### 197. Scale envelope: 10–100M vectors, namespace-isolated, with self-measured corpus telemetry (Grok, R33) — MEDIUM-HIGH
Published: Reddit 340M vectors evaluated with a 1B-vector sub-100ms-P99 requirement (first-party); Pinecone customers 135M/480M/1.4B vectors, ~380–5,700 QPS (vendor-claimed, no methodology); Notion 10B+ vectors across millions of namespaces, ~10× scale / ~90% cost reduction over two years (strongest claim + growth rate); ScyllaDB 1B vectors at 252K QPS is an engine ceiling, not a deployment. The honest gap: no agent-memory product (Mem0/Zep/Letta) publishes any corpus-size or growth figure — Mem0's closest number is 186M API calls/quarter. Fix: design for 10–100M vectors per deployment; ~100 QPS sustained with ~5K headroom; 1B+ forces IVF-PQ/DiskANN off HNSW-in-RAM; per-tenant namespaces from day one (Notion pattern); track memories/user, vectors/user, read QPS, index-growth/week — the numbers the industry lacks.

### 198. Red-team exercise operations: bug bar + regression-pin + multi-session poisoning scope (Fo, R33) — MEDIUM
The loop: scan → triage (ML bug bar) → harden → pin the attack as a regression test → follow-up test; only the full loop counts. Scope by three boundaries (inference/write-read path, training/personalization data, integration/injectable sources). Memory poisoning is the memory-specific first-class risk: persisted contamination resurfaces in sessions that never caused it — exercises must test multi-session persistence (does poison survive compaction/summarization/refresh?), and fixes may require quarantining already-persisted memories. Manual round first, then systematic measurement; state attempt counts per attack class (10%-rate bug needs ~20 tries for 88% coverage). Safe execution: staging/production-adjacent, tenant-scoped fixtures, synthetic PII, rollback snapshot, trace-level assertions. Cadence: pre-release manual + continuous automated + re-run triggers; EU AI Act Art. 55 makes artifacts audit-required. Fix: red-team chapter of the Phase-3 ops spec with the bug bar, regression-pin, and trace-level assertions as required fields.

### 199. Write-path PII pipeline: detect → classify → route → audit, with quarantine as a workflow (Fo, R33) — MEDIUM
Canonical stage order: schema-aware mask → free-text detect (Presidio-style regex+NER) → classify (sensitivity tier) → route (store | redact | quarantine) → audit/manifest. False negatives dominate: regex-only recall 0.65 (~35% leaks) vs hybrid NER 0.96/0.94; miss classes are implicit/coded/multilingual identifiers and domain IDs. Leaked writes compound — persisted, summarized, re-retrieved — so write-path recall matters more than export redaction. Quarantine is a first-class HITL workflow (hold until compliance approval; unretrievable-until-approved, not a flag). False positives are the operational tax (backlog → rubber-stamping → real leaks). Cost: hybrid NER +30–40% CPU, +40–60ms P99; regex-first tier for hot path, LLM escalation only below 0.6 confidence. Pseudonymisation ≠ anonymisation — evaluate the gate at store level. Fix: write-path PII chapter of the Phase-3 ops spec with stage order, hybrid config, quarantine SLA, precision/recall acceptance gates (≥0.90/≥0.95 band), and store-level pseudonymisation gate; multilingual coverage needs its own validation track.

## Ideas 200–205 — Partner watch pipeline (round 34, 6 analyses, 2026-10-17)

Ranked by build relevance. Sources: `hidden_files/research/watch-log/202-*.md` through `207-*.md` + ROUND-34-SYNTHESIS.md. ChatGPT consulted directly; Grok/Fo analyses research-derived (OpenRouter credits exhausted; no live browser in scope).

### 200. Enterprise-retrieval-first doctrine: HERB's 20–33/100 with failed retrieval as the binding constraint (Grok, R34) — HIGH
The independent enterprise-RAG benchmark (Salesforce HERB, EMNLP 2025 Industry Track, 815 answerable + 699 unanswerable over 39,190 heterogeneous artifacts): best standard RAG 20.61/100, agentic ReAct+GPT-4o 32.96/100 — and fancier retrieval (RAPTOR 14.77, GraphRAG 10.31) *underperformed* plain hybrid on realistic data, directly contradicting vendor GraphRAG claims (90%+). Unanswerable-query detection ranges 6%–64% by base model. Cleanlab: production hallucinations persist at 3–27%; RAGAS fails on 83.5% of production examples. Fix: for enterprise KM, the binding constraint is retrieval coverage over heterogeneous sources, not the reasoner; the ingestion/parsing layer is where accuracy is won (OHR-Bench: reading order 11.9%→67.1% from parsing fixes); abstention must be engineered per model, not assumed; quote HERB's numbers whenever anyone claims enterprise RAG is "solved."

### 201. Canon-store pattern: status-graded facts + character-knowledge/world-truth split + two-pass verification (ChatGPT, R34) — HIGH
Narrative memory is a canon store, not a longer context window: story bible + character sheets + world-state ledger + outline-conditioned generation + retrieval. Key sub-designs: character knowledge vs world truth tracked as distinct records (catches accidental omniscience); immutable-facts vs changing-state split; status-graded canon (idea/developing/canon/revised/deprecated) so brainstorming never hardens into contradiction; per-chapter state snapshots as the generator's unit; two-pass verification (extract claims → check against canon) with confidence-scored flags and audit trail — decomposed into bounded-context stages (ingest → store → check → explain) because one prompt breaks past ~2 chapters. Hands-on: Sudowrite drafts ~20k words/hour but forgets main characters past ~45k words — the human/agent remains canon authority. Fix: adopt the canon-store pattern for any long-horizon agent task with accumulating facts; ConStory-Bench's 5-category taxonomy (characterization/factual/narrative/temporal/world) as the measurement spine; chapter-window consistency checks (FLAWEDFICTIONS: detection collapses 0.67→0.53 with length).

### 202. Governed knowledge service: permission-aware retrieval + point-of-work capture + freshness schema (ChatGPT, R34) — MEDIUM-HIGH
Enterprise KM as agent memory converges on: permission-aware RAG with citations (filter *before* context injection — presentation-layer filtering is unsafe; the security gate); tribal knowledge captured at the point of work (resolved cases, incident reviews, decisions) with applicability/exception/evidence prompts, routed to named owners — never vacuumed chat; freshness/ownership/versioning as first-class fields with automatic expiry of unreviewed content; knowledge graphs only as supplements with every claim attached to source passages and dates. Staleness is the dominant silent failure (fluent wrong answers; users stop consulting sources). Measured outcomes are all throughput/adoption (Klarna, Intercom Fin ~51%, MAHLE, Glean $300M ARR) — org-wide memory with proven net productivity gains is unproven. Fix: instrument the honest metric set from day one (correctness vs expert labels, citation precision, recall@k, permission-leak rate, abstention quality, freshness lag).

### 203. Dual-mode moderation: pre-write scan + retrospective re-scan with quarantine semantics (Fo, R34) — MEDIUM
Five-stage pipeline (detect → risk-tiered queue → human review → act → log/appeal); SLAs: triage ~1 min, high-severity <5 min, appeals 24–48h. Both errors endemic: ~10% FP on leading classifiers vs sarcasm/dog-whistle FNs — "count false positives like misses" (over-blocking gets the filter turned off). Appeals are a quality instrument: every overturn charged back to the firing rule. Evasion needs Unicode normalization before matching + layered detection (algospeak, homoglyphs, steganography surviving Llama Guard). Fix: gate the write path (cheap classifier every write, sub-second) *and* retrospectively re-scan stored memories on model/policy updates; quarantine = stored-but-not-retrievable; blast-radius-ordered triage (widely-retrieved first); per-language detection metrics (20–40% higher FPR for Black users' speech; Swahili 10–20% of English efficacy).

### 204. Hardware decision order: quantization before instance; GPU only for batched throughput (Fo, R34) — MEDIUM
RAM is the binding constraint: 10M×1536 float32 ≈ 61.4 GB raw → ~85–130 GB working set (~1.4× raw); rule of thumb ≥100 GB RAM for full in-memory HNSW. BQ + 8× rescore holds 0.990 recall at 32× less RAM — the dominant cost lever, chosen *before* the instance. CAGRA GPU: 33–77× throughput over CPU HNSW, but at batch size 1 CPU wins on latency — GPU pays only under sustained batched throughput (Milvus ships GPU; Qdrant experimental; Weaviate/pgvector CPU-only). Engine ceilings: Chroma/pgvector ~10–20M, Qdrant ~50M single-node, Weaviate 100M+, Milvus 10B+ clustered. Fix: sizing procedure = (count × dims × bytes × index multiplier) → quantization/tiering → per-role instance selection (search highmem, ingest NVMe) → 2× headroom; validation = the five production-predictive tests at actual scale with cost-per-billion-queries at fixed recall; re-benchmark on every version upgrade.

---

### 205. Consistency-benchmark spine: ConStory-Bench taxonomy + length-degradation law (Grok, R34) — MEDIUM
ConStory-Bench ("Lost in Stories"): 2,000 prompts targeting 8–10k-word stories, 5-category error taxonomy (characterization, factual accuracy, narrative coherence, temporal logic, world consistency) × 19 subtypes, CED/GRR scoring — GPT-5-Reasoning leads at CED 0.113; its automated checker finds 3.2× more errors than human experts (F1 0.678 vs 0.229). FLAWEDFICTIONS (COLM 2025, plot-hole detection): models near random chance (~0.50) except Claude 3.5 Sonnet + verifier (0.67 = human); performance collapses on longer stories (0.53 for o1 on ~2.7k-word stories) — consistency reasoning breaks before context windows do. Fix: adopt the 5-category taxonomy as the measurement spine for any long-horizon memory eval (factual accuracy and temporal logic dominate failures); chapter-window consistency checks rather than full-context reliance; "Stick to the Script" commitment-preservation framing as the acceptance-test shape (commit-ledger + violation detection).

### 206. Implicit-memory-as-prefix: byte-identical memory prefix + dynamic-state-trailing architecture (ChatGPT, R35) — HIGH
KV-cache/prefix caching is lossless "implicit memory" that saves prefill, not context: vLLM hashes blocks by exact tokens + prefix hash; SGLang RadixAttention walks a radix tree; SGLang reports 50–99% hit rates on prefix-heavy workloads. Reuse geometry is strict: append cheap, mid-prefix edit forces re-prefill of everything after, leading-byte change invalidates all; ~128 KiB/token (32-layer/8-KV-head BF16) means 8k tokens ≈ 1 GiB VRAM per request. The cache is not memory — it stores computation, not facts; use it to accelerate access to memory-in-the-prompt, never as the store. Design: system prompt, tool schemas, injected memory blocks FIRST, user-varying content LAST; keep the stable parts prefix-stable; hit rate is a bill-relevant dashboard metric (agentic loops cut blended inference cost 60–85% by stabilizing prefixes).

### 207. Retrieve-or-reason gate as an explicit learned policy knob (ChatGPT, R35) — HIGH
The retrieve-vs-think tradeoff: retrieve when uncertainty is a *missing fact* (entity, date, user-specific, must-be-current — reasoning cannot recover it); reason longer when premises are in hand (puzzles, math, planning, synthesis). ThinkRetrieve: pure sequential thinking degrades at high budgets (83% → 52% on GSM-8K) while retrieval-interleaved thinking stays stable or climbs (+13.4 absolute points on hardest benchmarks). For multi-hop agent work the winning pattern is retrieve-then-reason, not either/or. DeepRAG-style per-step retrieve-or-skip gating — answer from parametric memory when confident, retrieve otherwise. No universal token threshold exists; frame as a compute allocator across reformulation, retrieval, rerank, reasoning, verification under latency/cost SLOs. If retrieval returns weak evidence, say so — don't burn reasoning as a substitute.

### 208. Prompt-architecture caching law: 7% → 84% hits from one layout refactor; 5–6.5× TTFT at 8k prefixes (Grok, R35) — HIGH
ProjectDiscovery (independent, production): agentic workload hit rate 7% → 84% and cost −59% (−70% peak, 9.8B tokens served from cache) via one prompt-layout refactor — hit rate is an architecture property, not a provider property. PrefixBench-H100 (academic 2026): 5–6.5× TTFT reduction at 8,192-token shared prefix; vLLM and TensorRT-LLM statistically identical cache effectiveness. AWS vLLM benchmark: P50 TTFT −71–77%, throughput +15–16% at 8k prefixes; hit rate 25–82% config-dependent. Billing: cached reads ~0.1× base (newer tiers 0.02–0.05×; Grok weaker at 0.16–0.25×), writes 1.25–2×; support bot 67–77% bill reduction, 30-step coding agent 80–89%, RAG where only instructions repeat 15–17%. Target ≥80% hit rate on agentic loops; sub-2k prefixes buy single-digit TTFT gains; API-side caching cuts dollars, engine-side cuts TTFT — design for both.

### 209. Difficulty-routed thinking budgets: log-linear, then flat, then degrading — cap the curve (Grok, R35) — HIGH
o1's AIME curve: accuracy ≈ baseline + k·log(thinking tokens), k ≈ a few pp per doubling; Snell et al. (2024): optimally allocated test-time compute beats 14× parameter scaling at fixed FLOP budget. But saturation is measured: s1 budget forcing flattens at ~6× budget with repetitive-loop pathology; Gemini 3.5 Flash writing gains nothing measurable from high thinking; FLAWEDFICTIONS showed more inference compute degrading consistency reasoning (0.67 → 0.53). Marginal rate: DeepSeek R1-0528 doubled reasoning tokens (~12k → 23k) for +17.5 pp AIME 2025; Anthropic effort ladder: cheaper model at low effort beat bigger at high effort (88.9% at ~1¢ vs 74.4% at 4.6¢). Working model: saturation ≈ 5–10k thinking tokens per problem; tiered mix ~5× cheaper than flat-high. Rules: difficulty-routed budgets, retrieve-before-think (retrieval ~0.1× input vs thinking at full output price), pass@k-with-verifier over deepening past saturation, hard budget caps. Cost figures decay ~10×/year — re-derive annually.

### 210. Inference-cache ops: silent-miss observability, TTL-as-policy, cache_salt tenant isolation, failure-mode table (Fo, R35) — MEDIUM
Caching fails silently: below-minimum-token prompts engage nothing with no error; dynamic content before the breakpoint breaks the hash; tail breakpoints can fall outside Anthropic's ~20-block lookback window. Control: log the three input-token counters (fresh/cache_creation/cache_read) on every response and emit a hit-rate metric — the only reliable hosted observability hook. TTL is the provider's invalidation policy (Anthropic 5-min sliding/1-hr extended, OpenAI ~5–10 min auto, Gemini explicit handles to 24h with storage fee) — heartbeat-warm long batches, treat prompt deploys as invalidation events. Multi-tenant: vLLM hashes KV blocks with parent-hash + block tokens + `cache_salt`; PROMPTPEEK (NDSS 2025) reconstructed other tenants' prompts at >95% via timing alone — salt from authenticated tenant identity, audit to sha256-class. Ops spec chapters: controls, observability (hit rate, eviction rate, spill latency, affinity skew), invalidation playbook (version-bumped keys at rollout), failure-mode table (silent non-engagement, stale-cache serving, timing leakage, hash-collision poisoning, hot-pod eviction).

### 211. Long-generation serving runbook: 5 streaming failure modes, deadlines per decode iteration, runaway guardrails (Fo, R35) — MEDIUM
Five documented streaming failure modes — silent SSE freeze (proxy buffering), ghost generation after disconnect (burning tokens on discarded text), gateway OOM, LB idle-timeout kills during slow reasoning, partial JSON corruption — mitigations: disable proxy buffering, bind upstream to downstream context, bounded queues with backpressure, SSE keepalives ~15s, verified frame delimiters. Cancellation-on-disconnect is the highest-leverage control (track abandoned connections separately). Timeouts must be absolute deadlines propagated through gateway/queue/runtime/stream and checked per decode iteration; never blindly retry after visible output. Preemption metastability: at ~98% load, recompute-preemption spirals never recover (18 min–2.5 h observed) — short benchmarks overstate capacity; use admission control + sustained-load testing. Overthinking attacks = DoS-shaped cost risk (26× output inflation via adversarial suffixes; 3–9× measured academically) — hard max-reasoning-token caps, cost-per-request alerting, agent step caps, spending limits. True single-generation checkpoint/resume is effectively nonexistent; use agentic loop checkpointing + idempotency keys + client-designed resume.

### 212. Two-tier consolidation: session-end staging + idle-triggered deep pass, episodes append-only (ChatGPT, R36) — HIGH
Design consensus across ChatGPT, talks, and implementations: lightweight session-end extraction (candidate facts with provenance + confidence into a versioned staging area) plus deep idle/capacity-triggered consolidation pass. agent-sleep's 8-stage pipeline as reference: priority replay (prediction error) → deterministic episodic distillation → procedural recipe extraction → trajectory abstraction → rule promotion (seen ≥2x) → epistemic status (observed vs verified) → episodic compression → self-competence EMA. Replay ranking blends surprise × future-task relevance × importance × recency with a diversity guard for older high-value episodes (Generative Agents' classic scoring; Runa recomputes importance with full-day context). LLM Sleep (CMU/Maryland preprint May 2026): offline recurrent passes GSM-Infinite 6-op 0.742→0.812 — but on internal weights, not episode stores; transfer plausible but unproven. Laws: episodes append-only and always re-queryable; promote only corroborated patterns; retire by reversible soft-invalidation; NREM/REM splits speculative; for symbolic stores EWC/pseudo-rehearsal don't transfer — analogues are versioned facts, provenance, confidence, dedup. Measure consolidation separately from retrieval (held-out multi-session recall + contradiction rate, replay schedule ablated).

### 213. Graph-lane memory: bi-temporal invalidate-don't-delete edges, hybrid controller, extraction as the fragile joint (ChatGPT, R36) — HIGH
Facts live on edges carrying temporal validity (valid_from/valid_to + event-time vs ingestion-time); new episodes invalidate contradicted edges without deleting history — fixes vector RAG's stale-fact failure mode ("what plan is the customer on?"). Consensus: episodes + embeddings for recall; small typed temporal graph for durable entities/relations/time-sensitive facts; provenance + validity interval + confidence on every material edge; graph traversal for relational/temporal questions, passage retrieval for open-ended; clarify-first when extraction confidence is low. Graph-native retrieval = vector + BM25 + graph, no LLM at query time (vendor sub-second p95; 5–50ms three-hop traversals on indexed Neo4j). Extraction is the breakage point: false merges, negation, hypotheticals, attribution — keep source passages available for diagnosis. Update semantics must distinguish corrects/contradicts/qualifies/adds; hard deletion is a privacy operation, distinct from historical invalidation. Evidence is vendor-tinged (Zep +18.5% LongMemEval / 90% latency, Mem0 LOCOMO) — no independent controlled graph-vs-vector-vs-hybrid comparisons. Ingest hygiene: store decisions and state changes, not chit-chat; cap injected facts (~50 hurts answers). The graph lane's extraction/promotion/retirement lives in the Tier-2 offline consolidation pass (idea 212).

### 214. Retrieval-stack measurements: graded-eval embedder selection, tuned fusion, shallow rerank pooling (Grok, R36) — HIGH
Leaderboard reshuffled: gemini-embedding-001 tops multilingual MTEB (~68.3), Qwen3-Embedding-8B the self-hosted default — but binary MTEB over-ranks: ZeroEntropy's graded-NDCG@10 re-eval moves zembed-1 8th→1st while harrier-0.6b collapses 2nd→11th (a small model matching its large sibling is an overfitting red flag). Danish snapshot: multilingual giants beat language-specific models; fine-tuning a strong embedder on narrow data destroyed it (−7 to −13 points) — mix the original distribution back in or don't fine-tune. WANDS: tuned hybrid + field boosting 0.7497 NDCG vs BM25 0.6983 / dense 0.6953 (+7.4%), basic RRF only +0.012; Sep-2026 preprint: equal-weight RRF loses to dense on BEIR macro-average (0.479 vs 0.519) — fusion must be tuned per corpus (train-then-freeze). Cross-encoder rerank: +0.04 nDCG@10 class, recall invariant, top-5 captures the lift, ~1000–3000× retrieval latency; NFCorpus null (+0.0011 nDCG for 1.1s/query) — rerank is a per-corpus measurement, not a default. HNSW: 99.4–99.9% recall@10 at 3.3–7.1 ms p50; ef_search ≈ 2–3× topK. Missing eval anywhere: ANN-recall sensitivity of hybrid retrieval quality — write it before locking index targets. Version the embedding pipeline (champions turn over ~annually).

### 215. Memory quality ops: atomic write units, synchronous read-path gates, six-metric dashboard, real quarantine (Fo, R36) — MEDIUM
Write path is the control point: atomic commits (sequence-numbered event log + engine snapshot + extracted facts/items in one multi-document transaction; ~22 ms p50 per MongoDB-authored case study); `event_seq` monotonicity turns lost writes into detectable gaps; partial writes are the dominant silent-corruption source. Synchronous read-path gates: consistency-check retrieved memory against reference APIs *before* prompt construction; halt/isolate/re-query on low consistency. Continuous layer: ~10% live-traffic sampling, Quality-State Calculator, paging on rolling thresholds, low-scoring sessions promoted to the golden set (documented drift: 98%→80% customer-ID accuracy over three 30-min windows). Dashboard thresholds: retrieval precision ≥70%, write-back success ≥95%, stale rate ≤10%, repeated-failure non-zero = episodic not read at session start, re-explanation >5%, escalation attribution. Quarantine workflow: redirect to clean replica, operator sees hash + 16-char preview + score, release-with-reason, false-positive release-and-relearn. Corruption enters through compression (summarization dropping conditions that become baseline knowledge) and staleness — measure semantic divergence and factual retention at the compression point. Ingest filter catches lazy injection, not adversarially optimized payloads — scope the claim.

### 216. Durable execution ops: Effect Sandwich checkpointing, mandatory idempotency, Temporal-style replay, per-tool replay policies (Fo, R36) — MEDIUM
"Never let the model own the only copy of progress." Effect Sandwich (Pi-Durable): commit intent + idempotency key before the external effect, perform effect outside the commit, commit outcome + receipt after; crash taxonomy (before intent / mid-effect / after outcome) each with a defined recovery action. Activities are at-least-once — idempotency is a production requirement: keys generated in the intent phase (never inside the effect), honored downstream, reconciled on long pauses (Stripe prunes keys after ~24h). Temporal's Workflow/Activity separation: deterministic coordination with event-sourced replay, heartbeat/timeout/retry policies per activity, bounded history (Continue-As-New), versioned deploys, retry classification (permanent vs transient). Replay ≠ context reset: state recovery and prompt reconstruction are distinct procedures; persist the decision, not just the transcript. Human-approval waits are durable paused state (never a sleeping worker); commit state before streaming tokens. Every tool declares `replay: "safe"` vs `"unsafe"`. Migration signal: state tables + hand-rolled retries + business-logic DLQs = you're building a workflow engine; decide Temporal-style vs embedded-durable at Phase-3 inception, because retrofitting durability onto a naive loop is the documented failure path.
