### 217. Index operating point: HNSW recall/latency curve, ANN downstream loss, scale economics, embedder lock-in (Grok, R36) — LOW
Measured: 50K real embeddings — flat 100% recall at 26.6 ms p50 vs HNSW ef=100 → 99.4% at 3.3 ms, ef=500 → 99.9% at 7.1 ms (~3.8× faster than exact; synthetic Gaussian tuning doesn't transfer — max 38.6% recall vs 99%+ on real embeddings). Connapse's 100k–1M pgvector scale test: recall@30 0.975–0.987 at 25–45 ms p95; ef_search 800 → 0.990–0.997 at ≤73 ms. Downstream studies: ≤~0.02 nDCG@10 loss from ANN approximation, "minor" RAG QA effects even at 0.7 recall. Operating point: ef_search ≈ 2–3× inner topK, halfvec indexing. Scale economics: 1B×768 FP32 ≈ 3TB vectors + ~1TB graph in RAM for HNSW; IVF-PQ at 16 bytes/vec fits one large machine at 1–3% recall cost; hosted $50–500/mo per 1M vectors (2025–26), self-hosted 5–10× cheaper at scale. Lock-in: re-embedding 100M docs = hours-to-days — start with a hosted-open model, version the index, shadow-cutover. All engines clear ~0.99 recall at our scale, so the index choice is dominated by ops cost, not recall.

### 218. Outcome-aware rehearsal scheduling: explicit outcome labels, Leitner baseline, value-weighted budget (ChatGPT, R37) — MEDIUM
Rehearsal must be event-driven and outcome-aware: map retrieval outcomes onto review grades (successful_use, retrieved_not_used, relevant_missed, contradicted, no_opportunity) — non-use is not forgetting, and retrieval success ≠ truth, so only grounded success raises stability. Ship an auditable Leitner-box or fixed 1–3–7–16–35-day baseline first with memory-specific retention targets (not one global 90%); earn FSRS-style per-memory stability learning only after enough labeled outcome data (implicit reviews: access = "Good", archive = "Again", automatic). "Rehearsal" is five distinct operations — retrieval test, re-encode, merge, graph re-walk, idle pass — separately flagged, budgeted, ablated (re-encoding risks paraphrase drift; idle passes aren't reviews). Under a fixed budget schedule by expected value (priority = expected_loss_avoided × probability_of_future_need × uncertainty/decay / review_cost) with coverage constraints and a calibration-exploration reserve. Hard caveat: no controlled study isolates spaced-rehearsal scheduling as the cause of better agent performance — schedule as a budgeted, measurable intervention. R12 covered decay; this is the rehearsal side.

### 219. Self-model as typed memory: capability/calibration/episodic schemas, evidence-hierarchy updates, pre-action routing (ChatGPT, R37) — MEDIUM
Three separate schemas, never free-text autobiography: capability records (scoped success estimates + provenance + evidence counts + conditions + decision policy), calibration records (pre-action predictions vs defined outcomes, scored by proper scoring rules per task class), structured episodic failure records (failure type, root cause, recovery, prevention rule, hypothesis tags). Update gate: typed evidence hierarchy — external checks > independent outcome evidence > independent judge > self-report (proposal channel only, never a truth channel); self-validated capability claims rejected. Agreement is not correctness ("unanimous, 96% sure, wrong answer" demo); verbal confidence is poorly calibrated — routing uses externally validated per-task-class calibration. Operational payoff is pre-action routing: attempt / clarify / delegate / decline with explicit thresholds on success probability × failure cost × verification availability. Separate capability (measured), instructions (asked), episodic history, task state; capabilities versioned and decayed across model/tool updates. Causal evidence missing — Phase-3 runs its own ablations (no self-model vs episodic-only vs self-report vs externally-calibrated).

### 220. World-model memory: evaluate by rollout, not one-step error; inject into context, not auxiliary slots (Grok, R37) — MEDIUM
RDR (preregistered 10/10): valid prediction time 1.80× (3.87→6.97) by training free-running rollouts like evaluation — cheap, parameter-free train/eval alignment gain. SALT: 1.48–2.19× worse one-step error but +10pp closed-loop success — one-step error is a misleading memory metric. Latent diffusion-policy world models degrade roughly linearly with horizon (MSE 0.012→0.087, 1→10 steps). Independent: WorldMemBench (Oct 2026) — all 9 video world models degrade on repeated scene revisits (best static-retention model initiated only 31.7% of prescribed events); MIND: memory-enabled models beat memory-less but capture only short-term memory; "On Memory" head-to-head: context-window injection won, Titans-based neural memory hallucinated entirely — inject memory into the context window, not auxiliary slots. MemoryVAM: LIBERO-Mem 5% → 42.5% with episodic memory. Design: evaluate by multi-step rollout metrics (valid prediction time, revisit consistency, event initiation); budget the revisit problem as the primary failure mode.

### 221. Prompt memory: reflective evolution (GEPA) and distilled reasoning libraries (Grok, R37) — MEDIUM
GEPA (ICLR 2026 Oral): +6% avg / up to +20% over GRPO with up to 35× fewer rollouts; beats MIPROv2 by >10% (+12% AIME-2025); ships in DSPy — natural-language reflection on full trajectories beats scalar rewards; run it without new infra. ReasoningBank (Google Cloud AI, ICLR 2026): +8.3pp WebArena (40.5→48.8), +4.6pp/−2.8 steps SWE-Bench-Verified — distilled reasoning memory beats raw-trajectory (Synapse) and workflow (AWM) memory; but LLMWatch's independent game benchmark found raw history winning on one backbone (distilled rules can lock in a false rule) — keep raw trajectories as the audit layer under the distilled library. Independent: 15/19 agent prompts scored worse when removed (refuting "delete your prompts"); "Be concise." −28.7% tokens and cuts output variance (±15%→±4%). Dead in 2026: personas (162-role study: no accuracy gain), tips/threats (no effect), hand-tuning (replaced by DSPy/GEPA); Chroma context-rot (18 models) bounds injectable library size. Practice: prompts as versioned, benchmarked artifacts (AGENTS.md pattern, 60k+ repos); A/B every prompt version against the same query set; measure inside the production harness (7–17 point swings across harnesses).

### 222. Refresh runbook: event-driven incrementals, version-pinned embedder, tombstone deletes, operator freshness panel (Fo, R37) — MEDIUM
Scheduled full re-embeds are an anti-pattern at scale; cadence is event-driven (change events) with nightly/weekly reconciliation as backstop. Content-addressed chunk IDs → idempotent upserts. Embedder version pinned per index partition: model upgrades mean backfilling the whole corpus into a new version partition, verified, then atomic cutover — mixed vector versions silently corrupt recall. Deletion is first-class: tombstone-first ordering, "delete everything I didn't just write" re-index filter, nightly source-vs-index reconciliation with drift reported to operators (never silently repaired); treat the index as a cache, never a second source of truth. Freshness SLIs: oldest-pending-source age, small-k recall on a labeled set, top-result freshness, share of answers with traceable URLs — an operator freshness panel. memX's maintenance-script taxonomy (reindex/migrate-embedding/FTS migration/smart-dedupe with dry-run gates) is a copyable pattern. Budget re-embedding as an explicit cost line.

### 223. Postmortem-to-memory pipeline: capture → distill → admit, belief-delta templates, capped playbook (Fo, R37) — MEDIUM
End-to-end pipeline: every failed run fills a fixed template before context discard; an independent distiller (not the failing agent — it writes defensive rules) proposes compact rules (≤2 sentences, applies-when + what-to-do, ≥2 incident citations, each with a replay scenario); an admit gate runs discriminative replay (before must fail, after must pass) plus the full regression suite. One build log: repeat failures 38% → 6% over three months — though total failures barely moved (71→64/month); lessons convert repeat waste into new failures. Load-bearing field: `believed` vs `actual` — the assumption delta, not the stack trace. Ops: hard playbook cap (60 rules, last-hit timestamps, continuous cold retirement — or it becomes the unread 900-line doc); provenance on every lesson; vector isolation per domain; causal embeddings (separate symptom/cause/resolution/precursor spaces) for incident-time matching; triage gate on distillation cost (~50-token pre-filter cuts cost 10×); a second sink for ambiguity-rooted incidents (spec templates, not agent memory). Primary KPI: repeat-failure share. R13's failure memory was retry-steering; this is the retrospective pipeline.

### 224. Three-way memory routing law: external store default, context working set, weights only via reviewed pipeline (ChatGPT, R38) — HIGH
Context = temporary task-local facts and active instructions; external store = default durable tier for episodic, personal, changing, attributable, access-controlled facts (mutability, per-item granularity, auditability, provenance, blast-radius containment); weights/versioned skills = only stable, generalizable, broadly applicable behavior that passed review and evaluation — because weight updates have the widest blast radius, no provenance, and no item-level deletion. Hard-code: no direct per-conversation weight writes; separate reviewed pipeline with evaluation, versioning, rollback, approval. "No retrieval step" ≠ reliably available — weight-encoded facts can still be inaccessible or confused; task-critical constraints never depend on parametric recall alone. LoRA/adapters-as-memory: stable reviewed behavioral patterns (not changing facts); no item-level attribution or deletion; per-user adapters carry routing/versioning/privacy burdens. Terminology: pin "parametric memory" = information in parameters; call test-time writes "weight writes." (R23 covered fact editing; this is the routing decision.)

### 225. Measured memory economics: $0.0013/recall vs $0.0293 long-context; curated retrieval +5% tokens for +16.1pp; prompt caching as first-class lever (Grok, R38) — HIGH
Beyond the Context Window (arXiv Mar 2026, LongMemEval, 500 conversations, mean 101,601 tokens): fact extraction + embedding ≈ $0.0435/conversation one-time; retrieved-fact answering ≈ $0.0013/query — ~22× cheaper than GPT-5-mini full-conversation baselines ($0.0293/request); memory front-loads cost at write, long context pays per turn. LaRA (ICML 2025): long-context 8–82× more expensive at scale (conservative band). Curated retrieval: +5% tokens for +16.1pp task completion vs full guideline injection +51–78% per task — memory cost is input-token inflation, not longer trajectories; gate on curated retrieval, fail full-injection designs. Prompt caching is the biggest real-world lever (50–90% discounts; 400K-token manual $1,200/day uncached vs ~$120 cached vs $24 RAG; crossover ~10–20 queries per corpus); cache-aware prompt design is a first-class constraint. Nonlinear curve: the "token tax of epistemic accuracy" — modest correctness gains cost disproportionately; durable KV-state restore 2.8–4.3× faster and 8.8–12.3× less GPU-energy than recompute. Design: front-loaded write + fixed small per-query read; per-query cost ceilings alongside accuracy bars.

### 226. Hierarchy-as-roles: record types with semantics, four separated decision functions, role-routed retrieval (ChatGPT, R38) — MEDIUM
Working (immediate needs), episodic (timestamped records), semantic (distilled facts/preferences), procedural (versioned skills) are roles with different retention and retrieval rules — "three tiers" is a practical pattern, never an established optimum. Route retrieval by role: working → deterministic injection; episodic → temporal/session filters + recency-aware ranking; semantic → semantic+lexical+structured filters; graph only for multi-hop/relational queries. Single-search failure catalog: semantically-similar-but-stale episode beats the current preference; temporal events missed on wording; old facts without corrections; near-duplicate bloat. Separate paging, eviction, promotion, consolidation into four decision functions with separate signals/budgets/audits (never one "importance" score); don't promote on retrieval frequency alone. Hybrid preservation: append-only episodes + provenance-linked derived facts; summaries from source records, never from summaries. Evidence honesty: "production consensus" = LOW (ChatGPT correction); no controlled promotion-policy comparison exists under common conditions. (R32 covered cognitive architectures; this is the store hierarchy.)

### 227. Neural memory measurements: Titans recall dominance, SSM efficiency crossover, semantic-recall evaluation discipline (Grok, R38) — MEDIUM
Titans S-NIAH at 16K: MAC holds 98.4%/97.4%/95.2% where Mamba2 collapses to 5.4%/0.0%/0.0% — forgetting/weight-decay mechanism is the demonstrated differentiator (architectures that can erase memory generalize); also wins generic LM at fixed scale. Jan-2026 head-to-head: Mamba 12.46× more memory-efficient, 10.67× faster at 4K, crossovers ~220/370 tokens — but attention keeps the edge on precise associative recall; hybrids win (Gated DeltaNet-H2 40.1 vs Transformer++ 37.0 vs pure recurrence 30.6). Forgetting laws: Mamba-2 training length for robust forgetting scales linearly with state size; accurate recall context scales exponentially. Evaluation discipline: NIAH is saturated (>90% at 1M) — single-needle scores are marketing; NoLiMa 30-point semantic-vs-lexical gap (99.3%→69.7% at 32K); HELMET: synthetic NIAH doesn't predict downstream long-context performance. Design: rank by S-NIAH ordering not parameter count; architect hybrid attention + recurrent memory; test semantic recall, not lexical. Mostly author-claimed; Titans has no independent reproduction.

### 228. Debuggability ops: event log as hard requirement, three-layer wrong-memory runbook, retrieval-decision inspection (Fo, R38) — MEDIUM
LLM control flow is non-deterministic, so debugging is trace reconstruction, not reproduction — an append-only event log (every write/read/evict/overwrite with record id, source, query, retrieved-set, timestamp, session) is a hard requirement. MemTrace (3,000+ ops): complete event history gives automated root-cause classification (evicted/overwritten/invalid-read/hallucination-despite-correct-memory — all 100% categorizable; evictions dominated 3× over hallucinations). Wrong-memory runbook: preserve four observations (approved source / stored memory / retrieved context / output), find the first layer that disagrees before mutating the store. Most failures are retrieval failures, not storage (LoCoMo-based study) — log top-k/scores/filters per query; debug starts at the ranker. Provenance rides on the record: pinned records exempt from decay; compaction writes a durable copy before summarizing (write-ahead rule). Mainstream tools capture memory ops only via generic custom spans — Phase-3 needs its own memory.write/memory.recall span conventions on OpenTelemetry GenAI semantics.

### 229. Memory FinOps: attribution tagging, SLO-grade budget alerts, cost-per-successful-recall, lag-aware reconciliation (Fo, R38) — MEDIUM
Attribution tagging (pipeline, tenant, feature, memory op) is the cheapest control and prerequisite for everything. Budget alerts, not dashboards, catch runaway spend — pre-flight cost estimation (<0.5ms), per-agent budget caps, halt-on-breach circuit breakers (a real $47K multi-agent failure traced to missing caps + step limits + loop detection). Hierarchical attribution (root/sub-agent/rollup with dedup rows) answers "which sub-agent drives 80% of costs." Wasted-spend analytics (productive vs burned on halts/retry loops/semantic failures) feeds cost-per-successful-recall, not cost-per-query. Hidden-cost trio with memory equivalents: thinking tokens, context-caching reconciliation, misclassified tool fees → embedding burn (15–25% of AI infra spend per Pinecone 2025), compaction passes, vector-DB standing costs. Anomaly recipes: spend >2× rolling 7-day average, token-explosion on recall context, repetitive-operation stuck loops. Lag-aware reconciliation: reserved-vs-actual counters with provider-API reconciliation — local trackers drift (10% error ≈ $500 underreported on $5K; 5-min API lag = $8K underreport window); conservative budget resets. "Memory FinOps" is an extrapolation from LLM/agent FinOps — no source documents memory-specific cost ops.

### 230. Conversational memory: no universal unit, raw-vs-derived separation, unresolved items as first-class state (ChatGPT, R39) — MEDIUM
No universal right unit: turn good for attribution/ordering, discourse segments/topic episodes better for coherent tasks, sessions too coarse, sentence spans drop context — separate storage granularity (fine, source-linked spans) from retrieval granularity (query-driven). Raw evidence distinct from derived memory: summarization is lossy by construction (negation, uncertainty, corrections, exact quantities, unresolved questions die first); "compress before you store" is advice, not a rule. Record types: source transcript/span, derived summary, extracted fact, entity/reference link, topic/episode, unresolved item — observation-vs-inference tagging, provenance; "unknown" and "unresolved" are legal states. Unresolved items (open questions, pending decisions, promises) are the most summary-vulnerable — first-class state with completion/cancellation transitions. Dialogue-state tracking (TRADE/TripPy/MultiWOZ) transfers as structure for bounded domains only; coreference/topic links stored as provisional confidence-tagged hypotheses. No controlled comparison of turn-pruning policies exists — eval compares ≥4 baselines under matched budgets.

### 231. Memory API contract: six verbs, four-way lifecycle, principal≠subject, mandatory retrieval observability (ChatGPT, R39) — MEDIUM
Controller contract, not CRUD: `ingest`, `retrieve/search`, `get`, `supersede/update`, `retract/delete`, `history` — provenance, status, validity, version, access policy on every record; ranked search results carry scores, source/version, policy trace. Lifecycle split: supersession / invalidation-retraction / expiry / physical deletion — no silent last-write-wins; conditional updates, idempotency keys, async job states. Separate conversation-event ingestion from durable-fact commitment; turn hooks opt-in and observability-identical. Identity: acting principal ≠ memory subject ≠ namespace string — shared memory an explicitly named ACL'd resource; namespace strings validated against authenticated identity. Retrieval observability mandatory (trace ID, scopes, ranking signals, policy decisions) without leaking inaccessible content; retrieved content treated as untrusted. Machine-discoverability yes; autonomous self-registration/self-payment premature — agents act through delegated credentials. Vendor SDK claims mostly UNVERIFIED — borrow principles, specify our own contract.

### 232. NPC memory measurements: 42% story survival at 20 turns, fact conflicts 40–68%, moderation-of-recall (Grok, R39) — MEDIUM
NCP-Bench: GPT-5.2 keeps only 42% of stories intact at 20 turns; fact conflicts (40–68%) dominate across six frontier models — models contradict facts they themselves established a few turns earlier. NPC-Bench (UKCI 2025, peer-reviewed): Gemini Flash 2.0 at 94% on immersion/safety — but character/world consistency, not memory; no cross-session recall-accuracy benchmark exists for game NPCs. Generative Agents (UIST 2023): full memory-stream architecture μ=29.89 vs μ=21.21 fully ablated (d=8.16) — strongest independent evidence, but 2023-era, no modern replication. Shipping: NVIDIA ACE (inZOI) three-layer memory at ~1GB VRAM for the on-device SLM — vendor claims only, zero published recall numbers. Human-factors study: NPCs score well on long-term memory but over-recalling makes players "feel watched" — memory needs relevance gating, not maximal recall. Design: fact-conflict-rate metric alongside recall; relevance/permission layer gating recall aggressiveness.

### 233. Memory benchmark design methodology: LongMemEval template, LoCoMo 6.4% key error, protocol-on-every-number (Grok, R39) — HIGH
LongMemEval (ICLR 2025) is the golden-set template: 500 hand-curated questions × 5 abilities (extraction, multi-session reasoning, temporal, knowledge updates, abstention) × 115K–1.5M-token distractor histories — GPT-4o drops 30.3% oracle→full-history; per-ability splits reveal sign flips (Zep +38.4% temporal, −17.7% single-session). Independent LoCoMo audit (Mar 2026): 6.4% of answer keys wrong (caps perfect at 93.57%); gpt-4o-mini judge accepted 62.81% of deliberately wrong answers; one vendor score above the mathematical ceiling. Protocol choice moves scores ~36 points (Zep LoCoMo 58–95% by reader/judge/retrieval depth); independent reruns: Mem0 OSS ~32–49% vs 93.4% self-report. Judges: kappa-correct agreement (raw 80–85% deflates ~38 points; >half the judges shift 4+ rank positions). BEAM's scale rule: histories must exceed the reader window (10M tokens), else the benchmark tests context stuffing not memory. Four-rule eval spec: synthetic + mandatory human verification with reported edit rates + answer-key audit (~5% noise floor); per-ability decomposition; full protocol on every number; histories exceed the reader window with adversarial/abstention items. DMR saturated (mid-90s) — benchmark shelf life is real.

### 234. Serialization ops: memory-state envelope, optimistic concurrency, restore-fidelity tests (Fo, R39) — MEDIUM
Version-stamped blobs + load-time migration is the de-facto pattern; retrofitting version detection onto unversioned dumps is the most common migration failure. Memory-state envelope: `{schema_version, created_at, embedding_model_version, checksum}` on every checkpoint/export/migration output. Optimistic concurrency (sequence/version counters) rejects saves against stale versions — without it, lost-update corruption looks like "the agent forgot." Capture-time truncation silently degrades restore fidelity — verify round-trip equality on samples, not just load success. Embedding-model changes are the most expensive unplanned migration (full column reindex) — pin model versions in metadata, treat as major schema migrations. Soft-delete tombstones with a separate logged purge job; transactional migrations with rollback; documented JSON interchange format for cross-system transfer (no common standard exists — vendor lock-in is the default). Serialize tool-call history and pending approvals for resume safety — restore without them can double-execute actions. Compress-then-encrypt.

### 235. Regulated-vertical memory ops: per-jurisdiction retention, prompts+outputs as books and records, lineage bar (Fo, R39) — MEDIUM
Retention conflict: HIPAA 6–7yr and SOX/SEC/FINRA 5–7yr demand long retention; GDPR caps most logs at ≤90 days — per-jurisdiction retention profiles on the same store, with legal-hold overrides; a single global policy violates at least one regime by construction. FINRA (2025/2026): AI-generated and AI-assisted records — including prompts and outputs, not just deliverables — are books and records; most common failure is assumed coverage (memory store outside the archiving pipeline's scope). PII redacted at the memory-write path — the embedding already encodes it; PHI in an unencrypted vector store is a HIPAA exposure on landing. "Auditable memory" = versioned snapshots tied to agent state + attributable lineage (which memories influenced which actions) — the examiner asks "reconstruct why it did X." Supervision extends to memory reads/writes as surveilled objects; break-glass human review for consequential memory-influenced actions; vendor contracts need data-return/retention-handoff/destruction terms; automated deletion respects legal holds. Examiner export: record + approval + event + audit trail + index, human-readable and machine-usable. Legal-vertical (e-discovery/privilege) weakest-sourced — needs a follow-up pass.

### 236. Convergent law: provenance-gated writes + no silent overwrites across analysis and meeting memory (ChatGPT, R40) — HIGH
Two independent domains converged on the same two design rules: no memory write without a source (data-analysis: execution event graph — cell/code hash, input fingerprints, environment, seeds — must exist before the write commits; meeting: no timestamped transcript source span, no write); decisions event-sourced (append-only log with supersedes/reverses/clarifies edges; current-state views computed, never stored as the only record; a later statement is not automatically a reversal). Cache keys = data fingerprint + code hash + params + env, never code hash alone; semantic similarity suggests candidates, never silently authorizes reuse. Four stores, four lifetimes for analysis agents: live run state (discardable), curated durable knowledge (dataset cards, quality findings, tested snippets, failed approaches with reasons), provenance-indexed artifact cache (explicit invalidation), plus the provenance trail. Explicit uncertainty: owner/date/dependency ∈ {explicit, inferred, unknown} — invented deadlines/owners are the #1 extraction failure class. Privacy: pointers/recipes in memory, never raw rows. (Same consultant same day — convergence, not independent evidence.)

### 237. Tutoring memory: equivalence at 918× lower cost, pedagogy-over-scale, KT bands as student-model bar (Grok, R40) — MEDIUM
StudentBench (Sep 2026, 2,469 sessions): AI tutoring statistically equivalent to expert human tutoring (Δ −0.58pp, equivalence p=.015); best AI beat humans in 5/7 GRE domains; $0.0052 vs $4.81 per percentage point gained (~918× cheaper) — one-hour sessions, immediate post-test, adults only. Harvard physics RCT (peer-reviewed): AI tutor >2× the learning of active learning in 49 vs 75 min — pedagogy scripted into the tutor (one-step-at-a-time scaffolding) drove the effect, not model scale. Eedi × DeepMind (165 students): human-in-the-loop AI matched expert tutors (93.0% vs 91.2% mistake-fixing). Knowledge tracing: DKT ≈ 0.74, AKT ≈ 0.76, BEKT 0.8397 AUC on ASSISTments — the student-model reference bands; behavioral features (hints/attempts) lifted SAKT 0.509 → 0.900 AUC (preprint). LearnLM: vendor +31% expert preference, but independent teach-vs-solve diagnostic nearly tied on pedagogy (0.594 vs 0.592) — score memory systems on pedagogy dimensions, not solution correctness. Design: measure retrieval frequency and teach-vs-solve; cost-per-unit-of-gain as the efficiency axis; no randomized longitudinal learning-gains data exists anywhere found.

Peer-reviewed null (n=68): tablet/laptop/handwriting statistically indistinguishable on factual (p=.38) and conceptual (p=.61) recall — capture polish is a non-differentiator; invest in retrieval and reuse.
