Germany is a brand-home and a precision-manufacturing site whose finished-tool flow into India is real but unmeasured in-round; Korea, named in the brief's country line, has zero in-round evidence at all — no brand, no plant, no shipment. The UAE is neither brand-home nor origin: it is a re-export hub — half of the UAE's power-tool export value goes to India (2024), the "exporters" are named cargo consolidators (Freight System DWC, Mega Speed Cargo, Bin Thani), and Chinese drills enter Dubai at $21.90 a unit, dearer than what India pays China directly, because the hub sells logistics and grey-channel routing, not price. Who imports is three-tiered: the brands themselves are the biggest importers (Stanley Black & Decker India leads Volza's China-parts import table with 26,920 shipments, feeding its Pune assembly plant; a DeWalt angle grinder on Indian retail carries "Country of Origin India, Manufacturer Stanley Black & Decker India Pvt Ltd"); beneath them the distributors import Chinese-brand (DongCheng) finished tools in 160-piece lots; beneath them the filmed grey bazaar — Delhi's Meena Bazar, tools sold by the kilogram, ₹350 blowers, a commerce-rich YouTube culture that never mentions compliance once. And the domicile triad cuts the other way too: Bosch's Chennai plant has made 10 million tools since 2015 toward a 55% localization target and exports globally; Hilti's Vadodara plant (Aug 2023, ~300 people) makes only diamond consumables — the Hilti hammer itself comes from China or Europe. Official trade closes the loop: FY24-25 imports ₹4,359.7 crore (~$525M, ≈50% of the retail market's value) against exports ₹2,049.04 crore (~$247M, growing 2× faster at 22.5% CAGR) — import-dominated, yes, but with a two-way door and domestic making. The corpus rule to bank: in an import-dominated vertical, verify all three domiciles before naming an "import source" — brand-home, manufacturing-site, and import-source are independent variables, and the brief that conflates them will misread every enforcement and pricing story that follows.

### 1768. The battery is the product: platform capture in India's cordless shift

**Body:** India's cordless transition (30% of power-tool sales in 2023, doubling from 15% in 2020 — convergent across IMARC and zipdo) is not a tool upgrade cycle, it is a **platform capture cycle**. The Li-ion pack is 30–40% of a cordless tool's cost (India trade-press, dial4trade), and Indian buying guidance has already converged on the rule "pick the brand and range before you pick the individual tool" — because three incompatible battery systems multiply chargers, strand spares, and kill resale value. Once a buyer commits to a voltage platform (Bosch 18V, Makita 18V LXT, DeWalt 20V MAX, or the value-tier INGCO/BUILDSKILL 20V kits at ₹3,999–₹5,949), every subsequent tool purchase is captured: the marginal tool is cheap, the switching cost is the entire battery fleet. The GeM record shows capture reaching public procurement — a 2026 bid specifies not just "Commercial Cordless Portable Drill Machine, Make Bosch" but the exact model **GBH 185-LI** and its **18V 4.0Ah Li-ion battery**, writing one vendor's platform into a government tender. The ₹ floor makes the mechanism mass-market: value-tier 20V cordless kits undercut a single Bosch corded kit, so lock-in now starts at the bottom of the ladder (₹1,835 floor → ₹127,673 Hilti Nuron top, ~70× spread), not the top. For the memory program this is a **market-structure identity primitive**: the durable commercial identity is the battery platform, not the tool — the drill is the razor, the pack is the blade, and every downstream signal (tender specs, resale listings, service networks) keys to the platform. Watch for the failure mode: platform-branded tenders (brand + model + battery named) as procurement-side lock-in, and "21V" badge inflation on economy-tier packs as the wattage-inflation analog at the floor.

### 1769. The pack is the product — battery-pack identity as the counterfeit and keying fault line

Power tools are the first vertical where a *bought-in component* (the battery pack) outranks the finished tool as the identity object. The pack is a separately marked article (IEC 60745 Annex K.8.1: own rated voltage, maker/vendor ID, model/type reference, country of origin — no serial or batch required), a separately sold SKU (DeWalt DCB184-class retail packs; Samsung SDI's "Pack for Power Tool" sold as a validated line distinct from cells), and carries its own date identity (Milwaukee pack nameplates encode year/week of manufacture, digits 6–9, independent of the tool's serial). Platform lock-in (Makita 18V/40Vmax across dozens of SKUs) makes the pack — not the drill — the identity anchor customers accumulate and compatibility is keyed against. Meanwhile the tool body carries only voluntary, non-standard-prescribed serials: DeWalt's rating-label/stamped-body serials and its DDYY-plus-plant-letter date code (date and domicile in one string: D Mexico, E China, G Germany, T Taiwan), Milwaukee's 13-character alphanumeric serial encoding date of manufacture and service bulletin. The enforcement consequence is a dual-identity attack surface: fakers can counterfeit the tool body cheaply (housings are contract-molded shells; one shell is already reused across 7.2V–18V with different cell counts, per iFixit teardowns) while the real quality and safety live in the pack's cells and BMS — the component most commonly bought, most commonly cloned, and the one part the teardown-and-rebuild YouTube culture (18650 cell-swap videos, BMS wake-up tricks) teaches consumers to open and tamper with. Memory rule to carry: for power tools, key the pack and the body separately (tool serial vs pack serial/date-code), treat the pack as the distinct-identity node, and expect counterfeit forensics to fail whenever they authenticate the housing but not the cells. Idea class: identity-architecture; feeds challenger (keying) and fraud-instrument (T2) lanes.

### 1770. The wattage inversion: the cheapest drill prints the biggest number

On India's drill shelf the wattage number inverts with trust: Bosch's most-rated home drill is 500W (₹4,399), while the value tier prints 650–800W — iBELL 650W at ₹2,699, BUILDSKILL's "800W copper motor" at ₹5,949 — and CE marks get laundered as domestic trust signals on brands that never leave the subcontinent. With no QCO, there is no ISI mark to anchor genuine-vs-fake keying, so buyers key on price, dealer tenure, serials and holograms — and all of them are corroding: 23 of 86 Amazon drill listings print MRPs that "cannot be true," cross-brand battery adapters break the battery-as-genuine signal, and the entire BIS platform-as-party enforcement machine built for QCO goods cannot touch a vertical that has no QCO. Power tools' rich YouTube culture (shootouts, teardowns, restorations) contains zero compliance content — the hard-zero streak survives its first rich-YouTube vertical.

### 1771. The fossil QCO: dry batteries' 1987 mandate outlived its parent Act

**Thesis.** The hostile check on I4's brief found the mirror image of every prior record-rich round's failure: not a dead instrument in the brief, but a *fossil* one the brief couldn't even name correctly. The live mandate is the **"Multiple Dry Batteries (Quality Control) Order, 1987"** (S.O. 516(E), 25 May 1987, Dept. of Civil Supplies, in force 1 Oct 1987) — 39 years old, issued under **s.14 of the BIS Act 1986**, an Act repealed when the 2016 Act came into force on 12 Oct 2017. No amendment, supersession, or rescission surfaced; no replacement QCO under the 2016 Act's s.16 exists. The brief's title ("Multipurpose…", no year) swaps in the *standard's* adjective for the *Order's* — and the same swap is live on compliance-consultant pages, which is how the error propagates.

**Why it matters for the corpus.** (1) The scheme-geometry rule's **enforcement-age** axis now has its extreme case: a mandate older than the Bureau's current parent Act, kept alive by repeal-and-savings. (2) The **live-instrument rule gains a fifth prong**: Gazette title + year, ministry, in-force date, amendment chain, **and parent-Act repeal-and-savings status**. R287 taught us instruments can die silently after deferral; I4 teaches they can also *survive* silently after their parent Act dies. (3) Enforcement under a 1987 order means four decades of licence records, CM/L numbers, and factory inspections exist — the richest paper trail of any I-arc vertical, and a natural hunting ground for the misbranded (47th) and identity-fraud (69th) legs. (4) The adjective-swap is a reusable challenger subtype: briefs that name the *standard* where they mean the *instrument*.

**Testable follow-ups.** Pull S.O. 516(E) from egazette.nic.in to bank the title string at primary depth; sweep the corpus's other pre-2000 QCOs for repealed-Act survivors; check whether BIS's current mandatory-products list still cites the 1987 order or silently re-bases it on the 2016 Act.

### 1772. The paper-armed vertical: dry cells' dark identity-fraud record

**Thesis.** I4 is the first ARMED vertical in the corpus whose identity-fraud node is completely dark despite a live QCO (S.O. 3855(E), 13 Sept 2021): no named BIS fake-ISI seizure, no named counterfeit-brand docket (Duracell/Eveready/Nippo/Panasonic), no EPR paper-fraud case — misbranded 47th non-positive (streak 4), identity-fraud 69th at 2/3 unchanged, fraud streak 0 (96th). **Armed ≠ enforcement-armed.** A QCO with no docket is paper-armed; the corpus should mark the distinction explicitly rather than letting the "ARMED" tag borrow enforcement credibility the record does not show.

**The wrong-limb docket rule.** The one NAMED battery docket — the CCI cartel case (DG search & seizure 23 Aug 2016; Eveready ₹245.07 cr, Nippo ₹52.82 cr, Panasonic ₹74.68 cr; AIDCM facilitated) — belongs to the Competition Act, not the BIS Act. It must not populate the misbranded limb or the identity-fraud node. New challenger subtype: **wrong-limb enforcement docket** (same vertical, wrong instrument) — sibling of R287's adjacent-enforcement mirage (neighbouring vertical, any instrument). Synthesis check: whenever a leg banks a docket, record its instrument; a docket without an instrument tag is a mirage candidate.

**The scope-boundary gap.** Rechargeable NiMH/Li-ion AA/AAA cells are OUTSIDE the Dry Batteries QCO (convergent: ChatGPT, BIS Product Manual PM/IS 8144/3 Aug 2025 licensing scope R03/R6/R14/R20/6F22 S/P, compliance guides; rechargeables sit under IS 16046/MeitY CRS). They retail in the same channels as QCO-covered dry cells. New challenger subtype: **form-factor scope arbitrage** — a cell that looks like the regulated article, sells beside it, and is regulated under a different instrument buyers never see. Watch item: whether e-commerce listings of uncertified dry cells (Q6's lane) exploit this confusion.

### 1773. **The lane that closed: Eveready's Jammu plant ends the finished-alkaline import era six months before the brief noticed**

India's dry-cell market is a ₹4,000-crore chemistry ladder — 85% zinc-carbon (₹3,400 cr, 2–3% growth, overwhelmingly domestic-made) and 15% alkaline (₹600 cr, >20% growth) — and the brief's "alkaline import lane (China? Indonesia? Thailand?)" question arrived six months after the lane's biggest channel closed. On 22 April 2026 Eveready commissioned India's first and (claimed) only alkaline battery plant in Jammu — ₹200 crore greenfield, 360 million units a year at peak, 456 million installed — and CEO Anirban Banerjee said the company would "stop completely importing any finished goods for the alkaline batteries," raw materials excepted. The old geometry is now measurable history: Panasonic's shipment records still show the pre-closure pattern — EVOLTA AA cells from Thailand at $0.118 a cell (~₹10 landed against a ₹19–25 street price), button cells from China and Japan, CR1220s of Indonesian origin — China primary, Thailand a real second lane (brand-home Japan, manufacturing-site Thailand, import-source China: the domicile triad in one cell), Indonesia button-cell-only, Japan marginal lots. The value-density corollary explains why the lane lasted as long as it did: an AA cell is 23 grams and ₹15–19 at retail, so freight is a rounding error and import was *easy* — Jammu is not a logistics play, it is a margin play (Eveready guides ~10 percentage points of alkaline-margin uplift, toward 25% EBITDA) plus a QCO-era control play, with white-labelling and export ambitions attached. The split-domicile test (44th) passes with a live-transition annotation: sub-chapter 8506 imports ₹807.49 crore against exports ₹151.72 crore in FY24-25 — a structural −₹656-crore value deficit with a unit-surplus door (cheap zinc-carbon out, dear alkaline and specialty cells in) — but the import fifth of the market is now shrinking under the test instead of growing, the first time the corpus has caught a lane closing in-round. Two honest brakes: Duracell India's domestic-manufacturing status is unverified (a 1994 JV exists in the history books; no plant is named anywhere in-round, so it sits in the importer lane until proven otherwise), and the "only domestic manufacturer" superlative around Jammu sits in tension with Panasonic's and Duracell's claimed domestic capabilities — banked as a challenger, not a fact. The corpus rule to bank: in a high-value-density vertical, an import lane dies on margin and instrument, never on freight — and a brief that asks the lane's geography six months after its closure is the stale-premise analog of R287's silent rescission.

### 1774. The sleeve is the identity: dry cells have no body to forge

**Body:** R287 established the cordless battery pack as a distinct identity object — its own marking, its own SKU, its own nameplate, platform lock-in strong enough that "the battery is the product." The retail dry cell carries the same structure one layer weaker, and the weakness is the point: **a zinc-carbon cell is an anonymous can.** The zinc cup, the brass cap, the carbon rod carry zero identity. One hundred percent of the commercial identity — brand, chemistry, size, use-by date, and now the mandatory ISI mark — lives on a paper label or heat-shrink sleeve: a printable, peelable skin. Identity-detachability is total. Counterfeiting a premium cell costs a sleeve, not chemistry; Duracell's only hard forensics (the spot-welded false negative-terminal plate, the ink-dot codes) sit *under the wrap* where no buyer ever looks, and Which?'s field test is literally "if the outer skin peels off easily, it's a doppelganger." India in-round shows the phenomenon dark on dry cells specifically — no named Indian dry-cell counterfeit docket surfaced (honest negative; the named Indian battery enforcement is the CCI zinc-carbon cartel of 2018: ₹171.55 cr on Eveready, ₹42.26 cr on Nippo, Panasonic 100% leniency-waived) — but the adjacent mechanics are all live: a May 2026 Delhi Police racket seized a *printing press* churning out brand labels and retail packaging (the counterfeit choke point is the print shop, never the cell maker), and India's lithium trade runs the identical play with Grade-B cells under scraped QR codes. The armed instrument changes the keying game uniquely: with the Multipurpose Dry Batteries QCO making the ISI mark mandatory on R03/R6/R14/R20/6F22, the sleeve finally carries an identity layer a buyer can verify — the CM/L licence number checked against BIS's own registry in the BIS Care App — so keying **splits on the armed line**: HOLDS where the mark is checkable, FRAGILE in the loose-cell kirana lane where price and retailer are the only signals and no brand runs a hologram or scratch-code program. Watch the three failure modes: (1) sleeve-print shops as the counterfeit choke point — enforcement that raids warehouses but not printers misses the factory; (2) use-by date overprinting on the sleeve, the one buyer-keyed field (leg 1769 owns the marking clause); (3) white-label contracts — Eveready's Jammu alkaline greenfield (₹200 cr, India's only operating alkaline plant) is explicitly positioned for white labelling — turning legitimately sleeved cells into identity-commodities, the legal twin of the counterfeit mechanism. The memory primitive: identity strength is a function of binding depth — sleeve-only binding (dry cells) < housing-nameplate binding (R287's tool packs) — and the armed instrument's real anti-counterfeit work is giving the sleeve one verifiable anchor.

### 1775. THE EXPIRY-OR-CODE DATE

**Thesis.** After nine rounds without a batch-code PASS, dry cells deliver one — but in the weakest possible form. IS 8144's marking clause (cl. 8) delegates entirely to IS 6303 cl. 4.1.6, which mandates on each battery **either** an expiry ("expiration of a recommended usage period") **or** a manufacture date "which may be in code." The famous battery expiry is therefore **standard-prescribed**, made legally mandatory by the QCO's Scheme-I bite, and **not** prescribed by LMPC (whose "best before/use by" limb covers only commodities for human consumption, and whose package-level "month and year of manufacture" is a separate, clear, pack-level obligation). No batch number, lot code, serial, or heat number is prescribed at standard level — the batch and lot limbs are a definitive NO, and one certification consultant's "batch number, heat number" marking table is over-claim beyond the sighted text.

**Why it matters for the memory system.** This is the corpus's first sighting of a *disjunctive* identity prescription — the standard lets the manufacturer choose expiry *or* coded date, and the coding allowance is what creates the entire consumer date-code decoder genre. The memory lesson: a prescribed mark that "may be in code" is traceability for the manufacturer and opacity for the consumer — the mark exists, but the reading key is private. The convention stays OPEN because the corpus has not yet decided whether "may be in code" satisfies its traceability bar.

**Watch:** whether any future IS 8144 amendment (or the QCO schedule) hardens the disjunction into a clear-date requirement — the 2025 revision did not.

### 1776. The standard-anchored puff: when the ISI bench becomes the ad copy

**Thesis.** The challenger book has a new family: the *compliant* puff. Eveready Ultima's relaunch claims "400% / 800% longer-lasting performance" — and the fine print reads "400% longer lasting **than IS 8144: 2018 R6P standard for motor/toy**." The brand does not fake the ISI mark; it *cites* the mandatory standard as its ad comparator, borrowing the instrument's own test bench to substantiate a marketing multiple. Same campaign, second axis: "Turbolock Technology which **prevents leakage**" — a leak-proofness claim planted directly on the fragility axis the standard type-tests (IS 8144 cl. 9.6), where no consumer can re-run the bench.

**Analytic form:** in armed verticals, the final challenger evolution is not mark-forgery but mark-*citation* — the instrument's authority gets laundered into advertising, and the claim migrates to exactly the parameter (leakage) the standard measures but the buyer cannot verify.

**Watch rule:** whenever an armed-vertical brand's headline number is footnoted to an IS clause, treat the footnote as the fraud surface, not the substantiation. Banked into challenger as (a) standard-anchored puff and (b) anti-leak/fragility puff. Candidates held, not banked: expiry-date manipulation (Consumer Affairs Secretary, Apr 2026: date-rubbing is "a very, very huge problem"; 1.2 cr counterfeit listings on one platform — but no battery-specific case yet), made-in-China relabelling (honest negative).

### 1777. The number-injection rule: brief-supplied standard numbers are hostile until resolved

R289's hostile check found the brief's two "candidate" BIS numbers for mosquito coils — IS 3367 and IS 12979 — are both real standards for entirely unrelated products (burnt clay irrigation tiles; foundry linear-shrinkage moulds), while the actual coil standard IS 13438:1992 was unnamed by the brief. The method fix: any standard number arriving in a brief, a partner consult, or a case summary must be resolved against the BIS catalogue or a standard-text mirror before it is written into an analysis — the number is hostile input, not a citation. The same check caught the consult's Maxo→GCPL misattribution (two independent lines: retailer manufacturer field + trade press with GCPL-spokesperson data → Jyothy Labs), and the case summary's "Section 3(e)" licensing citation (operative provisions are s.12/13). Corpus-wide, this closes a recurring trap: numbers that look like precision are often the least-checked claims in the chain. Watch: whether the same number-injection pattern appears in future briefs for other armed-non-BIS verticals.

### 1778. The cession split fires twice in one vertical: sectoral register on content, IP law on name

The mosquito-coil vertical is the first armed-non-BIS vertical in the corpus, and its fraud record splits exactly the way R222's pesticide classifier predicted: the Insecticides Act 1968 bites the **content limb** — Maharashtra's 7 Feb 2026 statewide circular ordering raids, seizures, and prosecution against the unregistered mosquito agarbattis "Comfort" and "Sleep Well" (manufacturer M/S Dhoop Chaon/Chhav Company; director named in the FIR after the Santacruz West raid seized 29 boxes; Maharashtra Agriculture Dept lab detected the unapproved active **dimefluthrin**; earlier lab confirmation of Sleep Well in Andhra Pradesh; products sold under false "herbal" claims across TN, Maharashtra, UP, Delhi) — while the **name limb is ceded to IP criminal law**: every named Indian counterfeit docket in the category (West Bengal Police + GCPL, 18 Feb 2026, Kolkata & South 24 Parganas — S. Nawaz Stores Shyambazar, Sreehari Bhandar and Sarada Bhandar Sonarpur; the Jan 2026 Titagarh refilling unit with 2,540 ready twin-refill packs, 1,860 empty bottles, 6,200 labels, 6,500 cartons; Bengaluru CCB's ~Feb 2025 Kachohalli factory bust, ₹1.75 cr, labels from Surat printing hubs; the ~Oct 2022 Rajasthan Goodknight manufacturer, Bombay High Court suit) runs on **BNS + Copyright Act s.63**, never the Insecticides Act. One vertical, two fraud dockets, two registers — the s.29(1)(a) cession is not an agri-pesticide quirk but the standing geometry: **fraud domiciles wherever an armed register meets a claim margin, and the claim's limb picks the register.** The identity-fraud node's tiers read accordingly at 70th (2/3): T1 fake-CIR-number dark — the observed fraud is identity-**absence**, not identity-forgery; T2 counterfeit-brand fires at category level but is coil-form dark (every Indian counterfeit docket is LV liquid refills or mixed FMCG — zero named fake-coil dockets); T3 unregistered-identity fires named. Phase-3 implication: controllers must model the register split **within** a single vertical — the arming domicile (sectoral register) determines which fraud surface lights up, not the instrument family; and the CIR number (format CIR-XXXXX/XXXX) is the vertical's registry-mint candidate whose forgery has not yet been observed. Caveats: all dockets press-note grade, pre-trial; statewide seizure quantities unreported; one date approximate; coil-specific counterfeit and fake-CIR honest negatives held.

### 1779. The 18%-vs-grey tax wedge: GST misclassification as the agarbatti grey-lane's margin engine

**The mechanism.** Compliant mosquito coils and vaporiser refills sit at HSN 3808 → 18% GST (verified: Notification 9/2025-IT(Rate), 17 Sep 2025, Schedule II, effective 22 Sep 2025; bio-pesticide carve-out to 5%). EY's tax partner, in the April-2026 EY–HICA report, states on record that regulated household insecticides at 18% compete against "substandard alternatives that are often misclassified under lower slabs" — a structural, industry-attested asymmetry. Grey mosquito agarbattis (Comfort, Sleep Well — the Feb-2026 Maharashtra raid targets; Green India Marketing's shut unit in Telangana) sell at ₹1.7–2.1/stick into a market where the legal ₹1/night paper card (Good Knight Fast Card, ₹10/10pcs) already exists — so the grey lane's survival margin is *thin*, and a multi-point GST gap on the compliant side is what keeps that thin margin alive: every percentage point the grey lane avoids is a point of price cover against legal alternatives.

**Why it matters for the memory.** This is the I-arc's first *tax-wedge* fraud instrument: not a forged mark or a fake registration, but a classification-rate arbitrage where the evasion is built into the HSN choice itself. It also reframes the raids — enforcement treats agarbattis as an Insecticides-Act licensing problem (no CIR number), while the economic root is that compliant products carry 18% and grey ones effectively carry less. The EY–HICA 5%-cut ask is the industry's own proposed fix; if adopted, it would compress the wedge and — per HICA's claim — "increase government revenues through higher consumption" by formalizing the lane.

**Falsifiability.** The wedge is *asserted by EY/HICA* but not *measured*: no seized-agarbatti invoice has been published showing the lower slab actually claimed. The test is concrete — pull a Feb-2026 seizure inventory or a grey-agarbatti GST invoice and read the declared HSN/slab. If they declare 3808 at 18% and evade the *Insecticides Act* only, the wedge story dies and the grey margin is pure licensing-evasion. Also watch: the 5%-cut proposal's outcome (accepted → wedge compresses; rejected → wedge persists).

**Watch rule.** In any vertical where (a) the compliant product carries a high GST slab and (b) the grey lane exists in a neighboring HSN with a lower slab, check seizure invoices for declared-slab before theorizing the evasion mechanism — the tax gap may be the margin, not the license gap.

### 1780. The pack-only identity: CIR number as an anchor nobody can read

In armed-non-BIS verticals the statute writes an identity anchor the buyer cannot use. The Insecticides Act's misbranded definition permits exactly one registration-reference on a label — the registration number (s.3(k)(vii)) — and HICA confirms the CIR number (format CIR-XXXXX/XXXX, e.g. CIR-67468/2025) sits on the back or bottom of legal mosquito-repellent packs. But the mosquito coil itself carries nothing: no mark, no number, only color and smell — proxies forgeable at zero cost — and in the loose kirana trade not even a pack survives. The detachability ladder now runs housing-nameplate → sleeve-only (I4 batteries) → **pack-only binding** (I5 coils) → **proxy-only** (loose coils). GCPL's anti-counterfeit advice tells buyers to key on the sales invoice and a hotline; HICA's advice tells them to check the CIR number. Neither points at a lookup anyone can perform — no consumer-grade CIR verification tool exists in the public record. So keying splits: brand-pack coils hold thin on trust, while the loose and agarbatti-form channel is fragile by construction, and that is exactly where the ~₹300-crore illegal incense-stick market lives. Meanwhile the IS 19412:2025 agarbatti standard explicitly bans insecticides in agarbattis, so a "mosquito agarbatti" can never carry the BIS agarbatti mark — the two regimes partition cleanly in law and collide only in the buyer's perception, which is the fraud's entire business model: sell the name of an unarmed fragrance object wrapped around an unregistered insecticide. The policy gap is not a missing law but a missing reader: mandate a machine-readable, publicly checkable CIR lookup before the next enforcement cycle, because a prescribed anchor that cannot be verified is an anchor that protects nobody.

### 1781. The batch-code convention's first CLEAR PASS — a Rules-level mandate with a machine-readable batch tuple, and why the PASS is regime-conditional

The Insecticides Rules prescribe the batch tuple at statutory level, and the prescription has hardened three times: **1971** — Rule 19(1)(vi)–(vii), batch number + expiry date in indelible ink on the innermost container *and* the outermost covering (primary-text verified; no coded-date carve-out); **2016** — G.S.R. 797(E) substitutes Rule 19, adding date of manufacture + manufacturing licence number to the compulsory tuple (corpus-verified [A], R222); **2025** — the Pesticides (First Amendment) Rules (MoA&FW, June 2025, effective immediately; triple-source converged) require a **QR code on every retail insecticide packet resolving to unique identification/GTIN, batch number, manufacturing and expiration dates, and licence/manufacturer information**, with customer-care details and an explicit "For Household Use" indication on household products. Six-month compliance grace; non-compliant sale/stocking barred after thirty months (~Dec 2027). This is the convention's first CLEAR PASS because it is (a) statutory rather than standard-level, (b) uncoded — real dates, no "may be in code" escape — and (c) machine-readable. R288's open coded-date question is untouched by it: the convention stays OPEN on whether a coded date counts as traceability; I5 simply never offers the code option. **Design implication for Phase-3:** batch-code nodes need a `prescription_tier` (statute/Rules vs standard vs voluntary), a `machine_readable` flag (QR tuple), and a `transition_state` with dated phase-in windows (2025-06 → 2027-12) — "prescribed" and "present on shelf" are different states. And the PASS is **regime-conditional**: the ~30% illegal/unregistered burning-format segment (Godrej/HICA via PRNewswire 2021) carries no label tuple at all — the convention adjudicates what the regime prescribes, and prescription only bites registered goods (the R222 "generic-volume fraud as a distinct mode" in household form). Serial numbers remain unprescribed — the QR's "unique identification" is GTIN/product-level, so serial-1's 30th non-adjudication holds. For the coil vertical specifically, the bought-in finding sharpens the traceability picture: 75–95% of coil mass is domestic agri-waste + starch, but the intelligence layer (pyrethroid technical, <1%) is split between domestic manufacture (Shogun Organics — the GoodKnight/HIT lineage's own actives arm) and Chinese/Japanese imports, with formulation in domestic MSME units (Rs 8–25 lakh) — integration-depth-variable confirmed, and R222's "the technical active mints NOTHING" transfers: the CIBRC registration and the label's ingredient-% line are formulation-level, the technical is a cited pointer.

### 1782. The enforcer-switch: the platform-named-as-party doctrine reaches Insecticides-Act goods through CCPA, not BIS

**Thesis.** R288 banked the platform-named-as-party doctrine as a BIS-Act creature (11 Feb 2026 Lok Sabha reply: 344 samples, 142 uncertified, warehouse raids on Amazon/Instakart/Blinkit). I5 shows the doctrine is *statute-bound, not platform-bound*: for goods armed under the Insecticides Act, 1968 — mosquito coils, mats, agarbattis, all non-BIS — the platform's shield fails under a different letterhead. On 26 Sep 2026 the CCPA fined Amazon and Flipkart ₹10 lakh each and JioMart ₹5 lakh for facilitating the sale and advertising of unregistered 'Cyclosinone' Herbicide, holding that "online marketplaces cannot completely distance themselves from responsibility by arguing that products are listed by third-party sellers," citing **Rule 10(E) of the Insecticides (Second Amendment) Rules, 2022** — the e-commerce entity must verify the validity of the seller's licence *before* allowing online sale of insecticides — plus the Consumer Protection Act, 2019's due-diligence duty. The Insecticides regime thus has something the BIS regime lacks: an **explicit e-commerce verification duty written into subordinate legislation**, and a standing enforcement path (Agriculture Ministry complaint → CCFI representation → CCPA fine + takedown + self-audit + 15-day compliance report).

**The gap the idea names.** The challenger form is *assuming the BIS doctrine's absence means platform impunity*: analysts who check only the BIS surveillance list will file coils as unreachable. The reach exists — but the bite is on an agrochemical herbicide, not on the coil lane: Sleepwell agarbattis are "sold online across all-India" (Dec 2025) while every sighted coil/agarbatti enforcement action is offline (Mumbai raid, Andhra Pradesh investigation, the Feb-2026 Maharashtra statewide circular). **Armed-reachable, coil-unbitten.**

**Falsifiables.** (1) Pull the CCPA's three separate Cyclosinone orders — do they name Rule 10(E) identically, and did any compliance report disclose coil/agarbatti listings caught in the self-audits? (2) Search Amazon/Flipkart/Meesho for CIR-less mosquito agarbattis today — is the 2022 duty visibly enforced on this lane, or is the herbicide fine a one-off? (3) Check whether any state Agriculture Department has directed Insecticide Inspectors at *online* sellers (the Feb-2026 circular names only field retail). (4) Trace whether the Rule 10(E) duty has ever been invoked against a household-insecticide (non-agrochemical) listing — if not, the enforcer-switch is proven in law but untested in the lane that needs it.

**Carry.** Shadow 65th: ARMED — reachable, unbitten. Challenger 240/39 (+enforcer-switch). Watch rule for future armed-non-BIS verticals: *name the enforcer that switches with the statute before declaring the platform lane dark.*

### 1783. The LMPC mirror: India's only compulsory mark on a suitcase

Luggage is dark under BIS, CRS, and every ministry QCO checked — but it is *not* mark-free. Under the Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011, a pre-packed suitcase sold at retail must carry declarations: MRP, manufacturer/packer/importer name and address, month and year of manufacture, customer-care contact, and net quantity (1 piece). In a vertical with no ISI anchor, no CIR number, and no QCO, this LMPC declaration panel is the only statutorily prescribed identity a suitcase carries — and therefore the only domicile where a luggage fraud can be *fraud against a register* rather than just fraud against a brand. Research pass: (1) photograph/survey the declaration panels on 20 suitcases across tiers (unbranded ₹1,500 bazaar bag, Safari/VIP mid-range, Samsonite premium, one Chinese-marketplace import) and score completeness against the LMPC checklist — is the importer line present on the import lane, is month/year of manufacture real or fictional?; (2) check e-commerce listings for the same SKUs — does the declared MRP/importer on the physical pack match the listing?; (3) map any counterfeit-luggage incident (if leg 1778 surfaces one) to whether the LMPC panel was the forged element. The hypothesis: where BIS cannot reach, fraud domiciles on the last remaining compulsory mark — the packaged-commodities declaration — making LMPC the thin-record vertical's equivalent of I5's CIR number.

### 1784. Failed-docket discipline: give every identity-fraud tier a verdict bit, and separate incumbent-imitation from shadow-counterfeit

The 1998 Samsonite v Vijay Sales docket is the series' first failed misbranding claim: named, dated, luggage-specific — but the Delhi HC dismissed the interim injunction and vacated the ad-interim order (para 74; market survey rejected as "cooked up", para 72). A binary fired/not-fired node would log this as a T2 hit indistinguishable from a successful one. Fix: every T1/T2/T3 entry carries a verdict bit — decreed/dismissed, injunction granted/vacated, ex-parte/contested, damages quantified — so the node records the ALLEGATION and the FINDING separately. Second split from the same docket: the 1998 defendants are organized incumbents (V.I.P. Industries, Blowplast) imitating trade dress, while the 2024 defendant (Titli Enterprise, Hooghly) is a shadow operator forging identity marks. These are two different fraud topologies — incumbent trade-dress imitation vs underground brand forgery — and the memory model should subtype the actor, not just the claim. Falsifiable: re-score nodes 1–70 with the verdict bit and report how many "fires" were actually failed claims.

### 1785. The hard-soft domicile pivot: key every market-structure cell per product form, not per vertical

**The mechanism.** In luggage, the single most predictive variable is not the brand, the price, or the HSN — it is whether the bag is **hard-shell or soft**. The Ken's line is the whole story in one sentence: hard luggage "does not require physical labour to stitch" and is "easily done domestically," while soft luggage "is usually made in China and Bangladesh because these countries have a more advanced and efficient textile ecosystem." Everything else pivots on this: hard-shell domiciles in Nashik and Halol (India); soft-shell domiciles in China and Bangladesh; the import lane is form-specific; the split-domicile archetypes (A/B/C) are all form-keyed; and even the GST row (HSN 4202 → 18%) treats both forms identically, which is precisely why a GST-based analysis would miss the divergence. The form split is not luggage trivia — it is the vertical's load-bearing joint, and the brief's player list (VIP/Safari/American Tourister) is meaningless without it because each player straddles both forms with different domicile strategies (VIP: hard in Nashik, soft imported; Safari: hard in Halol, soft imported; Samsonite: hard in Nashik, mass-market lines in China/Vietnam).

**Why it matters for the memory.** The memory's market-structure cells — split-domicile, bought-in, import-lane, even brand ladder — are currently keyed **per vertical**. Luggage proves that keying is too coarse: a per-vertical split-domicile verdict collapses three real archetypes into one false average ("the luggage market is import-dependent" is false; "the luggage market is domesticated" is also false — the hard lane is domesticated, the soft lane is imported). The design fix: any vertical with a **rigid/fabric (or equivalent form) split** gets sub-cells keyed per form before any per-vertical rollup. The rollup, if it exists at all, carries a `form_pivot: true` flag so downstream consumers never read the vertical-level cell as a claim about either form.

**Falsifiability.** The pivot is falsified for luggage if (a) any of the three archetypes is shown to be domicile-inverted on re-verification (e.g., Safari's hard luggage turns out to be substantially imported, or Mokobara's is substantially India-made), or (b) a vertical with a clean hard/soft split shows form-invariant domicile (all forms made in the same factories in the same countries) — in which case the pivot is luggage-specific lore, not a memory design rule. Also testable: the bought-in leg (Q5) should find the hard bill (polycarbonate/ABS shells, wheels, handles) domesticated and the soft bill (textile ecosystem) offshore — if it finds the reverse, the pivot breaks.

**Watch rule.** When a new vertical's product catalogue splits into a rigid form and a fabric/textile form (luggage, footwear, furniture, tents, prams), key the first market-structure draft per form and only roll up with the pivot flag — never let the vertical-level cell launder a form-specific fact.

### 1786. Minted-model vs minted-unit: keying must type what the warranty actually mints

**The finding.** Samsonite's warranty system mints a *model-level* product ID (alphanumeric code + QR label on the warranty card and inside the bag; my.samsonite.com decodes it to product info — a SKU lookup, not a unit registry), registration is explicitly optional, and claims key to invoice + inside tag. TUMI — the premium exception, Samsonite-owned — mints a *unit-level* 20-digit Tracer ID engraved on a metal plate, registered to the owner in a central database, doubling as authenticity verification (in service since 2004; 10,000+ recoveries in 2021). No mass-market Indian luggage brand (VIP, Safari, American Tourister) shows evidence of minting anything unit-unique. The warranty card buyers treat as an identity token is the most forgeable carrier in the stack.

**The design implication.** Keying nodes need a `mint_tier` attribute — `unit-serial` / `model-code` / `none` — because "the warranty is the closest thing to a registry" is false at two of the three tiers: a model-code lookup *looks* like a registry to buyers but cannot distinguish a counterfeit carrying a copied genuine code, and at the `none` tier there is nothing to look up at all. Buyer-verifiable lookup ≠ registry; only unit-unique + database-match resists code-copying, and even that fails against unauthorized-channel sales (fake tracer tags stamped on imitations). Keying 66th therefore resolves COMMERCE-ONLY: channel, price, and inspection carry the load the minting tier cannot.

**Falsifiable test.** Buy one genuine Samsonite unit, copy its product ID onto a counterfeit listing's documentation, and run both through my.samsonite.com — both resolve identically, proving the lookup is model-keyed. The TUMI control: two Tracer IDs resolve to two distinct owner records.

### 1787. The fossil-standard problem: when the only marking clause in the vertical doesn't cover the product — and the serial number that isn't

I6 is the first vertical whose *only* marking standard is older than the product it regulates: IS 8518:1977 — the one luggage standard I could read at clause depth — covers **leather and leather-cloth suitcases** (§1.1, Table 1), a full generation before polycarbonate/ABS shells. Its marking clause (§8) is an **exhaustive negative enumeration**: manufacturer name or trade-mark + size, and nothing else — no batch, no lot, no serial, no date. Combined with evtlindia's own admission that IS 8517:1977 sits **outside BIS compulsory certification**, and a certification-consultant house carrying *self-contradicting* mandatory/optional claims on the same URL family (the R289 consultant-over-claim subtype, now in self-refuting form), the batch-code question adjudicates cleanly: **53rd non-adjudication**, the mirror pole to R289's CLEAR PASS — and the convention gains a new instance type, *negative-enumeration*, for Phase-3 schema work. On serials, the vertical's flagship brand proves the negative: Samsonite's "product ID" (my.samsonite.com portal, warranty card, QR label, interior white label) is a **SKU-level model/colour/size code shared by every unit of the model** — registration is explicitly optional, warranty runs on model number + proof of purchase, and no unit-unique serial is minted anywhere. Worse, consumer guides tell buyers to "check the serial number" to spot fakes — a **verification-theatre** check that terminates at "a number exists," which a counterfeit satisfies with any plausible SKU string (proposed challenger subtype). The bought-in cell confirms integration-depth-variable with the luggage fingerprint: Safari molds PC/PP **in-house at Halol** (₹22 cr brownfield, 80k pcs/month, own moulds/handles/wheel systems) and VIP runs 10 in-house plants — deeper integration than anything seen in the arc — while **soft luggage is bought-in finished from China** and the component layer (YKK India zippers, the Nashik trolley/wheel/lock cluster) splits domestic-specialist vs import. Identity-persistence adjudicates **multi-homed-physical / single-homed-claim**: brand mark on shell + SKU on interior label + warranty card + lining print, but every home carries the same non-unique identifier — the detachability ladder extends to *mark-only*, below R289's pack-only. The Phase-3 implication: identity nodes need a `prescription_tier` (here: none) and a `uniqueness_scope` (here: brand/SKU only — no unit scope exists), because a vertical can have four identity homes and still mint zero unit identity.

### 1788. The doctrine has two limbs — in QCO-free verticals only the deception limb can fire

**Finding (research-derived):** The platform-named-as-party doctrine is not a single QCO-tethered hook (as R287 formulated it: "procured under QCOs" → no QCO means no platform liability). R289's enforcer-switch already showed the doctrine is **statute-bound, not platform-bound** — it rides whichever statute arms the vertical (BIS Act for toys: Snapdeal ₹5L; Insecticides Rule 10(E) for agrochemicals: Meesho/Flipkart ₹10L). This leg splits the doctrine into **limbs**: the **compliance limb** (failure to list/verify a certification that the law requires) genuinely cannot reach luggage — no QCO, nothing to verify, R287's conclusion stands on this limb. But the **deception limb** (CPA 2019 §2(28) misleading advertisement / §2(47) unfair trade practice; "substantial control" test; the caveat-venditor shift) carries **no certification precondition** — it bites platforms that facilitate *counterfeit-branded* Samsonite/VIP luggage or phishing storefront funnels, for deception, not for missing a mark. The shadow lane for luggage is counterfeit (name limb), not compliance; so the doctrine's reachable surface here is exactly the shadow's shape. **Doctrine-domicile corollary:** fraud domiciles wherever an armed register meets a claim margin (R289's cession split) — and so does the enforcement hook; name the *limb* before declaring the doctrine dark, because a blanket "no QCO → doctrine can't reach" silently cedes the deception limb that the platform fines actually run on. Status: armed-reachable, luggage-unbitten (no luggage-specific CCPA order sighted — honest negative). **Design implication:** the platform-as-party node needs a `limb` attribute (compliance vs deception) and an `armed_register` pointer per vertical; "doctrine dark" verdicts must cite the limb, not the vertical.

### 1789. The brief-falsification rule: Firozabad has a GI, and the hostile check must shoot at the brief first

> **[R291 arbitration retag]:** the idea's "registered 2014" is ODOP-compendium drift. The register dates it **09.02.2009, applications 155 & 156** (two independent DPIIT Lok Sabha annexes; legs 1784, 1787). 2014 is the journal-window confusion family (idea 1744) — corpus 2014-grep scheduled at closeout.

The R285 brief said Firozabad glass bangles had "NO GI (verified absent)" — the I-arc's no-GI third case, the foil to H7's hollow GI and H8's inhabited GI. It was wrong. "Firozabad Glass" is a registered GI, carried in the official ODOP compendium and the Ministry of Textiles GI book. The foil geometry inverts: Firozabad is not the no-GI case — it is the fourth state-filed UP GI alongside Moradabad's, with the same hollow-risk signature (state applicant, renewal unverified, authorized-user list unknown). The round's method finding: the hostile-check mandate must aim at the coordinator's own brief claims first — R285's audit said it ("the coordinator's own briefs are falsifiable") and R291 proved it. Paired with the IS 8702 confabulation in the same leg (a brief-injected number returned by the partner with a fabricated title and edition), the lesson is that briefs are the highest-risk lore vector in the corpus — they are cited by later legs as settled. New convention proposal: every brief claim carries a one-line provenance tag (audit-verified / exam-key lore / single-source), and any claim reused in a question file must survive its own leg's hostile check before the idea block is written.

### 1790. The unbitten register: a GI that has never been enforced is an instrument in name only

**Body.** Firozabad's glass cluster holds a registered Geographical Indication — "Firozabad Glass (Logo)", applications 155 & 156, registered 09.02.2009 per a Lok Sabha annexure of the Ministry of Commerce & Industry. The GI Act 1999 arms it twice over: s.22 civil infringement for false origin indication, ss.39–44 criminal punishment (6 months–3 years + fine) for falsifying or falsely applying a GI. On the observable record, no one has ever pointed either weapon at fake-"Firozabad" bangles: no court docket, no consumer-commission order, no seizure, no REACH/lead case — the enforcement cell is dark across two independent sweeps and a partner consult. The cluster's name is therefore protected in statute and unprotected in practice, and that split is a new typology entry distinct from the arc's earlier GI failures: H7's GI was hollow (registered but its goods absent from the market narrative); H8's was uninhabited (registered, nobody there to use it); Firozabad's is **unbitten** — inhabited by 400+ units, commercially live, and still never invoked against a false origin claim. The design rule: an armed register without an enforcer is indistinguishable from a dark vertical to every buyer, counterfeiter, and platform in the market — the register's existence changes the *legal* answer to "can this be misbranded?" from no to yes, while the *market* answer stays no. Corollaries banked in-leg: (1) "Firozabad-style" imports are style-vs-origin, not per se unlawful — the actionable event is a false origin claim, which requires someone to allege it; (2) ODOP branding confers no exclusivity — the only IP-grade logo in the cluster is the GI logo itself, and keying (67th) should test whether it appears anywhere in the retail channel; (3) the brief-premise falsification is itself method data — the R285 direction audit asserted "NO GI (verified absent)" and the GI Registry, via a government annexure, said otherwise; treat every absence claim in a direction audit as a hostile-check target, including the auditor's. Challenger subtypes proposed: official-record falsification of an audit premise; hazard-reporting-without-docket (lead/cadmium scare content naming no case); registration-year drift across secondary GI compilations (2009 vs 2012–13). Misbranded 50th: GI-armed, enforcement-dark (non-positive on dockets). Identity-fraud 72nd: 3/3 held — M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu (10 Dec 1996, labour directions naming the Firozabad glass industry) and Swan Bangle Stores v. ASO Firozabad (tax classification, single-commodity holding) are named dated dockets logged under verdict-bit discipline, not counted toward fraud.

### 1791. The apex-base split

On a vertical with **no QCO, a never-invoked GI, and Nil GST** (legs 1783/1784/1787 retag this leg's "no GI" framing; the finding below stands), the regulatory action lives at the furnace apex and dies at the worker's doorstep. **The apex:** ~400 registered pot/tank furnaces, GAIL-gas metered, the 1996 Taj-Trapezium coal ban the vertical's one real regulatory event — two-speed transition (muffle and pakai bhatti units stayed on coal, ~100,000 t/yr at the time), the 2026 Gulf gas shock (−40% output, 25–45% small-unit losses) the tariff-shock analog. **The base:** belan/sekai bangle furnaces and home-based finishing/decorating (ladayi/jodai, female, unregistered, piece-rate) — children: ChildFund (Feb 2026) reports ongoing home-based involvement ("industry prefers children — smaller hands") against the official Lok Sabha record of 4,656 identified (old); the Child Trust's ">50,000" is advocacy-grade, unverified. **The H7 erosion analog is rejected as framed:** no Chinese import flood into Indian retail, no glass→plastic substitution. Chinese factories sell "Firozabad"-branded bangles in B2B lanes (name-hijack, leg 1788) — offshore genericization, not retail invasion. The real erosion: demand migrated **up** to metal jewellery, and furnaces re-tasked to **bottles/lighting** (higher margin, machine-made). Brand ladder (₹/dozen): ₹15 plain floor → ₹80–90 designer wholesale box → ₹500–3,000 bridal sets; no consumer brand mints a mark — price keys to decoration weight, not identity. **Design rule:** on a craft vertical, mint the tier, not the bangle — registered, metered apex above unregistered, female, home-based base; fraud, labour and quality key to which side of the bhatti a question sits on. (Grok-lens, R291, research-derived, leg 1785.)

### 1792. The toponym did the work: Firozabad's identity with a never-invoked GI — and what that says about GI's marginal product

> **[R291 arbitration retag]:** leg 1786 filed this under the brief's falsified "no GI" premise. The GI **exists** — "Firozabad Glass (Logo)", registered 09.02.2009, appl. 155/156 (legs 1784, 1787). The experiment is therefore not no-GI: it is **GI-registered, commercially inhabited, never invoked** — the unbitten register (idea 1790). The leg's mechanism findings (what fills the identity vacuum) stand; only the premise framing changes: the register exists and still nobody uses it, which moves the yield from "identity is independent of legal architecture" to **"GI function tracks enforcement, not existence"**.

The H-arc's GI pair set up the experiment: H7 (Moradabad) — GI registered 2009, state-filed, zero authorized users, a dead letter. H8 (Bhadohi) — GI registered 2010, trade-filed, wielded by weavers as brand leverage in the 2012 district-name fight. Firozabad (retagged) is the third case: **GI registered 2009, inhabited by 400+ units, never invoked** — and the identity persists via the toponym anyway.

What fills the vacuum, ranked by evidentiary weight: (1) the toponym itself as generic descriptor — "Firozabad bangles" is a product-type noun in exam questions, IndiaMART categories, and Alibaba listings, unowned and unenforceable; (2) "Suhag Nagari," the cultural nickname, carrying the affective identity in the community-place bond; (3) ODOP state promotional branding — the state as identity BACKER without being a rights GRANTOR; (4) seller/channel identity — no consumer bangle brand in the record, only B2B wholesale names; (5) SEO-mill fabricated keying rituals — Alibaba buying guides inventing "ask for the artisan's village name and kiln number," invented master artisans, pseudo-certifications ("SGS tested") because there is no enforced statutory anchor to key against.

Keying 67th: PLACE-NAME-ONLY — buyers key on place-descriptor + seller + price tier + sensory inspection, below R290 luggage's COMMERCE-ONLY (the GI logo is a carrier that exists but is retail-invisible — the behavioral state holds with the unbitten-register qualifier). Identity-persistence 65th: EXTERNAL-ONLY — nothing lives on a bangle; the detachability ladder's true bottom; identity homes are the place, the box, the seller, the channel, state promotion. (Lore discipline held: the "Mughal-era" origin is lore-carry — scholarly tier says glass arrived ~1920; do not repeat as fact.) (Grok-lens, R291, research-derived, leg 1786, retagged at arbitration.)

### 1793. The latent-batch non-adjudication: the bangle's furnace has a batch, the bangle doesn't — and a heavy-metals regime would mint exactly it

R291 runs the batch-code convention against Firozabad's handmade glass bangle and finds a species R268's sitar didn't have: the physical lot construct EXISTS — each pot/tank furnace fill is a 12-hour, colour-mixed melt ("batch" is the trade's own word for the raw-material charge: silica sand, soda ash, limestone, 15–50% cullet, and the oxide bill — arsenic, lead, cadmium, zinc, copper, cobalt, selenium, manually mixed) — yet no token is ever minted from it. The lot dies at the gathering stage: the gulliwalla's glob becomes a belan-bhatti spiral (~368 bangles per muttha), diamond-cut, judai-joined by women at kerosene lamps, pakai-annealed, decorated in household units, strung on tora, boxed — bangles from different melts intermingle at every step, and the only date token in the vertical is the LMPC month/year-of-manufacture on the pack, seller-asserted and never batch-tied. Batch-code 54th therefore non-adjudicates on a NEW instance — the latent batch (upstream lot present, unminted downstream) — distinct from R268's 49th (no lot construct at all) and R290's 53rd (fossil-standard negative enumeration). Draft rule: batch-code adjudication must record WHERE the lot construct dies, because the latent kind is enforcement-activatable — the furnace batch is precisely the instrument a lead/cadmium regime would attach to, and the cullet loop that recycles broken bottles and furnace trimmings is already carrying those metals back into the melt. The absence is interesting for exactly this reason: it is not the sitar's structural absence but a dormant traceability circuit, visible only because the batch vocabulary survives buyer-side ("check color consistency across batches" in sourcing guides) while no seller mints it. Corollaries: (a) the vertical's identity architecture is article-void — no maker's mark, no serial (32nd non-adjudication, R268's rule unmodified), GI "Firozabad Glass (Logo)" 2009 mark-layer with no use sighted; (b) the round's "no-GI" premise is a phantom absence — the GI exists (registered 09.02.2009, appl. 155/156, two DPIIT Lok Sabha annexes), which is the symmetric failure to R268's phantom GIs and proposes the phantom-absence challenger subtype. (Fo-lens, R291, research-derived, 1787)

### 1794. Offshore genericization: the functional no-GI vacuum is the fraud instrument

> **[R291 arbitration retag]:** leg 1788 filed this under the falsified "no GI" premise. The register **exists** (09.02.2009, appl. 155/156) — but it is inhabited-and-never-invoked, retail-invisible, and unreached offshore. The vacuum is functional, not legal. The design rule retags accordingly: "protected term, no plaintiff" — the register's existence without an enforcer creates a fraud surface with no one to allege it.

**Finding (research-derived):** In a vertical with no QCO and a never-invoked GI, the shadow lane is not compliance evasion — it is **place-name genericization through the functional vacuum**. Documented at two depths: Guangdong Xuping Jewelry Co., Ltd. (China, 10 yrs, 4.9/5.0) sells bangles on Accio/Alibaba's B2B network under the verbatim title "51550 Xuping Firozabad Glass Indian Multicolor Silk Thread Online Bangles" — a Chinese manufacturer marketing "Firozabad" as a style keyword for products that may never have touched the cluster (and whose "glass" core is itself questionable next to the "silk thread" construction). With a GI nobody enforces, "Firozabad" is free text in every marketplace search index; offshore sellers ride the descriptor for its cultural-signalling value, and no Indian statute reaches the B2B cross-border seller. The platform-named-as-party doctrine's limb-split (1782) reaches its limiting case here: the compliance limb can't fire (nothing armed), and the deception limb (CPA 2019 §2(28) origin claims) has nothing falsifiable to grip in practice — "Firozabad style" keyword-stuffing is not, as written, a lie about a mark anyone defends. **Corollary for the memory design:** the identity-fraud node needs a *vacuum-exploitation* subtype distinct from forgery — fraud as identity-*absence* (R289 banked identity-absence for coils; here the register's absence-of-enforcement is mined by third parties). And the fraud-domicile rule ("fraud domiciles wherever an armed register meets a claim margin") gets its mirror image: **where no register is enforced, the claim margin is mined at zero enforcement cost — fraud domiciles in the vacuum itself.** Status: shadow ACTIVE on the name limb (offshore), doctrine armed-reachable-but-unbitten, GeM NEGATIVE, fragility FRAGILE (most literal of the corpus: 15–20% transit damage, annealing-dependent breakage, no type test). **Design implication:** identity nodes need a `register_absent` flag that, when set, flips the verdict logic — "no enforced term" is not "no fraud," it is "fraud with no plaintiff." (Fo-lens, R291, research-derived, 1788, retagged at arbitration.)

### 1795. The mandatory turn: watch the Handloom Mark draft regs, not the mark

> **[R292 arbitration]:** leg 1791 flagged this as "potentially now live"; leg 1789's gazette sweep resolved it: **draft, NOT in force** (no Gazette commencement found). Watch item retained, not banked. Challenger note: leg 1789 proposed this find as subtype 40; consolidated at arbitration to 272/40.

**Body.** The Handloom Mark has been a voluntary authenticity label since 28.06.2006 — no product standard behind it, no BIS instrument anywhere near handloom cloth (armed-BIS stays 27/12/19), and the 1985 Reservation Act never touched identity. That is the thin-regulatory picture the brief described, and it is accurate today. But the draft **Handloom Mark Standards (Labelling and Display) Regulations, 2025** (WTO-notified 11 Mar 2026, file 739623/2026/STCGI) would convert the vertical: s.5 makes the label **mandatory for anything marketed as "Handloom"**, with registration-via-Textiles-Committee-regional-offices, on-site loom/supply-chain verification, numbered/QR labels, inspection, **search and seizure**, and penal provisions under the Trade Marks Act (ss.101–104, up to 3 years) and the Textiles Committee Act. If gazetted, handloom becomes the corpus's next **armed-non-BIS** vertical (I5's Insecticides Act is the precedent) — armed through Textiles Committee + Trade Marks Act, not BIS — and the first mandatory origin-labelling regime for a craft vertical in the corpus. That matters because the GI layer is heavy but retail-thin (77 register entries under a strict weave rule; ministry claims 57→65): a mandatory mark with seizure powers is the instrument that could actually **bite** where the GI register sits unbitten (I7's foil). **Action:** (1) Gazette-commencement watch on the 2025 regs — the brief-expiry rule fires the day it notifies; (2) when live, re-run the keying/shadow legs: does the mandatory label reach retail, or does it become another unbitten register?; (3) bank the companion find — **phantom-QCO compliance-SEO fabrication** (rcgeotech.com inventing "IS 15623:2026"/"IS 15620:2026" mandatory bridal/wedding-attire regimes with mutually inconsistent dates and a number squatted from the 2005 Melamine standard) — treat every "new mandatory BIS" claim from consultancy SEO as hostile until a Gazette S.O. number is produced. (ChatGPT-direct, R292, leg 1789.)

### 1796. The half-bitten register: Pochampally's FIR and Assam's unprosecutable seizures

**Body.** I7's foil question — "is there a bitten handloom register anywhere?" — answered: **partly bitten.** **Pochampally Ikat: FIR filed 17 December 2015** at the Pochampally Police Station, Telangana, by the GI's authorized users against sellers/manufacturers of duplicate GI-registered product — triple-sourced (Textiles Ministry Jan-2016 release reproduced by fibre2fashion, in.apparelresources.com, indian-apparel.com), the only corpus instance of a ministry-level GI-enforcement directive in textiles; disposition dark (fires at complaint/docket level, not verdict level). **Assam gamocha lane: seizures biting since 1 March 2023** while adjudication is structurally blocked — no designated lab can distinguish handloom from powerloom (the lab gap); the test gap is a metrological block, distinct from non-invocation. **Banarasi GI: still unbitten** ("not one person has been hauled to jail," Crafts Revival Trust ~2011, unrebutted). Different fabric GIs occupy different bite states. Misbranded 51st: GI-ARMED, PARTLY BITTEN — the first bitten fabric-GI in the corpus. Identity-fraud 73rd: 2/3 (T1 + T3 fire, T2 dark; Hindustan Fashions 1984 logged under verdict-bit discipline, quarantined from the retail node). **GI-bite geometry is now five states:** hollow (H7 Moradabad), brand-leveraged-political (H8 Bhadohi), unbitten (I7 Firozabad), half-bitten (I8 Pochampally), brand-leveraged-commercial (I8 Banaras). **New convention:** when a GI-enforcement lane bites at seizure but cannot adjudicate, check *why* the adjudication lane is dark — a metrological block (no test method) is a different darkness than non-invocation, and it points at the exact instrument gap. Candidates proposed (not banked): complaint-gated enforcement structure (GI Act appoints no enforcement mechanism; monitoring sits with producer associations — structural, semantics call); seller-published authentication guides as verification theatre (behavioral variant, banked separately as challenger +1). (ChatGPT-direct, R292, leg 1790.)

### 1797. The wedding tax is blind: a ₹2-lakh Banarasi and a ₹6,000 Banarasi pay the same 5%

> **[R292 arbitration]:** the idea's "if the WTO-notified mandatory Handloom Mark is in force (flagged, unverified)" is **resolved by leg 1789: draft NOT in force.** The ladder-blindness finding stands unchanged.

A handloom Banarasi saree climbs a 160× brand ladder — genuine handwoven pure-silk entry at ₹6,000–8,000, heavy kadhua-woven bridal with dense zari jaal up to ₹50,000, real-zari kadhua/jaal bridal at ₹80,000–2,00,000, and heirloom Kadiyal/Tanchoi/Shikargah/Jangla pieces at ₹2,00,000–5,00,000+ — while powerloom and blended copies occupy every rung below at ₹3,000–12,000 (commerce-tier: Sacred Weaves price guide, Kankatala, MySilkLove; plain Chanderi handloom fabric retails ₹1,090–1,250/metre). The 56th GST Council (3 Sept 2025, effective 22 Sept 2025) cut handloom/handicraft items from 12% to 5% and left sarees — CBIC's "unstitched fabric," taxed at 5% "of any value or fabric" — untouched. That means the tax instrument cannot see the ladder at all: a fake ₹2,500 powerloom "Banarasi" and a ₹2,00,000 genuine kadhua-jaal bridal saree attract identical 5% GST, and the much-publicized 18% above-₹2,500 apparel slab never touches a saree of any price. In a vertical where the erosion equation is substitution + import-flood + name-hijack, the state's revenue instrument is ladder-blind — the price signal that could separate rung from rung exists only in the retailer's honesty and the buyer's eye. Idea exploration: (a) does any other corpus vertical have a tax instrument that is *structurally* blind to its brand ladder (compare I7's Nil, which is ladder-blind in the opposite direction); (b) if the mandatory Handloom Mark ever comes into force, does the compliance cost bite the ₹6,000 rung harder than the ₹5L rung — i.e., does identity enforcement have a regressive ladder incidence? (c) the keying question Q4 inherits: with price-only differentiation at retail, the 160× spread collapses to trust — which is exactly the channel the fake-Banarasi lane lives in. (Grok-lens, R292, research-derived, leg 1791.)

### 1798. The selvedge is the signature

The Handloom Mark and the fabric GIs do not compete — they certify different things, and the trade knows it: Silk Mark is the fibre, Handloom Mark is the process, GI is the provenance. "No single certification covers all three" (saartaj). By design, complement. On the shelf, coexistence — but only at the premium tier: Taneira (Tata) was newsworthy in August 2025 precisely for being "among the earliest" to stack GI tags onto collections that already carried the Handloom Mark and Silk Mark, and for doing the GI paperwork *with* the artisan clusters. If stacking were normal, it wouldn't be news.

The Banaras GI (applied July 2007 by nine weaver-and-government bodies, registered 4 September 2009) is therefore not hollow like Moradabad's (H7) and not unbitten like Firozabad's (I7) — it is **brand-leveraged, commercial variant**: premium retail pulls it as a trust lever ("GI-certified," weaver information on the tag), the state pulls it as a branding campaign (QR authentication, 'Silk Banarasi' trademarking), while the fakes it was registered to stop — Surat and Chinese powerloom sold as Banarasi — keep selling, enforcement stays dark, and "the grant of GI status has not changed the fortunes of the artisans" (TERI; Cambridge's "Vanity GIs" chapter concurs). H8's Bhadohi GI was brand-leveraged politically (the district-renaming fight); Banaras is brand-leveraged commercially. Same state, different hand on the lever. The corpus doctrine extends: **the GI works as a sign, not a shield.**

Buyers, meanwhile, key "real handloom" the way Firozabad buyers key glass — place-name, seller, and their own senses — *as if the registered anchors barely existed*. The difference is the article cooperates: the selvedge (pinholes, wavy edge, hand-finished fringe) and the reverse (floats, knots, kadhua interlocks) carry the process signature in the cloth itself. The Handloom Mark's retail footprint is thin (Salem: 250 of 28,000 weavers registered by 2009; Odisha: only export pieces carry it), its gate is open to any trader willing to buy labels, and buyers mostly don't know it. So identity lives in two places that barely meet: **in the selvedge, where the weave authenticates itself, and on detachable tags, where the state authenticates it** — selvedge-persistent, the corpus's first article-self-authenticating form.

Watch the expiry date: the draft Handloom Mark Standards (Labelling and Display) Regulations, 2025 (WTO-notified 11 March; adoption expected 1 April 2026, in force 1 October 2026) would make the mark compulsory for anything sold as "handloom" — **leg 1789 ruled DRAFT, NOT IN FORCE (no Gazette commencement)**. If it lands, the thin-regulatory premise of this entire vertical flips. (Grok-lens, R292, research-derived, leg 1792.)

### 1799. The warp is the lot: handloom's latent batch and the zari hinge

The handwoven article carries a production lot that never reaches the buyer. The **warp** is handloom's batch: one warp is set for 5–8 sarees at a time ("the warp for 8 sarees is given to weavers through the society" — Chowtuppal; "thirty yards to produce 5 saris are set in one warp" — Manamedu), dyed as a unit, wound as a unit, and allocated warp-by-warp through co-op/NHDC books. It is the exact analogue of the bangle's 12-hour furnace batch (R291): the lot construct exists, dies before retail (no warp number on any label, tag, or saree sighted), and is enforcement-activatable — the warp is what a traceable Handloom Mark would attach to, and the allocation records already exist. Batch-code 55th: non-adjudication, **second latent-batch of the corpus**, convention OPEN.

The bought-in bill confirms the integration-depth test. Handloom's BOM is yarn (cotton/silk) + **zari** + dyes + labour, and it changes by domicile: society weavers receive the warp issued to them, independents buy and price by the day, master operations source NHDC yarn and Surat zari wholesale. One input is bought in at *every* tier: **Surat zari**. And zari is the vertical's economic hinge — real zari adds ₹20,000–₹50,000 to a saree; it is, in the trade's own words, "where the fraud concentrates." The hinge has a built-in terminology trap: in trade usage, "real zari" means *tested* zari (copper/brass core, coated — the BIS-hallmarked premium grade), not pure gold/silver zari. The buyer who hears "real" and imagines pure gold is being arbitraged on meaning, not lied to about metal. That meaning-shift is a live challenger candidate (unbanked — needs a second instance). **Honest gap:** trade sources say tested zari is "BIS hallmarked" but no IS number was sighted — do not cite one. The zari standard is either real-but-unlocated or trade-lore halo; a BIS-portal leg should settle it.

Identity persists in two layers at once — the first craft vertical to do so. **Article-intrinsic:** temple marks woven into the selvedge (present in handloom, absent in powerloom — PMC), the pin/loom mark by the pallu, the pallu's re-threaded signature pattern, the GI thread for recognised clusters. **Mark-layer:** the Handloom Mark's backside-coded label and the Silk Mark's unique serial + QR. Serial-1 33rd passes on the Silk Mark serial; identity-persistence 66th is ARTICLE-INTRINSIC + MARK-LAYER — reconciled at arbitration as **SELVEDGE-PERSISTENT** (idea 1798's finer term). (Fo-lens, R292, research-derived, leg 1793.)

### 1800. The "handloom-look" fusion: selling the aesthetic, disclaiming the identity

**Body.** A live October-2026 listing (achinova.com) sells a "Banarasi-Style Silk Saree" whose description promises "a luxe **handloom look**" while its spec table lists Fabric: "Banarasi Silk", Type: "Banarasi" — at ₹2,250, roughly a fifth of the genuine handloom floor (₹10K–₹5L+, per Varanasi handloom sellers). One page fuses three things that the law keeps apart: the GI-adjacent name ("Banarasi-Style"/"Banarasi Silk"), the process claim ("handloom look"), and the disclaimers ("-Style", "-look") that keep both just deniable. This is the handloom vertical's native keyword fusion — R291's glass↔resin fusion fused materials; this one fuses PROCESS + NAME + DISCLAIMER in a single listing.

The doctrine question it poses is the one R290's limb-split was built for. The **compliance limb is dark** — handloom has no QCO and the Handloom Mark is voluntary, so there is no certification a platform could be failing to verify. The **deception limb is armed and reachable** — CPA 2019 §§2(28)/2(47) plus GI Act s.22 (civil infringement for falsely applying the GI) and ss.39–40 (criminal: 6 months–3 years, ₹50k–2 lakh fine) — but it has never bitten: no named seller takedown, no seizure, no docket in two sweeps, and the oldest on-record assessment ("not one person has been hauled to jail yet," Crafts Revival Trust, ~2011) still stands unrebutted. The trade itself maintains the linguistic airlock — "Powerloom can be 'Banarasi-style' but not 'authentic Banarasi,' like calling sparkling wine 'Champagne'" (houseofbanaras.in, commercial source) — and whether "-style" defeats s.22 is undecided. That undecidedness is the enforcement vacuum the fusion exploits.

Two structural facts make the vacuum durable. First, the **endogenous-powerloom bind** (academic paper, repec.umb.edu): Banaras master weavers invest handloom earnings into powerlooms *inside* the GI region, and the GI "does not distinguish between powerloom products made in Banaras versus outside" — the protected constituency and the infringing producers overlap, so the deception limb misfires where it is most needed. Second, the **triple-mark stacking**: the Ministry of Textiles simultaneously promotes India Handloom Brand (Textiles Committee-registered, "zero defect zero effect" — verified real via three 2025–26 PIB releases), Handloom Mark, and GI tags, bundling all three in single parliamentary breaths with no buyer-facing hierarchy — so even a diligent buyer cannot tell which mark certifies what. Meanwhile the entire consumer "difference test" genre (7-test guides, selvedge/reverse/zari checks) is sensory-only: not one guide references verifying any mark — instrument-test hard-zero.

And the demand side keeps the lane profitable while the supply side hollows out: the 4th Handloom Census counts 35.22 lakh weavers and allied workers, down 19% from 43.32 lakh a decade earlier, with 67% earning less than unskilled labour. The government buys (20% mandatory handloom procurement; KVIC's 26 khadi varieties on GeM; ₹50.24 cr in FY21; a 212,254-saree GeM bid), yet on the same portal buyers spec branded 100% polyester sarees — mandate-vs-spec drift.

**The test this idea proposes:** buy the ₹2,250 "Banarasi-style handloom-look" specimen; run the genre's own 7 sensory tests on it; then check the article for any GI logo, Handloom Mark, or IHB mark — and file which limb, if any, the listing violates. If the answer is "none, by design," the fusion is not a fraud incident but a **doctrine-shaped product**: engineered to fit exactly the space where the compliance limb cannot reach and the deception limb has never fired. (Fo-lens, R292, research-derived, leg 1794.)

### 1801. Apex-tier number injection: PIB's "IS 5404:2019" for sanitary napkins

The J-arc's opening leg produced the number-injection rule's first **apex-comms-tier** instance. PIB press release PRID 2058537 (Ministry of Textiles, 25 Sep 2024) states the notified specification for sanitary napkins is **"IS 5404:2019"**. The Gazette schedule and every trade source say **IS 5405:2019** — the injection is proven at the source. IS 5404 is not a phantom: per archive.org, IS 5404 (1984, reaffirmed 2005) is *Methods for Drawing and Handling of Food Samples for Microbiological Analysis*; no 2019 edition is sighted. This makes it worse than a phantom number — an injected number that genuinely exists in another product family is harder to catch, and five downstream outlets copied it verbatim (fibre2fashion ×2, textileinsights, technicaltextiles.in, krishijagran, affairscloud): a citation cascade seeded at the apex source. Two corollaries for the corpus: (1) the number-injection rule now has two documented tiers — consultancy/SEO tier (R285–R292 instances) and apex-comms tier (this round); hostile checking must include the highest-authority source, not just the lore tier; (2) the injected number is live at the import border — hnnafei's 2026 import guide carries an explicit FAQ "Does IS 17514:2021 apply to disposable pads? No... don't let a supplier hand you a 17514 test and call it compliant for disposables," i.e. number confusion is a working fraud surface, not just an academic one. Open threads: whether the 5404 injection appears in any BIS enforcement paperwork, counterfeit packaging, or customs paperwork; and whether the second injection (IS 17514-for-disposables) shows up in any seizure docket. (ChatGPT-direct, R293, leg 1795.)

### 1802. The absent-mark verdict bit: detentions for missing Standard Marks are misbranding data, not fraud data

**Finding.** The J-arc's first enforcement docket — M/s. Urban Essentials India Pvt. Ltd. vs Commissioner of Customs (Imports), Chennai II (CESTAT Final Order No. 40607/2026, 26.05.2026; ₹21,224,735 of Chinese sanitary napkins/panty liners detained) — alleged at every stage (OIO 22.08.2025, two Madras HC writs, CESTAT) only that the goods bore **no BIS Standard Mark at all**. No counterfeit mark was ever alleged, found, or pleaded. The sibling-SKU enforcement instance (BIS Chennai's 19.03.2025 search & seizure at Flipkart's Koduvalli warehouse — 286 unmarked baby diapers, PIB PRID 2113173) is the same shape: absent mark, not fake mark. And the honest negative holds: no reported Indian case of fake ISI marks on sanitary napkins exists in courts, BIS releases, or media; YouTube's instrument-test on "fake sanitary pads duplicate ISI mark" is hard-zero.

**Rule (extends the R290 verdict bit + limb-split).** When the identity-fraud T-tiers meet an absent-mark docket, the verdict bit records **NOT-FRAUD** and the instance banks to the **misbranded (compliance) limb**, never to the fraud tally. A detention for non-conformity is evidence of arming, not evidence of deception. Concretely: the fraud streak (101st watch) survives at 0 through this docket — the streak breaks only on a verified fake-mark finding, never on a confiscation order. Any future leg tempted to cite Urban Essentials as "fraud" gets the hostile check first: quote which paragraph alleges a fake mark. There is none.

**Corollary for the schema.** The verdict bit needs three states, not two: FRAUD (fake mark verified), NOT-FRAUD (absent-mark enforcement verified, as here), and UNVERIFIED (no docket). Collapsing the second into the third is how thin-record verticals manufacture phantom fraud; collapsing the first into the second is how armed verticals hide it. Phase-3 should carry the tri-state. (ChatGPT-direct, R293, leg 1796.)

### 1803. The bitten import lane: model the importer-vs-domestic-MSME asymmetry as the armed-BIS frontier fingerprint

**Body:** The Urban Essentials docket (B/E 2483649/9216489, ~₹13.83M assessable on the sighted bill alone) plus the DPIIT clarification of 19.03.2025 establishes something no prior arc has banked: an **asymmetric armed regime where the importer is held to a strictly earlier deadline than the domestic small manufacturer** — the 1-Apr-2025 micro/small extension was explicitly domestic-only, and the importer's sanitary-napkin/panty-liner consignment from Kawada (Zhejiang) Sanitary Products Co., Ltd. (declared CIF $0.0397–0.0588/pc, ≈₹3.4–5.0/pc) was adjudicated for confiscation/re-export + penalty anyway.
