Ranked idea (research, K-arc): K6 is the first vertical where the trade-remedy instrument splits down the middle of the product — semi-finished ophthalmic lenses carry a live, twice-petitioned ADD (2002 DGAD → 55/2004-Customs; 2021 DGTR → 32/2022-Customs, USD 0.15/piece, under CESTAT remand as of Sep 2026) while frames at 81% China import dependence carry no DGTR case at all — because the lens-blanks makers (GKB Goa, IPOLA) had domestic substitutability worth defending and the frame chain (Lenskart included) needs cheap imported frames too badly to petition; across the K-arc, test whether DGTR presence correlates with domestic manufacturing depth rather than import quantum, and run the falsifiable edge this leg produced: the Bangladesh duty-free frame corridor ($35M exports, China as Bangladesh's top frame supplier) is where a lens-ADD detour would pay most — a single verified Bangladesh-routed semi-finished-lens consignment at nil effective duty would prove the armed half is already being outflanked through the unarmed corridor.
### 1882 The cloned engraving: Phase-3 must key unarmed optical products to the pack and the invoice, never the lens

The fake-Ray-Ban lane (Mumbai SIIB seizure: 73,000+ logo-printed pairs in one China container, ₹25 crore as originals, passed customs' own first inspection until brand representatives adjudicated them fake) proves the K6 product key — temple-arm engraving, RB model code, laser-etched RB on the lens — is a seller-owned, state-unverifiable, clonable mark; because no BIS arm exists for plain spectacles/sunglasses (search-tier negative, contrasted against the 2022 Safety Glass QCO and the 2025 smart-glasses CRS pull-in) and no per-unit serial or batch code exists anywhere in the authentication corpus (serial-1 43rd and batch-code 68th both ABSENT), the Phase-3 design rule is to never key identity to the lens: key the *pair* to the pack (LMPCR 2011 Rule 10 importer name/address + Rule 6 MRP/country-of-origin, the only armed mark in the vertical) and to the register (GST invoices under HSN 9004 "Spectacles, goggles and the like" — the excise-touched-then-released chain), and treat the buyer's engraving key as hostile input, exactly as customs must.
### 1883 — The UV400 testability gate

The R306 Q5 hostile check produces a compound finding no single premise contained: the "UV400" claim is physically falsifiable (spectrophotometric transmittance per EN ISO 12312-1:2013, with a material-physics shortcut — polycarbonate and Trivex block UVA inherently while CR-39 transmits 10.3% of it, so an uncoated CR-39 lens labelled "UV400" is the definable fraud shape) yet has no observed Indian accredited test route and no named Indian fraud docket, while the companion vision-harm lane — wrong-dioptre grinding — carries six named Indian dockets including a child who needed a second eye operation, and blue-light claims have already been regulatorily owned abroad (UK GOC's £40,000 fine on Boots, Australia's Federal Court penalties on Lens Online) with no Indian equivalent — so the foldable idea is a UV400-testability gate for Phase-3: since the UV400 claim is testable but not tested anywhere observed in India, the controller should key every "UV400" SKU on a declared-material cross-check (poly/Trivex = inherently blocking; CR-39/glass = coating required, demand the coating evidence), route any "UV400" claim on uncoated CR-39 or unpriced-below-the-tariff-floor fashion sunglasses to chemical-optical assay as the hard falsifier, and treat the wrong-dioptre docket as the template enforcement lane — because in an unarmed optical vertical the fraud will not arrive as a fake BIS mark but as a quiet label ("UV400", "blue-cut") whose verifiable legs, transmittance and dioptre, are each checkable in seconds by equipment the retail market never deploys: if a suspect SKU's declared lens material cannot physically deliver the claimed cut-off, the fraud is confirmed without ever needing a lab; if it can, the lensometer and the spectrophotometer are the only two instruments that matter.
### 1884. The ±0.25-dioptre test — sample 60 powered pairs across the four retail lanes the leg mapped (15 unbranded bazaar frames fitted by street opticians, 15 Amazon.in, 15 Flipkart, 15 Lenskart — spanning budget to John Jacobs mid-tier), and meter each on a calibrated lensometer against the dispensing guidelines the record actually holds: sphere power vs ≤0.25 D tolerance, cylinder axis vs ≤5°, optical centre vs 2 mm of visual axis (the jyotirmay table); simultaneously sweep every listing and its packaging for ANY conformity or registration signal — IS 12870/IS 8980 test report, a third-party optical mark (predicted: zero — the leg found none in India), and CDSCO Item-801 registration on the prefabricated readers (a hit there would bank the arc's first buyer-facing registration key on the armed half); run the UV meter on the fake-branded sunglasses subsample and check RB etchings (etched vs painted, single vs double lens) against the spot-fake genre the leg found — the K6 prediction is a refraction gradient: the power error grows down the price ladder, the street lane fails the ±0.25 D tolerance while the "100% power match" claim ships unmetered, the brand-etched fakes fail UV, and the Item-801 registration count is near-zero on listings — which would bank the optical vertical's first measured defect quantum, confirm POWER-SILENT as a measurement rather than a metaphor, and test whether the brand gate (armed) is merely laundering a conformity void (dark). If any listing carries a verifiable CDSCO registration or third-party optical certificate, the arc banks its first buyer-facing spectacle key and the conformity-dark breaks; if the street lane passes tolerance while Lenskart drifts, the arbitrage leg gets its K6 case.
### 1885. Dormant-standard class: IS 11359:1985 ("Specification for wax candles", voluntary since 1985, reaffirmed 2026, already referenced in GeM procurement) proves a finished-product standard can sit unarmed for 40 years — the arc's unarmed verticals need a split between no-standard-unarmed and dormant-standard-unarmed, because a dormant standard is a reactivation away from an arm
### 1886. **Off-rail, docket-empty on every lane — the K8 closing variant of the 115th cell**: candles (R308/K8) close the K-arc as the thinnest thin vertical — no named Indian docket for counterfeit branded candles (2024–2026), no named docket for fake "soy wax"/"beeswax"/"organic" claims, no misbranded or substandard enforcement under any statute, and even the adjacent trademark register empty (contrast K6's Luxottica-era adjacent-rail docketing) — while the brief's unarmed premise held under hostile check (no BIS QCO, no mandatory mark; only the voluntary IS 11359-1985, a 1985 paraffin-wax specification; HS 34060010 imports sit on a "Free" policy) and the two concept cells resolved as J8 FAILS for K8 (concept NULL — no statute attaches "misbranded" to candles; contrast K5 where it held via the Insecticides Act s.3(k)) and the 82nd absent/fabricated/cloned split DOES NOT APPLY (no mandatory mark; ChatGPT-direct converged explicitly, with a prompt-assistance caveat), with the tier-3 OMISSION pattern checked and NOT present — independent search corroborated the partner's honest negatives on all four lanes. Proposal: close the K-arc with a three-variant taxonomy of the off-rail cell — K5's domestic-docket-empty, K6's adjacent-rail-docketed, and K8's all-rails-docket-empty — and fix K8's watch items as (a) any BIS candle QCO as the instant graduation trigger, (b) the fake-"soy wax" marketing-discourse lane as the most likely first conformity-adjacent fraud signal, and (c) the armed-adjacent precedent (mandatory IS 9994:2018 for lighters) as evidence BIS does arm this household shelf; in thin verticals, formalize the converged honest negative (partner + independent search agreeing on null) as a bankable finding equal in rank to a named docket.
### 1887 The export-parasol vertical: the tariff-only border works because India is a seller, and the EU's ADD wall may be handing it diversion

Ranked idea (research, K-arc): K8 is the arc's only net-exporter vertical ($108M exports vs $8.8M imports in 2024; 3rd-largest world producer at 8.7% of volume) and the cleanest tariff-only border in the K-arc — BCD 25% + IGST 5%, policy FREE, zero Indian DGTR/DGAD instruments, no BIS QCO, no live detention docket — while the same product is trade-remedy-active abroad (EU definitive ADD on Chinese candles from 26 Jan 2026, Reg 2026/157; US order since 1986); test the arc hypothesis that remedy instruments track domestic defensive need rather than import quantum — the falsifiable edge: if Indian candle exports to the EU surge post-26-Jan-2026 while China-origin imports into India stay flat, the tariff-only border is functioning as an export parasol, and if China-origin imports tick up alongside EU-bound re-export lines, the duty-free corridor is instead acting as a pass-through under the EU's wall.
### 1888 The self-consuming key: Phase-3 must schema identity-death at the consumption event and never key a thin consumable to its vessel

Candles close the K-arc with the only artifact that destroys its own identity in normal use: the buyer's key is the nose (scent, throw, burn — unarmed and GC-MS-replicable, with commercial duplication services selling the defeat as a price list), the sole Indian Standard (IS 11359:1985, fetched verbatim) is voluntary, excludes ornamental candles, and marks only the packet with a maker-name — no batch code, no ISI mark, never invoked as "ISI marked" even in live GeM procurement — and the LMPC pack declarations arm only the organised-retail slice while the loose festive lane has no key at any level; because the wax identity dies at the burn while the jar persists identity-agnostic through a documented refill/repour/repurpose economy, the Phase-3 design rule is to schema the burn as the identity-death event, treat every sensory and brand key as hostile input, and never let a branded vessel testify to its contents after first burn.
### 1889 — The GI the brief said didn't exist

The R308 Q5 hostile check produces a finding no single premise contained: the brief's negative bank said candles have no GI — but Nainital Mombatti received a GI tag on 2 December 2023 in Uttarakhand's record 18-product single-day batch, and the brief's 18% GST was never the candle rate (12% pre-2.0, 5% now, with the input stack sitting inverted at 18%), while the bought-in 44th leg is dark because India makes its own paraffin wax (IOCL; NRL's 45–50 KTPA plant cut wax imports by 50%) and exports candles at roughly 25 times what it imports — so the foldable idea is a GI-and-inversion double-check for Phase-3: since a brief can carry a wrong negative (no GI) and a wrong rate (18%) on the same vertical, the controller should treat every inherited "absent" and every inherited rate as hostile until re-verified against the notification and the registry, and for candles specifically it should key the vertical on its two true shapes — a +20 pp protective BCD wall (25% on finished candles vs 5% on paraffin wax) that explains the export surplus, and an inverted GST ladder (18% inputs → 5% output) that makes the domestic maker's margin an ITC-recovery game — while holding the challenger lanes as precedent-without-docket (lead wicks banned by name in the US, Australia, Finland and Denmark with zero observed Indian restriction; "100% soy" falsifiable to under 3% by GC-MS with zero observed Indian lab route; emissions attested in named studies with zero observed enforcement anywhere): in a vertical that is unarmed at home but armed abroad, the fraud will not arrive as a fake mark but as a quiet label ("lead-free", "100% soy", "non-toxic", "soot-free") whose verifiable legs — metal-core assay at 600 ppm, FAME/alkane profile, chamber emissions — are each checkable by methods the domestic market never deploys; if the declared wax cannot produce the measured profile, the fraud is confirmed without ever needing a docket.
### 1890. The wax-assay test — pricing the K-arc's thinnest vertical: sample 60 candles across the four lanes the leg mapped (15 unbranded Diwali-hawker candles, 15 religious-shop candles, 15 Amazon.in/Flipkart listings spanning the ₹99 bazaar anchor to the ₹999 premium, 15 Indian premium brands — Ekam, Tattva, Ellementry and the "free from paraffin" claimants), and assay each against the record the leg actually holds: wax composition vs label claim (FTIR or melt-point against the IS 11359:1985 paraffin baseline — the test the buyer can never run at the counter), lead-wick screening against the US CPSC 2003 benchmark (16 CFR §1500.17(a)(13), ≤0.06% lead — Q5's challenger lane, India's restriction status still dark at search tier), burn time and tunneling vs the 20–40-hour shelf claims; simultaneously sweep all 60 listings and their packaging for ANY conformity signal — ISI/CM-L, IS 11359 invoked in commerce (a hit would bank the arc's first buyer-facing candle key), a verifiable wax-certificate, batch codes (the 69th test — predicted ABSENT). The K8 prediction is a substitution gradient: the "100% soy/beeswax" claim degrades down the price ladder, the hawker candle is paraffin with a cotton wick, the premium candle is paraffin-blend with a soy story, the lead-wick screen finds at least one China-origin positive, and the conformity-signal count is zero across all four lanes — which would bank the thin vertical's first measured defect quantum, confirm WAX-SILENT as a measurement rather than a metaphor, and test the purest dark: whether e-commerce's gate list is truly empty even where the platform could ask for something. If any listing carries a verifiable IS 11359 certificate or CM-L, the arc banks its first buyer-facing candle key and the purest dark breaks on that listing; if the premium lane's wax matches its claims, the substitution gradient flattens and the fragility descriptor fails its first test — which is also a finding.
### 1891
When a partner hedges an instrument number ("commonly cited as S.O. 4249(E)" — wrong; actual S.O. 2986(E)), the hedge does not make the number evidence: treat every model-cited S.O./IS number as a hypothesis, run it through the three-tier rule, and record the failure when it breaks — a flagged guess that survives would have been worse than an honest refusal.
### 1892. **On-rail docket-empty: the L1 armed-variant of the fraud-watch cell, and the s.17-exists nuance for the R303 misbranded kill**: lighters (R309/L1) open the L-arc as the first armed vertical — rail-register docket-empty in-window (2024–2026) on all three fraud lanes (fake/spurious ISI marks, counterfeit brands, QCO non-conformity), partner + independent search converged, while the enforcer is provably active on other goods (730 helmets on a cancelled licence number + 1,158 LPG regulators, BIS Ghaziabad Sep 2026; PIB helmet/pressure-cooker seizure tables; two court cases against M/s Techvision International Pvt Ltd under BIS Act ss.17(1)/17(3)), so the lighter null is a product-level negative, not a capacity negative — and the adjacent trademark rail is populated but out-of-window (Clipper CS(COMM) 895/2016 and CS(COMM) 99/2017, Delhi HC; Zippo shape-mark injunction 13 Jul 2006), while BIC's counterfeit enforcement is US-only (ITC, 57,000-lighters Georgia seizure). Proposal: name the 116th cell ON-RAIL / RAIL-DOCKET-EMPTY / ADJACENT-RAIL-DOCKETED (OUT-OF-WINDOW) — the armed counterpart to K6's off-rail variant — fix the 83rd call as SPLIT-UNPOPULATED with a structural (ii) FABRICATED lean (the spurious-Standard-Mark offence, s.17 prohibition / s.29 cognizable penalties), and bank the R303 nuance that BIS Act s.17 EXISTS but is a conformity-prohibition anchor, not a misbranded anchor — the "no s.17 anchor" kill means no s.17 *misbranded* anchor, confirmed by partner with a section-citation imprecision flagged (partner's "s.17 improper use / s.18 penalty" mapping vs the official s.17-prohibition/s.29-penalty framing) — and set the watch items as (a) the first named s.17/s.29 BIS lighter prosecution as the FABRICATED-limb populator, (b) the QCO's two-standard arm (IS/ISO 9994:2018 + IS 8489:2019 for utility lighters) as the compliance perimeter to watch for customs-seizure notices, and (c) the partner's self-declared under-searched lanes (BIS press releases, magistrate filings, customs notices, private trademark actions) as the standing tier-3 sweep list for the L-arc.
### 1893 The dual-gate vertical: the DGFT value floor + BIS-QCO ratchet, and the parts line as the leak detector

**Ranked idea (research, L-arc):** L1 is the arc's first dual-gate vertical — K3 (BIS-QCO certification gate, IS/ISO 9994:2018, Scheme-I) layered over K4 (DGFT value-floor prohibition on finished lighters below ₹20 CIF, Notification 15/2023-DGFT) with a third instrument (parts 'Restricted', Notification 36/2024-25) closing the assembly lane — three instruments in fifteen months, each plugging the loophole the previous gate left, and zero DGTR/DGAD items because the industry got regulation instead of remedies (the EU, by contrast, walls the same product with a per-lighter ADD, EUR 0.065/lighter under Reg 1458/2007); the falsifiable edge for the arc: watch the 96139000 parts line in FY25-26 — if the +126% YoY parts flood (₹90.94 Cr, 83% of subchapter imports, mostly China) collapses after the Oct-2024 restriction while finished 96131000/96132000 lines stay flat under the ₹20 floor, the ratchet is biting, and if parts imports persist (re-routing through 961380 'other lighters' lines or misclassification) or reappear as 'Restricted'-licence volume, the gate leaks at the component level — with the BIS licence roll for IS/ISO 9994:2018 (domestic + FMCS) as the compliance census that separates the gate's real coverage from its paper coverage.
### 1894
KEY-LOCATION case study: lighters — the QCO mandates the ISI key but BIS practice permits it "on the product or its packaging," ISO 9994:2018 Clause 8 demands only a permanent manufacturer/distributor identifier at unit level, batch codes are absent from the standard (scheme-condition only), and enforcement stops at the ₹10 pan-shop unit — so lighters are the sharpest ARMED-BIS counterexample to any unit-level-key model; BEST-IDEAS should carry the PACK-CONTINGENT KEY hypothesis and test it against (a) whether any BIS market raid ever seized a single unit on unit-level mark grounds, (b) whether a BIS lighter recall has ever run on batch traceability (null so far), and (c) what share of sub-₹20 pan-shop disposables carry any unit-level ISI mark at all.
### 1895 — The child-resistance India doesn't require

The R309 Q5 hostile check produces a finding no single premise contained: both standards India's Flame-Producing Lighters QCO 2023 mandates — IS/ISO 9994:2018 and IS/ISO 22702:2018 — contain literally zero child-resistance mechanism requirements (verified by full-text find: no "child" in 9994, no "child-resist" in 22702, only "KEEP AWAY FROM CHILDREN" warnings), which refutes not only the brief's premise but the 2023 press claim that the QCO "mandates child-resistant features" and three BIS consultancies' claim that IS/ISO 22702:2018 covers "child-resistant mechanisms" — while the bought-in 45th leg shows India imports the parts to make these lighters (96139000 = ₹90.94 Cr, 83% of the 9613 import lane, DGFT-restricted since October 2024) from the same Chinese pool the US CPSC is currently warning against and recalling for missing child-resistant mechanisms (Creative Dice, Klasyt Jet Torch ~45,140 units, Jobon recall 26-626, Olivia ~60,000 — all 2024–2026, all [A]/[C] named) under regimes India never adopted (US 16 CFR 1210/1212, EU 2006/502/EC + EN 13869, Canada SOR/2008-231): so the foldable idea is a standards-text-vs-claim verification rule for Phase-3 — since press and even compliance vendors assert safety clauses the standard text provably lacks, the controller should never inherit a "mandates X" claim about a QCO without running a text-find on the cited standard itself, and for lighters specifically it should key the vertical on its three true shapes — an armed-BIS regime with a child-safety hole (CR-NULL in both standards), a parts-dominated bought-in stack (+5 pp thin tariff wall on the fuel leg, parts-leg delta held open, flat 18% GST with a non-inverted ladder — the inverse of K8's every cell), and a harm lane that is testable at the port (ISO 9994 cls. 5.3–5.6 cover fuel loss, drop, heat, pressure) but docket-dark at home after four targeted searches — because in a vertical where the hazard is imported through the parts lane and the domestic standard cannot see the missing safety mechanism, the fraud will not arrive as a fake mark but as a compliant-looking ISI-marked lighter that a child can operate, and no docket will ever record it until the burn does.
### 1896
**Twin-gate sequencing (from R309 lighters, first L-arc vertical):** on lighters the *trade* gate moved before the *conformity* gate — DGFT prohibited <₹20 CIF pocket lighters (29 June 2023) months before the Flame-Producing Lighters QCO took force (~Jan 2024), then extended the trade gate to lighter *parts* (Oct 2024). Proposal for the L-arc: record per vertical not just whether trade and conformity gates exist, but their *order* — when the trade gate leads, the shadow lane is already adapting (misdeclared "empty cases") before the conformity gate even fires, so the memory model's fraud watches should sequence surveillance accordingly: watch the evasion lane *before* the licence register, not after.
### 1897
Treat every partner-cited instrument number as a lead, never a fact: in R310 ChatGPT confidently reported the Fire Extinguishers QCO as "S.O. 4524(E), 23 Oct 2023" despite an explicit no-fabrication instruction — Gazette text pins it as S.O. 3585(E), 9 Aug 2023 (Gazette No. 3431, 10 Aug 2023). The number-injection three-tier rule (partner says → web confirms → Gazette pins) is load-bearing because partners fabricate plausible numbers.
### 1898
On-rail docket-empty has an L2 signature: fire extinguishers carry the same armed fraud-watch cell as lighters (fraud-watch ON-RAIL / RAIL-DOCKET-EMPTY / ADJACENT-RAIL-DOCKETED), but the adjacent rail is product-adjacent rather than time-adjacent — counterfeit TYCO fire *sprinklers* (W.P. (Crl.) 3516/2017, Delhi HC, 8 Feb 2018) and an in-window FM Approvals alert on counterfeit sprinklers in Mumbai (Dec 2025) prove the counterfeit-brand demand surface lives in the fire-protection aisle while the extinguisher rail itself stays docket-empty — and the extinguisher-specific refill fraud (substandard powder, expired units resold as new) is surface-real at the NBC 2016 / IS 2190:2010 / state-fire-service level but docket-empty in-window at every tier, which means the watch-list's most distinctive L2 item is a fraud register policed by fire departments rather than BIS — so name the 117th cell ON-RAIL / RAIL-DOCKET-EMPTY / ADJACENT-RAIL-DOCKETED (OUT-OF-WINDOW / OUT-OF-PRODUCT), fix the 84th call as SPLIT-UNPOPULATED with a structural lean (ii) FABRICATED primary + (iii) CLONED secondary (note the divergence from the 83rd's FABRICATED-only lean), bank the partner's J8 refinement that s.17 reach is not limited to spurious marks (offering a QCO good without the mark is itself an issue at s.17; marked-but-non-conforming is a separate one), and set the watch items as (a) the first named s.17/s.29 BIS extinguisher prosecution as the 84th limb-populator, (b) the first fire-department/NOC prosecution over a refilled-with-substandard-powder unit as the refill-lane populator, and (c) customs/port seizure notices on non-ISI extinguishers as the armed-perimeter check.
### 1899 The procurement-gated vertical: ISI as the GeM bid key, and the single-gate axis

**Ranked idea (research, L-arc):** L2 is the arc's first PROCUREMENT-VERIFIED armed vertical — the opposite of K8's null: GeM's extinguisher categories are literally named "ISI Marked to IS 15683/16018", listing requires a valid active CM/L licence owned by the applicant themselves, and bid docs (GEM/2025/B/5983322; NFL GEM/2026/B/7873276; SE Railway) demand the ISI-mark certificate and BIS licence copy at evaluation — with the NFL tender adding a second independent gate (CCE Nagpur/PESO licence) — so the QCO's conformity gate (S.O. 3585(E), 9 Aug 2023, in force ~Feb 2024, IS 15683:2018 + IS 16018:2012, Scheme-I) is the same key turned from the supply side and the demand side; the border axis is single-gate (twin-gate sequencing record: the conformity gate moved WITHOUT a trade gate — no ADD, absence banked; no DGFT restriction surfaced; unlike L1's trade→conformity→parts ratchet), and China holds ~48% of import shipments (count) into a line converging toward balance (₹130.90 Cr in vs ₹122.49 Cr out, FY24-25; import growth +2.36% YoY in the first QCO year vs +38.65% before); the falsifiable edge for the arc: watch FY25-26 84241000 — if imports flatten or the line tips to surplus while the FMCS licence census (Q6's probe) stays thin, the conformity gate is doing the import-substitution work a remedy would do, and if the China shipment share persists near ~48%, the leak is at the port gate (FMCS uptake or misdeclaration), not at the tender wall, which is already lit.
### 1900. The delegated key: fire extinguishers force a manufacture-key / agent-key / event-key split in the memory schema — the first durable-vessel refill lane

**Finding (research-derived):** The fire extinguisher is the corpus's first durable vessel with a refill lane, and it breaks the one-key model. Text-find on IS 15683:2018 (clause 10.2) establishes a SPLIT-KEYED identity: the certification key (ISI mark + CM/L licence number) lives on a replaceable transfix label (soft node — the STI permits label application, and the fake-spotting tier identifies poor labels as the counterfeit tell), while the vessel key (mandated sequential serial number cl 10.2.1.2; year of manufacture + factory test pressure "permanently marked into the extinguisher body" cl 10.2.1.3; buyer-driven embossing on the skirt) lives on the body. Text-find also kills batch-keying: "batch" appears only in two "Batch Test" contexts — the standard mandates no lot marking (batch-code 71st = OMITS, matching lighters' 70th). THE REFILLING PROBLEM resolves as delegation, not renewal: cl 10.2.4 makes recharge-by-manufacturer-or-authorized-agent mandatory, but no BIS refiller-licensing scheme exists — nobody re-certifies a refilled unit in BIS terms. Instead the refilled unit carries a three-part delegated key: (i) the unit-key (the original ISI label, manufacture-time, never renewed), (ii) the agent-key (the refill material's own ISI mark — powder per IS 4308/IS 14609, cartridges per IS 4947, mandated by tender SOWs), and (iii) the event-key (the refiller's per-unit service certificate keyed to the vessel's serial number, plus PESO-certified hydrotest reports tied to the "unique Identification number embossed on the cylinder body" and the test date stamped on the body). Identity-persistence verdict: 82nd = VESSEL-PERSISTENT / CERT-NON-RENEWING — the serial-tracked vessel survives refill cycles with an accumulating event history (IS 2190:2024 Annex F hydrotests every 3/5 years, condemnation on failure), but the ISI certification is a manufacture-time artifact that delegates rather than renews. Twin-gate order: BIS QCO (factory) → PESO (CO2 bodies) → fire-dept NOC (deployment) → buyer SOW (refill) — no single gate owns the lifecycle, which is exactly why the key delegates. **Design implication:** the memory schema needs a `key_lifecycle` model for durable-service verticals with three nodes — `manufacture_key` (product cert, one-time), `agent_key` (consumable-input cert, per-refill), `event_key` (per-serial service/hydrotest certificates) — plus a `key_renewal` attribute (`NON-RENEWING` here, vs. renewable keys in other verticals) and a split `key_locus` (cert-node vs. vessel-node). In refill-lane verticals the counterfeiter's cheapest attack is always the soft cert-node (printable label with a cloned CM/L), never the vessel anchor — the schema should weight key-strength by node, not by vertical.
### 1901 — The corridor between two standards is where the fires win

The R310 Q5 hostile check produces the arc's first reversal of the R308/R309 pattern: the challenger is not docket-dark but press-named AND probe-docketed — Jhansi NICU Nov 2024 (10 newborns; Republic: extinguishers "expired 2 years ago," eyewitness "didn't work" — government denial banked, three-tier probe ordered), Rajkot TRP Game Zone May 2024 (27–33 killed; "no fire extinguishers" per The Hindu; culpable-homicide FIRs, SIT), AMRI Kolkata 2011 (93 killed; extinguishers "several years old and never serviced"; arrests, licence cancelled), Bhandara 2021 (10 babies; required extinguishers absent) — three failure variants (expired / unserviced / absent) across four named incidents satisfying 294/40 domestically, while the tariff-delta run exposes why the product regime cannot see it: finished extinguishers (84241000, BCD 7.5%) sit *below* the extinguishing preparations (38130000, BCD 10% — a −2.5 pp input-up, verified on current seair pages plus eximguru duty-history), and flat against the parts leg (84249000 = 7.5% — the R306 spectacle shape), so the duty structure rewards importing charged units over domestic assembly from quality agents; and the bought-in 46th is PRESENT but import-complemented rather than parts-dominated (finished line consistently deficit at ₹130.90 Cr in vs ₹122.49 Cr out FY24-25; CE-approved brass valves, gauges, nozzles, part of the powder lane, and clean agents imported; cylinders domestic deep-drawn MS), with GST 24th cell a flat, stable 18% (Notif 9/2025-CT(R) Sch II S.No. 413 [A]; inputs all 18%, non-inverted) and GI banked absent — so the foldable idea is a lifecycle-corridor rule for Phase-3: IS 15683:2018 arms the factory gate and IS 2190:2024 governs the maintenance corridor, and the harm lane lives entirely in the corridor no QCO audits — meaning the controller must key fire-safety verticals on maintenance-lane events (probe reports, hospital audits, expiry/refill records) rather than on the product mark, because in this vertical the ISI mark never fails; the servicing schedule does, and no docket will ever record it as a product defect — only as a corridor failure, which is exactly what Rajkot's FIRs, AMRI's arrests, and Jhansi's probe already did.
### 1902
**Register-lighting by procurement (L-arc mechanism, from R310 extinguishers):** on tender-driven BIS-armed verticals, CM/L numbers surface per-bid in GeM/tender documents (L2: valid-ISI-licence + CM/L disclosure mandatory at bid opening; Ceasefire's CM/L-8886112 printed on its own IS 15683 datasheet) — the lit-register rule should count tender-attached CM/L disclosures as sparse singleton lighting and add a per-vertical "register-via-procurement" enumeration path (collect CM/L numbers from GeM bid docs + tender corrigenda) as the fallback when the BIS licence portal is JS-blocked, instead of scoring the register purely dark.
### 1903
**Consolidation-standard reference list as the instrument-chain shortcut (L-arc method, from R311 HSRP):** when a sector's standard was written to consolidate scattered notifications, its References section IS the primary-tier amendment chain — AIS-159 (Aug 2019, fetched from icat.in) lists its basis instruments a–t (GSR 221(E)/28.03.2001, S.O. 814(E)/22.08.2001, S.O. 938(E)/24.09.2001 … GSR 1162(E)/04.12.2018, S.O. 1081(E)/25.02.2019) plus MoRTH letters and parent rules, pinning the full chain in one fetch instead of Gazette-hunting each notification; it also exposed the partner's hedged "G.S.R. 338(E)/26.03.2001" as a non-existent number (arc's third fabrication catch) — so hedged-as-UNVERIFIED numbers still get the number-injection web tier, and the digit-floor nuance it revealed (2001-era "minimum seven digits" → AIS-159 "minimum ten digits") shows the standard text, not the partner's memory, decides "mandates X" claims.
### 1904
**Fraud-watch needs a two-tier docket rule: court tier + FIR tier (from R311 HSRP).** The ChatGPT-direct consultation honestly banked [D] nulls on *court* dockets for fake-HSRP/duplicate-plate enforcement, and that null holds — but the tier-3 web check found the enforcement alive at the FIR tier: Hyderabad's duplicate-plate actions (Warasiguda, BNS 318(4)/316(2), reg TS09 FE 4997 on three scooters; Khairatabad FIR No.118/2026, BNS 318(4) + MV Act s.192, reg TS08HS7658), a week-long 5–6-case seizure drive, plus a named Supreme Court docket (Shaker: masked plate = MV Act s.177, not IPC 420). Controller rule: never call RAIL-DOCKET-EMPTY from a court-tier null alone — score FIR/police-press tier separately, and record field-charge vs text-charge gaps (police charge s.192 for cloned plates though s.192 textually targets unregistered vehicles) instead of collapsing them into the statute text. (Fraud-watch 118th: ON-RAIL / RAIL-DOCKETED / ADJACENT-RAIL-DOCKETED; identity-fraud 85th: SPLIT-POPULATED, CLONED primary, FABRICATED secondary, ABSENT tertiary.)
### 1905. VAHAN forces the lit-register refinement: LIT-QUERYABLE but NON-ENUMERABLE by design — the register is a transaction gate, not a directory

**Finding (research-derived):** VAHAN is the lit-register rule's best test and it SPLITS the cell. The register is LIT: any registration number → public record, free, via parivahan.gov.in "Know Your Vehicle Details", the mParivahan app, or SMS to 7738299899 — 40+ crore records under a statutory mandate (s.62B & 63, MV Act 1988; Lok Sabha annexure, 6 Aug 2026). But it is deliberately NON-ENUMERABLE: captcha + mobile-OTP login + a last-5-chassis/engine gate on the fuller record is an explicit anti-bulk safeguard, and pre-2006 records remain incompletely digitised — aggregate analytics are open (VAHAN dashboard, CEIC monthly series) while record-level bulk pull is closed. And the register's KEY split matters for the whole arc: the public/human key is the REGISTRATION NUMBER; the laser-etched 10-digit serial is the machine key tracked INSIDE the record — the state mints the serial but the public queries the number. Beyond lookup, VAHAN functions as an ENFORCEMENT LEVER — a transaction gate: Maharashtra blocks ownership transfer, address change, hypothecation, re-registration, alteration and permit renewal for non-HSRP vehicles (from 1 Jul 2026); UP denies PUC certificates without HSRP. The vendor lane is a two-layer authorisation (type approval by testing agencies + state RFP/BOO tender or OEM authorisation) dominated by one player at >50% share (Rosmerta: 170M+ plates, 6.6M/month capacity, ₹1,200 cr FY26 revenue), and the compliance data shows the twin-gate lesson — the channel determines the bite: 91% new-vehicle compliance via the OEM channel (Maharashtra PTI) vs 19–29% old-vehicle retrofit compliance; split-domicile 65th = DEAD (cross-border vehicles run on permits, no plate corridor); government-vehicle procurement is NULL-shaped (no bulk lane; "many" of the 9.98 lakh non-compliant new Maharashtra vehicles were government-owned). **Design implication:** the memory schema's register cell needs three attributes, not one — `register_lit` (targeted queryability: YES), `register_enumerable` (bulk dumpability: NO — and the anti-bulk mechanism named), `register_public_key` (the human query key — here the registration number, distinct from the minted unit serial) — plus a `register_function` attribute (`TRANSACTION-GATE` where the register blocks services, vs. `DIRECTORY` where it only answers lookups). In armed-non-BIS verticals the register, not the court, is the compulsion engine — and the schema should record which channel a mandate travels through (OEM-at-sale vs owner-retrofit), because the channel, not the instrument, determined the bite (91% vs ~25%).
### 1906. The mint-key column: HSRP gives the serial-1 schema its first state-minted serial with an audited issuance ledger — and its first two-clock persistence model

**Finding (research-derived):** The HSRP plate is the serial-1 convention's best test yet, and it passes at a tier no prior vertical reached. Text-find on AIS-159 (Aug 2019, the live HSRP standard) establishes a six-node SPLIT-KEYED identity: (1) a laser-*branded* (the standard's verb, not etched) permanent identification number of *minimum* ten digits, bottom-left of the plate at 5.00±0.2 mm, preceded by a two-alphabet **mint-issuer prefix** identifying the type-approving test agency (ARAI A–D, CIRT E–H, CRRI I–L, GARC M–P, VRDE Q–S, ICAT T–V — §5.2, §6.6, Table 1); (2) a 20×20 mm hot-stamped chromium hologram, top-left, with stickers/adhesive labels explicitly prohibited (§6.3); (3) a metallic non-reusable snap lock, unremovable without break/cut (§3.17); (4) the VAHAN lit-register binding PIN↔registration mark↔chassis; (5) a self-destructive diffraction-foil third-registration sticker (100×60 mm, unremovable in one piece from glass — §3.16, §7.5.1) carrying the matching 12-character code (industry shorthand for 2α+10d, *not* a standards figure — the standards-text-vs-claim rule kills it); (6) IND/INDIA standardisation markers. The schema's two new structures: first, the **audited mint ledger** — §8.1 makes "Laser branding records and its dispatch" a Conformity-of-Production audit item, so serial issuance is a recorded, inspectable mint event, the first in the corpus; the mint-issuer prefix migrated from vendor (2001 Order, 7-digit floor) to test agency (2019, 10-digit floor) — the key's issuer moved from commercial to institutional. Second, **two-clock identity persistence**: within a registration the serial is VESSEL-PERSISTENT (resale transfers the plate with the car; VAHAN updates the owner field), but inter-state re-registration **re-mints** the serial for the same chassis — the PIN is registration-scoped, the chassis is the cross-registration continuity handle. Key-strength finding: fakers defeat HSRP by **omission, not forgery** — Pune's shadow market sells lookalikes openly admitting "the code will not be there" (TOI via obnews), and no forged-laser-PIN docket exists at the search tier; the mint node (laser brand + VAHAN agreement) has never been shown broken while the visual nodes are cloned routinely — so the memory schema should weight key-strength *by node*, with the register-binding carrying nearly all the weight. Batch-code 72nd = OMITS (zero "batch" hits in the full standard; production control is ledger-audited, never lot-marked — the third OMITS in the column). **Design implication:** the schema needs a `mint_key` node type (issuer-prefix + audited issuance ledger + register binding) distinct from `cert_key` (ISI-style) and `vessel_key` (embossed serial); a `persistence_clocks` attribute (vessel-clock vs registration-clock) for re-keyable serials; and node-weighted `key_strength` so that a six-node key isn't scored as six-times-strong — here, five nodes are glance-level and one (mint+register) does the real work.
### 1907 — Where the duty wall is thickest, the fraud goes domestic-theater

The R311 Q5 leg produces the arc's first positive-sign tariff-delta calibration: finished HSRP plates sit behind a **+10 pp protective wall** (BCD 20% on 83100090 since 02-Feb-2020 vs 10% on the reflective-sheeting input 39199090), the exact inverse of R310's −2.5 pp input-up — and the challenger lane's shape flips with it. R310's fraud pressure lives in the parts lane; R311's named harm never touches the import lane at all. Instead it is entirely domestic-theater: fake HSRP *booking portals* (Kapil of Ghaziabad via Gurugram cyber crime; Rishabh Gupta and mastermind Kapil Tyagi via Delhi IFSO Special Cell with thousands of victims; Vinod Bawale via Mumbai police), legacy *tampered plates* dodging challans and loans (Prasad Kadam's cloned MH01-EE-2388; Kolimi Yadaiah's 49-challan ₹20,815 sticker alteration; Syed Hussain Mehdi's fake TS 11 EK 0593 that pushed wrongful challans onto an innocent owner; Mohd. Rafiuddin's 16-Apr-2026 arrest), and an attack on the identity database itself (the Delhi ring's 10 arrests, 31 luxury vehicles, unauthorized VAHAN-portal credentials) — while the physical plate's security features (chromium hologram, laser PIN, snap locks) have **zero named counterfeit cases** at search tier, and toll-evasion-by-plate has none either (the ED Mirzapur/Mobdata toll case is operator fraud, honestly excluded). So the foldable idea for Phase-3 is a **tariff-delta → fraud-shape rule**: record the sign of Δ per vertical and route the challenger watch accordingly — negative Δ (duty punishes domestic assembly): watch the parts/import lane; positive Δ (duty protects assembly): watch the mandate's domestic trust edges — booking portals, retrofit deadlines, legacy-stock reuse, database access — because where the wall is thickest, counterfeiters don't smuggle the product, they counterfeit the *compliance theater around it*, and the harm lane that counts (294/41, live-domestic) is the one the security spec was never designed to see.
### 1908
**Register-gated point-of-trust test (from R311 HSRP):** extend the lit-register rule with a point-of-trust check — it is not enough that a register is lit; test whether the decision-maker at the checkpoint (traffic cop, counter staff) can reach the register un-gated at the moment of decision. HSRP's VAHAN is lit-for-lookup yet dark-at-the-checkpoint (OTP/captcha, per-vehicle, never roadside), which is exactly the mechanism that lets GHOST plates and the roadside shadow persist at industry scale. Score registers on two axes: (1) lit/dark for lookup, (2) reachable/unreachable at the point of trust; VAHAN scores lit/unreachable, and that gap is the tenth fragility analogue GHOST.
### 1909 — The docket-as-register: in prohibition verticals the record is the docket, not the good
**Finding (from R312 kites & manjha, L4):** when a good is banned outright, no product register exists — the prohibition's record IS the docket: five layers (the banning order, state s.5 notifications, regulator directions, the FIR/seizure violation layer, the continuing-court layer). It is lit-for-the-ban / dark-for-the-goods. The Phase-3 schema's register cell needs a PROHIBITION variant: track the ban's liveness, not the good's identity. Source: ROUND-312-QUESTIONS.md / 1909-chatgpt-r312q1.md, 1914-fo-r312q6.md.
### 1910 — Score the FIR tier separately from the court tier
**Finding (from R311/R312):** never call RAIL-DOCKET-EMPTY from a court-tier null alone — enforcement can be alive at the FIR tier (raids, arrests, chargesheets) while court dockets are dark. Record field-charge vs text-charge gaps (police charging BNS s.223(b) for manjha possession; charging MV Act s.192 for cloned plates though the text targets unregistered vehicles) instead of collapsing them into the statute text. Two-tier docket rule: court tier + FIR tier, scored independently. Source: 1910-chatgpt-r312q2.md.
### 1911 — Names are market terms, not supply-chain facts: verify the border axis before building on it
**Finding (from R312):** "Chinese manjha" is domestically manufactured synthetic — the name is a market misnomer, and the brief's import/smuggling axis was a dead hypothesis (no DGFT notification, no smuggling case, one factory sealed in Dadra & Nagar Haveli). For Phase-3: any origin label ("Chinese", "imported") is a claim to be verified at court-record tier, never a premise. Source: 1911-grok-r312q3.md.
### 1912 — Forensic keys, jurisdiction-contingent legality, CONSUMED-TERMINAL persistence
**Finding (from R312):** the prohibition vertical gives the schema three new constructs: (1) a `forensic_key` node type — the key is a burn test / fibre test / ocular ID, nothing printed on the good; (2) a `jurisdiction_contingent` flag — glass-coated cotton is legal nationally (NGT exclusion) but banned in Delhi and Maharashtra; the key's legal meaning changes at a state border; (3) CONSUMED-TERMINAL persistence — the manjha is designed to be severed in kite-fights; no identity was ever attached, so none persists except as pollution and docket evidence. Plus a new fraud mode: MISDECLARED FIBRE (banned synthetic sold as cotton) — labels as anti-evidence. Source: 1912-grok-r312q4.md.
### 1913 — Bans-as-walls: a 0pp tariff with an import ban is not neutral
**Finding (from R312):** record bans alongside tariff-deltas. Finished kites sit at 10% against inputs at 10–12.5% (Δ = 0pp to −2.5pp) — tariff-neutral — yet the NGT's import ban is the true wall, and where the wall is regulatory rather than tariff, the fraud doesn't reprice, it reroutes: inter-state consignments, mislabeled industrial stock ('Hero Plus – For Industrial Use Only'), brand evasion ('MONO KTC'), online listings. Challenger watches on ban regimes should key on festival-surge calendars and the four evasion channels. Hostile-check-first as a stored procedure: this leg's 2-fail-1-hold split (HSN and tariff-wall fails, one hold) is the template. Source: 1913-fo-r312q5.md.
### 1914 — DARK-BY-MISLABEL and the CHAMELEON fragility analogue
**Finding (from R312):** e-commerce on banned goods = DARK with a new shape: sellers camouflage listings as "industrial-strength polyester thread / heavy-duty sewing thread / craft cord / embroidery / fishing net" — adaptive product-category camouflage defeating naming-layer enforcement (MP HC 16 Jan 2026 geo-fence order vs Amazon/Flipkart/IndiaMART). Eleventh fragility analogue: CHAMELEON (distinguished from GHOST's forged register binding). Meesho: no evidence (honest negative). Source: 1914-fo-r312q6.md.
### 1915 — Write-path quality gates, deterministic and pre-storage (STRATA S1)
**Transferable design idea (from tool study of kytheros/strata):** three cheap deterministic gates run BEFORE anything is stored — actionability (action verbs, when…then conditionals, "instead of" comparisons, error-fix patterns), specificity (≥2 concrete-detail signals: numbers, versions, codes, refs), relevance (negative filter on casual-opinion openers). Any gate fails → rejected, never stored. This is the fail-closed write gate (idea 1505) implemented: reject fast, audit the rejection. Source: hidden_files/research/tool-studies/STRATA-study.md (docs/evaluator-pipeline.md).
### 1916 — Rejection audit trail (STRATA S2)
**Transferable design idea:** every rejected write records outcome + which-gate + why (rejected entries get a reason string; accepted entries too). A memory system that cannot explain what it refused to remember cannot be debugged. Source: hidden_files/research/tool-studies/STRATA-study.md.
### 1917 — Write-time importance scoring (STRATA S3)
**Transferable design idea:** composite salience computed ONCE at write, stored, applied as a bounded retrieval multiplier (1.0–1.5×) — never recomputed per query. Components: type weight (decision > learning > error_fix > pattern > procedure > preference > fact > solution > episodic), language markers ("decided to"/"going with", "root cause", "always"/"never"), cross-session frequency, explicit-vs-extracted. Source: hidden_files/research/tool-studies/STRATA-study.md.
### 1918 — Explicit-intent boost (STRATA S4)
**Transferable design idea:** user-stored memories outrank auto-extracted ones by a small fixed margin — the operational form of epistemic tiers (idea 1504). Source: hidden_files/research/tool-studies/STRATA-study.md.
### 1919 — Two-layer dedup (STRATA S5)
**Transferable design idea:** exact-match skip (project+type+summary+user) always; semantic conflict resolution (delete/superseded, update/merge, noop, trivial-duplicate) only when an LLM is available, behind a killswitch, with graceful fallback to exact-dedup and input truncation (prompt-bloat + injection guard). Matches the transfer caveat: don't make correctness depend on an LLM being present. Source: hidden_files/research/tool-studies/STRATA-study.md.
### 1920 — Benchmark honesty doctrine (STRATA S6)
**Transferable design idea:** separate the defensible third-party number from the self-authored smoke test IN WRITING, and say which one to cite. kytheros/strata's own example: the LongMemEval-S 500-question retrieval number (94.9% recall@20, MRR 0.907, ~16ms p95 — fully local) is citable; their self-authored 50-item corpus is "a sanity check, not proof of superiority," and they say so. Adopt as a reporting rule for our own gate reports. Source: hidden_files/research/tool-studies/STRATA-study.md.
### 1921 — Frozen-eval tuning (STRATA S7)
**Transferable design idea:** ranking parameters (RRF weights, recency/project/importance boosts) tuned against frozen eval suites, not vibes. Our Phase-3 calibration should do the same. Source: hidden_files/research/tool-studies/STRATA-study.md.
### 1922 — Own the storage layout (STRATA S8)
**Transferable design idea:** a memory layer that wraps a black-box vector DB cannot ship features that touch the write path (quantization, tiering, custom indexes). Strata owns storage end-to-end (SQLite/D1/Postgres behind a StorageContext interface) — enabling write-path features like 4-bit embedding quantization. Keep storage ours. Source: hidden_files/research/tool-studies/STRATA-study.md.
### 1923 — Silent-unless-useful hooks (STRATA S9)
**Transferable design idea:** lifecycle hooks (error recovery, prompt context, compaction survival, knowledge extraction on session end) that add zero latency on the happy path and stay silent when they have nothing to add. Source: hidden_files/research/tool-studies/STRATA-study.md.
### 1924 — Algorithmic Janitor (STRATA S10)
**Transferable design idea (from jeremykamber/strata-memory):** forgetting as a free deterministic process, not a paid judgment call — the forgetting doctrine (idea 71) implemented: migrate by file age (projects 14d, entities 60d, gtd 7d), evict by LRU, promote on use, rehydrate from archive — every operation with --dry-run ("first cycle is always a dry run, because nobody trusts a janitor that doesn't test the mop first"). Source: hidden_files/research/tool-studies/STRATA-study.md.
### 1925 — Use-based resurrection (STRATA S11)
**Transferable design idea:** promotion threshold — a cooled file accessed ≥3 times comes back to active. Recency of USE beats recency of WRITE; frequently-needed old knowledge must not be buried by age alone. Source: hidden_files/research/tool-studies/STRATA-study.md.
### 1926 — Separate extraction from organization (STRATA S12)
**Transferable design idea:** LLM distillation (batched transcripts through a small cheap model, opt-in, no key = disabled) and lifecycle management (algorithmic, free) are different concerns sharing a daemon — never one mechanism. The milestone's Phase-3 equivalent: consolidation (learned, expensive) and forgetting/aging (deterministic, free) must not be the same code path. Source: hidden_files/research/tool-studies/STRATA-study.md.
### 1927 — The phrase lives in the Rules: "mechanical contraceptives" locus
**Finding (from R313 condoms, L5):** the D&C Act s.3(b)(ii) "mechanical contraceptives" phrase is written out in MDR 2017's own text (Rules 3(zb)(B)/2(ii)), routing condoms to notification under the drug definition. The brief's routing was correct; the phrase lives in the Rules, not the Act's clause text. For Phase-3: pin the locus of every definitional phrase (Act vs Rules vs FAQ) before building the regime graph — the instrument that carries the phrase is the instrument that bites. Source: 1927-chatgpt-r313q1.md.
### 1928 — OFF-RAIL with a non-zero harm lane: enforcement zero, breakage real
**Finding (from R313):** fraud-watch 120th = OFF-RAIL / RAIL-EMPTY / ADJACENT-RAIL-POPULATED — zero Indian seizures, prosecutions, or convictions for fake/substandard condoms at any tier, while the harm lane is non-zero (breakage up to ~19% in cited studies; 3.4% of Indian users failing within 12 months). The Nirodh legacy shows no quality failure on record (~650M free/year, indelible overprint, zero complaints/recalls/blacklists) — the documented failure is market-share/supply/perception, not product quality. For Phase-3: enforcement-zero + harm-nonzero is a distinct fraud-watch geometry from OFF-RAIL-with-no-harm. Source: 1928-chatgpt-r313q2.md.
### 1929 — NACO indents, CMSS procures: procurement-as-register verified
**Finding (from R313):** the procurement-as-register lane is real — 75% captive to HLL (66M pieces 2023-24, <4% of India's ~2.3B/yr total flow), 25% via CMSS tenders won by licensed domestic makers; importers have no bid lane. Named manufacturer set verified (HLL 2.217B/yr, TTK, Mankind-Manforce as OEM brand play — packs read "Manufactured by Penta Latex LLP", GCPL-KamaSutra, Cupid, Durex with no Indian plant post-2012). Border axis inverted: import policy FREE (40141010), while a Schedule-2 export prohibition walls the subsidy in — India is simultaneously a top-4 exporter (HLL, Cupid → UNFPA/WHO). Split-domicile 67th = POPULATED. For Phase-3: registers can be procurement ledgers, and borders can wall subsidies in, not competitors out. Source: 1929-grok-r313q3.md.
### 1930 — LOT-REGISTERED: unit-terminal + lot-persistent geometry
**Finding (from R313):** identity-persistence 85th = LOT-REGISTERED (new cell) — the unit stays CONSUMED-TERMINAL but the lot persists in manufacturer batch records, NACO/GeM procurement registers, and recall dockets. Batch-code 74th = PRESENT at statutory tier (D&C Rules 1945 Rule 96; Schedule R; MDR Rule 44) — the first statutory PRESENT after three ABSENTs; serial-1 49th = ABSENT (the lot is the manufacturing atom; Durex single batch = up to 432,000 units). Key-strength = WEAK: ~500,000 fake Durex carried batch numbers shared with legitimate product (2005 MHRA/Irish case), forcing genuine-lot recall — the arc's richest printed key is its weakest verification. For Phase-3: marks checkable for presence are not marks checkable for authenticity; the schema must score key-strength by node, not by node count. Source: 1930-grok-r313q4.md.
### 1931 — The −60pp inversion: the wall protects the input, not the product
**Finding (from R313):** tariff-delta −60pp — finished condoms 40141010 at BCD 10%/IGST 0% vs latex concentrate at BCD 70% (stable since 2006). The wall protects Kerala's latex growers, not the condom maker — record as inversion, not protection. GST 27th cell: flat nil since 1-Jul-2017 (4014, Notification 2/2017 S.No. 112; still nil per Notification 10/2025) with a blocked-ITC wrinkle (exempt output + 5–18% inputs = uncredited embedded tax; nil ≠ free). The brief's "12%" history was rejected (sanitary-napkin memory misapplied). Consequence asymmetry: a failed condom fails silently — deferred harm, near-zero attribution — so the batch number is the only recall path; nine named verified cases (Durex 2018, Suretex 2000, ICMR 2006, China 2018, NACO 2009). Source: 1931-fo-r313q5.md.
### 1932 — PROXY: the twelfth fragility analogue, and registers unreachable at the point of trust
**Finding (from R313):** fragility twelfth analogue — PROXY (assurance-by-substitute: destructive QA means the unit you use is never the unit tested; the batch-proxy binding is a field-unfalsifiable print claim; failure is silent and consequence-delayed). CDSCO/SUGAM licensing DB = lit-for-lookup at regulator tier but unreachable at the point of trust (no consumer-facing licence token — the R311 refinement's second case); NACO/CMSS procurement = second register, lit-in-singletons, dark-for-enumeration. MDR-family note: condoms entered via s.3(b)(ii) "substances" door vs K2 syringes' s.3(b)(iv) "notified devices" door — a full risk class higher (Class C). WHO expanded device prequalification to condoms/IUDs (~Sep–Oct 2026) — a procurement-grade register above CDSCO/NACO. Source: 1932-fo-r313q6.md.
### 1933 — Class B pinned to CDSCO's 06.08.2021 ENT list; IS 16127 tender-driven not QCO-backed
**Finding (from R314):** Class B nailed to CDSCO's "Classification of Medical Devices Pertaining to ENT under MDR 2017" dated 06.08.2021 (item 6, BTE air-conduction hearing aid = B); the all-devices door is S.O. 648(E), 11.02.2020 (w.e.f. 01.04.2020); route MD-3→MD-5 (SLA, domestic) / MD-14→MD-15 (CLA/DCGI, import). IS 16127:2013 is tender-driven, not QCO-backed — no hearing-aid QCO surfaced at any tier, and the partner's "Medical Devices (Quality Control) Order, 2020" claim is NOT confirmed at web tier (quarantined as possible confabulation, 1910 doctrine). L6 stays ARMED-non-BIS (armed-BIS 38/12/20 unmoved). Double gate asymmetric: CDSCO statutory, ISI procuremental; logical order statutory-first. MDR reaches retail via 5th Amendment Rules 2022 (Rules 87A–87D: MD-41→MD-42 premises registration, ₹3,000) — but the fitting act is only person-regulated (RCI Act 1992 s.2 covers audiologists AND "hearing aid and ear mould technicians"; s.13 bars unregistered practice, no provision reserving retail fitting to RCI registrants; s.13 retail enforcement unmapped). Licensed device, unlicensed fitting establishment. Source: 1933-chatgpt-r314q1.md.
### 1934 — The emptiest fraud rail of the L-arc: double null against a non-zero harm lane
**Finding (from R314):** fraud-watch 121st = OFF-RAIL / RAIL-EMPTY / ADJACENT-RAIL-POPULATED (held from 120th) — double null at partner-direct AND search tier: zero named Indian seizures, FIRs, prosecutions, or convictions. Identity-fraud 88th = SPLIT-PARTIAL, MISDECLARED-dominant (held from 87th) — no universal mandatory mark, no BIS QCO, ISI tender-conditional; absent mark ≠ fraud; no docket of fabricated/cloned ISI or licence claims. Price band SURVIVES (₹8,490 floor → ₹7.2L+/kit, ₹10L+ top) but ZERO NPPA/DPCO ceiling or overcharge prosecution — high price ≠ overcharge. Zero prosecutions for online sales without prescription/fitting — lane definitional, no Indian OTC-hearing-aid rule. Adjacent rail live: Central Delhi DCDRC 6 Mar 2024 (Bengal Speech and Hearing; defective pair for an 11-year-old — defect, not fraud); Gurugram 15 Jan 2026 MD-35 seizure (optical/eye lenses — proof retail enforcement machinery is live elsewhere). With live adjacent machinery, the emptiness is a finding about hearing aids, not enforcement. Source: 1934-chatgpt-r314q2.md.
### 1935 — No Indian private maker of clinical digital aids; the flattest border in the audit
**Finding (from R314):** Big-5 India presence VERIFIED-MODIFIED — Sonova/Phonak ✓, WS Audiology/Signia ✓, GN/ReSound ✓ (but 2026 DKK 17B hearing-business sale to Amplifon moves the brand), Starkey ✓ Noida; hostile catch: Demant/Oticon shows NO subsidiary at search tier. NO Indian private maker of clinical digital aids exists. Makers = offshore Big-5 factories + ALIMCO (Kanpur PSU) welfare BTE lane; fitters = domestic fitting industry — Hearzap (420 centres, post-Aug-2026 Amplifon India acquisition ₹230+ cr, →500 by 2027) · Ear Solutions (75+) · C.C. Saha (1933). Fitting is the one chain link that cannot be imported. Border: ITC-HS 90214090 import policy FREE since 2006 (no DGFT gate); duty-nil for deaf-education institutions; exports open — the flattest border in the audit. Split-domicile 68th = POPULATED — FREE-IN + NO-CAPTIVE-PROCUREMENT + EXPORT-OPEN + CAPABILITY-WALL (manufacturing, not policy): the wall is India's inability to make DSP-powered aids, not any policy instrument. Bought-in 50th = PRESENT, import-dominated. Numbers three-tier: $235.34M (IMARC) / $74.54M (TechSci) / $900M (MRFR); ~500K aids sold 2013 (+15% YoY), penetration slightly above 1%; per-ear ₹14,995 → ₹8,50,000, MRP-vs-clinic gap ~30%. 2026 structural shock: Hearzap acquires Amplifon India while globally Amplifon buys GN's manufacturing — vertical-integration arrows point opposite directions. Source: 1935-grok-r314q3.md.
### 1936 — Batch-code 75th SPLIT, serial-1 50th PRESENT: the serial mandated by a foreign instrument, guarded by a private ledger
**Finding (from R314):** batch-code 75th = SPLIT (73rd ABSENT → 74th PRESENT → 75th SPLIT) — the pack keys at lot (MDR labelling, 2025 LMPC carve-out) while the shell keys at unit (on-device serial, US-mandated, universally practised); Singapore HSA encodes the same disposables→lot / powered-devices→serial split. Serial-1 50th = PRESENT (48th/49th ABSENT → 50th PRESENT) — hostile re-cut: NO Indian instrument mandates the serial; the mandating instruments are US — 21 CFR 801.420(b)(1) (Rx) and 21 CFR 800.30(c)(3)(i) (OTC, serial = sole mandatory on-device mark). India's label mandate is batch/lot only; UDI Rule 46 delayed since 31 Dec 2021. Key-strength = MEDIUM, LEDGER-GATED — serial is a real pointer to a private manufacturer ledger (Phonak HCP serial→warranty; "authentic devices check out, counterfeits don't") but buyer has no self-serve path (Oticon master DB closed); consumer apps pair via Bluetooth without authenticating; the working counterfeit tell is a *missing* serial. Identity-persistence 86th = UNIT-REGISTERED (private) — new cell: unit persists in manufacturer service registers, clinic fitting DBs (Noah: serial→patient→settings), warranty cards, insurance; NO statutory unit register. First unit-persistent/lot-secondary case — inverse of condoms' LOT-REGISTERED. Keying 88th = MARKED-SERIAL-KEYED (six nodes): on-shell serial + pack lot + licence trail (Mfg. Lic. No./import licence + importer) + fitting-pairing read/lock (Noahlink serial-read; chain-lock read-but-refused; Phonak duplicate-serial rejection) + warranty registration + ISI tender-conditional. Software trusts the claimed serial — no attestation. Fraud input: brand impersonation (Audien.us UDRP, Surender Kumar of India) + misdeclared amplifiers (PSAPs-as-aids); cloned-serial mechanically possible but unevidenced (banked, not claimed). ### 2077 — Refine-don't-overwrite observations (proof-count beliefs) [H1, from vectorize-io/hindsight tool study]
**Substance:** consolidated beliefs keep supporting evidence with exact quotes + a proof count; new evidence strengthens, weakens, or extends the belief instead of silently replacing it. **Transfer:** our conflict monitor shouldn't pick a winner silently when memories disagree — keep contenders with evidence and running proof counts; revision is a ledger, not an overwrite. (Caveat: LLM-dependent extraction end to end; treat as design pattern, not drop-in spec.) Source: tool-studies/HINDSIGHT-study.md.

### 2078 — Mental models as materialized standing answers [H2, from vectorize-io/hindsight tool study]
**Substance:** a standing question ("what are this user's preferences?") answered once, rewritten in the background as the bank learns; reading it = a DB read, no retrieval, no LLM. **Transfer:** precomputed memory views (extends cache contracts, idea 1506) — boot an agent with settled knowledge instead of rediscovering it every session. Source: tool-studies/HINDSIGHT-study.md.

### 2079 — Disposition traits as reasoning parameters [H3, from vectorize-io/hindsight tool study]
**Substance:** skepticism 1–5 (trusting→questions everything), literalism 1–5, empathy 1–5, set per bank, shaping the reasoning pass. **Transfer:** make *doubt* a tunable dial on our propose→deliberate→doubt→commit loop — high-stakes tasks run high-skepticism; casual recall runs low. (Caveat: traits are prompt-level steering with a 1–5 label, not a measured mechanism — UX pattern, not validated technique.) Source: tool-studies/HINDSIGHT-study.md.

### 2080 — Memory Defense at the write boundary [H4, from vectorize-io/hindsight tool study]
**Substance:** 45-pattern secrets/PII regex scanned on EVERY retain; action = redact (`[REDACTED:github_token]`) or block (422 if all items blocked); per-bank opt-in (off by default); trigger fires webhook + audit-log entry; forward-only (no retroactive scrubbing). **Transfer:** add a safety gate beside our quality gates — ours check *actionability*, theirs check *safety*; both belong pre-storage, both need audit trails. (Caveat: 45 regexes are gameable, US-PII defaults, a tripwire not a guarantee.) Source: tool-studies/HINDSIGHT-study.md.

### 2081 — Strict bank isolation as first principle [H5, from vectorize-io/hindsight tool study]
**Substance:** one brain per user/agent/project; no cross-bank leakage, ever. **Transfer:** we need an explicit stance for multi-agent memory (Council!) — Hindsight isolates, fleet-shared designs pool; our Phase-3 should declare which and enforce it in the storage layout. Source: tool-studies/HINDSIGHT-study.md.

### 2082 — Four-lane retrieval fusion (TEMPR) [H6, from vectorize-io/hindsight tool study]
**Substance:** semantic + BM25 + graph + temporal in parallel → RRF → cross-encoder rerank → trim to token budget. **Transfer:** our hybrid retrieval currently plans BM25+vector; add the graph lane (entity/temporal/causal links) and a rerank stage, and always budget-trim output. Source: tool-studies/HINDSIGHT-study.md.

### 2083 — Knowledge pages (self-writing wiki) [H7, from vectorize-io/hindsight tool study]
**Substance:** living documents a bank writes about itself, organized in folders, searchable, projectable to disk as plain markdown. **Transfer:** human-auditable memory exports — a memory system whose contents can't be read by a human can't be trusted. Source: tool-studies/HINDSIGHT-study.md.

### 2084 — Lifecycle webhooks [H8, from vectorize-io/hindsight tool study]
**Substance:** events fired on retain / consolidation / refresh. **Transfer:** our Janitor should emit migrate/evicted/promoted/rehydrated events — an observable memory lifecycle, not a silent one. Source: tool-studies/HINDSIGHT-study.md.

### 2085 — Bank templates (declarative provisioning) [H9, from vectorize-io/hindsight tool study]
**Substance:** banks created from declarative config (traits, policies, budgets). **Transfer:** memory-store setup as config-as-code, versioned with the agent's deployment. Source: tool-studies/HINDSIGHT-study.md.

### 2086 — Recall vs reflect as separate ops with separate budgets [H10, from vectorize-io/hindsight tool study]
**Substance:** cheap lookup and deep reasoning are different operations, not one "search harder" knob. **Transfer:** keep our deliberate/doubt stages budget-separated from recall — reflection spend must be visible and capped, never silently folded into retrieval. Source: tool-studies/HINDSIGHT-study.md.

### 2087 — Multilingual preservation end-to-end [H11, from vectorize-io/hindsight tool study]
**Substance:** facts stay in their original language and script (张伟 stays 张伟). **Transfer:** provenance fidelity — never normalize away the source form; translations are derived records (epistemic tier: derived), never replacements. Source: tool-studies/HINDSIGHT-study.md.

### 2088 — Independent-judge evals + reproduction discipline [H12, from vectorize-io/hindsight tool study]
**Substance:** eval suites scored by independent LLM judges; third-party reproduction treated as the real validation. **Transfer:** extend our benchmark-honesty doctrine (idea 1920/S6) — the goal for our gate numbers is independent reproduction, not self-reported wins. (Caveat: Hindsight's SOTA claim is vendor-framed; third-party reproduction ran on their harness and data.) Source: tool-studies/HINDSIGHT-study.md.

### 2107 — PI-1: Vectorless retrieval — the index is a layout tree, not a similarity search (from BEEHIIV-LIST tool study)
**Transferable design idea:** VectifyAI/PageIndex (installed and verified on our box: 3-page PDF → 16KB of pure JSON, zero embedding artifacts; smoke test answered a planted fact correctly) — retrieval as navigation of a document-structure tree, not vector similarity. Directly tests our "no black-box vector DB" doctrine and gives Phase 3 a concrete retrieval primitive to benchmark against. Source: tool-studies/BEEHIIV-LIST-study.md.

### 2108 — PI-2: Section-cited answers by construction (from BEEHIIV-LIST tool study)
**Transferable design idea:** PageIndex answers cite the exact node/page by construction — traceable, explainable retrieval. Our observed-vs-inferred marking, applied to the retrieval layer itself: every retrieved fact carries its provenance node. Source: tool-studies/BEEHIIV-LIST-study.md.

### 2109 — PI-3: Separate the index lane from the chat lane (from BEEHIIV-LIST tool study)
**Transferable design idea:** PageIndex separates the index lane (layout structure, cheap model) from the chat lane (reasoning, strong model) — different backends per lane. Our two-tier instinct made concrete: cheap deterministic structure work stays cheap, expensive reasoning stays in its lane. Source: tool-studies/BEEHIIV-LIST-study.md.

### 2110 — PI-4: Flash-vs-deep minimal effort (from BEEHIIV-LIST tool study)
**Transferable design idea:** PageIndex's flash mode (fast tree index for text PDFs) by default, deep mode only when layout is ambiguous — minimal-sufficient effort as an architectural default, not an afterthought. Source: tool-studies/BEEHIIV-LIST-study.md.

### 2111 — OJ-1: Belief-as-output — single-token probability readout (from BEEHIIV-LIST tool study)
**Transferable design idea:** OpenJev (open-weights single-shot decision model: one JSON in → decision + calibrated probability out; weights can't run on this VM — 16.5GB GGUF needs GPU; CC BY-NC 4.0) — the model's belief IS the output (single-token probability), no verbalized confidence to miscalibrate. Candidate answer to our gate-(b) calibration debt. Source: tool-studies/BEEHIIV-LIST-study.md.

### 2112 — OJ-2: Honest gap-to-reference calibration eval template (from BEEHIIV-LIST tool study)
**Transferable design idea:** OpenJev reports calibration as gap-to-reference on 10k+ real decisions (their claimed 84.0%, within 1.4pts of hosted Jev — project claims, not reproduced). An honest eval template for our Phase-3 calibration gate: state the gap, not just the accuracy. Source: tool-studies/BEEHIIV-LIST-study.md.

### 2113 — WK-1: Editable, diffable, rollbackable memory chunks (from BEEHIIV-LIST tool study)
**Transferable design idea:** Tencent WeKnora (LLM knowledge platform with self-maintaining wiki; study-only — Docker stack too heavy for this VM) — retrieval chunks editable, diffable, rollbackable: memory as a versioned store. Our reconsolidation idea, industrialized. Source: tool-studies/BEEHIIV-LIST-study.md.

### 2114 — WK-2: Admit-only-user-confirmed-facts write gate (from BEEHIIV-LIST tool study)
**Transferable design idea:** WeKnora's cross-session memory admits only user-confirmed facts/preferences — a fail-closed write analog from production, aligned with our fail-closed write path discipline. Source: tool-studies/BEEHIIV-LIST-study.md.

### 2121 — H1: Refine-don't-overwrite observations — proof-count beliefs (from HINDSIGHT tool study)
**Transferable design idea:** Hindsight consolidates facts into observations that keep supporting evidence with exact quotes + a proof count; new evidence *strengthens, weakens, or extends* the belief instead of silently replacing it. Transfer: our conflict monitor shouldn't pick a winner silently when memories disagree — keep contenders with evidence and running proof counts; revision is a ledger, not an overwrite. Source: tool-studies/HINDSIGHT-study.md (vectorize-io/hindsight, 51k stars, MIT).

### 2122 — H2: Mental models as materialized standing answers (from HINDSIGHT tool study)
**Transferable design idea:** a standing question ("what are this user's preferences?") answered once, rewritten in the background as the bank learns; reading it = a DB read, no retrieval, no LLM. Transfer: precomputed memory views (extends cache contracts, idea 1506) — boot an agent with settled knowledge instead of rediscovering it every session. Source: tool-studies/HINDSIGHT-study.md.

### 2123 — H3: Disposition traits as reasoning parameters (from HINDSIGHT tool study)
**Transferable design idea:** skepticism / literalism / empathy on 1–5 scales, set per bank, shaping the reasoning pass (1 = trusting, 5 = questions everything). Transfer: make *doubt* a tunable dial on our propose→deliberate→doubt→commit loop — high-stakes tasks run high-skepticism; casual recall runs low. Caveat: prompt-level steering with a label, not a measured mechanism — treat as a UX pattern. Source: tool-studies/HINDSIGHT-study.md.

### 2124 — H4: Memory Defense at the write boundary (from HINDSIGHT tool study)
**Transferable design idea:** 45-pattern secrets/PII regex scanned on EVERY retain; action = redact (`[REDACTED:github_token]`) or block (422 if all items blocked); per-bank opt-in (off by default); trigger fires webhook + audit-log entry; forward-only (no retroactive scrubbing). Transfer: add a safety gate beside our quality gates — ours check *actionability*, theirs check *safety*; both belong pre-storage, both need audit trails. Caveat: 45 regexes are gameable, US-PII defaults; a tripwire, not a guarantee. Source: tool-studies/HINDSIGHT-study.md.

### 2125 — H5: Strict bank isolation as first principle (from HINDSIGHT tool study)
**Transferable design idea:** one brain per user/agent/project; no cross-bank leakage, ever. Transfer: we need an explicit stance for multi-agent memory (Council!) — Hindsight isolates, fleet-shared designs pool; our Phase-3 should declare which and enforce it in the storage layout. Source: tool-studies/HINDSIGHT-study.md.

### 2126 — H6: Four-lane retrieval fusion (TEMPR) (from HINDSIGHT tool study)
**Transferable design idea:** semantic + BM25 + graph + temporal in parallel → RRF fusion → cross-encoder rerank → trim to token budget. Transfer: our hybrid retrieval currently plans BM25+vector; add the graph lane (entity/temporal/causal links) and a rerank stage, and always budget-trim output. Source: tool-studies/HINDSIGHT-study.md.

### 2127 — H7: Knowledge pages — self-writing wiki (from HINDSIGHT tool study)
**Transferable design idea:** living documents a bank writes about itself, organized in folders, searchable, projectable to disk as plain markdown. Transfer: human-auditable memory exports — a memory system whose contents can't be read by a human can't be trusted. Source: tool-studies/HINDSIGHT-study.md.

### 2128 — H8: Lifecycle webhooks (from HINDSIGHT tool study)
**Transferable design idea:** events fired on retain / consolidation / refresh. Transfer: our Janitor should emit migrate/evicted/promoted/rehydrated events — an observable memory lifecycle, not a silent one. Source: tool-studies/HINDSIGHT-study.md.

### 2129 — H9: Bank templates — declarative provisioning (from HINDSIGHT tool study)
**Transferable design idea:** banks created from declarative config (traits, policies, budgets). Transfer: memory-store setup as config-as-code, versioned with the agent's deployment. Source: tool-studies/HINDSIGHT-study.md.

### 2130 — H10: Recall vs reflect as separate ops with separate budgets (from HINDSIGHT tool study)
**Transferable design idea:** cheap lookup (recall) and deep reasoning (reflect) are different operations, not one "search harder" knob. Transfer: keep our deliberate/doubt stages budget-separated from recall — reflection spend must be visible and capped, never silently folded into retrieval. Source: tool-studies/HINDSIGHT-study.md.

### 2131 — H11: Multilingual preservation end-to-end (from HINDSIGHT tool study)
**Transferable design idea:** facts stay in their original language and script (张伟 stays 张伟) through extraction and storage. Transfer: provenance fidelity — never normalize away the source form; translations are derived records (epistemic tier: derived), never replacements. Source: tool-studies/HINDSIGHT-study.md.

### 2132 — H12: Independent-judge evals + reproduction discipline (from HINDSIGHT tool study)
**Transferable design idea:** eval suites scored by independent LLM judges; third-party reproduction treated as the real validation (Virginia Tech Sanghani Center + WaPo reproduced Hindsight's LongMemEval score on their harness). Transfer: extend our benchmark-honesty doctrine (idea 1920/S6) — the goal for our gate numbers is independent reproduction, not self-reported wins. Caveat: reproduction ran on the vendor's harness and data. Source: tool-studies/HINDSIGHT-study.md.

### 2159 — GI protects the name, not the packet: the origin-proof gap (from R345 saffron)
Kashmir Saffron, GI No. 635, Class 30 — granted May 2020 (GI Journal; PIB 2 May 2020; application 2018 by J&K Directorate of Agriculture with SKUAST-Kashmir and Saffron Research Station Dussu); registered proprietor: Director of Agriculture, Kashmir; ~32,000 growers slated for GI tag-code traceability. Under the GI Act 1999, misusing "Kashmir Saffron" on non-qualifying product is infringement — the legal weapon against relabelling exists. But the standard quality test (ISO 3632 absorbance) cannot prove geographic origin, and no GI-infringement enforcement docket was found. Transfer: name-protection without content-proof is a paper shield — any GI-style regime needs an origin test, not just a quality test, or enforcement stays theoretical.
**Source:** watch-log/2159-grok-r345q3.md; agronfoodprocessing.com; apnikheti.com/The Tribune; latestly.com/PIB.

### 2160 — The import lane is enforced; the repack lane is where the fraud lives (from R345 saffron)
HS 09102010; ~36% combined duties direct from Iran (trader claim, indicative); SAARC-via-Afghanistan zero-tariff routing is a TRADER CLAIM — flagged, not adopted, but it documents the origin-routing incentive (the relabelling vector). FSSAI Central import licence + IEC mandatory; FICS flow (document scrutiny → inspection → sampling → lab → NOC/rejection) with real teeth: any failed consignment resets the importer's history to zero → back to 100% sampling. Iranian saffron CAN clear legally as Iranian saffron; the fraud happens downstream at repacking — outside import clearance's line of sight. Transfer: enforcement boundaries create fraud migration — map where the regime's vision ends, because that is where the fraud goes.
**Source:** watch-log/2160-grok-r345q4.md; persatrading.com; rowhanisaffron.com; sjexim.services.

No commercial brand found with documented GI authorised-user status; the entire branded segment markets "Kashmiri" as a geographic descriptor. Challenger seat EMPTY on GI-authorised terms. **Source:** watch-log/2161-fo-r345q5.md.

### 2162 — MARKET-KEYED grading and the dye-blind test (from R345 saffron)
ISO 3632-1, 3rd edition (July 2025): FOUR grades now (Extra Class/I/II/III — pre-2025 sources citing three categories are on the old edition). Test = UV-vis of 1% extract (440nm crocin / 257nm picrocrocin / 330nm safranal). Indian trade grades mongra (all-red, top) / lacha / pushal are market conventions, not statutory. Mandatory layer = food safety only (FSSAI); IS 5453 and ISO 3632 grading are VOLUNTARY. Keying 119th: MARKET-KEYED — the first market-keyed cell (contrast regulator-keyed families). Critical structural fact: the ISO absorbance method **cannot distinguish synthetic dye from natural pigment** — a dyed product can score well on colour. Transfer: grade certifies strength, not authenticity — any quality regime whose test is blind to the main fraud mode is measuring the wrong thing.
**Source:** watch-log/2162-fo-r345q6.md; spiceography.com; BIS catalogue.
