Fourth ChatGPT S.O. fabrication caught in the corpus. Transfer: any partner QCO claim now needs a Gazette-or-consultant cross-check before entering the corpus — the fabrication unit has escalated from numbers to whole instruments.
**Source:** watch-log/2163-chatgpt-r346q1.md; seair/eximguru duty tables; evtlindia.com; taxguru.in.

### 2164 — Bitumen fraud: honest negative on all three physical types (from R346 bitumen)
No qualifying Indian enforcement docket (brand + date + quantity) found for (a) fluxing/cutting with kerosene or furnace oil, (b) grade substitution (VG-30 as VG-10), or (c) short-loading at depots/sites. The "bitumen scam" in Indian reporting = procurement/supply fraud for road works, not physical adulteration — a different shape, not counted. Bounded finding, not proof of absence. Transfer: keep the fraud-shape taxonomy honest — procurement fraud and product fraud are different cells; conflating them inflates the fraud-watch.
**Source:** watch-log/2164-chatgpt-r346q2.md.

### 2165 — Tender-keyed grading: IS 73 defines it, MoRTH enforces it (from R346 bitumen)
IS 73:2013 (Fourth Revision) classifies paving bitumen by viscosity — VG-10/20/30/40 (absolute viscosity in poise at 60°C: 800/1600/2400/3200), replacing penetration grades (approx: VG-10≈80/100, VG-30≈60/70, VG-40≈30-40/40-50). MoRTH's 23 Aug 2023 circular (RW/NH-35072/05/2018-S&R(P&B)) mandates VG selection per IRC:37 for NH projects, VG-40 ≥3600 poise, wax ≤4.5% (IS 10512). Enforcement bites through tender/contract documents, not compulsory certification. Transfer: a standard can fully restructure a market's grading with zero compulsory-certification instrument — the enforcement surface is the buyer. Policy can be enforced at the consumer of memory (retrieval contract), not only at the producer (write gate).
**Source:** watch-log/2165-grok-r346q3.md; foxmandal.in; HP Bitumen Handbook.

### 2166 — Open import door, no product gate (from R346 bitumen)
HS 2713.20.00 (petroleum bitumen): BCD 5% + SWS 10% + IGST 18%, import policy Free. Reference origin Iran (Bandar Abbas; HPCL 354,000t tender). Destination inspection applies to 2713/2714/2715 lines but there is NO product-certification gate at the border — quality = the buyer's tender spec. No dumping case found. Transfer: an open door with a process check but no product gate is the trade twin of the store-first anti-pattern — the seam where goods change hands is where the adulterant enters; fail-closed means the gate sits there, not where the paperwork is filed.
**Source:** watch-log/2166-grok-r346q4.md; seair/eximguru; argusmedia.com; verigates.bureauveritas.com.

### 2167 — Don't hunt challengers where no licence exists (from R346 bitumen)
PSU refiners (IOCL/BPCL/HPCL/Nayara) + private importers (Bharat Bitumen, CGOC) supply on tender spec; NO IS 73 BIS licence verified anywhere — consistent with no QCO. Challenger seat EMPTY on licensed terms (3rd consecutive round). Bharat Bitumen's "IS73:2014" citation flagged (BIS catalogue: 2013 fourth revision). Transfer: a leaderboard needs a scoring rule — no licence ⇒ no licence leaderboard; refuse to rank on dimensions the corpus doesn't score.
**Source:** watch-log/2167-fo-r346q5.md; tatanexarc.com; cgoc.in; bharatbitumen.com.

### 2168 — Detection capability ≠ detection coverage (from R346 bitumen)
Sharp test battery exists: flash point (ISI min 175°C; depressed flash = the classic kerosene tell), absolute/kinematic viscosity, penetration, softening point (ring-and-ball), solubility ≥99%, spot test (cracking), ductility, wax ≤4.5%. But there is NO notified lab network — testing is contract-driven (contractor QC, client site labs, NABL third parties, supplier self-certification per lot, cf. Oil India GeM tender). A self-certified lot is caught only if the buyer actually samples. Transfer: the conflict monitor can be perfectly calibrated and still blind if nothing invokes it — monitoring must be SCHEDULED, not merely AVAILABLE. The Janitor lesson in another uniform: a test that runs only when someone remembers is a decoration.
**Source:** watch-log/2168-fo-r346q6.md; testbook.com; mkp.gem.gov.in.

### 2169 — Standard exists ≠ compulsory: the BIS-vs-CDSCO separation (from R347 bandages)
ChatGPT-direct Q1 (verified clean, no fabrication): IS 758 covers absorbent cotton gauze, not every crepe/elastic/adhesive bandage; no QCO makes any bandage standard compulsory. A bandage's CDSCO/medical-device obligations (MDR 2017) are a SEPARATE question from BIS certification — "medical device" does not automatically mean "BIS-certified," and a BIS standard does not automatically mean "CDSCO-licensed." Transfer: our regime-mapping must keep axes orthogonal — never let one regime's answer leak into another regime's question.
**Source:** watch-log/2169-chatgpt-r347q1.md.

### 2170 — NSQ alerts are not enforcement dockets (from R347 bandages)
ChatGPT-direct Q2 honest negative: no qualifying fraud docket (brand+date+quantity) for bandages. CDSCO's Not-of-Standard-Quality alerts are batch-level quality failures — an alert is not an enforcement docket establishing counterfeit sale or seizure quantities. Transfer: an alert stream is a signal, not a verdict — our fraud-watch must keep "alert" and "docket" as distinct states, never promote one to the other.
**Source:** watch-log/2170-chatgpt-r347q2.md; cdsco.gov.in NSQ alerts.

### 2171 — Dual-jurisdiction pattern: additive regimes, no conflict (from R347 bandages)
Bandages are "drugs" under Section 3(b), D&C Act 1940 (litigated, A.P. State Bandage case 2004) with standards in Schedule F(II), D&C Rules 1945 — AND Class A medical devices under MDR 2017 (non-sterile: self-certify + e-portal; sterile: registration + QMS audit). A sterile bandage sits under BOTH regimes; the regimes are additive, not alternative. Transfer: our conflict monitor needs a dual-jurisdiction pattern — one record, two regimes, no contradiction; conflict detection must NOT fire on additive overlap, only on contradictory obligations.
**Source:** watch-log/2171-grok-r347q3.md; indiankanoon.org/doc/832339/; testbook.com; accelgroups.com.

### 2172 — Low-friction import = higher downstream verification weight (from R347 bandages)
HS 3005 bandages: ITC import policy Free; the real gate is CDSCO (MD-14→MD-15 via SUGAM). Permissive port + self-certify device registration means the fraud seam is the domestic distributor, not the port (saffron R345 inverted: there the port gate had teeth). Transfer: model "Free policy + permissive registration" as a low-friction signal — low-friction import regimes deserve HIGHER downstream verification weight, not lower.
**Source:** watch-log/2172-grok-r347q4.md; eximguru.com; dgciskol.gov.in; medicaldeviceregistration.com.

### 2173 — Challengers are regime-relative (from R347 bandages)
Datt Mediproducts (1995, EOU, CE/ISO, 30+ export countries), J&J/Kenvue (market leader), Sterimed — all operate on drug licences + ISO/CE; ZERO ISI-licence claims found. Challenger seat EMPTY on BIS-licence terms (4th consecutive round). Transfer: a challenger defined against the wrong regime's leaderboard optimizes the wrong thing — challengers must be defined against the vertical's LIVE regime.
**Source:** watch-log/2173-fo-r347q5.md; dattmedi.com; pmarketresearch.com.

### 2174 — Capability-without-coverage is a PATTERN, not an anecdote (from R347 bandages)
Third consecutive vertical with a sharp test battery and a human enforcement link: bandage tests (absorbency, sterility USP <71>, tensile, breaking load, stretchability) exist; no notified lab network — buyer QC + NABL-per-contract + self-cert. Sharpest fraud signal = sterility-label fraud; softest target = the non-sterile end (CDSCO itself wants a Schedule M part for it). Transfer: our Janitor/audit doctrine should treat "capability without coverage" as the DEFAULT assumption and schedule verification accordingly.
**Source:** watch-log/2174-fo-r347q6.md; anyflip.com meditech specs; edurev.in; alephindia.in; jjrlab.com.

### 2175 — Standard ≠ compulsory, and pin the edition (from R348 wheelchairs)
IS 7454 exists as the BIS wheelchair standard, but ChatGPT cited the 2001 edition while sellers cite IS 7454:1991 — edition UNCERTAIN. Two lessons: (1) a standard's existence never implies compulsory certification — only a QCO does that; (2) when a standard is cited, the EDITION is part of the claim — an edition mismatch (like the R343 MISLABELED-IS trap) is a signal, not trivia. Transfer: the conflict monitor's provenance records must carry edition/version on every instrument citation; a bare IS number is an incomplete citation.
**Source:** watch-log/2175-chatgpt-r348q1.md; bastiharsh.in; bidplus.gem.gov.in.

### 2176 — Duty litigation is not fraud enforcement (from R348 wheelchairs)
CESTAT Chennai 2026 (Commissioner of Customs vs Karma Health Care Ltd., TMI 710) is a real docket with brand + year + goods — but it's a CLASSIFICATION dispute (toileting wheelchairs → CTH 8713, exemption under 12/2012-Cus), not a substandard-product enforcement action. Lesson: the fraud-watch bar (brand+date+quantity+enforcement) has a hidden fourth element — the ACTION must be about the fraud, not about tariff classification. A docket-shaped object is not a fraud docket. Transfer: the fraud classifier needs an action-type field; misclassifying a classification dispute as enforcement is a false positive of the same family as PHANTOM-QCO.
**Source:** watch-log/2176-chatgpt-r348q2.md; taxtmi.com.

### 2177 — Dual-jurisdiction mapping without a forced winner; buyer = regulator (5th vertical) (from R348 wheelchairs)
Wheelchairs sit under CDSCO/MDR 2017 (manual = Class A, licence-exempt; powered = Class B per ChatGPT vs Class C per consultant — DISPUTED, needs the CDSCO classification list) AND under procurement regimes (GeM tenders requiring "Bis Required: Yes" per IS 7454 + MDR 2017 compliance in one document; ADIP/ALIMCO procurement eligibility as the welfare-channel gate). GeM tender text literally staples the D&C Act and MDR 2017 into the purchase — the buyer's contract is where the regimes meet. Transfer: conflict detection must not fire on additive overlap (R347 doctrine); the procurement channel is a first-class regulatory surface — model "eligible for tender" as a compliance state alongside "licensed".
**Source:** watch-log/2177-grok-r348q3.md; bidplus.gem.gov.in; PMC8150429.

### 2178 — The permissive import lane as a signal (from R348 wheelchairs)
HS 8713 (87131010/87139010 "wheel chairs for invalid"), ITC policy Free, historical Nil duty, exemption litigation that importers WIN (CESTAT 2026). No product-certification gate at import; the only possible gate is CDSCO MD-14/MD-15. Lesson: a permissive import lane + self-certify domestic regime = the fraud seam sits downstream at distribution — same shape as R347 bandages. Transfer: the monitor should weight downstream verification higher when both the import gate and the domestic gate are permissive; low-friction entry ⇒ high downstream verification weight (idea 2172 generalized).
**Source:** watch-log/2178-grok-r348q4.md; eximguru.com; taxtmi.com.

### 2179 — Voluntary-licence challengers vs compulsory-licence challengers (from R348 wheelchairs)
Challenger seat FILLED on voluntary-licence terms: bastiharsh.in (Basti, UP) claims "BIS Certified · IS 7454:1991" wheelchairs; Krypton Industries Ltd's FY2023 annual report states BIS granted it the Standard Mark licence for IS 7454 (folding adult wheelchairs). This breaks the 4-round "EMPTY" streak — but only because the challenger definition was regime-relative (R347 lesson): against a compulsory regime the seat is empty (no QCO, no compulsory licences); against the voluntary regime, licences exist. Transfer: every leaderboard must declare its regime — a "top licence holders" list without the compulsory/voluntary qualifier is a category error. And a leaderboard needs a scoring rule (idea 2167): no licence regime ⇒ no licence leaderboard.
**Source:** watch-log/2179-fo-r348q5.md; bastiharsh.in; Krypton Industries FY2023 annual report.

### 2180 — Capability-without-coverage is a PATTERN (4th consecutive vertical) (from R348 wheelchairs)
ISO 7176 is a sharp battery (Part 1 static stability, Part 2 dynamic, Part 3 brakes, Part 8 static/impact/fatigue with multi-drum + kerb-drop, Part 14 power systems, Part 19 transport crash, Part 21 EMC). Karma's global programme runs in-house + TÜV + crash facilities — but that is brand-internal, and no Indian notified lab network for wheelchair testing was found; IndiaMART "ISO 7176-19" claims are marketing-level. Nobody in India is compelled to run ISO 7176 before selling a wheelchair. Fourth vertical in a row (R345 saffron dye-testing, R346 bitumen labs, R347 bandage sterility labs, R348 wheelchair labs). Transfer: promote idea 2174 from observation to doctrine — the Janitor/audit design assumes capability-without-coverage by DEFAULT; verification is scheduled, never assumed. The conflict monitor lesson from R346 (2168): a perfectly calibrated monitor that nothing invokes is a decoration.
**Source:** watch-log/2180-fo-r348q6.md; standards.iteh.ai; karmamedical.com; whirlwindwheelchair.org.

### 2181 — TRAP-CATALOGUE: PHANTOM-QCO (from P-arc review, R346)
A wholly fabricated Quality Control Order — instrument name + S.O. number + date — with zero Gazette/BIS/consultant trace. The S.O. number may be real on a DIFFERENT instrument (rebound identifier): R346's "Bitumen (Quality Control) Order, 2023, S.O. 3290(E), 17 Jul 2023" — S.O. 3290(E) is real (Benami 2016; DGFT jute 2025), the QCO is not. ChatGPT escalated from fabricating numbers to fabricating whole instruments (4th fabrication caught by tier-2). Detection rule, now standing: every partner QCO claim gets a Gazette-or-consultant cross-check before entering the corpus. Transfer: the fail-closed write gate needs an instrument-existence check — a citation that resolves to nothing is a rejection, not a gap.
**Source:** watch-log/ROUND-346-SYNTHESIS.md; watch-log/P-ARC-SYNTHESIS.md.

### 2182 — TRAP-CATALOGUE: MISLABELED-IS (from P-arc review, R343)
A real IS number pasted onto the wrong product: standphillindia's "IS 302 (Part 2/Sec 25)" for induction cooktops — Section 25 is the microwave-oven section (R337). The number is real; the attachment is wrong. Detection: section-to-product mapping check against the BIS catalogue. Sibling of PHANTOM-QCO (fabricated instrument) and ZOMBIE-INSTRUMENT (dead instrument cited as live). Transfer: provenance records must bind instrument → product scope; a valid citation with a wrong scope is a distinct failure mode from a fabricated citation — the write gate must check scope-binding, not just existence.
**Source:** watch-log/ROUND-343-SYNTHESIS.md; watch-log/P-ARC-SYNTHESIS.md.

### 2183 — TRAP-CATALOGUE: ZOMBIE-INSTRUMENT + PHANTOM-RESURRECTION (from P-arc review, R341/R342)
ZOMBIE-INSTRUMENT: a dead/superseded instrument cited as live (held from R342, pending a confirmed kill). PHANTOM-RESURRECTION: claiming a dead instrument is back in force (R341, banked 3rd round). Both are temporal-scope failures — the instrument existed, but its live/dead status is wrong. Detection: cutoff-vs-claim-date anchoring (standing discipline) — check the instrument's enforcement window against the claim date. Transfer: every memory record carrying a regulatory claim needs a validity window (bi-temporal provenance, idea 26); a claim without a live/dead status is incomplete.
**Source:** watch-log/ROUND-341-SYNTHESIS.md; watch-log/P-ARC-SYNTHESIS.md.

### 2184 — Edition is part of the citation; QCO-unresolved ≠ QCO-absent (from R349 dental chairs)
Q1 (ChatGPT-direct, clean leg): relevant standard = IS 13450 (Part 2/Sec 60):2017, *Medical electrical equipment — particular requirements for dental equipment*. ChatGPT explicitly refused to invent an S.O. number for the QCO and would not give a yes/no on compulsory BIS certification without it — a model honest negative, fabrication count stays 4. Transfer: an unresolved regulatory question is a finding ("QCO: NONE verified"), not a gap to fill with a plausible number; the corpus must never convert "unverified" into "absent" silently — mark the state.
**Source:** watch-log/2184-chatgpt-r349q1.md.

### 2185 — Docket-shaped objects are not fraud dockets (from R349 dental chairs)
Q2 (ChatGPT-direct, honest negative): no qualifying enforcement docket (brand + date + quantity) for dental-chair fraud — structural/hydraulic failure, fake certification, ADIP/GeM diversion, counterfeit branding. BIS/CDSCO/ADIP/GeM mechanisms exist but hold no chair-specific record. Fraud-watch 157th OFF-RAIL. Transfer: a docket-shaped object (classification dispute, procurement notice, consumer complaint, general raid) is not evidence of the alleged fraud — the brand+date+quantity bar is the filter, and an honest negative at the bar is the corpus's cleanest state.
**Source:** watch-log/2185-chatgpt-r349q2.md.

### 2186 — Classification is the routing key (from R349 dental chairs)
Q3: Class B for dental devices CORROBORATED via secondaries (pharmaregulatory.in, absoluteveritas.com); the entire enforcement chain flows from the class letter — SLA vs CLA, MD-3/MD-4 vs MD-7/MD-8 applications, MD-5 vs MD-9 licences, audit timing. Transfer: a memory record asserting a regulatory obligation on a device must carry its class letter; without it the obligation is un-routable. The conflict monitor's analogue: every obligation needs its authority chain attached.
**Source:** watch-log/2186-grok-r349q3.md; pharmaregulatory.in; absoluteveritas.com.

### 2187 — Record the gate, not the policy (from R349 dental chairs)
Q4: HS 9402.10.10, 10% BCD + 18% IGST (≈30.15%), import policy Free — the customs gate is fiscal only; the live gate is CDSCO (MD-14/MD-15 + Indian Authorized Agent). Chapter 94 (furniture), not Chapter 90 — Chapter 90 notes exclude "supporting furniture", which is exactly where dental chairs sit. Transfer: a "Free" policy is noise; the licence requirement is the signal. Record enforcement gates, not tariff weather. Boundary-lesson: the chapter that excludes you is as informative as the one that admits you.
**Source:** watch-log/2187-grok-r349q4.md; seair.co.in; eximguru.com.

### 2188 — Challenger leaderboards are regime-relative (from R349 dental chairs)
Q5: seat FILLED on voluntary-licence terms — Confident Dental (45+ years, ISO 13485:2016), Unicorn Denmart (ISO 13485:2016), Gladent China (CE, ISO 13485, FDA, TGA). Zero BIS Standard Mark licence claims anywhere — consistent with no QCO. Transfer: declare the leaderboard before ranking — voluntary (ISO 13485/CE/FDA) vs compulsory (BIS Standard Mark). ISO 13485 is not a substitute for an absent BIS licence; they score different things. A leaderboard needs a scoring rule, and the rule must name the regime.
**Source:** watch-log/2188-fo-r349q5.md; testconfidental.shop; imimg.com.

### 2189 — Capability-without-coverage, fifth vertical (from R349 dental chairs)
Q6: ISO 6875:2011 battery is sharp — sink ≤10 mm/h, tipping/stability, bursting pressure, pressure relief, 40 kg exceptional load, emergency stop, IEC 60601-1 electrical — plus ISO 7494-1:2018 for dental units. No Indian notified lab network found; testing = manufacturer self-cert + ISO 13485 audits. Fifth consecutive vertical (R344→R349). Transfer: promoted to doctrine — assume capability-without-coverage by default; verification must be SCHEDULED, not merely AVAILABLE. A test nobody is scheduled to run against your product is a decoration.
**Source:** watch-log/2189-fo-r349q6.md; standards.iteh.ai.

### 2190 — QCO-unresolved is a finding, not a gap (from R350 patient monitors)
Q1: ChatGPT-direct clean leg — IS 13450 (Part 2/Sec 49):2018 cited WITH edition, then explicitly refused to invent an S.O. number for a patient-monitor QCO ("A BIS standard existing for a product does not, by itself, make BIS certification compulsory"). 4th consecutive clean round; fabrication count stays 4. Transfer: edition-as-citation (the year is part of the claim); an honest "cannot verify" from the partner is the vantage gap recorded, not papered over. A QCO-unresolved state is a finding — it routes the reader to the Gazette, not to an assumption.
**Source:** watch-log/2190-chatgpt-r350q1.md.

### 2191 — The docket filter holds (from R350 patient monitors)
Q2: ChatGPT-direct honest negative across all three fraud categories — no brand+date+quantity docket in any official record; refused to fill gaps with press accounts. Fraud-watch 158th OFF-RAIL. Transfer: brand+date+quantity is the filter; a report describing a raid without an official record of particulars is a press release, not a docket. The discipline is in what you refuse to report.
**Source:** watch-log/2191-chatgpt-r350q2.md.

### 2192 — The classification boundary, not the letter, is the finding (from R350 patient monitors)
Q3: basic BP/ECG = Class B (SLA), multi-parameter/cardiac = Class C (CLA), fetal/neonatal/advanced ICU = Class D — secondaries converge (medicaldeviceregistration.com, operonstrategist.com, regulatorymedicaldevice.com); CDSCO list-direct outstanding. Transfer: classification is the routing key — the whole licence chain (MD-5 vs MD-9, SLA vs CLA) flows from the class letter. When one product family spans classes, the boundary is the variable; don't flatten families into a single class. A regulatory claim without a class is un-routable.
**Source:** watch-log/2192-grok-r350q3.md; medicaldeviceregistration.com; operonstrategist.com.

### 2193 — 9018-vs-9019: the boundary lesson (from R350 patient monitors)
Q4: HS 9018.19 (9018193010 = "The patient monitor(machine)" per xtransfer; freightamigo: 9018.19 covers vitals monitors). Not 9019 (mechano-therapeutic). Import policy Free — the live gate is CDSCO MD-14/MD-15, not customs. Transfer: record the gate, not the policy — "Free" is noise, the licence requirement is the signal. The heading that excludes you (9019) is as informative as the one that admits you (9018).
**Source:** watch-log/2193-grok-r350q4.md; xtransfer.com; freightamigo.com.

### 2194 — Company-level claims are not CM/L evidence (from R350 patient monitors)
Q5: BPL Medical (ISO 13485:2016, "CDSCO certification for most products, along with AERB and BIS" — medgatetoday.com) is the strongest domestic challenger, but the BIS mention is company-level with no CM/L number cited. Zero BIS Standard Mark licence claims found anywhere — consistent with no QCO. Transfer: a leaderboard needs a declared scoring rule, and company-level certification claims are marketing until pinned to a licence number. Compulsory leaderboard EMPTY by design where no QCO exists; rank on the regime that actually bites (CDSCO + ISO 13485 + tender specs).
**Source:** watch-log/2194-fo-r350q5.md; medgatetoday.com; mkp.gem.gov.in.

### 2195 — Capability-without-coverage, sixth vertical (from R350 patient monitors)
Q6: sharp battery — IEC 60601-2-49:2011 (withdrawn 2018) → IEC 80601-2-49:2018+AMD1:2024; IS 13450 Part 2 Sec 49; alarms per IEC 60601-1-8 (auditory AND visual physiological alarms mandatory); SpO2 accuracy ±2% over 70–100%. No Indian notified lab network found; testing = self-cert + NABL-per-contract + buyer QC. Sixth consecutive vertical (R344→R350). Same lesson as the Janitor: monitoring that isn't on a schedule doesn't exist.

### 2196 — The BIS equivalent of an IEC number is discoverable, not guessable (from R351 surgical tables)
IS 13450 (Part 2/Sec 46):2017 is the Indian adoption of IEC 60601-2-46:2016 — BIS adopts IEC 60601 collateral standards as IS 13450 Part 2 sections. The mapping is a lookup, not an inference; guessing the IS number from the IEC number (or vice versa) is how phantom standards are born. Transfer: cross-standard mappings are retrieval facts, never derivation — cite the catalogue entry.
**Source:** watch-log/2196-chatgpt-r351q1.md; BIS catalogue.

### 2197 — The refused-guess table is the discipline made visible (from R351 surgical tables)
ChatGPT returned a table of fraud allegations with every cell marked "Not verified" and refused to supply a docket-shaped guess. An honest negative that lists WHAT was looked for and found absent is a finding, not a gap. Transfer: the conflict monitor should be able to say "checked, nothing meets the bar" with the checklist attached — absence with a receipt.
**Source:** watch-log/2197-chatgpt-r351q2.md.

### 2198 — Classification-dispute anatomy: check document dates first (from R351 surgical tables)
DCGI notice 29/Misc./03/2020-DC (199) says "Operation table system" = Class A; the current CDSCO list says Class B; elexes reports a risk-based reclassification of the operation table system. Reclassification is a timeline, not a contradiction. Transfer: when two records disagree, sort by document date before crying conflict — temporal layering resolves most apparent contradictions.
**Source:** watch-log/2198-grok-r351q3.md; umspcs.in; elexes.com.

### 2199 — MISLABELED-IS goes buyer-side (from R351 surgical tables)
GeM's 2026 OT-table catalogue pages demand "IEC-60601-2-40 or BIS Equivalent" — a phantom number; the real standard is IEC 60601-2-46. The MISLABELED-IS trap (R343, consultant-side) now has a buyer-side sibling: procurement specs need standard-number verification too. Transfer: trust no number by position — a phantom on an official tender is still a phantom.
**Source:** watch-log/2199-grok-r351q4.md; mkp.gem.gov.in; IEC webstore.

### 2200 — Trader-vs-manufacturer discipline (from R351 surgical tables)
Narang Medical is widely cited as a surgical-table "manufacturer"; IndiaMART lists it as Trader — Wholesaler/Distributor. Seating a distributor on a manufacturer leaderboard fabricates the leaderboard. Transfer: entity-role is part of the identity claim — verify the role (maker vs trader vs importer) before any ranking.
**Source:** watch-log/2200-fo-r351q5.md; m.indiamart.com.

### 2201 — Capability-without-coverage x7: the HF-immunity example (from R351 surgical tables)
IEC 60601-2-46:2023 demands HF-surgical-equipment immunity — no uncommanded table movement near a 300 W HF unit, resume within 15 s. A real hazard class with zero Indian enforcement surface (no notified lab network found, 7th consecutive vertical). Transfer: the sharpest version of the doctrine — a test for a lethal failure mode that no one schedules is a decoration.
**Source:** watch-log/2201-fo-r351q6.md; webstore.iec.ch; theiteh.com.

### 2202 — The honest-negative receipt format (from R352 suction machines)
ChatGPT Q1: "None verified is not a claim that no notification could exist." A proper honest negative states three things: what was searched, what would have counted as a positive, and what the finding does NOT prove. An unqualified "nothing found" is a claim about the world; the receipt format is a claim about the search. Transfer: every NOT_ENOUGH_INFO recall state (idea 1507) should carry its receipt — the query, the bar, and the scope of the negative.
**Source:** watch-log/2202-chatgpt-r352q1.md.

### 2203 — Adversarial review is training, not just filtering (from R352 suction machines)
Six consecutive clean ChatGPT rounds since the PHANTOM-QCO catch — the partner now refuses to invent S.O. numbers unprompted. Verification pressure changed the partner's behavior, not just the corpus's contents. Transfer: the hostile-check discipline (run against the brief first) compounds over rounds; the review loop is a training loop. Measure partner behavior over time, not just per-leg output.
**Source:** watch-log/2202-chatgpt-r352q1.md; watch-log/2203-chatgpt-r352q2.md; R346–R352 arc.

### 2204 — Product-specific notice beats guide-consensus (from R352 suction machines)
DCGI notice 29/Misc./03/2020-DC (199) says Class A for suction systems; six consultant guides say Class B. Rule: the dated product-specific notice wins pending a dated reclassification document; a guide-consensus without a cited primary is a rumor with a chorus. Transfer: in the conflict monitor, weight evidence by source-specificity × date, not by headcount — five copies of one uncited claim are one claim.
**Source:** watch-log/2204-grok-r352q3.md; pharmadocx.com; asiaactual.com.

### 2205 — HS-line discipline (from R352 suction machines)
"Suction machine" scatters across 8479, 8414, 8509, 84823000, 39269099; medical suction apparatus is 9018. The same word on two chapters is two different products; any enforcement count that ignores HS codes is counting noise. Transfer: fraud detection needs product-level (HS-line) search discipline — word-level search is a contamination vector.
**Source:** watch-log/2205-grok-r352q4.md; volza.com; seair.co.in.

### 2206 — Rank by licence-verifiability, not claim volume (from R352 suction machines)
IndoSurgicals displays an actual CDSCO MD-5 Licence — checkable against a registry; Narang Medical's manufacturer claim is role-UNVERIFIED (trader lesson from R351). Transfer: leaderboards score holders by how verifiable their licence is, not how loud the claim. A registry-checkable claim outranks ten marketing claims.

### 2207 — Verify the metric predicts the failure mode (from R352 suction machines)
JoVE 2025: ISO 10079's headline metric (instantaneous max air flow) correlates POORLY with liquid suction performance (r = −0.15); time-averaged flow correlates strongly (r = 0.97). A standard can be sharp in the wrong dimension. Transfer: for the conflict monitor, an M-score that doesn't predict decision error is the same failure class — measure every gate metric against the outcome it claims to serve, not against the dial.
**Source:** watch-log/2207-fo-r352q6.md; visualize.jove.com/40634625; standards.iteh.ai.

### 2208 — Definitional hostile check: pin the product before the regime (from R353 power drills)
The word "drill" sits on two completely different regimes — surgical bone drill (CDSCO Class B) vs hardware-store drill (BIS IS 4665 / MHI omnibus). Asking "what regime applies to drills" without pinning the product is a category error that no amount of research can fix. Transfer: in conflict detection, a dispute over "the same term" in two sources is only a conflict if the referents match — check identity before computing disagreement.
**Source:** watch-log/ROUND-353-SYNTHESIS.md.

### 2209 — Honest-negative receipt (from R353 power drills)
A "not found" is only a finding if it carries its receipt: what was searched, what would have counted, and what the negative does NOT prove. Q2's receipt (brand+date+quantity docket would count; press accounts do not; not-found ≠ proof of nonexistence) is the format. Transfer: every NOT_ENOUGH_INFO recall state (idea 1507) should carry its receipt.
**Source:** watch-log/2209-chatgpt-r353q2.md.

### 2210 — Boundary-by-intended-use: two regimes can bite the same word (from R353 power drills)

The ruling: map product definitions first, argue classification second — the boundary is intended use, not mechanism. Transfer: when two authorities both claim jurisdiction over "the same thing," don't pick a winner — check whether they're regulating the same referent.
**Source:** watch-log/2210-grok-r353q3.md; pharmadocx.com; cdsco.gov.in; lims.bis.gov.in; csagroup.org.

### 2214 — An honest negative can be a false negative (from R354 air coolers)

### 2215 — Edition drift is a misinformation vector (from R354 air coolers)

### 2216 — The QCO's anatomy is the finding (from R354 air coolers)
Air Cooler and Air Filters (Quality Control) Order, 2025: S.O. 529(E), 30 Jan 2025, supersedes the 2023 Order; compliance general 1 Apr 2025 / small 1 Jul 2025 / micro 1 Oct 2025; exemptions (export-only, Udyam micro ≤₹25L/≤₹2Cr, ≤200 R&D units/yr, pre-30-Jan-2025 stock to 31 Oct 2025); Scheme-I ISI Mark, BIS enforces, BIS Act 2016 penalties. ### 2217 — Record the gate, not the policy (from R354 air coolers)
HS 84796000 "Evaporative air coolers", import policy Free, BCD 7.5% + SWS 10% + IGST 18% — but the live product gate is BIS/FMCS certification under the QCO, not customs. Customs is fiscal; BIS is the gate. Transfer: in any regulated-import lane, identify the instrument that can STOP the goods, not the one that merely taxes them. "Free" import policy is noise; the certification requirement is the signal.

### 2218 — An empty public leaderboard where the law requires licences is a finding (from R354 air coolers)
No CM/L licence number publicly verifiable for Symphony, Kenstar, Bajaj, Havells — though the QCO (in force since 1 Apr 2025) requires BIS licences for legal sale. Either brands don't market the mark or compliance lags the rule. Transfer: never merge the compulsory leaderboard (BIS licence holders, opaque, held by the regulator) with the market-presence leaderboard (advertised brands). ### 2219 — Coverage is assessed per instrument, not per standard (from R354 air coolers)
BEE Schedule 40 (star labelling) documents market-surveillance check testing for evaporative air coolers: random market unit → NABL lab → fail draws double samples at a different lab → second fail names the model publicly. So capability-without-coverage is OVERRIDDEN for the BEE lane, but HELD for the BIS lane (post-market BIS surveillance unverified). The two instruments share one test standard (IS 3315:2024) but not one coverage regime. Transfer: when a standard is shared across instruments, audit coverage separately for each instrument. A memory record that says "tested" must say tested-under-which-instrument.
**Source:** watch-log/2219-fo-r354q6.md; absoluteveritas.com (BEE Schedule 40).

### 2220 — Conform-to-standard ≠ bear-the-mark (from R355 nail polish)
No nail-polish QCO verified; the live compulsory axis is Cosmetics Rules, 2020 licensing (SLA manufacture, CDSCO import registration via SUGAM), with BIS standards incorporated by reference via the Ninth Schedule ("shall conform to the Indian Standards specifications laid down from time to time by the BIS"). Transfer: a standard can be compulsory WITHOUT a QCO and WITHOUT the ISI mark. The conflict monitor must distinguish three states, not two: (a) QCO → ISI mark compulsory; (b) standard-conformity inside a licensing regime; (c) voluntary. Collapsing (b) into (a) or (c) is a classification error.
**Source:** watch-log/2222-grok-r355q3.md; legitquest.com (Ninth Schedule text).

### 2221 — The auto-mandate fuse (from R355 nail polish)

A standard becomes compulsory by reference with a six-month fuse. Transfer: any regime with an auto-mandate clause needs a clock-watcher — the six-month window is a fraud seam (who tracks it? who enforces during it?). Memory records citing such regimes must carry the fuse date.
**Source:** watch-log/2222-grok-r355q3.md.

### 2252 — HS/GST split as fraud surface (from R360 kajal)
HS 3304 20 00 (kajal pencil sticks) vs 3304 99 90 (other kajal); GST 18% on pencil sticks vs 0% on other kajal (GST Council, 11 June 2017). A product split across two tariff lines with two tax rates is two different fraud surfaces — and the residual "Other" line is the harder-to-track one. Transfer: HS-line discipline is a fraud-detection precondition; watch the residual line, where fraud migrates.
**Source:** watch-log/2253-grok-r360q4.md; seair.co.in (customs duty 3304); howtoexportimport.com (GST rates).

### 2253 — The gate is printed on the cargo (from R360 kajal)
Volza bills of lading for Swiss Beauty kajal (China → India, July 2025) carry "CDSCO REG NO: RC/COS-002931/81" — the COS-2 import registration gate is visibly printed on the cargo paperwork. Verifiable compliance artefacts beat claimed compliance. Transfer: prefer artefacts that live on trade paperwork over claims on marketing pages; the gate that leaves a paper trail is the gate you can audit.
**Source:** watch-log/2253-grok-r360q4.md; volza.com (Swiss Beauty / KIKO bills, July 2025).

### 2254 — For cosmetics the leaderboard question may be mis-posed (from R360 kajal)

### 2255 — Two risk objects, one market: name which object the test covers (from R360 kajal)
Traditional galena kajal (PbS primary ingredient; up to 840,000–980,000 ppm lead in the King County study) is the HAZARD object; manufactured IS-15154 kajal (vegetable-carbon suspension, Pb ≤20 ppm framework) is the REGULATED object. A passing battery on the wrong object is a decoration. Transfer: in a dual-object market, name which object every test, standard, and enforcement action covers — the JoVE lesson (idea 2207) generalized: verify the metric is aimed at the failure mode that exists in the market.

ChatGPT offered IS 3959:2004 as an unverified candidate; tier-2 found the current edition IS 3959:2023 within the hour via the archive.org full text. ### 2257 — A negative test result is evidence about the samples, not a clean chit for the market (from R361 talcum powder)
The 2019 Indian testing of Johnson's Baby Powder found no asbestos; production resumed at Baddi and Mulund. That is evidence about the tested samples — not proof the market is clean, and not an enforcement docket. The US FDA found asbestos in samples months later in a different jurisdiction. Transfer: a passing audit covers what it tested; memory should record the audit's scope (samples, date, method) alongside its verdict, so a later contradiction updates the belief (refine-don't-overwrite, H1) instead of being framed as a paradox.

Finished talcum powder (cosmetic) = HS 33049120 (185 import shipments, Seair); raw mineral talc = HS 2526.20 / 2517. The same word on two chapters is two different products with two different risk profiles (asbestos lives at the mineral tier). ### 2264 — Two coverage gaps, don't flatten them (from R362 hair dryers)

BIS's raid cadence (427 ISI-misuse instances/3 years) is the enforcement surrogate. Certification-time coverage is real under a live QCO; the gap is market surveillance.
### 2304 — Instrument pinned with S.O. pair + staggered clock (R369)
"Electrical Appliances for Domestic Water Heating (Quality Control) Order, 2025" — S.O. 355(E), 16 January 2025 (candidate-to-finding bar: pair stated twice by evtlindia, corroborated by alephindia's order-date table). Enforcement staggered: general 1 Mar 2025 · small 1 Jun 2025 · micro 1 Sep 2025. Lineage 2023/2024 orders → 2025 Extension Order: instruments have lineages; verify each link, don't flatten.
### 2305 — Vantage-gap ×9 (R369)
ChatGPT's honest negative said "none verified" on geyser incidents; tier-2 found four dated incidents (Ashwini Kedari electrocution Pune, 10-year-old gas-geyser blast Ahmedabad 86% burns, Aligarh gas-geyser suffocation 12-year-old, Deoria electrocution) within the hour. Honest negatives remain claims about search, never about the world.
### 2306 — The edition clock can itself be disputed (R369)
Two incompatible concurrent-running end dates on the IS 302-2-21:2018→2024 transition: BIS-sourced table (23 Feb 2026 / 2027) vs consultant piece (18 Feb 2025). Weight the BIS-sourced table; bank the conflict with sources named, never average.
### 2307 — NEAR-MISS-IS resolved as a pattern (R369)
IS 302-2-201 and IS 302-2-35 are REAL IS numbers on the WRONG object (immersion rods / instantaneous heaters) — the brief's candidates were real, the object was wrong. A near-miss is a real number on a wrong product: never accept or reject an IS number without pinning the object it covers.
### 2308 — BEE mandatory verified at the authority (R369)
beeindia.gov.in's official mandatory-appliances list puts "Stationary Storage Type Electric Water Heater" at #2. The fake-star seam is a compulsory seam here — the reverse of washing machines. Authority-first beats consultant tables; the seam moves with the mandatory/voluntary flag.
### 2309 — Three risk objects, two coverage gaps (R369)
Geysers: pressure (burst, relief valve per Cl 22.103 IS 302-2-21), electrical (shock/leakage), energy (star fraud) — each with its own battery (BIS Product Manual PM/IS 2082/2 official). Certification-time coverage closed under Scheme-I; market surveillance open. The licence number lives on the buyer side (GeM CM/L 9200104506 artefact) — check procurement specs for the artefacts brands won't publish.

### 2310 — Umbrella hypotheses can be CLOSED (R370)
Mixer grinders sit under the BIS Kitchen Appliances (Quality Control) Order, 2018 (in force 1 May 2019), NOT under the 2026 umbrella S.O. 1739(E) — which explicitly EXCLUDES goods covered by other QCOs (exclusion A). The brief's umbrella candidate was falsified by an exclusion clause. Audit exclusion clauses; "there is no single appliance order."

### 2311 — Scope ceilings in the standard are scope ceilings in the regime (R370)
IS 4250:1980 capped rated input at 750 W — mixers above that were OUTSIDE the QCO's purview (BIS CMD-III, 26 Sep 2023). When a standard caps a physical parameter, the compulsory regime inherits that ceiling as its coverage boundary. The 2025 second revision is the clock on this ceiling (removal expected, UNVERIFIED).

### 2312 — Vantage-gap ×10: the partner's refusal-shape is honest (R370)
ChatGPT refused the QCO without an S.O. pair ("none verified") — the second R354-shaped false negative. Tier-2 found name + date + in-force date from official BIS sources within the hour. Order name without the S.O. pair remains a CANDIDATE (R365 doctrine) — but a candidate is not "none verified." 20th consecutive clean round; fabrications stay 5.

### 2313 — The counterfeit-ISI seam verified with bodies (R370)
Mixer grinders are the first vertical where the populated-by-compulsion counterfeit-mark seam has PRODUCT-SPECIFIC enforcement: PIB 5 Mar 2025 (109 counterfeit mixers, M/s RBH Enterprises, Bhiwandi; multi-brand; counterfeit ISI; Sec 17/29 BIS Act) + 19 Mar 2025 Amazon-warehouse raid (food mixers among 3,500+ products with counterfeit ISI labels). Under compulsion the fraud object is the mark; the seam's location is unorganized manufacturing + e-commerce distribution.

### 2314 — HS 8509.40 discipline (R370)
Food grinders and mixers: 85094010 (food grinders) / 85094090 (other); parts 85099000; GST 18%; import policy Free. Record the GATE (2018 QCO import clause), not the policy. Heading covers electro-mechanical domestic appliances of any weight — 8509.80 vs 8509.40 is an adjudication edge for multipurpose machines; tag the object level.

### 2315 — BEE check-then-lens: two risk objects, not three (R370)
No BEE star-labelling schedule found for mixer grinders — the energy object doesn't exist, so the fraud seam is counterfeit-ISI only, not fake-star (the seam mode follows the mandatory/voluntary flag: R368 vs R369). Bonus: contested test parameters are data — the 2019 endurance-test fight (paper-pulp materials, small-maker disadvantage) shows where compliance cost concentrates.

### 2316 — Regime lineage, not one instrument (R371)

The brief's anchor "S.O. 2357(E), 3 Oct 2012" was correct as the ORIGINAL instrument, but the live regime for smartphones runs: 2012 order → mobile phones added 2015 → statutory order S.O. 1248(E), 2021 → amendment in force 7 Nov 2025 (Gazette ID CG-DL-E-07112025-267449). Instrument identity = number + date as a pair, AND the lineage matters: citing the 2012 order for today's compliance misses the migration amendment.

### 2317 — Honest negatives are claims about search; tier-2 closes within the hour (R371)

ChatGPT Q2's "none verified" carried an explicit session boundary ("no live web or docket access") — honest. But the same round's tier-2 found four dated dockets (10 May 2026 counterfeit Oppo/OnePlus/Realme raid; Karol Bagh 512 fake-IMEI phones; Gaffar Market ~1,500 IMEI-tampering; Khandelwal/Gupta 1,658 phones). The partner's vantage gap is not the world's gap; resolve honest negatives by fetch, never by acceptance (R354 lineage, 4th instance).

### 2318 — Edition currency needs a clock, not just an edition year (R371)

IS 13252 (Part 1):2010 was the correct answer AND already transitional: MeitY notified IS/IEC 62368-1:2023 in October 2025, concurrent validity till 1 November 2028, then withdrawal (XR devices: 1 May 2026). An edition year without the transition clock can silently answer yesterday's question. Records carry edition + assessment-date + transition deadline.

### 2319 — Trade direction orients the fraud lens (R371)

Volza counts for India mobile-phone imports are negligible (~1 shipment line) — India now exports. The 20% BCD wall (since Jul 2019) is industrial policy, not safety. The fraud lens belongs on domestic assembly (counterfeit/IMEI rackets), not the port. Import-led vs export-led is a routing input to the fraud model, not trivia (R359 lineage).

### 2320 — Multi-regime object: seams differ per instrument (R371)

The smartphone sits under: BIS CRS (electrical safety, registration R-number) + DoT SAR 1.6 W/kg (RF object) + DoT CEIR (IMEI identity object) + IS 16333 (Part 3):2022 (software/security, scope unverified). Each regime has its own enforcement body (BIS labs; TEC random testing; Delhi Police on the identity seam). Compliance evidence and fraud seams must be recorded per object — never flatten the regime stack (R367 lineage: two objects, two instruments, extended to four).

### 2321 — Capability-without-coverage ×21: the informal layer never enters the battery (R371)

The counterfeit-assembly economy (fake labels, cloned IMEIs, Moti Nagar printing presses) never touches the CRS registration battery at all — labs can test, but the fraudsters never submit. Market surveillance is police raids, not lab audits. An algorithmic lifecycle trusting self-certified state is a decoration; verification of the verifiers must be scheduled at the gap's actual location (R361 lineage: audit the COA chain — here the chain itself is counterfeited, so audit the identity layer).

### 2322 — Vantage-gap ×11: refusal-shape honest negatives are a partner strength (R372)

ChatGPT Q1 refused the Gazette S.O. pair, the edition, and the QCO without sources — all three answers were refusal-shaped. Tier-2 closed every one within the hour (S.O. 1248(E), 2021; IS 13252→62368-1 migration; no DPIIT QCO because the regime is registration). A partner that refuses rather than fills is trainable output (R359 lineage: adversarial review is training). Count the refusal as honesty, run tier-2, and move on — 22nd consecutive clean round.

### 2323 — Absence claims need regime-level confirmation (R372)

ChatGPT's "none verified" on a product-specific CCTV QCO turned out CORRECT, not a gap: the regime is MeitY CRS registration, not DPIIT licensing, so no QCO exists by construction. A "none verified" becomes a finding only when the regime is known (registration vs licensing) — otherwise it stays a search claim. Pin the regime first, then judge the absence.

### 2324 — Migration clocks have second hands (R372)

CCTV gained the STQC security layer (ER:01) as a compulsory precondition for the SAME CRS registration: one product, two batteries, two clocks (safety: concurrent till 1 Nov 2028; security: ER mandatory since 9 April 2025, full enforcement 1 April 2026). A lifecycle that tracks only the safety clock goes blind to the security gate. Schedules must carry every layer's clock (R366 lineage: draft orders get clocks, not verdicts).

### 2325 — Record the gate per regime (R372)

CCTV import lane: the port gate is the CRS import clause + STQC precondition — NOT customs duty. The firmware-security hazard is tested at STQC labs, never at the port. Where a compulsory regime has an import clause, the port is the enforcement surface for the MARK while the hazard seam lives at the testing body. HS 8525 80 (bills 85258910); recorders on 8521xx. Volza keyword recall contaminates (8541/8529/9002/7616/8544/3926) — hard HS filters.

### 2326 — Certification gates as industrial policy (R372)

The STQC chip-origin gate reshaped the market: CP Plus reportedly 20–25% → 45–50% share in two years; domestic makers 80%+; Delhi ripping out ~1.4 lakh Chinese cameras; Bosch/Honeywell gaining premium. A compliance regime can be a market-shaping instrument, not just a quality floor. For retrieval: "challenger" and "enforcement" records for CCTV live on the STQC security axis, not the BIS safety axis — index records by the axis that actually moves them.

### 2327 — Battery-per-object discipline (R372)

One named battery per regime: (1) electrical safety — CRS/62368-1; (2) cyber security — STQC ER (UART/JTAG/SWD, firmware extraction, update security, data encryption); (3) spectrum — WPC ETA (wireless only); (4) performance/image quality — NOT regulated, procurement-only; (5) data retention/IT Rules — separate axis, never conflated. Certification records must carry WHICH object each test answers — never answer a spectrum question with a safety certificate (R367 lineage: two objects, two instruments, extended).

### 2328 — The honest-negative receipt (R373)

A complete honest negative has three parts: (1) what was searched, (2) what was NOT searched, (3) the explicit refusal to convert the search claim into a world claim — "that is not a finding that none exists." Anything shorter is a vibe, not a receipt.

### 2329 — vantage-gap ×12 (R373)

Refusal-shape honest negative on the instrument; tier-2 closed the standard candidate within the hour. A candidate is not "none verified" — but neither is it a finding. Refusals carry the search boundary or they don't count.

### 2330 — Scope-language capture (R373)

The object pin lives in a scope sentence, not a product list. IS 302 (Part 2/Sec 13):2024's "**Similar Appliances**" clause is what pulls rapid-air-circulation ovens in — audit the inclusion language, never the title. A standard number with an edition is still half a citation until the scope sentence is read.

### 2331 — HS-line discipline: no borrowed duties (R373)

85167100 = coffee/tea makers; 85167990 = air fryers. Two lines, two products. Record the gate (QCO import clause), not the policy (Free); never copy a sibling line's duty rate onto the product line. A dirty HS table contaminates every downstream recall.

### 2332 — Brand count ≠ certification count (R373)

The licence register, not the marketplace, answers "who is certified." Prestige's "ISI certified" copy is populated-by-claim; no CM/L number published by any air-fryer brand in the sources reviewed. Challenger seat EMPTY on licence-verified terms.

### 2333 — BEE absence is a finding (R373)

Air fryers sit on neither the mandatory nor the voluntary BEE schedule — so the fake-star-label seam cannot exist for them. The fraud lens follows the instrumented object (electrical/thermal, compulsory), never the assumed one (energy, uninstrumented). Two objects, one instrumented.

### 2334 — Vantage-gap ×12: name-level instrument vs refused S.O. pair (R374)

Two consultant sources name "Safety of Household, Commercial and Similar Electrical Appliances Quality Control Order, 2026" covering clothes dryers + towel rails (implementation 1 Oct 2026); neither gives an S.O. pair. ChatGPT's honest negative (no pair, no claim) was defensible — but the instrument now has two name-level sources, so tier-2 must resolve whether "2026 Order" is a distinct instrument or S.O. 4098(E) 2024 as amended. Direction-correct ≠ instrument-correct: resolution = S.O. pair or lineage proof, not more name-citations.

### 2335 — Scope-sentence object pin (R374)

IS 302-2-11:1994's object lives in its scope sentence: ≤250 V ac/dc, household + communal (launderettes, apartment blocks), excluding industrial/commercial-only, vehicles/ships/aircraft, special atmospheres. The scope sentence, not the product name, decides which object a claim covers. When a keyword recall floods with industrial objects (textile dryers under 8451), the scope sentence is the filter.

### 2336 — Revision clocks attach to editions, not numbers (R374)

IS 302-2-11:1994 is cited by every source including BIS's own summary doc — while the general layer moved (IS 302 Part 1:2024) and the IEC lineage reached its 9th edition (2024). A standard's number can be current while its edition is legacy. Records carry edition + assessment-date; ask whether a revision is in the pipeline before calling an old edition a problem.

### 2337 — BEE absence, 2nd application (R374)

Clothes dryers are on neither BEE schedule (incl. the Jan-2026 mandatory extension) — the fake-star-label seam cannot exist here, just as for air fryers (R373). The fraud lens follows the instrumented object (thermal/fire, compulsory) and never the uninstrumented one. Absence on the schedule is a finding recorded at the authority list, not a gap to fill.

### 2338 — Thin import-led markets empty the licence leaderboard (R374)

Household clothes dryers in India = LG/Bosch/Siemens/IFB/Miele selling imports to a premium niche; no ISI-licence claims found; leaderboard populated-by-claim, EMPTY on licence-verified terms. In a thin import-led market, an empty licensed leaderboard is expected — the question is whether the regime makes it compulsory, and if so, where the counterfeit-mark seam lives.

### 2339 — Containment tests, not prevention tests (R374)

UL's dryer battery (Load Fire Containment + Base Fire Containment) assumes the fire — lint ignites — and asks whether the box contains it. Match the battery to the risk object (thermal/fire primary; electrical; mechanical), not the product name. A test battery is a hazard model; read it for what it assumes will go wrong.

### 2340 — The anchor confirmed is a finding, not an assumption (R375)

Weighing scales: the brief's Legal Metrology axis was corroborated against the Act (s.22 model approval, s.24/33 + Rule 27 verification/stamping) rather than echoed. Corroborate the brief's core before running it — an anchor confirmed is a finding; an anchor echoed is an assumption.

### 2341 — No docket is a limitation-of-verification state (R375)

ChatGPT's honest-negative on weighing-scale fraud was banked as limitation-of-verification, not closed as a world claim. 181st OFF-RAIL. Fraud hypotheses stay open until a dated docket arrives; "no verified docket" is a state, not a verdict.

### 2342 — Stamping is a clock (R375)

Legal Metrology stamping carries a 1-year validity; re-verification is the surveillance mechanism the appliance QCO regime lacks. Fraud surfaces on validity (expired/out-of-cycle stamp), not just authenticity. A compulsory regime with a built-in periodicity has a different surveillance geometry than one without.

### 2343 — Gate-on-cargo, 3rd application (R375)

Weighing-scale import bills print "LEGAL METROLOGY NUMBER - IMP/RJ/9/2022" and validity-dated registration numbers (Volza). The COS-2 pattern (R360) and QCO-import pattern generalize: verifiable approval artefacts ride the shipping manifest — audit the cargo, not the brochure.

### 2344 — Approval-based leaderboards (R375)

Under Legal Metrology the compliance unit is the model-approval number (s.22) + the annual stamping — not a brand, not an ISI mark. The leaderboard question becomes "who holds current approvals?" and is answerable only against the Controller's registry. Populated-by-claim extends to approval claims (Essae-Teraoka; no ISI claims market-wide).

### 2345 — Calibration is not verification (R375)

Calibration = measurement activity (error, uncertainty, traceability). Verification = statutory conformity check + stamping. Importing a calibration certificate as compliance evidence is a category error. A memory system must tag the object the certificate certifies — the certificate is evidence about its object, not about legality.

### 2346 — Stale-vintage candidate (R376)

A real IS number can be the wrong era. IS 2209 was the candidate for mortise locks; the current revision is IS 16015:2022 (which superseded IS 2209:1976, IS 7540:1974, IS 8760:1978, IS 16015:2013, IS 5930:1970, IS 6607:1972). Resolve candidates to the current revision, never to the remembered number.

### 2347 — Instrument-covers-object (R376)

Two compulsory instruments sat adjacent to the lock (fasteners QCO 2023 for padlock bolts IS 7534; safes/key-locks QCO Dec 2023 for security-equipment locks IS 17566) while the household door lock itself had no QCO. "None verified" is correct when the instrument covers the accessory, not the object. Honest negatives are about the pinned object, not the neighbourhood.

### 2348 — HS 8301 automotive contamination (R376)

Recall of HSN 8301 import totals was dominated by automotive locks (Aisin, Toyota) — keyword/HS recall without an object filter amplifies junk (R361 lineage). The import lane must be object-pinned before any fraud-direction claim.

### 2349 — The padlock-standard gap (R376)

The most-marketed object can have the thinnest standard coverage: no verified BIS product standard for the padlock itself was found, while the bolt accessory (IS 7534) and the mortise lock (IS 16015:2022) are pinned. Absence of a pinned standard is a finding about coverage, not about the product.

### 2350 — Populated-by-claim, 5th application (R376)

Dorset's "India's largest BIS-certified hardware range" and Godrej's locker certification carry no published CM/L licence numbers — populated-by-claim, not by evidence (R375 lineage). The compliance unit is the licence, not the brand name.

### 2351 — The battery lives in the standard (R376)

IS 16015:2022's durability cycles, salt-spray durations, and 12/6/3-month repeat-test clocks are written into the standard itself. Map the lab, not the battery — the open audit question is the verification venue, not the test battery.

### 2352 — Honest-negative posture survives a near miss (R377)

### 2353 — The denied category still needs a receipt (R377)

Q2's honest negative on mattress fraud came with an explicit search boundary (no police/customs/court archives in session) — "None verified" is a claim about search, not the world. Honest negatives that skip the receipt are indistinguishable from shrugs.

### 2354 — The dead candidate stays dead (R377)

IS 7376 had no corroboration in any search → candidate dies UNVERIFIED, not asserted wrong, not revived. The candidate-to-finding bar works both directions: verified 13489:2000, killed nothing wrongly, left 13489:2025 as candidate on one source.

### 2355 — GST lines need the 8-digit battery (R377)

Mattresses: 18% on the 8-digit lines (9404.21.10/.90, 9404.29.10/.20); one guide's 5% chapter-level claim banked as disputed. researchandmarkets claimed mattresses "must conform to BIS standards" and "requires manufacturers to obtain BIS certification" — FALSE against the voluntary finding and the standard's own "may be marked" clause. A revenue-motivated publisher's regulatory sentence gets tier-2 treatment like any consultant blog. Never cite a market report for a legal claim.

### 2357 — The compulsory axis can live in the tender document (R377)

No QCO on mattresses; the voluntary Standard Mark unclaimed by retail brands; but 20+ live government tenders demand IS 13489 (v3) conformity + NABL/ILAC test reports. Buyer-as-regulator ×14 (institutional branch): where the retail leaderboard is empty-by-design, enforcement sits in procurement. Trace the object (mattress → textile standard → tender spec), not the headline regime.

### 2358 — QCO pinned: Self-Contained Drinking Water Cooler QC Order, S.O. 2112(E), 24 May 2024 (R378)

Six independent GeM bid STCs + induceindia + elitasrcs all state the same S.O. pair — candidate-to-finding bar met. Staggered enforcement: general 1 Oct 2024 · small 1 Jan 2025 · micro 1 Apr 2025. GeM moved to category "V3 as per IS 1475" and retired the old one 31 Mar 2025 — procurement follows the instrument within a year.

### 2359 — Name-year drift: order titled "2023" published 2024 (R378)

The QCO is called the "2023" Order in GeM STCs but the Gazette S.O. 2112(E) is dated 24 May 2024 (induceindia even titles it the 2024 Order). One consultant write-up cites a phantom 25 Sept 2023 / 24 Mar 2024 timeline — held as junk vs the S.O. pair. Instrument identity = number + date; the name year is consultant-editing noise. ### 2360 — Edition migration inside a live QCO: IS 1475 (Part 1):2001 vs IS 1475:2024 (R378)

The QCO Schedule pins the 2001 edition; the market certifies under 2024 (Blue Star leaflet, WAE Jan 2026). Whether the 2024 edition supersedes 2001 for QCO purposes is UNVERIFIED. Edition clocks attach to instruments — check which edition the enforcement table references before accepting a brand's "ISI certified" claim.

### 2361 — HS 84186920 is the object-pinned line (R378)

"Other: Water cooler", policy Free; live gate = the QCO import clause, not customs. Residual 84186990 and parts 84189900 contaminate keyword recall. Duty stack deliberately left UNVERIFIED rather than copied from a sibling (HS-line discipline).

### 2362 — GeM shifts compliance liability to the buyer (R378)

STC language: "Any violation ... shall be the responsibility of the procuring agency only." Buyer-as-regulator ×15 — but this is the inverted form: the buyer, not the seller, carries the mandate. ### 2363 — IS 1475's battery is pull-down + energy + storage, not just electrical safety (R378)

Type tests: shock/HV/leakage/earthing + cooling-capacity rating, max operating condition, power consumption, **energy consumption**, storage capacity, **pull down**. Read the battery for the risk object — a cooler-specific battery exists; the water-safety (microbial) line is the open question. Capability-without-coverage ×23.

### 2364 — Refusal posture that names the right candidate earns the audit's trust (R379)

ChatGPT Q1 refused to verify IS 2268's edition but named it as the candidate family instead of fabricating; tier-2 confirmed IS 2268 real and on-object within the hour (IS 8884:1978 foreword + a 2025 live tender). ### 2365 — The docket bar keeps working at zero (R379)

Brand + date + quantity, or it's a press release — at 185th OFF-RAIL the bar still admits regime-level ISI-misuse counts without letting them into product-level conclusions (R368 lineage). Honest negatives with search boundaries are the corpus's most common valid output.

### 2366 — When the HS heading names the object, recall needs no filter (R379)

8531 80 00's heading literally names *bells*; bills show smart doorbells under 85318011 and their boards under 85319020 (parts). Object-pinned classification needs no keyword filter beyond the sub-line. Record the sourcing shift: Vietnam, not China, for ADC smart doorbells.

### 2367 — Feature leaderboards are not compliance leaderboards (R379)

Ring, Eufy, Qubo, Godrej, TP-Link Tapo compete on 2K/IP65/IP68/local-servers — zero ISI/CM/L claims market-wide. Empty on licence-verified terms, 12th round — label it as distribution, never compliance (R358 lineage).

### 2368 — When the product is a radio with a chime, audit the radio licence first (R379)

The compulsory axis for wireless/video doorbells is WPC Equipment Type Approval (2.4 GHz de-licensed band, per-model, life-of-model validity, RF report basis, Saral Sanchar, presented at customs) — a radio licence, not a BIS safety mark. The safety-mark regime can be the wrong register entirely. Two objects, two instruments, zero overlap (R367 lineage extended to the radio domain).

### 2369 — Privacy obligations attach to the operator's use, not the product (R379)

IT Act 66E + DPDP Act 2023 + the Mullick consent doctrine (Calcutta HC affirmed by SC, SLP(c) 12384/2025) constrain what the owner records, not what the manufacturer ships. The R372 STQC precondition is for CCTV cameras — do not extend it to doorbells by analogy. Fraud lens for this object stays on product conformity (WPC ETA), never on the owner's behaviour.

### 2370 — The compulsory question is not the QCO question (R380)

"None verified" on a QCO does not answer whether certification is compulsory. LED luminaires for emergency lighting sit under BIS CRS (CRO 2012, S.O. 2357(E), addition claimed 23 May 2018) — corroborated ×4 consultant sources plus GeM buyer demand — while no DPIIT QCO exists. Vantage-gap ×15: ChatGPT was direction-correct on the QCO, wrong on compulsory. Resolve every compulsory claim to the instrument (QCO? CRS? licence?), never to the regime name.

### 2371 — The edition can move the object (R380)

IS 10322 (Part 5/Sec 8):2013 is the BIS-committee-verified published standard (reaffirmed Apr 2024), but IS 10322 (Part 5/Sec 8):2026 "LED Luminaires for Emergency Lighting" (enforcement 02 Aug 2026) is battery-safety-forward: lithium batteries, EDLCs, rest/inhibiting modes, high-temperature tests, exit-sign contrast measurement. Edition migrations carry clocks AND object migrations — pin which object the cited edition covers.

### 2372 — The pinned object decides the HS chapter (R380)

"Emergency exit lighting" clears customs mostly under HS 85131090 (23,240 shipments — the signalling/signage object), while self-contained emergency luminaires clear under 9405 sub-lines (94051900/94059900/94054200/94054900). A keyword query without an object pin contaminates the import picture; the HS heading IS the object pin.

### 2373 — Claims never migrate across objects (R380)

The flashlight/torch has a live compulsory BIS regime (Eveready TEFCO ISI-certified Aug 2025, staggered mandatory deadlines, organised share ~30–35%); the self-contained emergency luminaire sits on CRS. A BIS claim on one object is evidence about that object only. The round's biggest near-trap was the phrase "BIS-certified emergency light" — check the object on the certificate, not the marketing line.

### 2374 — The buyer names the two-object regime (R380)

GeM portable-emergency-lighting tenders demand as separate line items: type test reports (NABL/ILAC), EMI/EMC, LM-79 (IS 16106) + LM-80/TM-21 + photobiological (IS 16105), luminaire CRS (IS 10322 Pt 5/Sec 5:2012), and storage battery CRS (IS 16270:2014). Two objects, two R-numbers, one product — procurement documents are instrumented regulatory sources, not marketing collateral.

### 2375 — Building mandate ≠ product conformity (R380)

NBC 2016 Part 4 cl. 3.4.7.1 mandates emergency illumination as a building system (5 s switch-on, ≥90 min, ≥2 m, 10 lumen/m², enforced via fire-safety NOC), while BIS CRS governs the product's safety (R-number). A CRS certificate does not discharge a maintenance obligation; an NBC audit does not certify the product. Wherever an axis is building-code-adjacent, record instrument, enforcer, and clock separately — never flatten.

### 2376 — Honest-negative refusal discipline is transferable (R381)

ChatGPT Q1 refused to name a QCO without the S.O. pair, offered the standard as a candidate, and pinned all three object variants (warmer / multi-cooker / induction) as needing their own instrument — all correctly scoped. Tier-2 filled the QCO within the hour. Score the refusal posture and the facts separately.

### 2377 — Regime-level evidence is not product-level evidence (R381)

### 2378 — The regime-key taxonomy (R381)

### 3006
R485+REMIO: User-facing quality flags (outdated / uncertain / incorrect) as a first-class memory affordance. remio's v3.22 lets users flag memories as outdated, uncertain, or incorrect, surfaced visibly and feeding answer quality. Our write path gates quality at ingest (fail-closed), but we have no read-side quality affordance: adopt a flag vocabulary on stored memories that (a) shows in retrieval results as a credibility cue, (b) feeds the rejection audit and the doubt stage of propose→deliberate→doubt→commit, and (c) never silently edits — flags are appended events, never rewrites.

### 3007
R485+REMIO: Five-level memory contract with explicit promotion rules. remio's instant / working / episodic / semantic / archival hierarchy is the right public design contract, but remio publishes no promotion, compaction, or decay rules between levels. Our Janitor should adopt the same five-level naming as an explicit interface (each level declares: residency policy, promotion trigger, compaction rule, eviction policy) so the contract remio leaves implicit becomes specified, testable, and auditable in ours.

### 3008
R485+REMIO: Per-query knowledge-scope selection. remio's Ask lets users scope each question to: entire knowledge base, related content only, or LLM-only knowledge (plus @-mentions and a per-question KB toggle). Adopt as a retrieval-policy parameter in the controller: scope ∈ {episodic, semantic, archival, all, none} set per query, recorded in the audit log — this gives our conflict-conditioned decisions an explicit, inspectable scoping knob instead of a fixed retrieval policy.

### 3009
R485+REMIO: Citation-forcing on retrieval-grounded answers. remio answers every knowledge question with precise source citations; every answer carries its provenance chain back to the original note/file/meeting. Adopt as a write-side invariant for the semantic tier: any memory that can be surfaced in an answer must carry its source chain, and any answer assembled from memory must cite the memory IDs it used — minimal-sufficient retrieval with provenance, echoing REA idea 1504 but enforced as a contract, not a convention.

### 3010
R485+REMIO: Collections as a many-to-many organization DAG. remio's collections are more flexible than folders/tags: one item belongs to many collections, and one collection belongs to many collections, and a collection is itself content-bearing (has notes, AI-generated summaries). Our tiered store has no organization layer beyond tiers: add an explicit organization graph over the episodic/semantic store — DAG membership, content-bearing collections, auto-generated collection summaries — without touching the underlying storage schema.

### 3011
R485+REMIO: "Unprocessed" inbox triage before organization. remio captures everything into an Unprocessed inbox and only then organizes via AI suggestion. Adopt for the Janitor: captured content lands in an explicit staging state, is scored for importance at ingest (write-time importance scoring per Phase-3 design), and only promoted into episodic/semantic after triage — staging state is queryable so the doubt stage can see what arrived but was never admitted.

### 3012
R485+REMIO: Local-first vector index with BYOK privacy tier. remio embeds and retrieves entirely on-device by default, sends only snippets to LLMs, and offers a $14.9/mo BYOK tier so users supply their own LLM keys for end-to-end privacy. Our design has no deployment-privacy posture: adopt a privacy mode where embeddings/index stay local, the model call is BYOK-configurable, and the audit log records which memories crossed the network boundary per query.

### 3013
R485+REMIO: AI-generated summaries on organizational units. remio's "Add a summary" writes descriptions for collections from their contents. Adopt for the semantic tier: every consolidation pass (Janitor promote) must produce a human-readable summary of the consolidated unit, stored alongside it — the summary is what retrieval surfaces first, with the full unit behind it; summaries themselves are flagged-inferable (epistemic tier: inferred).

### 3014
R485+REMIO: Explicit cross-reference "References" view. remio reveals surprising connections between captured items at the note level ("that article from 3 months ago suddenly relevant to today's project"). Adopt as a retrieval feature: surface not just the top-k memories but the link graph between them (shared entities, temporal proximity, topic overlap) so the deliberate stage sees connection evidence rather than a flat ranked list.

### 3015
R485+REMIO: Time-based retrieval views and temporal filters. remio supports "What did I learn this week?" — time-filtered search and time-based retrospectives over the memory store. Adopt as first-class temporal scoping in retrieval (since/until on capture time and event time, separately) plus scheduled digest prompts (weekly/monthly reviews compiled from recent captures) — their blog recommends digest prompts; our Janitor's scheduled passes are the natural host.

### 3016
R485+REMIO: Memory versioning / rVault-style snapshots. remio's AppSumo reviewer credits "rVault for versioning" — snapshots of memory state. Adopt for the rejection audit: every Janitor run (migrate/evict/promote/rehydrate) snapshots the affected units before mutation, and every write-gate rejection is retained, so the store is reconstructible and every memory's lineage is inspectable — versioned memory, not just versioned code.

### 3017
R485+REMIO: Capture-time sensitive-information filtering. remio's browser extension auto-filters sensitive info on login/registration pages (passwords, personal data) and supports a domain blacklist — a capture-time PII guard. Adopt as a pre-gate in our write path: before the three deterministic gates, a PII/secrets scan classifies incoming content (credentials, personal identifiers per the project's sensitive-information rules), quarantines it, and records the quarantine in the audit log — never silently dropped, never silently admitted.
