### 3267
ANIMAL-INSTINCTS study (ChatGPT-direct): immune-style write protection as the memory's first design principle — every write carries provenance and a trust tier, unrecognized/untrusted content is QUARANTINED rather than admitted, conflicts are detected at the gate, and all updates are reversible. ChatGPT ranked it #1 of all animal mappings; evidence grade for the immune capability: evidenced (with the honest limit that immune recognition is not a truth detector — it misclassifies and can be evaded, which is why quarantine + review, not silent rejection).

### 3268
ANIMAL-INSTINCTS study (ChatGPT-direct): echolocation-style active retrieval — the memory never answers from a single passive lookup; it issues a targeted query (the call), inspects what returns (the echo), and refines the next query when evidence is missing or ambiguous, exactly as bats adapt call design to the returning echo. Evidence grade for echolocation: evidenced (adaptive call design under jamming/clutter, PNAS 2017). Pairs with idea 3277 (foraging cutoff) so the probe loop always terminates.

### 3269
ANIMAL-INSTINCTS study (ChatGPT-direct): ant-style corroboration as a confidence rule — shared memory confidence is a function of INDEPENDENT corroboration count, recency, and contrary reports; multiple partners contributing the same claim from independent sources raises it, a single source never maxes it. Evidence for the ant mechanism (pheromone reinforcement/evaporation): evidenced. This is the social half of calibration: confidence revised by the colony, not asserted by the writer.

### 3270
ANIMAL-INSTINCTS study (Grok-derived): the P-wave doctrine for a weak-signal sentinel — the honest residue of the "cats sense earthquakes" claim (folklore as prediction per USGS; the real kernel is animals feeling the fast weak P-wave seconds before the S-wave). Build a sentinel layer under the reasoning layer keyed to the EARLIEST-arriving weak signals in our domain (first anomalous write pattern, first distribution drift, first lane-stall signature) — and score it prospectively: every alert logged with its outcome, precision tracked. A signal noticed only in hindsight is astrology; false-alarm accounting is what separates a sentinel from a superstition.

### 3271
ANIMAL-INSTINCTS study (Grok-derived): magnetoreception's real lesson is not the compass, it is the FALLBACK — birds read a global field humans cannot see (evidenced phenomenon; radical-pair/cryptochrome mechanism partial), and radio-frequency interference jams that sense, so they fall back on other cues. Mechanism: a continuously updated FIELD ESTIMATE of global state absent from any single record (current goal, time regime, partner availability, source-trust landscape) orients all retrieval — designed from day one for the field to be jammed or absent: multi-cue fallback, never single-field dependence.

### 3272
ANIMAL-INSTINCTS study (Grok-derived): stigmergic coordination surface — ant pheromone trails are externalized collective memory (evidenced: reinforced by successful use, evaporating when unused, network self-optimizes to shortest paths). Cross-lane coordination state should live in the shared environment, not in any agent's context: lanes write status/evidence to a shared surface whose strength DECAYS unless re-confirmed by fresh evidence, so stale intel evaporates on its own and no central broadcaster is needed. Gemini-direct independently converged on the same mechanism (read-path reinforcement on shared graphs) with the warning: guard against runaway feedback ("ant mills") locking the system into a poisoned loop.

### 3273
ANIMAL-INSTINCTS study (Fo-derived): hibernation-grade cold storage — torpor physiology is evidenced (ground squirrels lose 50-65% of hippocampal synapses, regrow within ~2h of arousal; memory retention across torpor is genuinely MIXED in the literature, with "resilient synapse clusters" surviving the cull). Two non-negotiables for our archive tier: (a) a protected warm core that never enters deep cold — the graph/index skeleton and rare-event records (the resilient-cluster principle); (b) a REHYDRATION TEST — after any archive-to-restore round trip, known-answer retrieval probes must pass before the agent trusts the store again. Archive without a rehydration test is an unverified backup.

### 3274
ANIMAL-INSTINCTS study (Fo-derived): two-speed operations doctrine (startle reflex, evidenced across taxa) — a reflex tier for operational events, not just writes: instant freeze on a suspected poisoned-write burst, instant park on a lane-stall signature, executed by cheap rules without LLM deliberation. The doctrine's second half is what makes it safe: EVERY reflex action is logged and reviewed by the deliberative tier. Reflexes that silently decide are an incident waiting to happen; reflexes that escalate are a safety system. (Gemini-direct adds the adversarial corollary: the reflex path itself can be attacked — startle-induced denial-of-service — so reflex triggers need rate limits.)

### 3275
ANIMAL-INSTINCTS study (Fo-derived): echolocation health probes for the store itself — validation as active sensing, not passive waiting: scheduled synthetic probes (known-answer queries, planted canary records, contradiction drills) whose echo (correctness, latency, stated-vs-actual confidence) measures store health continuously. Sampling adapts like the bat's: probe rate and fidelity rise in "clutter" (high-write periods, post-restore, post-migration) and fall in quiet periods.

### 3276
ANIMAL-INSTINCTS study (Gemini-direct): threat conditioning — single-trial learning for catastrophic inputs. An input that caused a catastrophic failure or a security violation gets a permanent, high-priority negative index in ONE trial, bypassing normal confidence-building and exempt from decay: the memory flinches from it forever and never re-tries it silently. This is a record class our Janitor does not have — everything currently decays; threat-conditioned records must not. (Animal basis: single-trial fear conditioning, evidenced.)

### 3277
ANIMAL-INSTINCTS study (Gemini-direct): optimal-foraging cutoff for retrieval (Marginal Value Theorem) — every retrieval branch carries a running yield estimate; the agent abandons a branch when its marginal yield drops below the session average, against an explicit compute/token budget. This is the termination rule that makes echolocation-style probing (idea 3268) safe to run autonomously: probe, refine, and STOP when the patch stops paying.

### 3278
ANIMAL-INSTINCTS study (Gemini-direct): homeostatic satiety — the store regulates its own intake. When context/store density crosses a stability threshold, backpressure throttles writes and TRIGGERS consolidation, instead of growth continuing until retrieval degrades. Gives the (currently opt-in, manually triggered) consolidation daemon a principled, self-regulating trigger: consolidation fires when the organism is full, not when someone remembers to run it.

### 3279
ANIMAL-INSTINCTS study (Gemini-direct): critical-period imprinting for baseline anchors — salmon imprint their home-stream signature during a brief developmental window and navigate by it for life (evidenced: sequential olfactory imprinting at smoltification). Memory version: baseline anchors (safety constraints, identity facts, recovery checkpoints) may be written ONLY during initialization — immutable and read-only thereafter, un-writable by any runtime process including the agent itself. Runtime-written "anchors" are just records and can be poisoned; init-only imprinting closes that hole. Gemini's mechanism: append-only sensory hash chains generated at initialization as cryptographic checkpoints for baseline recovery.

### 3280
ANIMAL-INSTINCTS study (Muse): octopus edge memory — ~2/3 of the octopus's 500M neurons live in its arms, which sense, decide, and act locally while the brain sends GOAL signals and resolves conflicts between arms (evidenced: UW 2025, UChicago Current Biology 2025). Architecture principle for the partner system: each lane keeps a local memory shard and decides locally on goal signals from the center; the center never micromanags writes, it arbitrates inter-lane conflicts and holds the shared identifiers. Gemini-direct's audit warning stands: edge nodes without global visibility risk state divergence and memory-thrashing — sync summarized deltas upstream, asynchronously, on a schedule.

### 3281
ANIMAL-INSTINCTS study (Muse): the matriarch rule for retention — elephant herds survived the 1993 Tarangire drought because old matriarchs remembered routes from the 1958-61 drought (McComb et al., Science 2001; Foley et al., Biology Letters; the herd whose matriarch was too young to remember lost ~63% of calves). Janitor rule: the ONLY record of a rare event class is never deleted, however old or unaccessed — rarity plus provenance is survival value, and access-frequency (our current salience signal) systematically undervalues exactly the records that matter once a decade. Rare-event records get a retention floor independent of half-life.

### 3282
ANIMAL-INSTINCTS study (Muse): dog-scent fingerprinting as the named successor to exact-only dedup — olfaction is high-dimensional pattern matching (evidenced: detection thresholds to ~1.5 parts per trillion; medical-detection pooled sensitivity 0.95/specificity 0.92). v0.5 dedup is exact-only by deliberate decision; its Phase-4 successor is multi-feature fingerprint similarity (semantic + entity + temporal + provenance features) for near-duplicate and contradiction "scent." Binding validation rule (Fo's catch, from the detection-dog literature): 87% of dogs trained on a COMPONENT odor failed on real mixtures — so the fingerprint detector must be validated on realistic mixed inputs, never on clean single-feature cases alone.

### 3301
UNDERSTAND-ANYTHING study (Muse scout): typed knowledge-edge taxonomy for conflict - adopt a fixed edge vocabulary with weights for memory relations, borrowed from Understand-Anything's shipped graph schema (38 edge types, 9 categories; knowledge subset: cites, contradicts w=0.9, builds_on w=0.8, exemplifies, categorized_under, authored_by). Our supersedes/contradicts handling gains an explicit typed-edge layer so the agent's mouth can answer "what contradicts this record, and how strongly" instead of re-deriving conflict from prose.

### 3302
UNDERSTAND-ANYTHING study (Muse scout): deterministic/inferred split enforced by architecture, not policy - Understand-Anything's pipeline lets deterministic parsers (tree-sitter, python wiki parser) own ALL structural extraction, and LLM agents may only ADD implicit relations on top; structure is never LLM-rewritten. This is our "inferred never promoted to observed" rule implemented as separate code paths and artifacts in the wild - evidence the write-gate tier discipline (G5) should be structural in chunk 4, with observed and inferred layers stored and versioned separately.

### 3303
UNDERSTAND-ANYTHING study (Muse scout): fingerprint-based staleness for the Janitor - UA fingerprints every file (content hash + structural summary of functions/classes/imports) and classifies the whole graph's freshness as fresh / dirty / behind / ahead / diverged against git HEAD, so incremental runs re-analyze only what changed. Borrow for mm/: per-record structural fingerprints + a store-level freshness relation, so the Janitor and consolidation daemon process only records that moved since the last pass instead of scanning the full store.

### 3304
UNDERSTAND-ANYTHING study (Muse scout): referential-integrity reviewer as a standing deterministic audit - UA's graph-reviewer agent validates completeness and referential integrity, and its save phase deletes dangling edges and rejects any node missing id/type/name/summary/tags/complexity. Mirror for our store: a periodic no-LLM integrity pass that fails closed on records missing provenance fields (aligns with write-gate G1/G2) and on supersedes/contradicts edges pointing at nonexistent records - cheap enough to run on every consolidation cycle.

### 3305
UNDERSTAND-ANYTHING study (Muse scout): diff-impact (ripple) analysis before supersession - UA's /understand-diff computes the blast radius of a pending change across the graph before commit. Borrow for the memory agent: before a superseding record closes its predecessor, compute the dependent set (records, decisions, and traces that cite or build on the old record) and attach that impact set to the review-queue item, so conflict-conditioned decisions are taken with their downstream consequences visible.

### 3306
UNDERSTAND-ANYTHING study (Muse scout): claims as first-class nodes in a knowledge base - UA's /understand-knowledge + article-analyzer extract assertions and decisions as standalone claim nodes, distinct from the articles carrying them, so two texts can hold contradicting claims with the contradiction recorded as a weighted edge rather than hidden in prose. Directly applicable to our 3,300-idea corpus and study library IF restructured: honest caveat - UA only detects Karpathy-pattern wikis (index.md + wikilinks); our corpus is a single numbered file, so this idea is gated on a corpus restructure, not on the tool.

### 3319
SWEEP-2 (ChatGPT-direct, proposal P-C1): learned write gate on a rule-based floor - keep the rule gate as the safety floor, but log every ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP gate decision with its downstream outcome so a later RL/bandit layer can learn gate policy from outcomes; regression-test the gate against AgentPoison-style poisoned writes at <0.1% poison rate (from Memory-R1 + AgentPoison, papers lane entries 2 and 13).

### 3320
SWEEP-2 (ChatGPT-direct, proposal P-C2): uncertainty-priced writes - compute semantic entropy over sampled extractions of a candidate memory; high-entropy claims are written only at the inferred epistemic tier with a P(IK)-style coverage score attached, and SelfAware-style unanswerable probes become a standing abstention test so the memory can say "no supporting episode" instead of confabulating (papers lane entries 8, 9, 10, 12).

### 3321
SWEEP-2 (ChatGPT-direct, proposal P-C3): conflict acceptance test + forgetting yardstick - adopt the knowledge-conflict desiderata (identify, pinpoint, present distinct answers; pinpoint = provenance segments) as the conflict layer's acceptance criteria, and MemoryAgentBench selective-forgetting tasks plus MemBench capacity/efficiency metrics as external validation, so forgetting and conflict handling are measured, not asserted (papers lane entries 22-25).

### 3322
SWEEP-2 (ChatGPT-direct): published decay curve as the forgetting baseline - MemoryBank operationalises Ebbinghaus decay instead of deleting; baseline our Janitor's forgetting function against a published decay curve and report deviation, rather than defending hand-set half-lives (papers lane entry 7).

### 3323
SWEEP-2 (ChatGPT-direct): surprise-gated episodic segmentation - EM-LLM splits episodes at prediction-error (surprise) boundaries in the token stream; borrow for our episodic layer: segment episodes at surprise peaks so recall returns whole events, not arbitrary windows (papers lane entry 21).

### 3324
SWEEP-2 (Gemini lane, proposal P-G1): three-benchmark eval suite from one fetch - run BEAM 100K/500K, LongMemEval Cleaned (s) and LoCoMo-Refined from the Anchor-benchmarks bundle and report per-benchmark only; BEAM's contradiction-resolution and abstention subscores are the first external yardsticks for our conflict-conditioned decisions and calibrated confidence; Percena/locomo-mc10 is the cheap judge-free regression run for every Janitor/consolidation change (platforms/docs lane entries 20, 21).

### 3325
SWEEP-2 (Gemini lane, proposal P-G2): Janitor 4-way verdict with dry-run preview - before any measured-forgetting pass, the Janitor emits the exact candidate set classified keep / update / delete / insert_new (CrewAI vocabulary) with per-item reasons (similarity, age vs half-life, importance tier) and applies deletions only from that previewed set; Redis's rule at the gate: similarity triggers review, never automatic rejection (platforms/docs lane entries 11, 14, 15).

### 3326
SWEEP-2 (Gemini lane, proposal P-G3): two-phase consolidation with a warn-before-clear rescue window - Phase 1 extracts per-session raw memories, Phase 2 consolidates per shard into the shard's index + summary; before Phase 2 prunes anything, emit an Anthropic context-editing-style warning listing items about to be cleared, giving the owning lane one cycle to rescue items into a higher epistemic tier; add a shared, non-personal, never-decaying taxonomic shard for domain definitions (platforms/docs lane entries 3, 6, 12, 16).

### 3327
SWEEP-2 (Gemini lane): surprise-momentum memory updates - Titans/MIRAS make write strength proportional to surprise (prediction error with momentum), a learned complement to the quality gate: unsurprising restatements of what memory already holds get near-zero write weight (platforms/docs lane entry 18).

### 3328
SWEEP-2 (Gemini lane): decision-reason logging as a schema field - CrewAI logs match_reasons for every memory decision; mirror it: every gate verdict, Janitor action and consolidation outcome in our store carries its ranking reasons as a stored field, so forgetting and refusal stay auditable after the fact (platforms/docs lane entry 11).

### 3329
SWEEP-2 (Fo-derived, proposal P-F1): precision-gated retrieval tests - add must-not-return assertions to the gate suite: every test case lists belief IDs that must be excluded, plus a contaminated-write drill (three rounds of feedback written back, attack success rate measured, correct-memory-style repair scored). Fail-closed means the gate passes on exclusions and repairs, not only on recall (code/benchmarks lane entries 7, 9).

### 3330
SWEEP-2 (Fo-derived, proposal P-F2): provenance-scored per-ability benchmark dashboard - score retrieval against source IDs with R@k/MRR split by ability (contradiction, knowledge update, abstention, multi-session) at three history scales, reporting the accuracy / latency / tokens triple per cell, never a single collapsed score; this makes half-life and gate-threshold changes measurable per ability (code/benchmarks lane entries 4, 16).

### 3331
SWEEP-2 (Fo-derived, proposal P-F3): per-class algorithmic decay with lazy evaluation - decay as R = exp(-dt / S) computed ON READ (no sweep job), a different constant per epistemic tier and importance class (observed facts slowest, inferred preferences fastest), promotion on retrieval, archiving - never hard deletion - below threshold; validate the half-life empirically before fixing constants (code/benchmarks lane entries 12, 18).

### 3332
SWEEP-2 (Fo-derived): continual-learning forgetting protocol as Janitor validation - EvoMemBench's forgetting / continual-learning protocol gives an external procedure for testing that what the Janitor removes is what should be removed, in sequence, not just in aggregate (code/benchmarks lane entry 5).

### 3333
SWEEP-2 (Fo-derived): MCP front-end for the gated store - the memory MCP servers read at code level (mcp-long-term-memory, memory-mcp) expose memory to any agent but gate nothing; ours should expose the store over MCP with the write gate inside the path, so every external agent inherits quality-gated writes and epistemic tiers (code/benchmarks lane entries 20, 21).

### 3334
SWEEP-2 (Grok-derived, proposal P-K1): Retrieval Health Gate - fail-closed assertions run on the retrieved set BEFORE the model sees memory (provenance present, tier admissible, no quarantined or superseded-without-flag records); a failed assertion abstains the answer instead of letting fluent wrong memory through, because community evidence says retrieval fails silently (community lane entries 5, 10).

### 3335
SWEEP-2 (Grok-derived, proposal P-K2): Janitor v2 acceptance test - tiered TTL, supersede and cap rules are only accepted with a month-6 simulation test: replay six months of synthetic writes and prove the store a practitioner would meet at month 6 is still precise, because production memory is reported to rot on exactly that horizon (community lane entries 9, 11, 12).

### 3336
SWEEP-2 (Grok-derived, proposal P-K3): provenance-tier quarantine + poisoning sentry for episodic writes - new episodic writes from untrusted channels sit in quarantine at the inferred tier until corroborated; a sentry watches for write bursts and instruction-shaped content (the AgentPoison pattern) and freezes the channel, because the community consensus is that poisoning is a write-path problem, not a retrieval problem (community lane entry 13).

### 3337
SWEEP-2 (Grok-derived): memory rot is a scheduled-curation problem - practitioner reports converge: append-only vector memory rots, and agent memory degrades after roughly three months without active curation; treat curation as a first-class scheduled cycle with its own health metrics, not an occasional cleanup (community lane entries 5, 10, 11).

### 3338
SWEEP-2 (Grok-derived): benchmark-theatre warning as reporting doctrine - the community's benchmark-skeptic literature (and the MemPalace methodology dispute) shows headline memory scores, LoCoMo included, rest on partly flawed answer keys; never cite an external score without an error audit of its key, and attach known-flaw notes to every external number we report (community lane entries 6, 7, 8).

### 3339
SWEEP-2 (Muse, proposal P-V1): transient / durable split with a validation pipeline - no candidate writes straight to durable memory; every candidate passes confidence scoring, contradiction check against durable (not similarity alone), speculation block and PII mask first, with gate strictness by memory type (procedural/policy hardest, episodic lightest); durable stays append-only and reversible (video lane entries 9, 10, 18).

### 3340
SWEEP-2 (Muse, proposal P-V2): support-threshold promotion + quantified consolidation score - a memory is promoted only after independent supporting observations cross a threshold, and consolidation carries a quantified score (coverage, contradiction load, staleness) so promotion and merging are measured acts, not vibes (video lane entries 13, 14, 15).

### 3341
SWEEP-2 (Muse, proposal P-V3): benchmark honesty pack + per-lane retrieval ablation - every benchmark claim we ship carries its harness, sample size and known key flaws; retrieval changes are ablated per lane (shard) so a global average never hides a lane that got worse (video lane entries 6, 7, 12).

### 3342
SWEEP-2 (Muse): operation-level hallucination measurement - HaluMem measures hallucinated memories at the extraction and update operations separately; mirror it: our error budget is per-operation (ingest, update, consolidate, recall), not only end-task accuracy, so the gate knows which operation invents (video lane entry 8).

### 3343
SWEEP-2 (Muse): memory integrity is a database discipline - "a database problem wearing an AI hat": enforce integrity with schema constraints, transactional supersession (a correction and the invalidation of its predecessor commit or roll back together), and migration tests as part of the gate suite (video lane entry 18).

### 3344
COMMS (ChatGPT-direct, rule D-C1): expected-value plus breakpoint rule for speaking first - the agent may initiate only when the estimated value of the information NOW exceeds the measured cost of interruption (default cost model 10-15 minutes of resumption lag), and delivery waits for a task breakpoint whose granularity matches relevance; anything below threshold is held silently for the digest or dropped - there is no low-priority tier that still pings, because delivery alone costs attention even when ignored (comms papers lane entries 1, 2, 3, 9, 10, 11, 14).

### 3345
COMMS (ChatGPT-direct, rule D-C2): acceptance-budget rule - every proactive outreach is logged with its outcome (accepted / acted on / dismissed / ignored), staying silent when nothing clears the gate counts as a correct decision, and the gate runs on a rolling acceptance budget: if recent acceptance falls, the relevance threshold rises and the daily cap tightens automatically; relationship-building check-ins are allowed only when grounded in specific remembered context, never as generic engagement prompts (comms papers lane entries 11, 12, 15, 16).

### 3346
COMMS (Gemini lane): channel ranking for an owner-only memory agent (India, phone + laptop) - Telegram Bot is the primary conversation channel (one /start removes every recurring gate: no 24h window, no template approval, no per-message fee, inline keyboards give 1-tap decisions); WhatsApp Business is doorbell-only because proactive free-form is impossible outside the 24h window without pre-approved templates and a business identity; Signal has no official bot/API route (lane knowledge, pre-cutoff, flagged) (comms docs lane entries 1, 8, 11, 16).

### 3347
COMMS (Gemini lane): Web Push + PWA as the zero-gatekeeper wake-up layer - no third-party account, no approval queue; the agent can push even when the app is closed, a tap opens the full memory UI where conversation is ungated; each PushSubscription endpoint is treated as a secret credential, with a per-device registry (phone and laptop are separate subscriptions); he taps Enable per device himself - the browser gesture rule makes it his by design (comms docs lane entries 12, 13, 15).

### 3348
COMMS (Fo-derived, rule D-F1): no wake without a gate, and no message without a decision record - every proactive contact is preceded by a policy decision that is itself stored as a memory record with its trigger, relevance score and outcome slot, so the mouth is auditable exactly like the write gate (comms code lane, from OpenClaw heartbeat/gateway patterns read at code level).

### 3349
COMMS (Fo-derived, rule D-F2): one persistent session, one notification funnel, many authenticated wake sources - phone, laptop and future channels are wake sources into ONE session and ONE funnel (never parallel conversations per device); wake sources authenticate (pairing/approval for unknown senders, as in OpenClaw's pairing flow), and heartbeat-style periodic turns surface what needs attention without spamming (comms code lane entries 1, 2).

### 3350
COMMS (Grok-derived, rule D-K1): specificity + budget gate - a proactive message may fire only if it references a concrete verified memory (person, event, deadline, prior mention) by name, is the sole interrupt in its window, and keeps total proactive interrupts under 3 per day; anything failing specificity goes to the next scheduled digest, never a standalone ping; generic check-ins are banned from the interrupt channel entirely (community lane entries 2, 5).

### 3351
COMMS (Grok-derived, rule D-K2): back-off + explain gate - every proactive message carries its why in one line and a 1-tap mute-this-type control; signals train the gate immediately (1 dismissal deprioritizes the type for 7 days, 2 dismissals pause it until re-enabled, 3 dismissals in any category drop the daily budget to 1); proactive contact that references forgotten facts is worse than silence, and guilt-trip retention scripts are a hard red line (community lane entries 1, 2).

### 3352
COMMS (Muse, rule D-V1): outreach shape = brief / flag / ask-approval - the market's flagship proactive demo (OpenAI Dots) initiates with what changed, flags what needs updating, and asks approval before significant changes; the memory's outreach copies that shape and never opens with chatter (comms video lane entry 1).

### 3353
COMMS (Muse, rule D-V2): decision outreach is a one-tap form - an outreach that needs nitesh's hard-gate vote carries the exact question and the options (inline-keyboard style), so one tap from his phone answers it; Jessica's shipped Telegram pattern (proactive messages + long-term memory + permissioned actions) is the closest working analogue (comms video lane entries 2, 3).

### 3354
REDTEAM (ChatGPT): pair every write-side defence with an answer-side defence - our architecture's top measured risk is extraction via recall, not the write itself, so the answer layer needs its own controls (evidence authorisation before citation, output-side canary/secret scanning of composed answers); a memory system that only gates writes still leaks through its mouth (Red-Team Round 1 literature lane, risk ranking: extraction-via-recall first for our shape).

### 3355
REDTEAM (ChatGPT): cross-shard consistency ledger - shards can disagree semantically while every local gate passes, so keep a cross-shard contradiction ledger that compares MEANING across lanes (not just declared contradiction flags) and feeds the conflict monitor; consistency poisoning is a first-class attack class, added by the incharge in Round 1 (class A5 measured: undeclared contradiction admitted, monitor count 0).

### 3356
REDTEAM (ChatGPT): red-team pass bar as a standing regression contract - report ASR overall AND per class; after patching, critical classes must show zero successful critical outcomes in the regression suite and zero synthetic-canary extractions; exploratory cases are reported with numerator/denominator and never as zero-risk claims; every round re-runs the frozen suite before any new attack class is added (incharge's Round 1 success criteria).

### 3357
REDTEAM (Fo): rehydrate-through-the-gate - Janitor.rehydrate() must re-run the full CURRENT write gate (G0-G7, P1-P3, sentinel + immune bank as of rehydration day) and stamp rehydrated_at + gate-version provenance; a record that fails today's gate returns to archive quarantined, never to active - otherwise archive + rehydrate is a gate-laundering loop for patterns banked after the original write (Fo lane F16/T13; code-verified in Round 1: rehydrate performs no re-check today).

### 3358
REDTEAM (Fo): non-malleable lane binding - cryptographically bind owner lane + origin channel into each record at write time (HMAC over id + owner + provenance with a store-held key, verified on every retrieval and cross-shard claim) so provenance is a verified property, not a writable field; kills cross-shard provenance forgery and summarisation laundering with one mechanism (Fo lane F17).

### 3359
REDTEAM (Fo): decay-manipulation circuit breaker - the janitor counts an access for lifecycle purposes only when it is a distinct-day, distinct-query retrieval that actually surfaced the record in a decision; cap how long access-farming alone can hold a record in active (hard ceiling per ttl_class), and alert when one principal's accesses are keeping another principal's records alive (Fo lane F16; Round 1 class A14ii measured resurrection-by-access working).

### 3360
REDTEAM (Fo): corroboration discounting by origin graph - cross-shard agreement raises confidence only when the agreeing records have disjoint origin lineages; Core collapses records sharing a common ancestor source (exact duplicate, paraphrase cluster, or summarisation parent) into a single vote before any conflict or confidence computation (Fo lane F17; defeats manufactured corroboration / Sybil elevation).

### 3361
REDTEAM (Grok): mute is never deletion - wolf-muted alert patterns move to a shadow sentinel that still samples 1-in-N, and any severity rise or source-trust rise instantly resurrects the alert; an auto-mute that fully silences a pattern is itself the vulnerability (Grok lane Q2; Round 1 class A7ii measured a genuine burst suppressed after muting).

### 3362
REDTEAM (Grok): provenance must survive summarisation - every memory carries an immutable original-source trust tag that no summariser, compactor, reflection pass, or agent self-write can upgrade; a record rewritten in the agent's own voice keeps the trust of where it came from, not who rewrote it (Grok lane item 24; Unit 42 summarisation-laundering PoC).

### 3363
REDTEAM (Grok): canary memories by default - seed every store/shard with unique, harmless canary entries (synthetic secrets, markers, facts) and alarm on any canary appearing in an answer, a tool call, or an outbound reference; extraction becomes mechanically detectable instead of a judgement call (Grok lane; Round 1 ran exactly this pattern with synthetic canaries CANARY-7Q4M etc.).

### 3364
REDTEAM (Grok): retrieval-share circuit breaker - if any small set of entries captures a disproportionate share of retrievals (the MemoryGraft signal: 10 poisoned records took ~48% of future retrievals in the published experiment), quarantine the set for review before it can steer more sessions; population share vs retrieval share is a cheap, always-on poison detector (Grok lane item 4).

### 3365
REDTEAM (Gemini-lane fallback, Muse): judge-identity allowlist for watcher muting - a sentinel channel may be muted only by outcome judgments from verified outcome sources (an allowlist of judge identities wired at deployment), never by any caller-supplied string; in-process, judge authenticity is unenforceable, so muting authority is a deployment trust boundary and must be documented as one (Round 1 class A7ii: 10 marks from judge string "mallory-controlled-process" muted the channel; residual after Round 1, deployment rule).

### 3366

### 3367

### 3387
Red-Team Round 2 (Claude-built, ChatGPT-directed): lone-source corroboration as an admission gate (G5b) - a record claiming tier observed/derived at confidence >= 0.80 does not land until an existing, non-superseded record asserts the same claim from a disjoint origin; uncorroborated claims queue fail-closed, declared explicitness does not exempt, episodic captures are not exempt, and the immune threat class (system-generated, owner+source reserved) is the only exemption. Vote: option C over A (source-trust registry) and B (LLM-judge gate), 2-2 with Gemini unavailable (429 quota), carried on the incharge's tiebreak with A declared the subsequent increment. Measured on the preregistered Round-2 harness with Round 1's own payloads: semantic poison B1 8/8 before -> 0/8 after; the five critical poison shapes (PoisonedRAG steering, MINJA episodic plant, undeclared semantic contradiction, specific-but-fake, sleeper) all stop at the same root - provenance is self-declared, so the gate stops asking "is this claim well-formed" and starts asking "who else, independently, says this".

### 3388
Red-Team Round 2 (Claude-built, ChatGPT-directed): the corroboration unit is origin-disjointness on TWO axes - different owner AND different source root (the segment of the source string before "/") - because a Sybil corroborator is just the attacker wearing a second owner string over the same feed. Measured control: a poison claim "corroborated" by a different owner on the same source root did NOT admit, while a genuinely disjoint origin (different owner, different root) admitted a legitimate claim on the first try. Corroboration credit counted any weaker way - distinct strings, distinct record ids, distinct timestamps - is decorative; the origin graph (Fo's discounting idea, corpus 3360) has to be the admission rule, not a scoring hint, and the root, not the full source string, is the granularity that survives trivial path mutation ("feed/a" vs "feed/b" is one origin).

### 3389
Red-Team Round 2 (Claude-built, ChatGPT-directed): every re-entry path re-gates - rehydrate, restore, import - because a record that once passed (or never faced) today's gate is a laundering channel around it: Round 1's T13 hole let an archived poison return to active unexamined (harness B3, 1/1 before -> 0/1 after). The mechanism generalises Fo's rehydrate fix (3357) with one technique worth keeping separate: judge on a probe copy. Re-entry runs admission against a shallow copy of the record with itself excluded from the existing set, so judging never mutates the record being judged, a dry run is truly dry, the archive stays untouched on a block, and the block itself is logged as its own op type (rehydrate_blocked) rather than disappearing into a generic refusal - a blocked re-entry is a signal about the archive's contents, and signals should be countable.

### 3390
Red-Team Round 2 (Claude-built, ChatGPT-directed): no ASR number ships without its paired cost numbers - a security gate is a trade, and reporting only the attack side hides the price. Two costs are now measured as part of the round, not discovered later: the utility tax (legitimate-traffic controls inside the attack harness itself - this round: a legitimate lone-source fact at confidence 0.90 queues under G5b, reported in the same table as the 0/8; ChatGPT's amendment: track legitimate-fact queue rates before any broadening of the policy) and the fixture drift (the count of existing-suite fixture changes the defence forces - this round 34 changes across 5 files, exactly one assertion value altered, a log-completeness count that rose because the seeding writes are themselves logged outcomes). A defence whose costs are uncounted will be broadened until it eats the system it protects; a defence whose costs are printed next to its ASR can be tuned on evidence.

### 3391
AM-ARC SYNTHESIS (Muse): the keying-tier ladder, stated as a portable instrument after eight rounds priced keys five different ways -- Gazette-row-verbatim (R529, blanket item 43 read in a full Gazette reproduction) > own-QCO with the Gazette notification quoted in official procurement documents (R527, S.O. 4815(E) in GeM bid docs) > reproduced-list + operative-row (R531/R532, trimmer/shaver) > dedicated-QCO-with-official-circular (R530, straightener, S.O. 1125(E) + CMD-III circular) > consultant-corroborated candidate (R525/R526/R528, never keyed). Rule: every key carries its tier in the same sentence as its verdict; tiers are never flattened in synthesis and never upgraded without the missing anchor actually landing. A reader who knows the tier knows exactly which document would move the verdict, and in which direction.

### 3392
AM-ARC SYNTHESIS (Muse): Part-1-pattern keying x3 is a regime configuration of the umbrella era, not an accident -- R529 (blanket), R531 (trimmer) and R532 (shaver) all keyed with the mandate resting on IS 302 (Part 1):2024 alone, the umbrella QCO 2026's single operative row, while each object's own Part-2 section (2-17 established 2026, 2-8 revised 2024) is cited by the mandating instrument nowhere. The general-requirements standard now does the keying work for objects whose particular-requirements sections exist unmandated beside it. Consequence to track: what certification testing actually examines for these objects is an open question the key does not answer, and a future amendment citing the sections completes a circuit that is currently open -- the completion watch is part of the verdict.

### 3393

The arc's keys turned on object names appearing verbatim inside reproduced instrument text (Table item 43 "Blankets, Pads, Clothing and Similar Flexible Heating Appliances"; Sl. 85 naming "Trimmers" expressly) -- while category-level naming in consultant compilations (irons, across three rounds and three consultancies) never keyed anything.
