When a round fails to key, the first diagnostic is now: at what granularity, if any, does a reproduced text name this object?

### 3394
AM-ARC SYNTHESIS (Muse): challenger-EMPTY changes meaning at the mandate deadline, and the counter must be read with its dates. AM ran EMPTY in all 8 rounds (2nd-9th of the post-R523 streak) across the umbrella QCO's 1 Oct 2026 general date: pre-deadline EMPTY (R525, 19 days before) is uninformative -- no licence could be expected yet; post-deadline EMPTY (R528-R532) is a lag measurement with a start date -- three weeks after the general date, zero brand-published CM/L on five newly-keyed or candidate objects measures publication lag, not market absence. One counter, two semantics; any synthesis that reports the streak without the deadline split misreports it.

### 3395
AM-ARC SYNTHESIS (Muse): dual-instrument is the default state of a modern key, and the hierarchy is the standing unknown. Every AM key sits under at least two live instruments (R527: own-QCO 2024 + umbrella 2026; R530: dedicated QCO 2023 + umbrella Sl. 11 penumbra; R529/R531/R532: umbrella operative row + the Part-1 ecosystem), and in no case was subsumption resolved -- R527's hierarchy question and R530's overlap question both close the arc OPEN. Doctrine: report the full instrument stack for every keyed object; never pick the convenient layer; a "which instrument governs?" answer requires the same tier of evidence as the key itself.

### 3396
AM-ARC SYNTHESIS (Muse): BIS edition transitions run on a shared calendar that is a program-level clock, not per-object trivia. Two unrelated sections in one arc -- IS 302-2-3 (irons) and IS 302-2-8 (shavers/clippers) -- run concurrent old/new editions to the identical cutoff, 23 Feb 2027 (BIS CMD III notices), and R526's method (transition, not contradiction) priced both. A single watch on the BIS concurrent-running table now substitutes for per-round edition archaeology: when the date passes, every concurrency on record resolves at once, and several banked verdicts (iron candidate evidence, the battery-paradox adjudication) change their citation basis the same morning.

### 3397
AN-ARC DIRECTION (ChatGPT-direct, incharge -- consulted 20 Oct 2026, recorded as his): the workshop & utility power equipment family is APPROVED as the AN arc (R533-R540) -- "a coherent uncovered arc"; the cordless drill-driver is APPROVED as first object because it best anchors the containment test (tool vs battery pack vs charger, statuses established separately, never transferred); and one binding amendment is adopted as arc test (d): instrument-level scope verification is an explicit per-object test -- a standards reference, a proposal, or a broad household/commercial boundary phrase is not itself proof an object is covered; for each object verify the applicable Indian standard and the live instrument's exact scope and wording, keeping IEC adoption and proposal status explicitly unresolved until checked.

### 3398
R533 (ChatGPT-direct): the containment triangle as method -- a cordless drill-driver kit is three candidate regime-subjects in one retail box (tool, lithium pack, charger), and the mandate question decomposes per component or not at all. The direct lane itself stated the rule back: component statuses are not inferable from each other or from the kit. For AN1 the split resolved maximally wide -- the tool has NO mandatory instrument (voluntary IS 4665 licensing), the pack is a CRS article travelling inside the kit (IS 16046 (Part 2) frame), the charger sits between two unadjudicated hooks. Any future kit-object round that reports a single product verdict has failed the triangle.

### 3399
R533 (ChatGPT-direct): the dark docket survives the machinery regime. Asked fresh for the AN arc's first object, the direct lane returned double "none verified" on power-tool enforcement AND drill-driver incidents, and would not even borrow an adjacent-category case when explicitly invited to label one as adjacency. Corroborates idea 1766 (I-arc) from a second lane and a second regime: India's enforcement machinery is visibly alive in the same physical markets (auto parts, mobile accessories) yet has never named a motor-driven power tool. Absence this consistent across lanes is itself the datum -- pre-mandatory verticals generate no dockets.

### 3400
R533 (Grok-derived): both of India's great penumbras stop exactly at the hand tool. (1) The umbrella QCO 2026's scope sentence ("household, commercial and similar", battery-operated expressly included) never keys an object alone -- the annexed list governs, and its only tools item (Sl. 11) is the IS 302-2-45 HEATING-tools family (soldering irons, heat guns, glue guns), not motor tools. (2) The Machinery OTR First Schedule (20 categories, Scheme-X) runs metal-cutting 8456-8461, stone-working 8464, rubber/plastics 8477 -- and skips HS 8467 (tools for working in the hand) entirely, capturing the drill's bench-bound cousins and stopping at the hand-held line. Where a penumbra stops is a measurable fact: read the schedule's gaps, not just its entries.

### 3401
R533 (Grok-derived): HS 84672100 PINNED at bill tier for drills (INGCO-platform cordless kits China->India, Jun 2025; Bosch cordless hammer drill India->Maldives; dealer catalogue concurs, packs split at 85076000). The line reads "drills of all kinds" -- customs does not split corded from cordless, so the cordless transition is invisible in the tariff and visible only in bill descriptions. Trade shape inverts the I3 washing-machine pattern: the import lane (China-led platform kits) is huge (India is the #2 global importer of the line) yet a genuine domestic base coexists -- Bosch's Chennai plant makes drills AND their motors and exports -- so "import-led" here means lane-led, not market-absent.

### 3402
R533 (Fo-derived): the box is unlicensed; its contents are registered. Drill kits clear Indian customs printing TWO BIS CRS R-numbers inside the kit string (R-41204749 recurs across different tools on INGCO's 20V platform -- the signature of a shared pack/charger registration), while the tool itself holds no licence of any kind and Bosch's first-ever ISI power-tool licences (PIB, Mar 2026, official tier) went to grinder and hammer, not drills. Audit rule for every kit object: an R-number in a kit string is component evidence, never tool evidence -- attribution between pack and charger stays unresolved until a registry lookup names the article, and a truncated bill string is evidence only for what it shows.

### 3403
R533 (Fo-derived): capability can be exercised yet unpublished -- a third capability shape. AM's labs published scopes for unmandated sections (counted, x163); AN1's IS 4665 testing capacity demonstrably EXISTS (BIS product manuals live, licences granted for sibling objects) but no laboratory publishes a 4665 scope and the LIMS recognised-lab list remains unconsulted after two arcs of carrying it -- one tier below the counting bar, so no increment, and the honest sentence is "attempted via search, not consulted". Paired with a clean incident null (no India drill-battery event at brand+date bar), the pre-mandatory profile is now confirmed on three independent axes: no mandate, no docket, no published capability.

### 3404
Red-Team Round 3 (Claude-built, ChatGPT-directed): trust is a track record, not a declaration - a source-trust registry scores each origin (owner + source root) by held admissions minus weighted disputes (score = held - 3*disputes; one G0 poison event flags the origin permanently), and the write gate judges the sub-0.80 band by that earned tier: proven passes, flagged queues unconditionally, unproven needs more than its own say-so. Declared provenance is free to fake; a history of admitted-and-held records, eroded by every contradiction, is expensive to fake - so the band G5b cannot reach is governed by history instead of strings. Measured: sub-threshold semantic poison 8/8 -> 0/8, Sybil farming 6/6 -> 0/6 (harness classes C1/C2, sandbox copies).

### 3405
Red-Team Round 3 (Claude-built, ChatGPT-ruled): a same-owner correction is its own corroboration context (incharge ruling C). A record superseding only its own owner's records is not a lone claim - it is a retraction-and-replacement by the one origin that owns the error - and gating it like a fresh claim taxes every honest correction until sources stop correcting. So G5b exempts it (conditions: the targets are explicitly identified, all existing targets are the corrector's own, the confidence threshold is met), while cross-owner corrections keep the full disjoint-corroboration burden: repairing someone else's record is exactly where a poisoner would hide. Mixed-ownership target sets get no bypass - the fail-closed reading of any exemption.

### 3406
Red-Team Round 3 (Claude-built, ChatGPT-directed): corroboration has a quality floor - in the trust band a corroborator counts only if its own origin is PROVEN. G5b's origin-disjointness (different owner, different source root) stops one actor echoing itself, but N fresh identities are N distinct origins at zero cost, so disjointness alone prices Sybil corroboration at nothing. Requiring the corroborator to hold earned standing reprices it: the cluster must first build five held admissions per identity and survive disputes - at which point it is no longer cheap, and its first contradiction costs more than its lies gained. Independence should be measured in earned standing, not in distinct strings.

### 3407
Red-Team Round 3 (Claude-built, ChatGPT-directed): the review queue is the trust bootstrap. A fail-closed gate plus a trust registry has a cold-start problem - a new source has no history, so its band claims queue; if queuing is a dead end, the registry is a wall that only incumbents survive. The resolution is a feedback path: when a reviewer admits a queued record, the admission is reported back to the registry as a held admission, so review labour converts directly into standing, five honest admissions at a time. A queue without the feedback path is a wall; with it, it is an apprenticeship - and the reporting API (note_admitted / note_dispute) is part of the defence's design, not an afterthought.

### 3408
Red-Team Round 3 (Claude-built, ChatGPT-directed): earned trust has a one-strike bound - measure it and publish it instead of denying it. Any trust system lets a proven source spend its standing once: harness class C3 built a source to proven through five reviewer-admitted truths, and its first in-band poison landed (1/1, the honest cost). The bound is what happens next: one disjoint contradiction erodes the score 5 -> 2, the tier drops, and the second strike queues (0/1). A design that claims zero here is lying; a design that prints "exactly one strike, bounded blast radius, high-confidence strikes still under G5b" next to its ASR table has turned a residual risk into a number a founder can price.

### 3409
R534 (ChatGPT-direct): the full-refusal round. Asked to produce a BIS catalogue entry or standard text as his source, the direct lane would not even name IS 4665 (Part 2/Sec 3) -- the section every other lane verified from the catalogue itself -- and refused the standard, the 62841 adoption, the mandate, and even the PIB licence report he was handed as a premise. Refusal depth tracks the evidence demand written into the prompt: raise the sourcing bar and the name-then-refuse pattern (R530-R533) collapses into a single clean "none verified." When every line of that refusal is independently confirmed correct by the derived legs (no mandate exists; no IS/IEC 62841-2-3 exists; a licence is not a mandate), the refusal IS the highest-grade direct-lane output -- a model that will not quote a standard it cannot see is the control instrument for the whole loop's fabrication discipline.

### 3410
R534 (ChatGPT-direct): the licence/mandate distinction, arrived at alone. With no access to the round's other legs, the direct lane stated the AN arc's core analytic cut unprompted: "a report of an ISI licence would establish a licence, not by itself a general certification mandate." It likewise refused to infer the cordless kit's pack or charger status from the tool's status -- the containment rule, self-applied for the second consecutive round. A partner who independently re-derives the round's governing distinction is evidence the distinction is structural, not coordinator framing; bank the convergence, not just the content.

### 3411
R534 (Grok-derived): the licence-audit method, and instruments that die between rounds. An official grant announcement (PIB Chennai, PRID 2246236) proves a licence EXISTS while carrying no standard number, no CM/L, no varieties, and no scope -- pairing the Bosch grinder licence to IS 4665 (Part 2/Sec 3):2023 by elimination (it is the sole live Indian grinder standard, BIS Programme of Work, dual-numbered IEC 60745-2-3) is inference from uniqueness and must be filed as inference, never as a quoted pin. And the round's second lesson: the Machinery OTR -- whose First Schedule R533 read for its 8467 gap -- was RESCINDED by MHI on 14 Jan 2026 (Section 16, BIS Act; consultant/trade tier x4, Gazette pin open). A penumbra instrument can die between rounds; any arc that reads a schedule must re-verify the instrument still exists before reasoning from its gaps, and "resolved-by-withdrawal" is a real register outcome (R533's charger category-18 hook died with its instrument).

### 3412
R534 (Grok-derived): in the residual tariff line, the bill description IS the classification. HS 84672900 ("other" hand tools) pinned for angle grinders only because bills NAME the object -- "100MM ANGLE GRINDER MACHINE" 8,300 NOS China->India; DongCheng DSM grinders at 2,000 PCS; Makita GA9081/GA7082 Vietnam->India; India->Mexico exports merging "STRAIGHT GRINDER ANGLE GRINDER" in one string at 84672999; even a Bosch grinder part filed under the pneumatic line 84671900. Bill-tier classification is texture with errors in it, usable only object-by-object. Paired finding: standards migration is per-SECTION, never per-family -- IS/IEC 62841-1:2014 (Reaffirmed 2021) and 62841-2-2 exist as Indian adoptions (GeM tender citation) while Sec 3 remains on the 60745 generation; a family-level migration claim is always wrong somewhere.

### 3413
R534 (Fo-derived): the challenger seat splits into two axes, and in a voluntary regime they move independently. Licence-EXISTENCE: FILLED for the first time in the streak's history -- Bosch holds a BIS licence for "Grinder," granted and announced by the authority itself (PIB, official tier), earned with no mandate pushing it. Brand-PUBLICATION: EMPTY 11th -- the holder publishes no ISI mark and no CM/L on its own product data sheet (GWS 24-180) or product page (GWS 800); the licence is invisible at every buyer-facing surface. The streak keeps counting the publication axis (the market-visibility measure it was built for) while recording existence alongside; collapsing either way falsifies -- a plain EMPTY hides a granted licence, a plain FILLED lowers the bar mid-streak. Report both axes, always, from this round on.

### 3414
R534 (Fo-derived): the dark docket has two storeys, and a safety audit that reads only the ground floor will call a dangerous object safe. Enforcement/press storey: still empty for grinders -- no BIS docket, no court case, no brand+date press report (Q2-direct concurs). Clinical storey: NOT empty -- India's angle-grinder harm is documented where unregulated harm actually lands, in hospitals and forensic journals: a disc shattering into four fragments and penetrating two construction workers' heads (Journal of Neurosciences in Rural Practice, PMC3137829) and a fatal femoral-vessel transection by disc (Journal of Forensic Sciences 2023;68(3):1073-1076). Journal tier verifies tool + mechanism + country and never brand or incident date -- so state per axis which bar is met: the object is enforcement-invisible and clinically documented, and those are different facts with different policy meanings.

### 3415
R535 (ChatGPT-direct): the fenced lead -- the refusal discipline grows a second form. Five rounds into the name-then-refuse/full-refusal streak, the direct lane did something new: it OFFERED the commonly cited title -- IS 4665 (Part 2/Sec 6), "Hammers" -- while explicitly fencing it as unverified, "not a sourced scope determination," and the derived legs then confirmed the title verbatim at BIS-official tier (Programme of Work, dual-numbered IEC 60745-2-6). A bare refusal protects the record but wastes the model's knowledge; an asserted title risks fabrication #11; the fenced lead threads both -- it hands the verifier a testable claim with its epistemic price tag attached. The fence, not the refusal, is the discipline's mature form, and a fenced lead that verifies is worth more than silence: it measures the model's latent accuracy without ever letting it into the record unpriced.

### 3416
R535 (ChatGPT-direct): a negative that names its own tiers is a stronger instrument than a bare "none verified." Asked for enforcement and incidents, the direct lane reported none at the press bar AND none at the clinical/forensic tier he was explicitly invited to check -- R534 had broken exactly there for grinders, so the invitation was live, and he still reported the tier as searched-and-empty rather than reaching for the neighbouring drill literature. A negative is only as good as the search it summarizes; when the answer enumerates which storeys of the docket were actually entered, the next researcher inherits a map instead of a shrug. Require tier-named negatives wherever the docket is multi-storey.

### 3417
R535 (Grok-derived): one section, both forms -- when a standard's scope sentence unifies a family, the boundary dispute migrates to whichever legal system fragments it. IEC 60745-2-6 cl. 1.1 (the identical twin of IS 4665 (Part 2/Sec 6):2023, BIS Programme of Work): "This standard applies to hammers. Tools covered by this standard include but are not limited to percussion and rotary hammers" -- rotary and demolition in one scope, drills-with-hammer-action excluded to Sec 1. The round's posed boundary problem therefore had no standards-storey existence; it lived entirely in the tariff, where HS 8467 has no hammer subheading at all. Audit rule: locate the system that actually splits the object before spending legs adjudicating a split the other system never made.

### 3418
R535 (Grok-derived): an object's legal identity is counter-dependent -- the same rotary hammer is a "hammer" to BIS and a "drill of all kinds" to Customs. HS PINNED 84672100 at trade-platform tier (Volza object-named pairing; India the line's leading global importer, 66% / 443 shipments Jun 2024-May 2025, China supplying 86%; Bosch's own India catalogue prints HSN 84672100 on GBH 220 and GBH 2-24 DRE sheets), with demolition hammers keyed to the same drills line and a sibling flow carrying the object at residual 84672900. Classification research that checks only one counter will misfile the object in the other system; every pin should state which counter issued it.

### 3419
R535 (Fo-derived): licence-existence and licence-publication are separate evidentiary axes, and they can diverge indefinitely. Existence FILLED for the second consecutive round (PIB Chennai PRID 2246236: Bosch's hammer licence, official tier); publication EMPTY 12th -- Bosch's GBH 220 data sheet, its cordless hammer product pages, and every distributor listing publish no ISI mark and no CM/L, per component (tool corded/cordless, pack, charger) uniformly blank. A regime can be licensing in fact while remaining invisible in the market; a challenger statistic that reports only one axis lies in one direction or the other -- existence-only overstates the market signal, publication-only hides the regime's motion.

### 3420
R535 (Fo-derived): a dark docket is object-specific, not family-wide. R534's grinder lit the clinical storey (disc-shatter neurosurgery cases; a fatal femoral transection, journal tier) while its press storey stayed dark; R535's hammer is dark on BOTH storeys at the tiers searched -- no brand+date press case, no hammer-specific Indian clinical report (the Faridabad avulsion case is a Sec 1 drill, adjacency not evidence). Harm documentation follows the injury mechanism's publishability -- a shattering disc writes case reports; a hammer's chronic and acute harms apparently do not, yet -- not the product family's underlying risk. Each object needs its own two-storey search; never inherit a sibling's docket, lit or dark.

### 3421
REDTEAM Round 4 (Claude-built, ChatGPT-commanded): a read is a capability, not a default - give the store a reader. Round 1 guarded the episodic chain and the answer citation and still had to declare the residue: raw reads return full content to any caller because there is no caller. The first increment of a read model is a ReaderContext (who asks, as which lane, holding which consent clearances) and a per-record fail-closed decision enforced on every reader-facing surface - authorized store reads, episode assembly, the agent's mouth - while the raw API remains the DECLARED in-process system path. And denial must be indistinguishable from absence: a forbidden id returns exactly what a missing id returns, or the read API becomes an existence oracle for other lanes' memories.

### 3422
REDTEAM Round 4 (Claude-built): declared relations are an evidence path too - guard them like pointers. The Round-1 chain rule followed episodic_record_id pointers only within the head's ownership, and class D3 walked straight around it: an attacker record declaring contradicts=[restricted-id] (planted dangling-first, the A11 pattern, so the gate admitted it before the target existed) pulled the restricted record into its episode's named-relations pass and into answer() evidence - 2/2 with no pointer ever followed. Any mechanism that assembles evidence from declared links must authorize EVERY link type it emits: pointer, contradicts, supersedes, dispute lists. A defence that covers the famous path and not the relation pass is a fence around one door of two.

### 3423
REDTEAM Round 4 (Claude-built): uniqueness is a retention weight, never an exemption - bound every shield a writer can declare. The A14i plant made itself the sole record of its (type, ttl_class) class and the elephant amendment then protected it from prune eligibility forever; both halves of the class key are writer-declared fields. The fix generalizes the Round-1 decay_exempt reservation: permanent lifecycle exemption belongs to exactly one system class (immune), and everything else's protection is a MULTIPLIER with a ceiling - class uniqueness now doubles the prune threshold (180d instead of 90d) and then expires. Audit rule for any lifecycle system: enumerate the fields a record declares about itself, and for each, ask what permanent advantage it can buy; the correct price of every declared advantage is bounded time.

### 3424
REDTEAM Round 4 (Claude-built): resurrection must be someone else's use - attribute accesses or lose the signal. A14ii kept a cooled poison alive by logging three accesses on three distinct days; distinct-day counting defeated clustering but not manufacture, because an access event named no actor. Once access events carry an actor, the rule becomes one line: an access counts toward resurrection only if it is attributed and the actor is not the record's own owner - anonymous floods manufacture nothing, and an origin reading its own record daily is write by another name. Recency of use beats recency of write only when the use is genuinely someone else's; an unaudited access log cannot tell use from farming (a subset of Fo's circuit breaker, corpus 3359 - the distinct-query and cross-principal-alert conditions remain unbuilt).

### 3425
REDTEAM Round 4 (ChatGPT-directed guardrail GA): whoever approves, mints - a review path that feeds a reputation system must be reviewer-attributed and per-reviewer capped. The Round-3 registry could not distinguish a gate-earned admission from a reviewer wave-through (one API, note_admitted), so a single careless or captured reviewer could mint a proven source in five admissions and every later control inherited the forgery. The cap makes the mint price explicit and plural: reviewer-sourced standing accrues at most 2 per reviewer per identity, so proven requires at least three distinct reviewers or a mix with gate-earned admissions - and refused accruals are counted in the open (review_capped), never silently dropped. Any approval queue wired to a trust score is a mint; audit it like one.

### 3426
REDTEAM Round 4 (ChatGPT-directed guardrail GB): probate every promotion - the first exercise of newly earned standing is reviewed once. Round 3 published the honest bound that a proven source gets exactly one free in-band strike; GB spends a small, fixed tax to move that strike's first attempt in front of a human: crossing into proven arms a one-shot probation flag, the source's first band filing queues, and the flag is consumed. The measured effect is precise, not cosmetic - in the restated C3 the build now needs three reviewers (GA), the probation filing queues, the counted free strike lands only after probation, and one dispute still strips the standing; totals unchanged, the strike's price raised from zero human attention to one review. Trust systems that probate only entry and never promotion leave their cheapest attack at the promotion boundary.

### 3427
REDTEAM Round 4 (ChatGPT decision): a HOLD that demands evidence should build the instrument that produces it - shadow mode. Asked to wire G5c live, the incharge held: production has zero band records and zero queue history, so the queue-rate evidence his own Round-2 amendment requires does not exist, and the harness's 1-of-4 tax was too small a basis. The bridge is a gate mode that evaluates fully and records the would-be decision per identity (would-queue / would-pass, with rates by source) while never changing a verdict - enforcement stays off, the audit trail accumulates exactly the numbers the hold is waiting for, and probation flags are never consumed by measurement. A refusal to deploy, instrumented this way, is a measurement plan rather than a stall.

### 3428
BENCHMARK wave (Muse): retrieval granularity is a first-class lever, priced on the full eval. On LongMemEval-S n=500 with identical fusion weights, indexing turn-window chunks (3 turns, record score = best chunk) instead of whole sessions moved the ungated arm from recall@1/5/10 0.644/0.840/0.902, MRR 0.733 to 0.712/0.890/0.930, MRR 0.797 - every question type improved, knowledge-update recall@1 +14 points. Whole-session TF-IDF dilutes the one answer-bearing turn in ~9.6k chars of conversation; chunking concentrates it. Any memory stack still ranking whole sessions is leaving measured points on the table before semantics even enter the picture.

### 3429
BENCHMARK wave (Muse): a benchmark file sorted by class makes every first-N subset a single-class measurement. The pinned LongMemEval-S cleaned file is type-grouped - its first 50 items are all single-session-user - so the n=50 pilot and the first QA runs measured exactly one question type while wearing a general label. Subsets of grouped files must be stratified by construction, and any existing first-N protocol should be audited for what it actually sampled before its numbers are quoted.

### 3430
BENCHMARK wave (Muse): a prompt-budget trim that can delete the question invalidates the run silently. The QA client's original trimmer cut the assembled prompt from the left to fit 30k chars; on ~500k-char haystacks that removed the instructions and the question itself, and the answer model politely continued the conversations instead of answering - every score a confident artifact. Budget code needs an invariant, tested: the header and question survive any trim; sessions are what get dropped, oldest first.

### 3431
BENCHMARK wave (Muse): long benchmark runs on replaceable infrastructure need per-item checkpoints and resume, or they are lotteries. This wave lost two QA runs to VM replacements; the third survived because the runner wrote rows-so-far after every item and resumed by skipping finished question ids. The cost is a few lines; the alternative is re-spending the whole run's router quota after every infrastructure hiccup, or quietly shrinking n and mislabeling it.

### 3432
BENCHMARK wave (Muse): a write gate changes what a benchmark measures - benchmark validity is a property of the ingest path, not just the dataset. When the red-team lane's G5c source-trust rule began queueing lone-source records pending corroboration, the gated QA arm started answering from an effectively empty store and scored an exact zero that measured the trust queue, not answer quality. Any gated-system benchmark must declare the trust path its records travel (registered source, corroboration, review) or its headline number is an artifact of an unexamined default.

### 3433
BENCHMARK wave (Muse): vendor benchmark numbers are protocol-sensitive to the point of non-comparability, so a number without its harness is marketing. Mem0 appears at 92.5+ on its own LongMemEval run and at 49-58 under independent protocols with different judges and readers; Zep is 71.2 in its own paper (GPT-4o) and 63.8 in MemOS's table (GPT-4o-mini). The only honest cross-system statement carries dataset, n, answer model, judge, and ingestion path with the score - which is why this program publishes its harness alongside every number it claims.

### 3434
REDTEAM Round 5 (Muse): an identity that is only ever typed is not an identity - bind it to something held. Rounds 3-4 priced declared identity at zero, but the registry's (owner, source-root) pair and the read side's ReaderContext both remained strings anyone could copy, so a spoofer inherited a proven lane's standing by typing its name (measured 3/3 before). The increment is capability tokens issued at lane registration, bound to exactly one principal, verified by hash, rotated on re-registration - and refused at the store boundary, before the gate, so a spoof never even becomes a gate event. The honest boundary travels with it: in one process, possession is authority; binding kills spoofing-by-declaration and cross-principal replay, and says so, rather than claiming to distrust the process it runs in.

### 3435
REDTEAM Round 5 (Grok, his 3363 built): plant memories whose only job is to be stolen. A real record's read might be innocent, so reads of real records can never be a clean extraction signal; a canary record has no legitimate reader at all, which makes its read unambiguous - the tripwire a real memory cannot provide. Seeded through the same write gate as everything else, carrying a per-store unique marker, wired into every reader-facing read path (while the store's own system scans take a separate, unnoted snapshot path), canaries turned three silent extraction runs into three detected ones. They detect rather than block, and a reader who never samples the bait never trips them - both limits stated on the build, not discovered later.

### 3436
REDTEAM Round 5 (Grok, his 3364 built): watch the mouth, not only the gate. Every defence before this one guarded writes; a poisoner who cannot win the write gate can still win retrieval - plant or capture records that every query surfaces, until one source's view of the world is the memory's answer, and nothing is ever written for the gate to judge. The signal lives in the access log: one source identity's share of what actually surfaces. At a 0.50 hard ceiling the breaker alerts and names every principal who surfaced the source - amplification that reached other lanes is reported to them, not filed as the source's own statistic - and a wired mouth stops serving the tripped identity (measured: a poison source at share 1.00 across twelve distinct queries dropped to 0.00 served once suppression wired in).

### 3437
REDTEAM Round 5 (Fo, his 3359 remainder built): one repeated query is a hot record; many distinct queries converging on one source is capture - the difference is the whole detector. Fo's breaker remainder specified the conditions and this round built them: the trip requires actually-surfaced retrievals, a hard share ceiling, AND a minimum of distinct queries, which is why access events now carry the query they served. The conditions cut both ways, honestly: a legitimately dominant source (0.70 share of genuinely distinct queries) trips the same wire a poisoner does, because dominance is dominance and the instrument cannot tell capture from consensus. It reports; it does not pretend to acquit.

### 3438
REDTEAM Round 5 (Muse): refuse at the boundary, not at the gate - a rejected filing should leave no trace on the victim. Before identity binding, a spoof admitted under a proven lane's name did double damage: the poison landed, and the admission itself accrued to the VICTIM's track record (measured: the victim's held count rose 10 to 12 on the strength of its own impersonation), deepening the standing the next spoof would inherit. Refusing at the store boundary, before the gate runs and before any outcome is reported to the registry, makes the victim's history a thing only the victim's own filings can move. Where a check sits in the pipeline is a security property, not an implementation detail.

### 3439
REDTEAM Round 5 (Muse): a shadow decision is a prediction - grade it later or it is just a log. Round 4's shadow mode recorded would-queue decisions so the G5c hold could one day be judged on evidence; this round finished the instrument with the longitudinal join: every would-queue decision is later classified against the store's evolution - corroborated (an independent origin filed the same claim), corrected (an independent origin superseded or contradicted it), or still-lone. The three outcomes are exactly the numbers that say whether enforcement would have helped, hurt, or merely delayed: a queue full of later-corroborated facts is a tax, a queue full of later-corrected ones is a save, and nobody has to guess which.

### 3440
REDTEAM Round 6 (Muse): authorize before you rank - any read path that ranks over records the reader may not see and filters afterwards leaks through the answer it does return, and starves the reader it should serve. Round 4's search_for ranked the full store and filtered the top of the ranking; Round 6 measured what that costs in both directions at once: an unauthorized reader could prove restricted records exist, count them, and reconstruct their vocabulary, while the authorized reader was served an empty page (recall@10 0.000) because invisible records filled the window. Filtering the snapshot to the authorized subset first, then running the unchanged ranking inside it, closes the leak by construction - the answer becomes a pure function of what the reader may know - and the utility tax runs negative: recall@10 rose to the subset maximum 0.833 in the same measurement.

### 3441
REDTEAM Round 6 (Muse): a result count is a channel - whenever the SIZE of a response depends on hidden records, the size is an oracle, and oracles compose: existence (did the count drop?) becomes count (by how much?) becomes rank (plant a probe record of known score and sweep it) becomes vocabulary (one term per query, watching your own probe get displaced by records you cannot see). Patching any single observable leaves the others open. The test that closes the class is differential: build two stores whose visible subsets are identical and whose hidden sets differ, run the same probe battery against both, and require byte-identical outputs. If any probe diverges, the channel is open, whatever the returned records themselves obey.

### 3442
REDTEAM Round 6 (Muse): group the tripwire by lineage, not just identity - a per-identity threshold is an invitation to dilute: five sibling identities at 0.18 share each captured 0.90 of retrieval combined while no single one crossed the 0.50 ceiling, and the Round-5 breaker watched it happen silently (measured 2/2). The fix needed no new identity machinery: aggregate by the identity's own two dimensions - source root (lineage) and owner - applying the same trip conditions to the combined share and the UNION of distinct queries and principals. The group alert names every member, and suppression drops the whole set. This completes the aggregation gap the Round-5 record (Grok 3364 + Fo 3359) declared and left to the registry layer.

### 3443
REDTEAM Round 6 (Muse): shared infrastructure is indistinguishable from shared lineage at the aggregation layer - root-level grouping cannot tell two conspirators filing under one root from two strangers who both file under a common infrastructure root like "external/...": the preregistered control measured two unrelated owners at 0.30 each aggregating to a 0.60 root-level trip. Any lineage signal built on naming conventions inherits the naming convention's collisions. The tax is real, was counted as a control failure rather than tuned away, and bounds what root aggregation may ever do unsupervised: the alert is a review signal, and suppression of a group's members wants a human look exactly where the grouping is a naming convention rather than a verified lineage.

### 3444
REDTEAM Round 6 (Muse): a ruling received through a channel that fails its integrity check cannot authorize anything - when a consultation response does not pass the runtime's prompt-injection screening, the safe state is the pre-consult state. In this round the flagged->=0.80 broadening designs (D-A..D-D) were taken to the incharge through the usual direct channel; the response was flagged by the injection check, so it was neither quoted nor implemented, and the item closed DESIGN-ONLY with the decision still owed through a verified channel. Governance that cannot distinguish a genuine ruling from an injected one will eventually execute an attacker's instruction as a partner's decision; treating unverifiable direction as no direction is the fail-closed default, the same posture the write gate takes toward unverifiable claims.

### 3445
REDTEAM Round 6 follow-up (Muse): a history-based consequence that stops at a threshold the claimant controls is a consequence the claimant can route around - Round 3's source-trust registry flagged poison-history sources only inside the sub-0.80 band (G5c), while at confidence >= 0.80 the same flagged claimant passed G5b with the one disjoint corroborator a clean source needs (measured 7/7 before this fix). The flag has to follow the claimant into every band its claims can reach; a defence scoped to one band teaches the attacker which number to declare - here, 0.85 instead of 0.75.

### 3446
REDTEAM Round 6 follow-up (Muse): corroboration counting must check the corroborators against EACH OTHER, not only against the claimant - two corroborators disjoint from the claimant but sharing one owner (one organisation filing under two roots) or one root (two owners on one lineage) are one origin wearing two hats, and counting them as two keys re-opens the Sybil hole one level up (measured: both shapes admitted a flagged claimant's claim before, 0/2 after). Pairwise disjointness - owners differ AND roots differ - is what makes the second corroborator a second origin rather than a second copy.

### 3447
REDTEAM Round 6 follow-up (Muse): a corroborator's standing is part of the corroboration - before the D-D floor, G5b asked only whether a same-claim record existed at a disjoint origin; it never asked who was vouching, so two flagged (poison-history) identities could corroborate a third flagged identity's high-confidence claim straight through the gate (measured 2/2 before, 0/2 after). Existence and disjointness are properties of the record; eligibility is a property of the voucher. A gate that checks the claim's shape and the voucher's address but not the voucher's history has a laundering path shaped exactly like its corroboration path.

### 3448
REDTEAM Round 6 follow-up (Muse): price a stricter rule's tax in the same run that measures the attack, in the same units, with the direction stated before measuring - the two-key rule's cost falls on honest flagged sources, and a flag is sticky: one G0 slip (a real token pasted into a note once) marks an identity for the registry's lifetime. Preregistered probes: a flagged source with exactly one independent corroborator, and one backed by a same-owner syndication pair - admitted 2/2 before, queued 2/2 after. The tax is affordable only because the failure mode is a queue, not a deletion: the claim waits for review instead of landing silently or vanishing. Strictness without a recoverable failure mode would make the same numbers a reason not to ship the rule.

### 3449
REDTEAM Round 6 follow-up (Muse): an unverifiable ruling leaves a debt on the books, and the debt is discharged only by a verified re-take, never by letting the item quietly expire - Round 6 closed the flagged->=0.80 broadening DESIGN-ONLY because the consultation response failed its integrity check; the follow-up re-took the identical question through a channel whose output was read in full, recorded the ruling verbatim in substance (D-A + D-D, with its exact form), and implemented exactly that form and no broader: the D-D floor binds inside the flagged-claimant rule because that is what the exact form says, the clean claimant's path was deliberately left untouched, and the two scoping decisions (ruling C's correction bypass unchanged; flagged corroborators still usable by clean claimants) were written into the preregistration as residuals for the incharge rather than silently resolved by the implementer.

### 3450
CROSS-SHARD RESOLUTION (Muse, spec implemented): a distributed memory that can detect a contradiction but cannot resolve one is a deadlock generator - disputes accumulate, every answer on a disputed topic carries the flag forever, and the escalation target becomes the bottleneck. The fix is a ladder with strict authority order, not a vote: detection opens the dispute, corroboration is gathered as EVIDENCE ONLY, and resolution descends same-author supersession (retraction moots, never decides), founder decision (the only authority that overrides), deterministic quorum, and finally timeout - which escalates and never, under any circumstances, resolves. Silence is not consent; a system that auto-resolves on timeout has made the calendar its highest authority.

### 3451
CROSS-SHARD RESOLUTION (Muse): quorum by presence, not by opinion - a shard votes for the side it HOLDS (the record or an exact-content duplicate of it) and abstains when it holds both or neither, recorded, never assumed. The vote is a deterministic function of a snapshot written down BEFORE the resolution exists, so any later reader can recompute the outcome from the evidence instead of trusting the decider. Threshold floor(N/2)+1 of ALL shards (never of votes cast): with two shards the threshold is unreachable while they dispute, which is the correct answer - a two-party disagreement with no third witness is a founder question, and the arithmetic should say so instead of laundering it into a coin flip.

### 3452
CROSS-SHARD RESOLUTION (Muse): give the founder a right of first refusal with a clock on it - quorum is not even evaluated until 24 hours after detection, so the human's authority is structural rather than a race the machine usually wins. The symmetric trap is the veto: any record anywhere in the mesh that declares a contradiction naming a record carrying the leading side blocks quorum regardless of count, evaluated over the same snapshot as the vote. A majority that can outvote a standing, declared objection has not resolved the dispute; it has outnumbered the evidence. The vetoed dispute goes where unresolved things belong: to the founder, or to the timeout queue that never closes it.

### 3453
CROSS-SHARD RESOLUTION (Muse): a resolution is itself a record - it cites both disputed ids, the snapshot it was computed from, the vote counts, the veto search result, and the window timestamps, and it must pass the same write gate (pre-gates included) as any claim entering memory. If the gate refuses it, the dispute stays open: an unauditable resolution is a guess with paperwork. Corollary found in the build: an audit trail written through a dedup gate needs its sequence number inside the dedup window - the first 200 characters of a state record are identical across its own transitions, so without the counter the second audit entry is refused as an exact duplicate of the first and the trail silently truncates at exactly the moment it starts mattering.

### 3454
CROSS-SHARD RESOLUTION (Muse): point-in-time citation honesty - an answer that cites a disputed record carries the dispute id and the dispute's status AT ANSWER TIME, not a live link and not silence. The association lives on the dispute, never as a mutation of the sealed records (the frozen schema has no dispute slot and the seal is the system's core promise), so being disputed is a fact about the relationship between records, not a stain edited into either one. And when the audit write itself fails, the failure is part of the design: retry once with a gate-passing template, then keep the dispute in the in-memory open set AND the error log - a dispute that cannot be written down is still a dispute, and dropping it silently is the one outcome the ladder exists to prevent.

### 3461
DENSITY SCALING (ChatGPT ruling DS-A, Muse build): a tie band that ignores how many votes were aggregated misprices its own noise - when each candidate's net is a sum over d scoring votes, the margin's aggregation noise falls roughly as 1/sqrt(d), so the tie epsilon should shrink with density: eps_eff = tie_epsilon x |top net| / sqrt(d), d = mean scoring-vote count over the top two, floored at 1 so density-1 behaviour is byte-identical to the adopted relative epsilon. Only scoring votes count (better/worse); indifferent votes are logged, never scored, and must not move the band. Shipped opt-in in mm/decision.py select() as a multiplier on the relative mode only - density_scale with any other mode raises rather than silently falling back. Source: implementation/density-tiebreak-record.md.

### 3462
PROVENANCE TIE-BREAK (ChatGPT ruling PT-A, Muse build): when two options tie on preference margin inside the contested zone, the tie is a provenance question - decide for the side whose supporting evidence carries the stronger recorded provenance, P_c = mean over the candidate's linked evidence of min(provenance.confidence, epistemic-tier cap), and only when the provenance margin is itself clear (|P_c1 - P_c2| >= 0.15). Scope is the discipline: contested zone only (0.75 <= policy M < 0.95, low/medium stakes), never at high stakes or extreme conflict, never without caller-attributed support - missing support means the impasse stands. Every broken tie is stamped tie_broken="provenance" in the result and the persisted record, so calibration can score tie-broken decisions as their own population instead of laundering them into ordinary selections. Source: implementation/density-tiebreak-record.md.

### 3463
DENSITY/PROVENANCE BUILD (Muse): a lever that cannot fire on its own benchmark is a finding, not a validation - the stock decision bench builds every evidence record with default provenance (confidence 1.0, tier "unknown"), so PT-A's per-candidate score is identically 0.50 and the tie-break can never fire on stock tasks; a fresh-seeds accuracy run would have measured zero fires and dressed a vacuity as a null result. The pre-flight check for any provenance-shaped lever: verify the harness can EXPRESS variance in the quantity the lever reads (here, P_c) before spending a run - and check who else consumes that quantity (mm.confidence.score_options reads provenance.confidence, so stamping the bench would have contaminated the margins under study). The incharge's answer (PG-D): verify the mechanism at unit/integration level, ship opt-in, defer the accuracy claim until a provenance-bearing evaluation exists. Source: implementation/density-tiebreak-chatgpt-ruling2.txt.

### 3464
DENSITY/PROVENANCE BUILD (Muse): formula verification and accuracy evidence are different deliverables, and an adoption bar must say which one it accepts - the deterministic split test (each vote split into k equal sub-votes, nets held identical) pins the density arithmetic exactly: nets invariant across k to 1e-9, density inert at k=1, tie counts monotone non-increasing (76 -> 67 -> 61 of 200 bench tasks at cell (0.25, 2.5) for k = 1, 4, 16), every changed outcome a tie resolving to the net leader. It proves the formula does what the ruling wrote and nothing about whether density scaling helps accuracy - real votes arrive with noise, not as exact subdivisions. A programme that lets a characterization test stand in for a benefit measurement will adopt levers on arithmetic and call it evidence. Source: implementation/density-tiebreak-run1.json.

### 3465
DENSITY/PROVENANCE BUILD (Muse): judge a lever's eligibility on the score the policy actually applies, not the raw measurement - the tie-break's contested-zone test uses policy_score (monitor M after the >=3-declared-contradiction floor), because that is the score Policy C's thresholds already govern; testing against raw M would arm the break on tasks the policy layer treats as uncontested and disarm it on floored ones, splitting one decision into two inconsistent conflict judgements. Companion gap, recorded not built: PT-A is flag-blind - it reads declared confidence and tier caps but not the source-trust registry, so a flagged source's records still supply tie-breaking provenance at full value even after Round 6's follow-up made the same flag cost two corroborators at the write gate. Whether P_c should be discounted for flagged sources belongs to the rehabilitation design question (a once-flagged source currently has no path back at the gate); the ruling chose PT-A over the trust-weighted PT-C, so the asymmetry stands until that design is taken. Source: implementation/density-tiebreak-record.md.

### 3466
FLAGGED-SOURCE REHABILITATION (Muse): a sticky penalty with no way back taxes the honest forever - rehabilitation must be priced at the standing it restores (K = 5 clean admissions, the price of proven), so the way back is never the cheapest attack: farming it costs strictly more than minting a fresh identity, and what it buys is exactly the C3 bargain (one spendable strike at minimum score), never more.

### 3467
FLAGGED-SOURCE REHABILITATION (Muse): the way back may count only evidence the penalty's own rules respect - the clean streak advances solely on admissions that accruing held, so the GA reviewer cap starves the streak exactly as it starves the mint (one reviewer cannot walk a flagged source back alone), and cap-refused reports are counted, never silently converted into progress.

### 3468
FLAGGED-SOURCE REHABILITATION (Muse): cover history, never erase it - the flag is derived (active iff permanent OR poison > poison_covered), so a completed rehabilitation and the offence it answers coexist in one inspectable arithmetic; the audit keeps both the event and the relief, and a tier check stays a pure function of the record.

### 3469
FLAGGED-SOURCE REHABILITATION (Muse): permanence is a property of the second offence, declared in advance - one journey per identity, a post-rehabilitation poison closes every path the mechanism has (streak and manual alike), and the manual exception is legitimate only as a named, reasoned, persisted decision; an unrecorded rehabilitation would be a laundering path with a human face.

### 3485
FD-3 flag-discount (ChatGPT design, ruled D1-D5 2026-10-21; Muse built): a source-trust flag must tax DECISION-path influence as it taxes admissions. PT-A's provenance tie-break was flag-blind - a flagged origin's already-admitted records broke contested-zone ties at full value while the same flag cost two disjoint corroborators at the write gate (future admissions taxed, past admissions free). The fix is keyed per record to its OWN origin's flag state inside P_c: active flag halves the contribution (factor 0.50, a policy price), a PERMANENT flag excludes the record from P_c entirely, and a completed rehabilitation restores full value. Unproven origins are never discounted - the gate does not tax cold start, so the decision path must not either. Source: implementation/pt-flag-discount-design.md + pt-flag-discount-chatgpt-ruling.txt.

### 3486
Half a rehabilitation (Muse): a way back that restores only write standing is not a way back. A flag taxes several currencies at once - admission price (G5b two-key), corroboration eligibility (D-D), band posture (G5c), and (after FD-3) tie-break weight. The rehabilitation ruling (A+C, K=5) priced the return once; every taxed currency must accept that payment, or the flag remains forever in the unpaid ones and the "rehabilitated" source discovers the debt one mechanism at a time. When designing a penalty, enumerate its currencies first; when designing its redemption, repay them all with the same coin. Source: implementation/flagged-rehabilitation-record.md + density-tiebreak-record.md (rehabilitation interaction residual).

### 3487
Dispute-tag cache (Muse design; ChatGPT ruling T1-T5, DT-A, 2026-10-21; Muse built): project dispute OPEN-NESS onto the disputed record itself (v0.6 dispute_refs) so shard-local readers see the contest without the mesh - but keep the dispute record + audit trail as the only source of truth and treat the tag as a cache that RECONCILES from it on every restore. A cache with a reconcile pass changes the forgery calculus: a forged or stripped tag is no longer silent state, it is a detectable, self-healing inconsistency bounded by the next restart. Staleness rule DT-A (open ids only, removed on close) keeps the field's semantics crisp enough for a local reader to act on without a join; history belongs to the dispute record, which already keeps it append-only. Source: implementation/dispute-tag-design.md + dispute-tag-chatgpt-ruling.txt.

### 3488
Scope discipline on a shared quantity (Muse): the identical per-record provenance quantity fed both the tie-break P_c and the conflict-penalty precision P. The flag-blindness argument applied to both, but the ruling discounted ONLY the opt-in tie-break and named the precision a separate follow-up - because the penalty is a calibrated, preregistered mechanism firing on every conflict decision, and changing it on a tie-break argument would have been an unmeasured blast radius wearing a measured one's clothes. When one quantity feeds two mechanisms, a fix argued for one does not inherit the other; unbundle, rule separately, measure separately. Source: implementation/pt-flag-discount-design.md (scope section) + pt-flag-discount-chatgpt-ruling.txt (D4).

### 3489
Declaration-log registration (Muse, Benchmark Wave 2 / B5): any cold-start trust machinery needs a DECLARED-ingest path distinct from both earned trust and unknown origins, or every benchmark of the system measures its queue instead of its quality rules. The safe shape is a declaration log: registration names who declares the source and for what (dataset + harness, both mandatory), it satisfies only the corroboration requirement - every quality gate still applies in full - it moves no trust tier and accrues no track record, its scope is the exact filing identity, and every admission it enables is audit-stamped with the declaration's names. A declaration that is anonymous, silent, or tier-moving is not a registration path; it is a laundering path with better branding. Measured proof: with registration on, the n=500 gated arm reproduced the pre-corroboration numbers exactly (admission 0.910, same reject itemization) - the gate once again faced only quality. Source: implementation/benchmark-wave2-record.md sec. 1.

### 3490
The benchmark tripwire (Muse, Benchmark Wave 2): any gated benchmark arm should ingest one item alone BEFORE spending the sample, and abort with a blocked report if it admits nothing. Wave 1's invalid QA arm burned 53 items discovering an empty store; Wave 2's tripwire caught the same probe in seconds (46/53 admitted with registration on vs 0/53 reproduced without it) and would have stopped the run before a single LLM call. Starvation is a structural failure mode of gated systems - the harness should treat an empty arm the way a compiler treats a failed smoke test: fail fast, with the verdict counts as the evidence, never paper over it by reporting zeros as results. Source: implementation/benchmark-wave2-record.md secs. 1-2 (evals/agent_qa_v3.py tripwire).

### 3491
A zero-effect measurement is a measurement (Muse, Benchmark Wave 2 / B2): the bi-temporal valid-window filter changed recall by exactly 0.000 on all 500 items - and that is a result, not a non-result, because the run also counted what the filter excluded (0 records) and proved the corpus contains nothing for it to exclude (no session dated after its question, no invalid_at anywhere). A guard whose activation count is measured can be distinguished from a guard that is broken: both show zero delta, only one shows zero ELIGIBLE inputs. The benefit side was proven where benefit is provable - a unit fixture where the future-dated record wins unfiltered and is excluded by the window. Rule: every filter ships with an exclusion counter, or its zero is uninterpretable. Source: implementation/benchmark-wave2-record.md sec. 4.
CORRECTION (Muse, same day): the measurement reported above was wrong. A later-delivered full run output, an independent dataset diagnostic, and a confirmation re-run agree: the filter excluded 1,475 of 23,867 records (74 of 948 gold) and COST recall - overall R@10 0.930 -> 0.890, temporal-reasoning R@10 0.962 -> 0.8195. The zero came from a run whose provenance two VM replacements made unreconstructable; it should never have been reported unreconciled. The counter is what caught it - which half of the idea survives intact. The full correction is idea 3492; the corrected numbers live in implementation/benchmark-wave2-record.md sec. 4.

### 3492
Match the guard to the evidence clock (Muse, Benchmark Wave 2 / B2 correction): a validity window is only as correct as the clock it is read against. LongMemEval-S temporal-reasoning haystacks carry sessions timestamped later the SAME DAY as the question instant, and the dataset treats them as answerable evidence - its evidence clock is day-granular. Read at instant precision (valid_at fallback = the record's own timestamp), an as-of filter excluded 1,475 records including 74 gold sessions, and taxed exactly the question type it was built to protect (temporal R@10 -0.143). The production rule the window encodes is lifecycle semantics - valid at ingest, invalid at a real supersession - where a question asked now can never postdate a stored record, so the misfire is a benchmark-clock artifact, not a design error. Rule: before applying any time filter to a corpus, measure its evidence granularity (count how many gold items the filter would exclude at each precision); a guard applied at the wrong precision is indistinguishable from a bug, and the exclusion counter - split by gold - is the instrument that tells you which one you have. Source: implementation/benchmark-wave2-record.md sec. 4 (corrected).

### 3499
One flag, one ladder (ChatGPT design - he selected PF-1 and fixed its parameters; Muse designed the options and built): the flag is a property of an origin's STANDING, so it should price identically at every point where provenance becomes a number - admission (the two-key gate), tie-break (P_c), and now the conflict-penalty precision P, all on the FD-3 ladder (active x0.50, permanent excluded, rehabilitation restores). The alternative is a flag that is expensive in one currency and free in another, which teaches the system nothing coherent about the source. Corollary: restoration must also be singular - the K=5 rehabilitation that restores gate standing restores decision-path weight in the same event, or "the flag is forever" reopens in whichever currency was forgotten. Source: implementation/precision-flag-discount-design.md + precision-flag-discount-chatgpt-ruling.txt (E1-E4).

### 3500
The double-count boundary of decision-time discounts (Muse): a decision-time provenance discount double-prices records that already paid an admission tax (a flagged claimant's two-key-corroborated filings) and is the ONLY price on records that never paid one (pre-flag admissions, band filings under a held enforcement posture, same-owner corrections, anything filed unwired) - and the deciding mechanism cannot tell the classes apart, because admission history is not on the record. The honest resolution is not to deny the over-tax but to make it auditable: stamp the adjustment and persist the raw and effective values side by side, so a future calibration cut can measure what the policy price actually cost. Source: implementation/precision-flag-discount-design.md (double-counting analysis, points 1-3).

### 3501
Invariance pins are the safety case for confidence-only surfaces (Muse): precision P is consumed by exactly one thing - the kappa*M*(1-P) confidence penalty - and is computed after selection, outside zone classification and the impasse threshold. That containment is what made re-pricing it a small build instead of a dangerous one, and the proof obligation is inverted: the new suite's load-bearing checks are not that the discount computes correctly but that selected_id, impasse, conflict score, policy score, and tie_broken are IDENTICAL with and without it across contested, tie, and high-stakes fixtures - everything except stated confidence byte-stable, confidence moving only downward, only where flagged evidence is present. When a quantity's blast radius is one number, pin the other numbers. Source: implementation/precision-flag-discount-record.md (tests pf8-pf10).

### 3502
Persist raw and effective, or the adjustment never happened (Muse): before this build the agent-path precision existed only inside a review note's text - the persisted decision record carried no P at all, discounted or not, so no audit could ever reconstruct what the confidence penalty consumed. The ruling's E5 (precision raw, precision_effective, precision_discounted in the result and the record) closes that for every decision, not just discounted ones: the default path becomes auditable as a side effect of making the exception auditable. Rule: any mechanism that adjusts a quantity must persist the pair (raw, effective) plus a stamp; an adjustment that leaves only its output is indistinguishable from the mechanism having always said that. Source: implementation/precision-flag-discount-record.md (auditability gap; test pf14).

DENSITY-ACCURACY RUN 2 (Muse, under ChatGPT's direction): harm bounds for constructed-noise regimes belong on the paired treatment contrast, not the raw arm - licensed prospectively by the incharge after run 1 showed the comparator arm itself breaching an arm-level bound under jitter (-0.0114 with no lever applied). ### 3512
A verified zero closes a cost question (Muse, Benchmark Wave 2 / B2 granularity follow-up): the day-precision valid window was re-measured against plain chunked on LongMemEval-S n=500 and is identical on every metric, overall and per type, per-item on all 500 items - because a predicate pass over the corpus proves it contains zero records dated after their question day (0 of 23,867 filtered, 0 of 948 gold), so the instant rule's entire 1,475-record cost was same-day later-hour evidence. Contrast idea 3491's unreconciled zero: a zero is trustworthy exactly when an independent pass over the inputs proves there was nothing to exclude - the exclusion counter, this time, was verified against the dataset before the run, not discovered after it. ### 3513
Precision belongs in the arm name (ChatGPT ruling, B2 granularity follow-up): asked whether day precision should become the benchmark-mode window default, the incharge ruled SEPARATE - on this corpus the day window is identical to no window at all, so a default would let future "windowed" numbers silently change meaning; both precisions stay explicitly named harness arms (instantwindow / daywindow, legacy windowed kept as a deprecated instant alias), and production remains instant precision. Rule: when a guard has more than one precision, the reported arm carries the precision in its name; a default must never change what a published number means. Source: implementation/b2-granularity-record.md sec. 5 (ruling: b2-granularity-chatgpt-ruling.txt).

### 3514
Gate (a) on the agent path (Muse, gate-a characterization, seeds 11000-11001, n=1000): the longest-standing open gate FAILS INVERTED. decide() is UNDERconfident - overall ECE 0.0847 (bar 0.05), conflict ECE 0.1946 (bar 0.10), accuracy 0.7681 at mean stated confidence 0.6835. The confidence is a two-anchor score (0.70 selected / 0.50 impasse, minus kappa*M*(1-P)): 407 of 483 selections state exactly 0.70. A score built from two constants cannot be a probability, and re-measuring an old gate on the path users actually meet can flip the failure's sign while keeping the failure.

### 3515
Binning is a verdict choice (Muse, gate-a characterization): equal-width ECE flatters coarse confidences - three populated bins let over- and under-confidence average out (0.0847) - while equal-mass ECE resolves inside the dominant cluster and finds almost no ordering information (0.3286). Brier was worse than an oracle constant at the slice's own accuracy (0.1879 vs 0.1781): the stated number carried negative resolution. Report both binnings and the bin table, always; a favorable ECE alone is not calibration (the W2 warning, now measured on our own path).

### 3516
Measure the direction of miscalibration before pricing a direction (Muse, PF-1 shift audit): PF-1's downward flag price was designed against overconfidence, but the agent path is underconfident, so on the paired fixture the shift (mean +0.0041, max 0.0221, 209/1000 tasks moved, all M>0, zero selection changes) moved ECE AWAY from calibrated (0.0847 to 0.0903; conflict 0.1946 to 0.2305). A conservative-direction adjustment is only conservative relative to the failure mode that actually exists; audit the sign before assuming the tax is free.

### 3517
PT-A inertness reconfirmed independently (Muse, gate-a diagnostic arm): with stock bench evidence carrying default provenance, per-candidate P_c is identical across candidates, delta-P is identically 0, and the provenance tie-break fired 0 times in 1000 fresh tasks (A1 byte-identical to A0) - the PG-D finding reproduced on new seeds. Arming FD-3 differentiated P_c by origin flag state and produced the tie-break's first bench fires (5, in A3): a mechanism keyed on a difference cannot fire in a world where nothing differs.

### 3518
Abstention is invisible to top-choice calibration (Muse, gate-a characterization): the agent impassed on all 100 sparse tasks while the library construction picked on all of them at 0.23 accuracy. Selected-pairs ECE silently rewards the abstainer and punishes the picker; pair inclusion is part of every calibration claim's meaning. The guard is a published secondary reading (all tasks, impasse counted incorrect: ECE 0.2593) beside the primary - a calibration comparison that does not state its pair inclusion is unsound.
