### 3526
Cool the dead on the invalidation clock, not the access clock (ChatGPT ruling J-A, B2 remainders): a record whose validity window has closed becomes cooled-eligible at invalid_at + 14d (the existing schedule's first period) regardless of later access - reads of a no-longer-in-force record do not keep it warm. Later lifecycle steps stay idle-based; the rule grants cooled-eligibility only, no archive or prune acceleration, and the immune class (decay_exempt) still never migrates. "ttl" in the spec meant the schedule's own first period, not an invented per-class duration map (a per-class map with a never-cooling class would have recreated the permanent-shield shape Round 4's A14 ruling abolished). Source: implementation/b2-remainders-record.md sec. 1 (ruling: b2-remainders-chatgpt-ruling.txt).

### 3527
A succession is not a conflict (ChatGPT ruling W-A + adoption ruling; Muse build and measurement, B2 remainders): a declared contradiction pair whose validity windows are disjoint was never simultaneously in force, so it contributes zero to M - the monitor's score is now the windowed value, with the pre-signal M retained on every report as score_unwindowed for audit. Adoption was earned, not assumed: built measurement-only (ruling Q3), then a preregistered bar - stock-bench inertness against a printed denominator (1,957 declared pairs, 0 resolved, max delta 0.0) plus an exact fixture battery - and a separate adoption ruling on those numbers. Rule: a signal that would change a priced quantity ships as a reported shadow first, adopts only on measured inertness-where-it-should-be-inert plus exactness-where-it-should-fire, and keeps the old value on the report so the adoption stays inspectable. Source: implementation/b2-remainders-record.md sec. 2 (rulings: b2-remainders-chatgpt-ruling.txt, b2-remainders-adoption-ruling.txt).

### 3528
Band, don't bare-number (ChatGPT ruling, gate-(a) remediation R-A): a two-anchor score that fails its calibration gate (agent path ECE 0.0847 equal-width / 0.3286 equal-mass, UNDERconfident) must not reach a user-facing surface as a bare number. Present state + Policy-C zone + the harness-measured accuracy of the closest measured slice, labelled SYNTHETIC harness evidence, or suppress the number entirely; the raw value belongs to the audit trail and the pair registry, not the surface. An abstention carries no accuracy reference at all - an impasse is not a claim. Source: implementation/gate-a-remediation-record.md (ruling: gate-a-agentpath-chatgpt-ruling.txt).

### 3529
Acceptance is not correctness (ChatGPT ruling, gate-(a) remediation R-C as amended): a calibration pair exists only when the outcome was independently resolved under a named source; acceptance, self-assessment, assumption and silence are refused mechanically - no pair recorded, the decision stays pending for a real resolution. Thirty real pairs unlock EVALUATION, not fitting: a threshold is a licence to look, never proof the data is adequate or representative. Source: implementation/gate-a-remediation-record.md (ruling: gate-a-agentpath-chatgpt-ruling.txt).

### 3530
Corrections are events, not edits (Muse, gate-(a) remediation R-C build): the calibration log is append-only and is never rewritten; a correction is its own appended event (original outcome, previous effective outcome, corrected outcome, source, resolver), and evaluation consumes a view that applies corrections - latest wins - over the untouched substrate. A pair's corrected flag reports that a correction EXISTS, even one that flipped the outcome back, because a contested outcome is audit-relevant either way. Source: implementation/gate-a-remediation-record.md.

### 3531
A consent switch must be load-bearing (Muse, gate-(a) remediation R-C build): pair recording over the founder's own decisions carries an explicit switch (constructor or runtime) whose OFF state persists across restarts and wins over the constructor default; while off, outcomes land no pairs and decisions stay pending. Pair records are data-minimized - numbers and resolution metadata only; question text lives only in the pending registry and is dropped at resolution, pinned by test against both persisted files. Source: implementation/gate-a-remediation-record.md.

### 3532
Zone-conditional bases (Muse design, ChatGPT-amended, gate-(a) remediation R-B): the agent path's calibration failure is structural - flat 0.70/0.50 bases yield three populated bins with near-zero within-cluster ordering, so no monotone remap of the score can manufacture calibration. Hypothesis: bases conditional on the Policy-C zone and tie state, absorbed by metacognitive_review as data; the tie-broken cell is the prime suspect (claims 0.70 at 0.6271 measured accuracy). Fit protocol if it ever runs: >=30 real pairs unlocks evaluation only, per-cell counts decide estimability, temporal out-of-sample validation, ECE must improve under BOTH binnings with no slice regressing. Nothing fitted; no code path consumes it. Source: implementation/gate-a-remediation-record.md.

### 3533
Gate every re-entry path with the same window that gated the exit (ChatGPT ruling; Muse measurement + build, janitor resurrection lane): J-A cooled records whose validity window had closed, but the resurrection path (cooled -> active on >= 3 distinct-day accesses) never read invalid_at, so a record 20d out of force resurrected on use and the two rules oscillated indefinitely - migrate, resurrect, migrate across passes (measured battery F1/F2, preregistered) while the record spent alternate passes in the active tier regaining consolidation pointer eligibility. Ruled: NEVER resurrect an out-of-force record; step 3 skips promotion whenever invalid_at is set and <= now. What resurrection restores is only the tier label, pointer eligibility, and one lifecycle stage - retrieval excludes only archive and episode assembly already gates on the window - so the promotion bought nothing the window allows, at the price of perpetual op churn. Rule: any transition INTO a warmer tier must evaluate the same in-force predicate as the transition out, or the paired rules fight forever. Source: implementation/janitor-resurrection-record.md.

### 3534
The grace belongs to the exit rule, not the re-entry rule (ChatGPT ruling, janitor resurrection lane): when a cooling rule carries a grace (J-A fires at invalid_at + 14d), it is tempting to key the paired resurrection gate at the same instant (invalid_at + 14d) for symmetry. Ruled otherwise: the gate key is invalid_at itself, so the 14d grace governs migration timing only and never becomes a resurrection window - a record out of force 5d blocks exactly like one out of force 100d, while accesses to a blocked record still log and count toward half-life estimation. Asymmetric keys are the point: grace delays forgetting; it must not license revival. Source: implementation/janitor-resurrection-record.md (ruling: janitor-resurrection-chatgpt-ruling.txt).

### 3535
NEXT-LEVER RANKED DIRECTION + THE (0, 2.5) RULING (ChatGPT, incharge, direct): toward the +0.22 accuracy-interaction target the ranked order is (1) noise-gated density multiplier, (2) asymmetric evidence-quality-conditioned tie band, (3) calibration-shaped interaction (measurement-led, only after the gate-(a) characterization reports), (4) PT-A accuracy via new measurement infrastructure (not actionable today). Cell (0, 2.5) - accuracy 0.0000, impasse 1.0000 under every arm ever measured - is ruled FAIL-CLOSED BY DESIGN for gap accounting: excluded from the recoverable gap going forward unless a separately specified mechanism demonstrates a correct decision there without violating fail-closed behaviour. Source: hidden_files/implementation/next-lever-chatgpt-ruling.txt.

### 3536
CROSS-RUN INTERACTIONS ARE NOT ADDITIVE (Muse, next-lever evidence memo): the +0.22 target is a Phase-2 RAW-PATH figure (+22.1pp [+20.8, +23.4], library scoring path); every agent-path interaction (+0.0514 Policy C, +0.1208 tie-lever stack) is paired WITHIN its own run on its own fresh seeds, so the numbers cannot be summed or subtracted across runs as if they shared a basis. A gap decomposition must separate measured facts from hypotheses and name the pools (impasse residue, tie-variant cost, calibration interaction, density-under-noise, PT-A's unknown) as OVERLAPPING, never as a partition. Source: hidden_files/implementation/next-lever-evidence-memo.md.

### 3537
DS-NG MEASURED - THE GATE FIXED THE HARM AND DILUTED THE BENEFIT (Muse): the noise-gated density variant is the first density form to PASS the corrected control-slice harm bound in every regime (R0 0.0000, R1 -0.0051, pooled -0.0025, bound 0.01; ungated DS-A failed R1 in both its runs), with high-stakes outcomes 209/209 identical - but its stage-1 primary contrast is +0.0072 [-0.0096, +0.0239], CI including zero, so under the preregistered conjunctive bar there was no stage 2 and no adoption (vote 0/5; the incharge closed the density line for default adoption). Withholding a quarter to a third of the shrinkage dose in both regimes alike bought harm-avoidance at the price of detectability: through a non-separating statistic, the two trade directly. Source: hidden_files/implementation/next-lever-record.md; next-lever-noisegate-run1.json.

### 3538
MEASURE A GATE STATISTIC'S SEPARATION BEFORE PREREGISTERING AROUND IT (Muse): the per-task vote-noise statistic (pooled centred log-weight dispersion) has R0/R1 means 0.554 / 0.607 with near-total overlap, because the signal dispersion (~0.55) swamps the injected jitter in quadrature (sqrt(0.55^2 + 0.25^2) = 0.60) - the statistic cannot identify which regime a task came from, and a percentile gate rule built across the two distributions (p75 of clean vs p25 of jittered) is ill-defined when they overlap this far. Any future gating design must publish the statistic's regime separation from a design-only diagnostic first, and freeze thresholds from ONE reference distribution, not from the gap between two. Source: hidden_files/implementation/next-lever-preregistration.md (diagnostic section).

### 3539
The LIMS registry holds pump testing coverage (Muse, LIMS fold lane; parent-run live pass 21 Oct 2026 ~04:05 IST, lims.bis.gov.in, read-only, no login): IS 9079:2018 (monoblock/monoset pumpsets) is listed by 11 accredited labs and IS 8034:2018 (submersible pumpsets) by 15, with OSL numbers, scopes, and validity dates recorded. Navigation: home-page "Search by IS Number" card -> Indian Standard Number field -> Search; both searches worked interactively. Site disclaimer: scope shown is as submitted by the lab, to be verified by BIS per the scope of recognition granted. Source: watch-log/LIMS-IS9079-IS8034-findings.md.

### 3540
Registry tier beats publication tier (Muse, LIMS fold lane): the AN arc's capability-without-coverage x167 counter measured lab-website publication only, and was falsified at the authoritative tier when the BIS LIMS registry showed 11 labs with IS 9079 and 15 with IS 8034. Lesson: a coverage counter must name its tier; "no lab publishes scope on a fetchable route" is a publication-tier observation, never an absence-of-capability finding. The correction is appended to ARC-CLOSE-AN.md as an addendum, not edited into the sealed body. Mandate verdicts unchanged - lab coverage is not a mandate. Source: watch-log/LIMS-IS9079-IS8034-findings.md; ARC-CLOSE-AN.md correction addendum (21 Oct 2026).

### 3541
Tie-variant membership separates correctness within the 0.70 anchor at strength (Muse, calibration-shaped interaction lane): on fresh seeds (12000-12001, n=2000, agent default), selections all stating conf exactly 0.70 split 0.4694 (tie-variant, n=98) vs 0.8248 (rest, n=822) - delta +0.3554, 95% CI [+0.2485, +0.455]. This is the sharpest form of the R-B prime suspect: the calibration failure lives in the tie cell, not in the anchor. Frozen verdict: CONFIRMS-EXISTING - no new implementation consult; R-B stays a hypothesis gated on real pairs. The tie-variant level is not seed-stable (0.6271 on the gate-(a) lane's seeds, 0.4694 here); the separation is. Source: implementation/calibration-shaped-interaction-record.md (preregistration: calibration-shaped-interaction-preregistration.md).

### 3542
The M>0 penalty points the wrong way (Muse, calibration-shaped interaction lane): the penalized slice (conf<0.70, n=153) is MORE accurate than the 0.70 anchor (0.8235 vs 0.7797, delta -0.0439, CI includes zero), and within the penalized slice deeper penalty is more accurate (0.8767 below median vs 0.775 at/above, delta -0.1017, CI includes zero); conflict_score as a correctness classifier is null (AUC 0.5157, CI [0.4868, 0.5428]). Directional evidence for the sign-aware-pricing research item already on the books (R-D, gated on real pairs) - nothing clears a consult bar, so no new consult opens. Lesson: a penalty whose price moves opposite to accuracy cannot be fixed by deepening it; the sign, not the size, is the question. The calibration-shaped interaction candidate stays measurement-led. Source: implementation/calibration-shaped-interaction-record.md.

### 3543
No silent absorption (Muse, next-arc consult): the incharge explicitly kept the AM key-candidate irons (R525/R526/R528) on the open register rather than folding them into the new kitchen arc, and kept abrasive wheels (R534) as a separate carry - a new arc's family resemblance never upgrades or resolves a prior arc's candidates without a documented trigger. General rule: open registers survive arc boundaries; reunion requires a trigger, not a theme. Source: watch-log/NEXT-ARC-PROPOSAL.md (ruling: watch-log/next-arc-chatgpt-ruling.txt).
### 3544
Kitchen-appliance arc approved, R541 = mixer-grinder (ChatGPT ruling, next-arc consult 21 Oct 2026): with AM (garment care, keyed 5) and AN (workshop power, 8 NO-KEY machines) both closed at keys 199, the incharge directed household kitchen appliances assessed against the applicable IS 302 Part 2 sections - with the umbrella QCO 2026 list framed as a specific scope QUESTION, not presumed coverage. First object mixer-grinder; proposed objects water heater, oven, toaster, each verified independently. Source: watch-log/NEXT-ARC-PROPOSAL.md (ruling: watch-log/next-arc-chatgpt-ruling.txt).

### 3545
A six-test arc spine (Muse synthesis of the incharge's required tests, next-arc consult): containment triangle (product scope / QCO row / operative legal scope quoted separately) - instrument-level mandate (mandatory vs voluntary Scheme-I vs mere applicability kept distinct) - part/edition discipline (exact IS 302 Part 2 section and edition; no family-level IEC inference) - boundary adjudication (pair-joint only where source text is materially ambiguous) - independent evidence tiers (registry / lab capability / lab-website publication / brand publication reported separately) - disposition (KEY / KEY-CANDIDATE / NO-KEY with tiers never flattened). Source: watch-log/NEXT-ARC-PROPOSAL.md.


### 3546
Fossil claims are reconciled, not inherited (Muse, test-ledger reconciliation): test_phase3_chunk2 measured 52 while its original Phase-3 record said 46/46 - three later records (next-steps, redteam-round1, density-tiebreak) all said 52 and the file's mtime matched the adding lane, so the 46 was a superseded documentation fossil, not a defect. Rule: when a record's count disagrees with the suite, the newest record plus a fresh measurement decides; an old claim is never edited into silence, it is outvoted by later evidence. Source: implementation/test-ledger-reconciliation.md (note 1).

### 3547
Measure the baseline yourself at lane start (Muse, test-ledger reconciliation): the gate-a-remediation brief carried 702 counted checks; the lane measured 713 before any edit (691 + 11 + 11 landed between the two closes) and recorded the correction itself - independently confirmed here. The night's full drift chain (691 -> 713 -> 739 -> 767 -> 782 -> 794) reconciles against a record at every step only because each lane measured its own start. Rule: a brief's numbers are a hypothesis; the suite's output is the count. Source: implementation/test-ledger-reconciliation.md (note 2 + drift chain).

### 3548
Tariff identity is not mandate identity (Grok, R541 Q4 tariff leg): pinning the HS code of an object (mixer-grinder -> 85094090, verified against India ITC(HS) with object-named India-party bills on both lanes) answers only what the object is called in trade; it says nothing about whether BIS certification is mandatory. A KEY verdict needs the QCO row and its operative legal scope quoted separately - the tariff row never upgrades or implies a mandate. Rule: an HS pin is a precondition for talking about the object precisely, never evidence for its key status. Source: watch-log/R541-Q4-grok-trade.md.

### 3549
Name the digit-length of a tariff pin, not the display string (Grok, R541 Q4 tariff leg): India's statutory pin is 8 digits (85094090), but trade platforms pad it to 10/12 digits (8509400000, 850940000000, 85094000000) in their listings. Quoting a padded string as the pin invites false mismatches against the schedule. Rule: a pin states its length (India: 8-digit ITC(HS)) and cites the schedule line; platform renderings are vendor extensions, never the statute. Source: watch-log/R541-Q4-grok-trade.md.

### 3550
The same object ships under sibling tariff lines (Grok, R541 Q4 tariff leg): object-named "MIXER GRINDER" bills clear under 85094090 (Other) and also under 85094010 (Food grinders) - e.g. 28-Apr-2025 India -> Guinea, 1 PCS, $76.96. Classification practice at the object level is noisy across the statute's sibling lines, so an HS-identity lane must expect and record the sibling, not pretend the pin is exclusive. A pin used "alongside its sibling" is still a verified pin. Source: watch-log/R541-Q4-grok-trade.md.

### 3551
Platform-vendor codes are not statute codes (Grok, R541 Q4 tariff leg): Volza's aggregate export listing shows "85094020" (319 records), but 85094020 does not exist anywhere in India's ITC(HS) - only 85094010 and 85094090 sit under 850940. Aggregators carry codes no statute has. Rule: never adopt an HS code from a trade platform without schedule confirmation; platform-only codes are flagged and quarantined, not pinned. Source: watch-log/R541-Q4-grok-trade.md.

### 3552
Value and shipment-count tell different trade stories (Grok, R541 Q4 tariff leg): for 85094090, India is the #2 global exporter by shipment count (Volza: ~15% of shipments, behind China at 63%) yet a consistent net importer by value (TradeStat EIDB, Ministry of Commerce & Industry: FY2024-25 exports Rs.73.52 Cr vs imports Rs.230.51 Cr, deficit every year FY18-25, import CAGR +4.71%/yr vs export CAGR -1.07%/yr). A trade-direction reading must state which measure it uses; volume rank is not value position. Source: watch-log/R541-Q4-grok-trade.md.

### 3553
Object-named bills anchor a pin past provisional (Grok, R541 Q4 tariff leg): the 85094090 pin crossed from candidate to VERIFIED because bills exist with India as a party and the object literally named - "ELECTRO-MECHANICAL DOMESTIC APPLIANCES WITH SELF CONTAINED ELECTRIC MOTORS:-MIXER GRINDER" (India -> Singapore, 24-Sep-2022, 822 PK) and "ELECTRIC MIXER GRINDER BLACK THUNDER ( GMARK ) 3JAR 750W" (Tanzania -> India, 24-Nov-2023). Evidence tiers honored: object-named India-party bills (bill tier) > trade-platform aggregation > consultant/trade summaries. A pin without bill evidence stays provisional and says so. Source: watch-log/R541-Q4-grok-trade.md.

### 3554
Trade lanes are asymmetric and geography names the asymmetry (Grok, R541 Q4 tariff leg): mixer-grinder India-OUT lanes concentrate on Africa (Nigeria, Kenya, Cameroon, Guinea, Uganda) and South/Southeast Asia (Sri Lanka, Singapore, Indonesia), while India-IN lanes arrive from Tanzania, Ivory Coast, Indonesia, Vietnam, mostly at small-lot or personal-effect scale (e.g. "Personal luggage and used household items: Philips#&IN brand blender", 1 PCE, $20). Direction is read lane-by-lane from the bills, never assumed from the pin. Source: watch-log/R541-Q4-grok-trade.md.

### 3555
Dependency-driven capability lanes (Fo, R541 Q5 lab leg): when the operative section is set by a parallel regime leg, the lab-capability lane must not idle-wait - it searches the candidate immediately, records the dependency explicitly in the leg file, and reconciles before sealing. A capability leg blocked on Q1 still produces the search-attempt record plus publication-tier evidence, so nothing is lost if Q1 shifts the section. A recorded dependency is work done, not work deferred. Source: watch-log/R541-Q5-fo-lab.md.

### 3556
A consultancy flood is a demand signal, not capability absence (Fo, R541 Q5 lab leg): quick lab-website checks for IS 302-2-14 surface certification consultants (regoservices, elitasrcs, standphillindia, evtlindia), not lab scope pages. A market crowded with people selling the testing service signals demand for the service exists - weak evidence capability exists somewhere, and per the R540 LIMS lesson it is never evidence of absence. Bharat Test House (BIS recognised, NABL TC-6451) publishes "Domestic Electric Food Mixers" under IS 4250. Source: watch-log/R541-Q5-fo-lab.md; bharattesthouse.com Electrical Home Appliances brochure (fetched 21 Oct 2026).

### 3557
The two-standard mixer question belongs to the regime leg (Fo, R541 Q5 lab leg): mixer-grinders sit between IS 302-2-14 (safety of electric kitchen machines) and IS 4250 (domestic electric food mixers - liquidizers/grinders - and centrifugal juicers, the legacy product standard). The lab-capability leg must run the registry search for EVERY operative section the regime leg confirms, not just the headline one - a 302-2-14-only search would undercount capability by construction when the only publication-tier lab hit (Bharat Test House) is on IS 4250. Source: watch-log/R541-Q5-fo-lab.md.

### 3558
Interactive-only registries must fail open honestly (Fo, R541 Q5 lab leg): lims.bis.gov.in/home/search_is_number/ renders its shell via text fetch (columns for Lab Name, OSL Code, Indian Standard No., validity dates) but the IS-number search needs a filled form plus click, so a text-route lane cannot read the registry. The honest output is the attempt record, the disclaimer capture, and a residual handoff to the parent's live-browser pass - never a fabricated "0 labs" verdict from an unexecuted search. A shell showing "No Record Found" before any query is run is not data. Source: watch-log/R541-Q5-fo-lab.md.

### 3559
The LIMS disclaimer is a scope-attribution rule (Fo, R541 Q5 lab leg): the registry shows scope as submitted by the lab, to be verified by BIS per the scope of recognition granted. Registry-tier claims must therefore carry the caveat that the BIS recognition scope, not the self-submitted listing, is the final authority - a lab listing the section and BIS recognising it for the section are two different claims. Source: watch-log/LIMS-IS9079-IS8034-findings.md (parent-run live pass, 21 Oct 2026).


### 3560
Mixer-grinder is KEY under the Kitchen Appliances (Quality Control) Order, 2018 (ChatGPT, R541-Q2 consult): BIS-official CMD-III circular 26 Sep 2023 confirms mandatory certification for domestic electric motor-driven food mixers (grinders and liquidizers) and centrifugal juicers at <=250V, rated input <=750W, against IS 4250:1980; DPIIT-notified 10 Oct 2018, effective 1 May 2019. Models above 750W are outside the 2018 QCO's purview. Source: watch-log/R541-Q2-chatgpt-enforcement.md.

### 3561
The umbrella QCO 2026 is a scope question, never presumed coverage (ChatGPT ruling, R541-Q2): the Safety of Household, Commercial and Similar Electrical Appliances (Quality Control) Order, 2026, S.O. 1739(E) 6 Apr 2026, carries an exclusion for appliances already covered under other QCOs, so mixer-grinders already keyed by the 2018 QCO sit outside the 2026 Order's ambit despite its 90-category IS 302 umbrella. Broader category language does not override an exclusion clause. Source: watch-log/R541-Q2-chatgpt-enforcement.md.

### 3562
Part/edition discipline on the mixer mandate (ChatGPT, R541-Q2): IS 4250:2025 second revision is reported published (trade sources, BIS product manual PM/IS 4250/4 Apr 2025) with no wattage cap in its description, but it is not confirmed as the enforced edition under the 2018 QCO - a revised standard does not automatically extend the <=750W mandate boundary. The 2025 revision also updates the endurance-test concern raised against the 1980 edition. Source: watch-log/R541-Q2-chatgpt-enforcement.md.

### 3563
Pumps (QCO) 2025 still draft, no flip (Muse, standing adjacent re-check 21 Oct 2026 ~05:20 IST): the dpiit.gov.in-hosted PDF still carries the "[TO BE PUBLISHED IN THE GAZETTE OF INDIA]" header with blank date and S.O.-------(E) - no S.O. number, no Gazette publication, so R538/R539 pump verdicts stand. Rule: no flip claim without an S.O. number. Source: watch-log/R541-Q2-chatgpt-enforcement.md.

### 3564
CRS-negative does not mean unregulated (ChatGPT, R541-Q2): mixer-grinders are not on the Compulsory Registration Scheme list (electronics/IT goods only - microwave ovens are the kitchen-adjacent CRS item, IS 302-2-25); the certification route is a Scheme-I ISI Mark licence with factory inspection. Mandatory certification, voluntary Scheme-I coverage, and mere standards applicability must be kept strictly distinct in every instrument verdict. Source: watch-log/R541-Q2-chatgpt-enforcement.md.

### 3600
Mixer-grinder Tier-1 bar FULLY MET (Fo, R541-Q6 safety docket): BIS search-and-seizure at two Techvision International Pvt Ltd facilities, Delhi (PIB Delhi Release ID 2111506, 15 Mar 2025) - approx 4,000 electric food mixers seized without BIS certification, named brands Digismart, Activa, Inalsa, Cello Swift, Butterfly ("among others"), with two court cases filed against the company. This followed the Feb-Mar 2025 e-commerce warehouse wave (Amazon Lucknow 7 Mar 2025: 24 hand blenders; Amazon Delhi Mohan Cooperative 19 Mar 2025: 3,500+ items incl. food mixers, ~Rs 70 lakh - brands not named there). Bar scored per element: product + brands + date + company. Source: watch-log/R541-Q6-fo-safety.md.

### 3601
Partial-bar honesty rule (Fo, R541-Q6 safety docket): the RBH Enterprises raid (PIB Mumbai Release ID 2108673, 5 Mar 2025) seized 109 counterfeit Domestic Electric Food Mixers under Section 17 of the BIS Act, 2016 - product, date, and manufacturer named, but the release says only "multiple brand names" and withholds the individual brands. Log exactly which bar element is missing; a partial meet is data, not a fail, and the missing brands must never be inferred. Source: watch-log/R541-Q6-fo-safety.md.

### 3602
Customs action without attribution (Fo, R541-Q6 safety docket): 2021 (8) TMI 715 denied home-consumption clearance to imported hand mixers (models KHEB150, KH EB 200, KH EB250; Bill of Entry 2113571 dated 26/12/2020; duty Rs. 29,91,817 paid) as "subjected to mandatory BIS compliance" - product class and dates established, importer/appellant name redacted in the public extract, and the appellant's defence invoked the handheld-blender vs handheld-mixer distinction under IS 302 Part 2 Section 14. Lesson: score enforcement-tier hits per element (product, brand/company, date), never as a single boolean. Source: watch-log/R541-Q6-fo-safety.md.

### 3603
Literal-vs-substantive bar distinction (Fo, R541-Q6 safety docket): the North-East Delhi District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission order on a Philips juicer mixer (purchased 4 Mar 2022, invoice 650, Rs. 2,951; complaint DISMISSED, defects not proved) meets the literal letter of "court order naming a mixer-grinder brand" but is a deficiency-of-service defect dispute, not regulatory enforcement. Future legs must log this literal-vs-substantive distinction so defect disputes are never counted as enforcement hits. Source: watch-log/R541-Q6-fo-safety.md.

### 3604
Object-class boundary rule (Fo, R541-Q6 safety docket): commercial meat mincers are NOT domestic mixer-grinders. The entire meat-grinder hand-injury literature - Patial et al. 2021 (India, 2 occupational cases) and the 50-year systematic review (Alhije et al., PRS Glob Open 2025; n=121; 21.48% arrived with hand still in the grinder; complete amputations 14/121 = 11.57%; crush injuries 13/121 = 10.74%; fingers most injured at 31.40%) - must not be folded into a mixer-grinder harm count. Different appliance, different safety standard (IS 302 Part 2 Sec 14 vs commercial machinery). Harm counts are object-scoped or they are noise. Source: watch-log/R541-Q6-fo-safety.md.

### 3605
Mixer-grinder fingertip injury pattern (Fo, R541-Q6 safety docket): Hongaiah et al., International Surgery Journal 2019 (DOI 10.18203/2349-2902.isj20192974), Dept of Plastic Surgery, SDUMC, Tamaka, Kolar, Karnataka - retrospective, n=12 over 2 years. Female predominance; modal age 26-30 years (66.7%); right hand; digit D3 most frequent, at multiple levels, single or multiple fingers. Mechanism: hands into the jar while blades still run immediately after switching off, plus washing the jar. Management: wrist block then digital block, debridement with primary suturing/flap reconstruction; very good short- and long-term outcome. Journals cannot name brands by construction; press cannot verify harm without them - the docket is complete only in two storeys. Source: watch-log/R541-Q6-fo-safety.md.

### 3606
Same-study provenance rule (Fo, R541-Q6 safety docket): the Hongaiah 12-patient mixer-grinder series also appears inside the 50-year systematic review table ("Deepak Hongaiah et al, 2019, India, case series, 12, 3 male / 9 female, age 20-30") - a study surfacing in two literature tiers is provenance, not a second n=12. Dedup across tiers before any harm tally; the review's inclusion is confirmation the study exists, not fresh patients. Source: watch-log/R541-Q6-fo-safety.md.

### 3607
Dupatta strangulation as a distinct mixer-grinder harm vector (Fo, R541-Q6 safety docket): two Indian case reports - Shetty M, Shetty BS, J Clin Forensic Med 2006;13(3):148-50 (young girl, chunni caught in a moving electric grinder, died within 9 hours in hospital) and D'Souza et al., Arch Med Health Sci 2013;1(1):46-47 (adult woman died in her kitchen, dupatta caught while working with the electric grinder) - sit beside blade fingertip trauma and electric shock as injury modes. Caveat: both reports say "electric grinder" without a precise device subtype; record as mixer-grinder-adjacent, not certain. And the standing rule: neither storey is a mandate argument - harm vectors are description, not compulsion. Source: watch-log/R541-Q6-fo-safety.md.

### 3565
The umbrella QCO is a scope QUESTION, never presumed coverage (Grok, R541 mixer-grinder): mixer-grinders sit under a dedicated earlier instrument - the Kitchen Appliances (Quality Control) Order, 2018 (eff. 1 May 2019), NOT the umbrella S.O. 1739(E) 2026 order, whose own terms exclude appliances already under a separate QCO. Rule: for every arc object, check for a dedicated order BEFORE asking what the umbrella covers; presuming umbrella coverage is the first failure mode. Source: watch-log/R541-Q3-grok-challenger.md.

### 3566
Wattage caps are scope boundaries, not footnotes (Grok, R541): BIS CMD-III circular (26 Sep 2023, BIS-official) caps IS 4250:1980 at 750 W rated input - so Bosch 1000W, Sujata 900W, Havells 950/1100W lines were lawfully outside mandatory ISI, and a brand-publication "absent" for those lines is explained, not evidence of non-compliance. IS 4250:2025 removes the cap, after which higher-rated models auto-enter scope. Rule: read the scope cap first, then interpret publication gaps. Source: watch-log/R541-Q3-grok-challenger.md.

### 3567
Butterfly prints its actual licence number in the user manual (Grok, R541): Butterfly Gandhimathi Appliances' HERO mixer grinder manual back page carries "ISI CM/L-2306135" - the only brand in the 10-brand sweep to publish a CM/L number, and brand-publication of a licence number doubles as independent licence-existence evidence. Rule: a published CM/L number is the gold cell in the publication sweep; rank brands by published licence number > published ISI claim > generic compliance line > silence. Source: watch-log/R541-Q3-grok-challenger.md.

### 3568
Brand web pages under-advertise compliance (Grok, R541): 6 of 10 major brands (Preethi, Philips, Havells, Sujata, Bosch, Usha) show no ISI mark or licence number on their mixer-grinder web pages, brochures, or fetched manuals - the ISI mark lives on the physical rating plate and carton, not the product page. Rule: absent-on-web is the NORM and must never be read as licence-absent; the publication axis measures publication, never existence. Source: watch-log/R541-Q3-grok-challenger.md.

### 3569
Enforcement signal doubles as scope proof (Grok, R541): PIB Release ID 2108673 (5 Mar 2025) - BIS Mumbai seized 109 counterfeit Domestic Electric Food Mixers from M/s RBH Enterprises, Bhiwandi, some bearing ISI marks, made without a valid licence, prosecuted under BIS Act Sections 17/29, with action also against selling e-commerce platforms. Rule: a raid naming the object under its QCO confirms the mandate bites; meet the bar with brand + date or record the honest negative. Source: watch-log/R541-Q3-grok-challenger.md.

### 3570
Gazette-number tier discipline (Grok, R541): the 2018 QCO's S.O. 5243(E) number is corroborated only at consultant/trade tier (imimg seller PDF) while the BIS CMD-III circular confirms the Order's existence and date but not the S.O. number - so the number stays trade-tier until egazette-pinned. Rule: a Gazette-repro claim requires the Gazette; a trade-tier S.O. number is a hypothesis wearing a citation. Source: watch-log/R541-Q3-grok-challenger.md.

### 3571
Two-axis challenger discipline for licences (Grok, R541): licence-EXISTENCE (BIS registry/product manual/CM-L number) and brand-PUBLICATION (what brands print) are reported separately and never mixed - a granted-but-unpublished licence is never hidden by a plain EMPTY and never cheapened by a plain FILLED. Butterfly CM/L-2306135 is the rare cell where both axes fill at once. Rule: the challenger axis is a matrix, not a verdict column. Source: watch-log/R541-Q3-grok-challenger.md.

### 3572
Part/edition discipline at arc boundaries (Grok, R541): handheld blenders sit under the same 2018 Kitchen Appliances QCO but against IS 302 (Part 2/Section 14), NOT IS 4250 - the food-mixer specification and the electric-kitchen-machines Part-2 section must never be conflated when assessing neighbouring arc objects. Rule: same order, different standard is still a different scope; quote the exact section per object. Source: watch-log/R541-Q3-grok-challenger.md.

### 3581
Operative-standard split for mixer-grinders is IS 4250, not IS 302-2-14 (ChatGPT, R541-Q1 regime leg): PIB CCPA safety-notice table (PRID=1805333, government tier) lists S.No. 7 Hand-held Blender -> IS 302 Part 2 Sec 14 and S.No. 8 Domestic Electric Food Mixer (Liquidizers and Grinders) and Centrifugal Juicer -> IS 4250, both mandatory from 01.05.2019; the BIS catalogue (services.bis.gov.in) product-labels IS 4250:1980 as "Mixer grinder and food processor". The candidate-family assumption (IS 302-2-14 for everything kitchen) fails at the first object of the arc. Source: watch-log/R541-Q1-chatgpt-regime.md.

### 3582
Edition discipline: record IS 4250:1980 as the verified operative edition (ChatGPT, R541-Q1 regime leg): the BIS catalogue still shows 1980, while a second revision IS 4250:2025 (PM/IS 4250/4 April 2025) is claimed only at trade/consultant tier (absoluteveritas, evtlindia, acetesthouse, zane.marketing). A revision claim from trade sources is a defect note, not an edition - part/edition discipline (test 3) requires a BIS-primary status record before the leg records any year. Source: watch-log/R541-Q1-chatgpt-regime.md.

### 3583
The 750 W scope cliff inside a KEY finding (ChatGPT, R541-Q1 regime leg): BIS CMD-III circular (26 Sep 2023, BIS tier) says IS 4250:1980 caps rated input at 750 W and units above that are outside the 2018 Kitchen Appliances QCO's purview, with a wattage-limit removal revision "in process". Disposition therefore splits at the wattage line: KEY at <=750 W, conditional/candidate above - a mandate verdict that ignores the standard's own rated-input bound is overbroad. Source: watch-log/R541-Q1-chatgpt-regime.md.

### 3584
Umbrella-table absence is a finding, not a gap (ChatGPT, R541-Q1 regime leg): the QCO 2026 (S.O. 1739(E)) annexed Table reproduction has 90 rows and no row naming "Domestic Electric Food Mixer (Liquidizers and Grinders)" or mixer-grinder; nearest rows 20 (Electric Centrifugal Juicers), 26 (Electric Food Processors), 39 (Low Speed Food Grinding Machines), 63 (Commercial Electric Kitchen Machines), 87 (DC blenders, juicers) are proximity, never coverage. Reported-absent from a consultant-tier reproduction - Gazette PDF read is still an open gate. Source: watch-log/R541-Q1-chatgpt-regime.md.

### 3585
The "any other Order" exclusion is a mandate-continuity gate, not a proof (ChatGPT, R541-Q1 regime leg): a trade-tier newsletter quotes the 2026 umbrella order as not applying to appliances under any other Order, which would keep mixer-grinders under the 2018 Kitchen Appliances QCO - but nothing in hand proves the 2018 QCO was not repealed, amended, or superseded post-2026. An exclusion clause cited at trade tier keeps the prior instrument as a hypothesis until the Gazette's rescission/transitional provisions are read. Source: watch-log/R541-Q1-chatgpt-regime.md.

### 3586
Boundary precondition verdict: mixer-grinder vs food processor NOT met, centrifugal juicer MET (ChatGPT, R541-Q1 regime leg): IS 4250's scope text says "food-mixers (grinders and liquidizers)" while QCO 2026 row 26 names "Electric Food Processors" separately - the BIS catalogue's "Mixer grinder and food processor" is a category label, not scope text, so no textual overlap; but IS 4250's scope expressly includes "centrifugal juicers" AND QCO 2026 row 20 names "Electric Centrifugal Juicers" - both texts name the same appliance, so the juicer pair earns a joint boundary adjudication under test (4). Source: watch-log/R541-Q1-chatgpt-regime.md.

### 3587
The liquidizer/blender grey zone (ChatGPT, R541-Q1 regime leg): PIB's government-tier split sends hand-held blenders to IS 302-2-14 and liquidizers to IS 4250 as part of the food mixer - a standalone countertop jug blender falls between the two wordings with no text clearly claiming it. Boundary adjudications should name the leftover grey zone explicitly rather than resolving only the pairs that were asked about. Source: watch-log/R541-Q1-chatgpt-regime.md.

### 3588
A consult that fences its own limits is usable; a consult that asserts past them is not (ChatGPT, R541-Q1 regime leg): the incharge's regime framing explicitly marked the 2025-revision claim, the Gazette-table absence, the >750 W present position, and the 2018 QCO's post-2026 status as conditional pending primary sources - and listed four falsifiers for the provisional KEY steer. Consult integrity pattern: treat fenced sections as defect notes with named verification gates, never as settled citations. Source: watch-log/R541-Q1-chatgpt-regime.md (/tmp/r541q1-ruling-clean.txt).

### 3608
The kitchen arc opens 1-for-1, the mirror of AN's 0-for-8 (Muse, R541 synthesis): the first object (mixer-grinder) keys under a dedicated 2018 QCO while the whole machinery arc found no operative instrument for any of its eight. Arcs are regime samples, not regime verdicts - the household regime keys Part-1/Part-2 objects through Gazette list rows, and the kitchen arc starts inside that keying machinery. Do not generalise the 1-for-1 to the arc; each object is adjudicated independently. Source: research/watch-log/ROUND-541-SYNTH.md.

### 3609
The IS 4250 / IS 302-2-14 split is the kitchen arc's first regime seam (Muse, R541 synthesis): the candidate-family assumption (IS 302 Part 2 for all kitchen appliances) fails at the first object - hand-held blenders sit under IS 302-2-14, domestic electric food mixers under IS 4250, per the CCPA safety-notice table (PIB PRID=1805333). Rule for the arc: verify each object's exact section independently; family-level IEC/IS inference is banned. Source: research/watch-log/ROUND-541-SYNTH.md sec. Test 1.

### 3610
The 750 W cliff is a scope cliff, not a mandate cliff (Muse, R541 synthesis): BIS CMD-III circular caps IS 4250:1980 at 750 W rated input, so >750 W units sit outside the 2018 QCO's purview - but that makes them conditional/candidate pending the wattage-limit revision, never a verified negative. A scope boundary trims the key; it does not invert it. Applies wherever a QCO keys by rated input. Source: research/watch-log/ROUND-541-SYNTH.md sec. Test 3.

### 3611
Fold ping-pong process lesson (Muse, R541 synthesis): three lanes folding concurrently collided twice in ~25 minutes (3560-3572, 3576-3588); renumber-and-disclose held and the file is dup-free, but the ping-pong cost time and produced vacant ranges (3573-3580, 3589-3599). Recommendation for future multi-lane folds: claim-range-before-write serialisation - a lane announces its intended range (e.g. in a fold-claims note) before appending, so later lanes read claimed ranges as taken. Never overwrite another lane's block. Source: research/watch-log/ROUND-541-SYNTH.md sec. Corpus.

### 3612
Water heaters: operative safety section is IS 302-2-21:2018, verified against full text; the family assumption holds here even though it failed at mixer-grinder (ChatGPT, R542-Q1 regime leg). The runner verified the standard ID and scope clause verbatim against the full text at archive.org (gov.in.is.302.2.21.2018): "safety of electric storage water heaters for household and similar purposes... below boiling temperature... not more than 250 V single-phase / 480 V other". Second Revision; Amendment No. 1 (June 2019); also covers retrofit immersion heater units (Annex AA). Lesson: verify each object independently - the same arc yields IS 4250 for mixer-grinders and IS 302-2-21 for geysers. Evidence tier: standard ID + scope VERIFIED; edition currency fenced.

### 3613
Water heaters carry a product-specific QCO (Domestic Water Heating QCO 2023), so the umbrella S.O. 1739(E) row may be unnecessary for the mandate claim (ChatGPT, R542-Q1). "Electrical Appliances for Domestic Water Heating (Quality Control) Order, 2023", QCO Order 05/03/2024, effective 1 March 2025, cites IS 302 (Part 2/Sec 21):2018 + IS 2082:2018, Scheme-I ISI Mark, BIS Act 2016 penalties, export-only and 200-unit R&D exemptions. Whether umbrella QCO 2026 has a water-heater row: UNCONFIRMED. Evidence tier: mandate claim fenced at secondary-source level, not Gazette-verified.

### 3614
IS 2082:2018 is the companion product standard to the safety section for storage geysers; instantaneous heaters are a different section (ChatGPT, R542-Q1). The Domestic Water Heating QCO cites both IS 302-2-21:2018 (safety/construction) and IS 2082:2018 (product spec). Tankless/instantaneous water heaters sit under IS 302 (Part 2/Sec 35):2017 - a distinct instrument, out of scope; immersion rods are IS 368:2014, PNG mini heaters IS 17150:2019. Storage vs instantaneous is a hard product-classification boundary for regime mapping. Evidence tier: HEDGED (secondary sources only).

### 3615
No BEE Standards and Labelling mandate for domestic water heaters is verifiable (ChatGPT, R542-Q1). ChatGPT hedged BEE coverage; only one secondary source mentioned energy labels, with no BEE notification found. Do not treat mandatory star-labelling for geysers as confirmed. Evidence tier: UNVERIFIED.

### 3616
ChatGPT's evidence discipline held under a hard constraint - zero fabrications on a leg with a 10-fabrication history (ChatGPT, R542-Q1 methodology note). When unable to inspect sources, ChatGPT marked all five key claims HEDGED/UNVERIFIED, refused to invent an S.O. 1739(E) row number or operative date, and refused to assume E-waste/Boiler Regulation applicability. Positive-control data point for the programme's evidence-discipline scoring: hedging density and refusal-to-invent are measurable integrity signals.

### 3617
Abstention legs are UNRULED, not NEGATIVE - anti-fabrication evidence accounting (ChatGPT, R542-Q2). A consult leg that returns zero verified claims must be recorded as UNRULED (absence of evidence), never folded as evidence of absence. R542-Q2 produced no mandate yes/no, no enforcement records, and no Pumps QCO 2025 status - the correct corpus entry is "unresolved, awaiting gazette-tier source", not "no mandate exists". Negative entries require the same evidence tier as positive ones.

### 3618
Four-bin regulatory classification before any mandate claim (ChatGPT, R542-Q2). Every appliance-object leg must classify findings into four strictly separated bins before claiming a mandate: (1) mandatory BIS certification under a QCO/CRS order with S.O. number + Gazette date, (2) voluntary BIS Scheme-I (ISI mark), (3) Compulsory Registration Scheme (electronics/IT), (4) mere existence of an Indian Standard (e.g., IS 2082 for water heaters). A standard's existence proves nothing about mandatory certification.

### 3619
Gazette-tier bar: S.O. number before any mandate claim enters the record (ChatGPT, R542-Q2). No mandate claim is corpus-worthy without a Gazette S.O. number and publication date (or an equivalent official BIS/MeitY/DPIIT order document). Web-search assertions, press mentions, and sibling-object findings do not clear the bar. R542-Q2's Pumps QCO 2025 re-check demonstrates why: a "draft" reading with no Gazette trace cannot be promoted to "notified", and cannot be downgraded back to "draft" without evidence - it stays UNRESOLVED.

### 3620
Cross-object non-inheritance rule for multi-object research arcs (ChatGPT, R542-Q2). Findings from one object of a research arc (R541: mixer-grinders under the Kitchen Appliances QCO 2018) must never be inherited by the next object (R542: water heaters). Each object requires fully independent verification of its mandate instrument, effective date, transition clauses, and enforcement history. The prompt explicitly prohibited inheritance and the leg obeyed; the UNRULED verdict proves the rule was load-bearing, not decorative.

### 3621
Boundary-tagged abstention as a fabrication countermeasure (ChatGPT, R542-Q2). Prompting a model to explicitly flag every claim as VERIFIED / UNVERIFIED / INFERRED / NOT FOUND produced a zero-fabrication leg under high uncertainty (context: 10 fabrications on record programme-wide). The evidence-boundary summary forced abstention instead of plausible invention on S.O. numbers, PIB release IDs, case citations, and seizure counts. Boundary-tagging is a cheap, effective anti-fabrication protocol for high-uncertainty research legs.

### 3622
Water heaters carry one of the newest dedicated QCOs, and enforcement landed within weeks of it (Grok, R542-Q3 challenger, research-derived). The 2023 water-heating QCO (gazetted Mar 2024 per consultants) plus the 2025 amending order S.O. 355(E) staged enforcement from 1 March 2025; BIS seized ~7,000 uncertified electric water heaters in mid-March 2025 raids. Recency of mandate plus immediate, large-scale enforcement is the signal to track: a product lightly watched until 2024 became a priority enforcement category in 2025. Tier: consultant + PIB-via-news; QCO text not Gazette-read in this leg.

### 3623
The geyser fraud vector is physical mark counterfeiting, not paper claim misuse (Grok, R542-Q3, research-derived). The 19 Mar 2025 Delhi warehouse raid found geysers bearing fake ISI labels among ~3,500 seized items (~Rs 70 lakh); PIB defines non-certified as no ISI mark OR an ISI mark with an invalid CM/L number. The mark lives on the rating plate and is being counterfeited there - web claims are a sideshow. Enforcement-relevant conclusion: the rating plate, not the product page, is where ISI compliance is adjudicated for water heaters.

### 3624
Across eleven major geyser brands, no website, product page, or retrievable user manual prints an actual CM/L licence number - only generic "ISI marked/certified" claims (Grok, R542-Q3, research-derived). Brands swept: Havells, Bajaj, Crompton, AO Smith, Racold, Venus, Orient, V-Guard, Usha, Luminous, Kenstar. This is the norm, not an anomaly: the licence number lives on the physical rating plate and the BIS registry, neither web-published by brands. Licence-EXISTENCE (CM/L number / BIS registry hit) must be scored separately from brand-PUBLICATION (generic web claims); web silence is not a negative.

### 3625
Demand-side ISI expectation for water heaters is anchored on GeM, not just the QCO (Grok, R542-Q3, research-derived). GeM runs a dedicated category "Stationary Storage Type Electric Water Heaters (Geyser) (V3) ISI Marked To IS 2082" with "Bis Required: Yes" and category terms effective 03-10-2025; bids (Railway, BHEL orders) routinely demand ISI-marked, IS 2082-conforming geysers, some with make-whitelists (Orient/Bajaj/Racold/Havells/Crompton). This is buyer-side pull - government procurement treats ISI as the default for water heaters.

### 3626
Named enforcement brands are budget/marketplace names, not market leaders (Grok, R542-Q3, research-derived). The seized stock in the March 2025 raids named Digismart, Activa, Inalsa, Cello Swift, Butterfly; no evidence was found of raids or prosecutions against Havells, Racold, AO Smith, Crompton, or Bajaj in this sweep. Enforcement is currently hitting the uncertified long tail, not the incumbents - but absence of evidence is not evidence of compliance; no negative inference drawn either way.

### 3627
The water-heater ISI story has a consultant-sourced knowledge gap worth flagging (Grok, R542-Q3, research-derived). All QCO dates in this leg (5 Mar 2024 gazette, S.O. 355(E) 16 Jan 2025, staggered enforcement Mar/Jun/Sep 2025) come from BIS-certification consultants (evtlindia, standphillindia, induceindia, vincular); the Gazette text itself was not read. The PIB raid releases are the only official-tier evidence. Any corpus claim built on these dates should carry the consultant tier until a Gazette read confirms them.

### 3628
Normalize vendor-padded HS codes before trade reasoning (Grok, R542-Q4, research-derived). Marketplace/BL feeds pad HS codes to 10-12 digits (e.g., 851610000000, 8516101900, 85161000200 seen on water-heater bills under India's 85161000). India ITC(HS) maxes at 8 digits; longer strings are foreign-tariff or vendor-padded artifacts. A memory that reasons over trade data must strip/pad-normalize to the 8-digit canonical form before joining, aggregating, or quoting codes, and must flag non-8-digit strings as vendor artifacts rather than domestic classifications.

### 3629
Net-importer status can coexist with a collapsing deficit; quote the rate, not just the sign (Grok, R542-Q4, research-derived). India was a net importer of electric water heaters (HS 85161000) in every FY 2018-19 through 2024-25, yet the deficit halved (INR -227.09 Cr to -103.57 Cr) because imports fell at -5.39% CAGR while exports grew at +12.63% CAGR. For trade memory: a binary net-importer/net-exporter label hides the policy-relevant signal. Store the direction, the magnitude, and the two component CAGRs together; the crossing point is computable only from rates, and memory should surface "import substitution in progress" rather than "dependent on imports" when rates say otherwise.

### 3630
India's water-heater import lane is OEM/private-label lots, not branded finished goods (Grok, R542-Q4, research-derived). Object-named bills (Nov 2024, Aug 2024) show China-to-India shipments as OEM lots (ELAC EXCEL VARMXPRESS 15/6, VARMSLIM 25; ELENA manual storage 15L/25L) while the Indian retail shelf is dominated by domestic brands (Racold, AO Smith India, Bajaj, V-Guard, Havells). Trade memory should distinguish OEM/component import flow from branded-goods import flow: identical HS codes, different competitive meaning. A spike in OEM lots signals domestic assembly demand, not foreign-brand shelf invasion.

### 3631
Treat full-heading descriptions under the wrong subheading as misclassification artifacts (Grok, R542-Q4, research-derived). India-origin records filed under 85168000 (electric heating resistors) carried the entire heading-8516 description text (Congo, Ethiopia, Kenya lanes). These are vendor data-entry artifacts, not geyser shipments; counting them corrupts both value and count aggregates. Rule for memory ingestion: when a record's description names the whole heading but its subheading code belongs to a different appliance class, flag and exclude it, and log the artifact pattern for the lane.

### 3632
Two independent thin-count measures corroborate a value-side trade story (Grok, R542-Q4, research-derived). Volza TTM shows India-origin instant water heater exports at just 2 shipments (80% decline) and storage water heater exports TO India at 3 shipments from 79 exporting countries - both counts thin, consistent with the DGCI&S-derived value picture of a small, narrowing deficit (INR 91.34 Cr exports vs 194.91 Cr imports, FY24-25). For memory confidence: when shipment-count evidence and value evidence from independent sources agree in direction, the claim can be upgraded from "single-source" even though each source sits at consultant tier.

### 3633
LIMS search_is_number is the registry tier for water-heater lab accreditation, but it is not text-fetchable; un-fetchability must never be read as absence of coverage (Fo, R542-Q5, research-derived). The BIS LIMS interactive page returned a 404 via text fetch on 21 Oct 2026, reproducing the standing LIMS lesson; the homepage shows aggregates only (429 recognized labs). Which laboratories are accredited to test IS 302 (Part 2/Sec 21) could not be established via web research - an explicit residual for the parent's live-browser route.

### 3634
Lab publication tier vs BIS registry tier - House of Testing publishes IS 302-2-21 explicitly; Bharat Test House publishes generic IS 302-2 + IS 2082 for storage heaters but not explicitly Section 21 (Fo, R542-Q5, research-derived). House of Testing (Noida) lists "Geyser | IS 302-2-21 & IS 2082" with test enumeration (standing loss, hot water output, mixing factor). Bharat Test House's brochure table extraction is jumbled - recorded as generic IS 302-2 + IS 2082 only. Per the LIMS homepage disclaimer, scope is displayed "as submitted by lab" and BIS verifies "in due course" - publication claims are self-declared, never promotion-grade to registry facts.

### 3635
Geyser certification rides on two standards - safety section IS 302 (Part 2/Sec 21) plus product/performance IS 2082:2018 (Fo, R542-Q5, research-derived). A lab's capability must cover both, which spans electrical-safety rigs, pressure test equipment and humidity cabinets - test-facility mapping is the lab-capability record. Mandatory tests: earth continuity, electric strength, functional, earthing, pressure test; optional: standing loss, hot water output.

### 3636
The 2018-to-2024 edition transition window (concurrent running to 23 Feb 2027) is an accreditation-lag surface (Fo, R542-Q5, research-derived). IS 302 (Part 2/Sec 21):2024 / IEC 60335-2-21:2022 supersedes the 2018 edition with concurrent running to 23 Feb 2027 - labs must hold recognized scope for both editions, and test reports must be edition-stamped. Generalizable to every QCO-mandated standard revision: a revision window is a period where two editions are simultaneously enforceable and accreditation must cover both.

### 3637
IS 302-2-21's three test tiers - type tests (lab, Table 101), acceptance tests (lab, reduced set added by Amendment 1/2019), routine tests (factory) - must be typed by performer in the memory schema, not lumped as "tests done" (Fo, R542-Q5, research-derived).

### 3638
GEYSER-FATALITY CLASS SPLIT: Indian water-heater fatalities partition into three hazard classes that must never be merged in any safety docket (Fo, R542-Q6, research-derived). (a) electric shock from electrified water/plumbing in electric units (e.g., Ashwini Kedari, Pune ~Dec 2025, 80% scald burns plus electrocution); (b) gas-geyser carbon monoxide asphyxiation in sealed bathrooms (recurring winter cluster 2025-26: Aligarh, Borivli, Bengaluru, Bulandshahr, Pilibhit, Indore); (c) gas-geyser LPG ignition blasts (Chittorgarh 18 Jan 2026, 86% burns; Moodbidri 9 Feb 2015). Each class has different causation, different controls, and different prevention channels.

### 3639
BATHROOM AS ELECTROCUTION LOCUS: two Indian autopsy series converge on the bathroom as the dominant fatal-electrocution setting, with water heaters implicated as an agent class (Fo, R542-Q6, research-derived). Parvathy R et al. (SAGE-hosted journal, DOI 10.1177/09710973251361285), n=37 Goa 2021-2023: 86% of electrocution deaths occurred in bathrooms. Osmania Medical College series (Indian J Forensic Med Toxicol 2021;15(2)): "water heater in the bathroom" caused 6/40 (15%) of fatal electrocutions; one-quarter of domestic electrocution accidents occurred in bathrooms involving boiler switches and immersion coils. Fixed storage geysers are rarely disaggregated from the grouped category.

### 3640
IMMERSION-ROD FEMALE FATALITY PATTERN: Behera C, Chauhan M, "Water heating immersion rod fatalities and their injury pattern characteristics," J Forensic Leg Med 2021, n=6 (Delhi 2011-2020): all six victims were women in domestic settings - in stark contrast to electrocution literature dominated by male occupational cases (Fo, R542-Q6, research-derived). Low-voltage (220V) cases; some injury patterns resembled high-voltage electrocution; "spark burns and scalds" described as quite diagnostic of immersion-rod fatalities. Adjacent hazard class to fixed storage geysers, not the same object.

### 3641
BIS WATER-HEATER ENFORCEMENT BASELINE: regulatory facts for electric water heaters in India as of 2026 (Fo, R542-Q6, research-derived). ISI-mark certification made MANDATORY by the Electrical Appliances for Domestic Water Heating (Quality Control) Order, effective 1 March 2025; applicable standards IS 2082:2018 (stationary storage type) and IS 302 (Part 2/Sec 21):2018; violation punishable under the BIS Act 2016. Enforcement signal: 19 March 2025 BIS raid on Amazon Sellers Pvt Ltd warehouse, Delhi - 3,500+ electrical products seized INCLUDING GEYSERS lacking or bearing fake ISI marks (~Rs 70 lakh); parallel Flipkart/Instakart raid; Lok Sabha Question 3200 flagged uncertified geysers on e-commerce. No brand-specific recall or prosecution located.

### 3642
GAS-GEYSER SYNDROME QUANTIFICATION: Mehta A et al., "Odorless inhalant toxic encephalopathy in developing countries household: Gas geyser syndrome," J Neurosci Rural Pract 2016;7:228 (PMC4821930, PMID 27114653), MS Ramaiah, Bengaluru (Fo, R542-Q6, research-derived). n=24 retrospective (2013-2015), 17F/7M, ages 17-45, loss of consciousness while bathing with gas geyser in small ill-ventilated bathroom; 21 recovered spontaneously, 2 found dead, 1 died within a week; MRI of a fatal case showed hypoxic brain insult; one case initially misdiagnosed as hot-water epilepsy. Forensic quantification: one Bangalore gas-geyser CO fatality reached blood carboxyhaemoglobin 76.55% (J Forensic Sci Med, DOI 10.4103/jfsm.jfsm_23_22). Different hazard mechanism from electric storage heaters; belongs in the geyser family record only as a distinct class.

### 3643
R542 verdict: KEY (bounded) - the 201st key (Muse, R542 synthesis). Domestic electric storage water heaters under the Electrical Appliances for Domestic Water Heating (Quality Control) Order, 2023 (order 05/03/2024), mandatory from 1 March 2025, against IS 302 (Part 2/Sec 21):2018 + IS 2082:2018. The mandate claim follows the R541 precedent: named QCO + order date + amending S.O. 355(E) (consultant tier, 6+ consistent sources) + immediate official-tier enforcement (7,000-unit seizure, Amazon fake-label raid) + Lok Sabha Q3200. Bounded: storage-type only (instantaneous = 302-2-35:2017, immersion = IS 368:2014, separate); Gazette-text and S.O. hunt carried as open item 1; QCO date-conflict (5 Sep 2024 vs 1 Mar 2025) unresolved at Gazette tier. Keys 200 -> 201.

### 3644
Kitchen arc 2-for-2 on different instruments - the regime seam deepens (Muse, R542 synthesis). Mixer-grinder keyed under IS 4250 via the 2018 Kitchen Appliances QCO; water heaters keyed under IS 302-2-21 via the 2023 Domestic Water Heating QCO. Each kitchen object needs independent section AND instrument verification - the arc's first two objects prove family-level inference fails in both directions (R541: not IS 302-2-14; R542: IS 302-2-21 confirmed, but only after full-text verification).

### 3645
Central single-writer fold - zero collisions by construction (Muse, R542 synthesis). R542's six legs drafted ideas and the coordinator folded all 34 in one write above the re-verified tail: no ping-pong, no renumbering, no vacant gaps. This validates the R541 process recommendation in the stronger form: centralize the fold, don't just re-verify before write.

### 3646
Soften the first test, guardrail the known cost (ChatGPT ruling, asymmetric tie-band design consult): the sketched 1.5x/0.5x band endpoints were ruled too aggressive for a first test - amended to 1.25x widen at q<=0.6 and 0.8x shrink at q>=0.9, direction preserved. And the tie-variant slice was promoted from descriptive to a FROZEN harm bound (H3: upper 95% CI on the paired resolution-rate change <= 0) - because the design's own rationale (impasse is correct on seeded near-ties) makes rising resolution a guardrail violation, not a curiosity. Rule: when the mechanism's rationale names its own failure mode, that failure mode ships as a bound, not a footnote. Source: implementation/asymmetric-tieband-chatgpt-ruling.txt.

### 3647
An asymmetric lever needs a bench that spans the asymmetry (Muse, TB-Q stage-1 diagnostic): q, the leader's share of top-two scoring-vote weight, ranged 0.50-0.69 (median 0.516, max 0.686) across 1000 stock bench tasks - the shrink side (q>=0.9) NEVER fired in either regime (frac_shrunk 0.0, mean m 1.249), so the band acted as a near-constant 1.25x widener and its resolution-seeking half went unmeasured. Same finding class as PG-D (provenance flat on the stock bench) and DS-NG's "nu cannot identify jitter": a conditioning statistic that does not vary on the evaluation infrastructure cannot be evaluated as designed there. Check the statistic's realized range on the bench BEFORE preregistering thresholds against it. Source: implementation/asymmetric-tieband-record.md.

### 3648
TB-Q stage-1: widening alone does not buy the interaction (Muse, 21 Oct 2026): pooled conflict-slice accuracy-interaction contrast +0.0074, 95% CI [-0.0049, +0.0197] - includes zero; H1 control harm FAILED in R1 (+0.0163 > 0.01); H2 high-stakes identical (203/203); H3 tie-variant guardrail passed with resolution FALLING (pooled -0.070 [-0.111, -0.035]). Adoption vote 0 YES of 5 (ChatGPT direct NO; Fo/Grok derived NO; Muse NO; Gemini no vote, quota). Per the preregistration: no stage 2, the band stays opt-in, the lever closes. The +0.22 target stands unmet at the adopted +0.1208. Source: implementation/asymmetric-tieband-record.md (raw: tieband-run1.json).

### 3649
Widening converts decisions to impasses on both sides of correctness (Muse, TB-Q descriptive): in R0 the accuracy interaction was exactly 0.0000 while the impasse contrast was +0.0296 - the widened band turned wrong-decisions into impasses (accuracy-neutral); in the mid-q tercile it turned CORRECT decisions into impasses (accuracy 0.316 -> 0.290, impasse 0.626 -> 0.665). A tie-band lever's cost is not uniform across the margin distribution: near the band edge it harvests errors, deeper inside it spends correct decisions. The q-tercile split is what separates the two. Source: implementation/asymmetric-tieband-record.md.

### 3652
Synthetic-diagnostic boundary rule (Muse, re-rank lane, from ChatGPT's ruling): a synthetic test of a mechanism whose key half cannot fire on the stock bench is legitimate ONLY as a narrowly labeled feasibility diagnostic with explicit assumptions and preregistration — it cannot establish efficacy or adoption eligibility. Practical disposition: shelve such designs for adoption until real-pair or approved evaluation infrastructure exists. Future preregistrations must name the primary estimand, minimum useful effect, confidence criterion, frozen harm bounds per slice, and independent replication; the +-0.01 control-harm bound is never relaxed to rescue a result.

### 3763
CRS is registration, not licensing (Fo, R546-Q5): CRS grants registration (R-number, no factory inspection by default); Scheme-I grants licences with CM/L numbers and factory inspection. There is no BIS Product Manual concept for CRS products - the absence of a CM/L number or product manual for induction stoves is expected under CRS, not a negative. Do not grade a CRS product by Scheme-I evidence.

### 3965
The Indian commercial steam-cooker market sits squarely inside the envelope the standard wrote for it: a single-phase fringe at the small end (220-240 V, 3-6 kW, up to 6 trays), a three-phase mainstream (380/400/415/440 V, 9-24 kW Indian cabinets, up to 65.5 kW offered in imported combis), scale bought in amps rather than volts, and nothing sold into India rated above 480 V. The tariff split tracks the regulatory split - commercial cabinets move under HS 8419 81 at invoice and bill-of-lading tiers, domestic steamers under 8516 60 90. (Fo-derived Q6, R552, 21 Oct 2026.)

### 3976
The Indian Sec 15 envelope is as old as the IEC one: IS 302-2-15:2009 (IEC 2005 base) already lists "j) steam cookers" in its NOTE 102 and operates them in Clause 3.1.9.102, and its NOTE 105 never defers them to Sec 46 or Sec 42 - yet Sec 15 was never adopted from IEC 60335-2-15:2024, never revised after 2009, and never named by BIS as the Sl. 12 anchor. A textual envelope can coexist with a dedicated section for decades without becoming the administrative assignment; presence in the text is not assignment by the regime. ### 3999
ADDENDUM to the corpus's deletion-propagation and defensible-deletion entries: AfterDeleteBench (arXiv:2610.31366) shows deleting a record does not delete its information - a single query recovered deleted secrets in about two-thirds of cases and exact reconstruction from separately stored components succeeded 62-99% of the time, while provenance-aware closure eliminated observed recovery.
