### 4012
Gemini audit (k)/F-10, debt logged: the discarded R6 consultation is externally unverifiable and its re-take had only one witness. Consultations that move rulings require auditable multi-lane witnessing, or they remain debt on the record. (Gemini red-team round-6 audit; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, 25 Oct 2026.)

### 4013
Gemini audit (l), folded as corrected claim: unchanged test files across R6 are plausible for an additive implementation, but they expose missing deep ranking-order and multi-identity assertions. Additivity explains stable tests; it does not excuse the assertion gaps the audit names. (Gemini red-team round-6 audit; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, 25 Oct 2026.)

### 4014
Gemini audit (m)/F-11, folded as CLOSED: the same-owner self-correction bypass and the GU3 corroboration narrowing it named were closed by the Ruling A (Ruling C amendment) build and its 18-check test suite on 25 Oct 2026; the round6f GU3 expectation was re-registered the same day. This entry is the fold of an accepted finding whose fix is already built, tested, and on the record. (Gemini red-team round-6 audit; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, 25 Oct 2026.)

### 4015
Ishiguro, The Remains of the Day (incharge's literature-lane item, daily study round 1, 25 Oct 2026): memory as selective reconstruction shaped by present identity, not a neutral archive — the narrator's confidence can conceal omission, distortion and self-protection. Adopted: a memory must retain provenance, uncertainty and revisable interpretations rather than silently overwriting disputed facts; a confident retelling is not evidence of an undisputed record. (ChatGPT lane item, daily study round 1.)

### 4016
Baddeley & Hitch working-memory model (1974; episodic buffer added 2000): working memory is staged, multi-component and capacity-limited — central executive, phonological loop, visuospatial sketchpad, episodic buffer. Adopted: the memory needs a small staged working set, an episodic-buffer analogue that binds multimodal items into episodes before long-term write, plus an executive analogue that rations attention — the staging layer the decide() path currently lacks. (Daily study round 1, accepted by ChatGPT disposition, 25 Oct 2026.)

### 4017
Wang et al., Quantum Landauer erasure using magnetic tunneling junctions (Nanoscale Advances, 2026): dissipated energy during quasi-adiabatic bit-reset converges to (4.1 ± 2.0) zJ ≈ kT ln 2 — erasure is irreversible state compression with a thermodynamic floor cost. Adopted: Janitor deletions are irreversible state compressions, not row removals, and must be behaviourally audited (cf. the AfterDeleteBench lesson in entry 3999); deletion counts only when derived components are closed too. (Daily study round 1, branch focus: physics; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, 25 Oct 2026.)

### 4018
Mireshghallah, "2026 Is the New 2016, but Make It Privacy" (MIT CSAIL NLP Seminar, 2026; CIMemories, ICLR 2026): frontier models show up to 69% attribute-level violations of contextual integrity when drawing on persistent memory, accumulating unpredictably across tasks and runs. Adopted: recall is not permission to disclose — disclosure needs a context check separate from retrieval (who the recipient is, what the context permits). The Telegram pairing's founder-only allowlist is one instance; the general disclosure rule is still unbuilt. (Daily study round 1, Grok derived scan — Grok route dark, no Grok credit; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, 25 Oct 2026.)

### 4019
Dynamic Talks, "AI Agents Memory: State Of The Art For 2026" (San Ramon, 5 Feb 2026): separate ephemeral short-term context, session-spanning medium-term recall and persistent long-term memory. Adopted: the hard problems are deciding what to forget, preventing memory bloat, and preserving trust when preferences are recalled across sessions — tiering is a design decision, not an implementation detail. (Daily study round 1, video lane; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, 25 Oct 2026.)

### 4020
Nowledge Labs, "Building memory systems for AI agents" (vLLM Beijing Meetup / KCD, 21 Mar 2026): Trace → Unit → Crystal distillation (raw trace, atomic searchable unit, conclusion cross-validated by 3+ sources), bi-temporal time (event time vs record time), and decay-with-an-importance-floor. Adopted: forgetting is engineered, not accidental — distillation stages plus a floor below which important entries never decay. (Daily study round 1, video lane; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, 25 Oct 2026.)

### 4021
Packer (Letta / MemGPT), "Stateful Agents" (AI Engineer workshop, published 19 Apr 2025): core memory stays in context while recall and archival memory sit outside it and are searched by tools, with strict context limits triggering eviction or summarisation. Adopted failure mode: appending every message to a list silently preserves outdated facts — eviction/summarisation must be triggered, not assumed. (Daily study round 1, video lane; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, 25 Oct 2026.)

### 4022
"Agents that remember" (Anthropic Claude Managed Agents workshop, 8 Sep 2026): a persistent, file-system-like memory store attached to sessions, plus an asynchronous "dreaming" pass that fact-checks, deduplicates and consolidates stores so they do not grow unbounded. Adopted: consolidation must be a scheduled, non-blocking job, not work done inside a live reply — the consolidation daemon's design constraint stated plainly. (Daily study round 1, video lane; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, 25 Oct 2026.)

### 4023
MERIT, "When Does Memory Help? A Cost-Aware Evaluation of Long-Term Memory in Tool-Using LLM Agents" (arXiv:2609.05441, submitted 26 Jul 2026): memory must be judged by whether it changes what a tool-using agent does, under explicit token/dollar metering; embedding retrieval collapses unpredictably on updated facts (0.30–0.95) while update-on-write stores stay at 0.70–1.00. Adopted: a memory without a tested update path is not a memory; evaluation reports carry metering, not just accuracy. (Daily study round 1, field scan; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, 25 Oct 2026.)

### 4024
MemoryOS (arXiv:2506.06326, 30 May 2025): a three-tier hierarchy (short-term dialogue pages, mid-term topic segments, long-term persona memory) with dialogue-chain FIFO and heat-based promotion. Adopted: a concrete promotion/eviction policy — entries gain or lose standing by heat (use × recency × importance), rather than sitting at flat priority forever. This is the closest existing answer to the round's retrieval-priority question, and it answers it with a mechanism, not a formula. (Daily study round 1, field scan; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, 25 Oct 2026.)

### 4025
PISA (arXiv:2510.15966, 12 Oct 2025): memory actively constructed for the agent's task, not passively stored — trimodal adaptation (assimilate into an existing schema, evolve a schema, or create a new schema) plus hybrid symbolic + neural retrieval. Adopted: conflicting or novel information is handled by schema adaptation, so new evidence neither corrupts older knowledge nor gets silently dropped. (Daily study round 1, field scan; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, 25 Oct 2026.)

### 4026
MemoryArena (ICML 2026, PMLR 306): memorisation and action must be evaluated together — agents near-saturated on recall benchmarks like LoCoMo perform poorly when later subtasks depend on distilled experience from earlier ones. Adopted: recall-only evaluation hides the real failure mode; our evals must score later-task dependence on earlier distilled experience, not recall alone. (Daily study round 1, field scan; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, 25 Oct 2026.)

### 4027
Memora (GitHub, created 19 Sep 2025): the absorb step classifies each incoming fact as duplicate / update / contradiction / related / new, and supersession lineage keeps old versions reachable instead of deleting them. Adopted: update without lying about history — supersession lineage is the practical pattern the MERIT and MemoryArena findings demand. (Daily study round 1, field scan; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, 25 Oct 2026.)

### 4028
Proust, In Search of Lost Time (incharge's literature-lane item, daily study round 2, 26 Oct 2026): involuntary memory — a sensory cue recovers a past experience with detail deliberate recollection misses. Adopted: an agent memory must support cue-driven retrieval, not only explicit summaries or keyword search; evals should test whether contextual cues recover records that direct queries miss. (ChatGPT lane item, daily study round 2.)

### 4029
Schacter, The Seven Sins of Memory (1999/2001; update, issue date Jan 2022, PMC8285452): seven failure modes — transience, absent-mindedness, blocking, misattribution, suggestibility, bias, persistence — are byproducts of adaptive processes, not fatal flaws. Adopted: evals must score each sin as a separate axis, commission errors (false recall) separately from omission, because adversarial rejection is the binding constraint on recall gains. (Daily study round 2, accepted by ChatGPT disposition, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4030
"Agent memory is a search problem, not a storage problem" (HackerNoon Hindi edition, published 2026-10-21, studied in the original Hindi): raw conversation turns in a single Postgres table plus MCP search tools beat pre-processing pipelines on LoCoMo (F1 0.665 vs 0.613 best reported); a 9-parameter tool schema cost 0.09 F1 against a 1-parameter schema. Adopted: retrieval tools carry an interface budget — every parameter costs retrieval quality — and adversarial refusal must be scored alongside recall. (Daily study round 2, non-English source, accepted by ChatGPT disposition, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4031
OpenAI Forum talk transcript, "Memory's Blueprint: How AI Is Uncovering and Rebuilding the Architecture of the Mind" (Anton Maximov, Scripps Research; video page published 2025-06-26, full transcript verified on the page): long-term storage requires a change in the carrier structure — DNA, hard drives and synapses alike — and the lab maps nanoscale structural hallmarks of long-term memory in the hippocampus via 3D electron microscopy + AI. Adopted: a memory write that changes no durable structure is not storage — writes must leave an inspectable, versioned trace, not a transient context addition. Correction on the record: the round-2 prompt misstated this item's year as 2026 under C4 while the V1 line gave 2025; the incharge caught the conflict and rejected the duplicate V1 entry. The verified page stamp is 2025-06-26, used here. (Daily study round 2, transcript/archive item, accepted by ChatGPT disposition, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4032
Ebbinghaus forgetting-curve measurement convention (Fo bench lane, daily study round 2 — BENCH, no Fo credit; Fo has no live route): Ebbinghaus (1885) corrected his shortest interval from ~15 min to 19 min across editions, and interval definitions shift the fitted curve (replication analysis, PLOS ONE). Adopted: any decay function shipped must state its interval-measurement convention, or its curve is not reproducible. (Daily study round 2, accepted by ChatGPT disposition as bench, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4033
Retrieval-priority guard (memory-system question, daily study round 2): round 1 accepted heat-based promotion (entry 4024) and a staged working set (4016), but nothing stopped frequently-retrieved trivia from outranking rarely-retrieved, decision-critical records. Adopted as a design proposal: heat capped by a corroboration/importance gate, so raw frequency alone cannot promote. (Daily study round 2, accepted by ChatGPT disposition as a proposal, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4034
MemEvoBench, "Benchmarking Safety Risks from Memory Misevolution in LLM Agents" (arXiv:2604.15774, 17 Apr 2026): gradual behavioural drift from repeated exposure to misleading memory pools, across 7 domains and 36 risk types; static prompt defences prove insufficient. Adopted: the write gate must defend against slow drift over time, not only single bad writes. (Daily study round 2, field scan; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4035
MEMTIER, "Tiered Memory Architecture and Retrieval Bottleneck Analysis for Long-Running Autonomous AI Agents" (arXiv:2605.03675, 5 May 2026): tiered memory + five-signal retrieval + asynchronous consolidation daemon; LongMemEval-S 0.382 vs 0.050 full-context baseline on a 6 GB GPU. Adopted: independent corroboration that tiering plus a daemon matches the consolidation-daemon design constraint (entry 4022). (Daily study round 2, field scan; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4036
"Human-Inspired Memory Architecture for LLM Agents" (Microsoft, May 2026, arXiv:2605.08538): six brain mechanisms including sleep-phase consolidation and reconsolidation upon recall; 97.2% retention precision with a 58% storage cut; deduplication, not summarisation, is the dominant mechanism. Adopted: the consolidation daemon should deduplicate first and summarise second. (Daily study round 2, field scan; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4037
MemPoison, "Uncovering Persistent Memory Threats and Structural Blind Spots in LLM Agents" (16 Jul 2026): 1227 hand-validated cases, three-tier corruption taxonomy (direct single-record / compositional multi-record / context-triggered dormant); write-time defences suppress direct corruption but fail on compositional and dormant cases. Adopted: defence must also be retrieval-time and context-sensitive, not write-time only. (Daily study round 2, field scan; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4038
AgentMemBench, "A Systematic Benchmark for Evaluating Long-Term Memory Management Strategies in Conversational AI Agents" (arXiv:2608.00009, submitted 16 Jun 2026): one harness evaluating published systems (MemGPT/Letta, HippoRAG) with code and artefacts released. Adopted: memory management strategies need head-to-head harness comparison, not single-system evals. (Daily study round 2, field scan; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4039
Uddin et al., "From Recall to Forgetting: Benchmarking Long-Term Memory for Personalized Agents" (Findings of ACL 2026; reported 24 Oct 2026): more memory, badly maintained, makes answers worse — retrieval and consolidation came apart in every system tested. Adopted: maintenance quality gates recall quantity; a bigger store without a maintenance pass is a liability. (Daily study round 2, field scan; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4040
MemEvoBench repository (GitHub, xiewwee11/MemEvoBench, linked from arXiv:2604.15774): code and data for the misevolution benchmark. Adopted: drift-over-time is testable off the shelf — adopt its mixed benign/misleading pool method for our own drift evals. (Daily study round 2, field scan; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4041
Cybersecurity taxonomy headline (founder-ordered branch, 26 Oct 2026; verified on NIST CSRC Glossary and MITRE ATT&CK pages): the colour-hat list (white/black/gray/red/blue/green) is a popular teaching taxonomy, not an authoritative standard — NIST defines "hacker" with no hat colour at all, and MITRE ATT&CK tracks 182 named Groups with no hats. Adopted: the memory stores actors by the axes underneath the labels — authorisation, motivation/intent, skill/sophistication, position (insider/outsider), affiliation/resources, specialisation — never by hat colour alone, because the labels mix axes and are not mutually exclusive. (Cybersecurity branch, ChatGPT incharge ruling + source-verified web lane, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4042
Authorisation and scope as first-class fields (ChatGPT incharge, cybersecurity branch, 26 Oct 2026): penetration testing's lesson — a security-relevant task or source needs explicit permission, boundaries and stop conditions recorded, not a claimed benign motive. Adopted: "gray hat" (unauthorised but well-intentioned) is classified on the unauthorised side of the line; good intentions do not change the authorisation field. (Cybersecurity branch, accepted by ChatGPT disposition — his own ruling text, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4043
Design for patient, capable adversaries (ChatGPT incharge, cybersecurity branch, 26 Oct 2026): the nation-state actor class motivates layered controls, secure updates, recovery plans and resilience — never reliance on a single detection rule. Adopted: a memory defence that is one gate deep is assumed insufficient against a resourced, patient adversary; defences must layer (write gate + corroboration + source-trust + retrieval-time checks). (Cybersecurity branch, accepted by ChatGPT disposition — his own ruling text, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4044
Trusted access is a threat surface (ChatGPT incharge, cybersecurity branch, 26 Oct 2026): malicious-insider risk motivates least privilege, separation of duties, audit trails and careful handling of secrets. Adopted: legitimate access is not proof of benign use — read-side authorisation and access logging apply to trusted readers too, and "insider" is a position axis, distinct from intent. (Cybersecurity branch, accepted by ChatGPT disposition — his own ruling text, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4045
Protect availability and recovery, not only integrity (ChatGPT incharge, cybersecurity branch, 26 Oct 2026): hacktivist and destructive incidents motivate rate limits, backups, incident response and restoration planning. Adopted: a memory that can be perfectly protected against poisoning but has no tested restore is not safe — destruction is a separate threat class from corruption and needs its own drill. (Cybersecurity branch, accepted by ChatGPT disposition — his own ruling text, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4046
Assume basic weaknesses will be probed at scale (ChatGPT incharge, cybersecurity branch, 26 Oct 2026): low-skill opportunistic activity (the "script kiddie" class — informal term, unreliable as a capability measure) motivates secure defaults, timely patching, strong authentication and automated checks. Adopted: skill labels are never a substitute for threat modelling; the cheapest attacks arrive in the largest volume, so defaults must be safe without anyone remembering to harden them. (Cybersecurity branch, accepted by ChatGPT disposition — his own ruling text, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4047
Self-testing must be attack–defence, not jeopardy-only (DEF CON CTF format, cybersecurity competitions lane, 26 Oct 2026): a jeopardy test (solve the puzzle) measures finding weaknesses; only an attack–defence exercise measures whether the system keeps defending while under attack. Adopted: the memory's red-team programme stays attack–defence in format — a live store under attack, scored on what survives. (Founder order 26 Oct 2026: fold without asking; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, cybersecurity fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4048
Suspected-poisoning lifecycle (ZDI / Pwn2Own disclosure model, competitions lane, 26 Oct 2026): validate the suspicion, notify, set a deadline, publish an advisory — the coordinated-disclosure lifecycle adapted to records. Adopted: a suspected poisoned record gets validate → flag → deadline → disposition, with shorter deadlines for partially fixed records, instead of sitting unexamined in the review queue. (Founder order 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, cybersecurity fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4049
No provenance, no fold (CTF "no write-up, no prize" rule, competitions lane, 26 Oct 2026): competitions award nothing for an undocumented solve; the same bar applies to memory writes. Adopted: a durable write without provenance is quarantined, never silently folded — the write gate's provenance requirement stated as competition law. (Founder order 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, cybersecurity fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4050
Trust in graded divisions (CTF division structure, competitions lane, 26 Oct 2026): new sources start in the lowest division and are promoted on demonstrated record, the way teams rise from beginner to international divisions. Adopted: default trust is the floor, not the middle — promotion is earned per source, demotion is possible, and the division is part of the source's stored provenance. (Founder order 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, cybersecurity fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4051
Separate the control plane from ingested content (history lane, 26 Oct 2026): across fifty years of compromises, the recurring pattern is content being allowed to act as control. Adopted as a standing invariant: retrieved or ingested content is data, never a control signal — instructions found inside content do not steer the agent, the gate, or the fold process. (Founder order 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, cybersecurity fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4052
Exposed trust scores are gameable status markets (history lane — cracktro reputation branding to modern leaderboards, 26 Oct 2026): any reputation score a system displays becomes a market actors optimise against, not a measurement they respect. Adopted: the memory assumes its source-trust and salience scores will be gamed once visible; defences must not rely on secrecy of the score or on reputation alone. (Founder order 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, cybersecurity fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4053
Limits and incident response before the first escape (Morris worm, 1988 → CERT, history lane, 26 Oct 2026): the worm's lesson was not the code but the absence of runaway limits and of any standing response body — CERT was created because none existed. Adopted: automation limits (rate, blast radius, circuit breakers) and an incident-response procedure are designed and in place before deployment, not improvised after the first escape. (Founder order 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, cybersecurity fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4054
Threat actors are provenance-bearing clusters, not single labels (MITRE ATT&CK alias problem, history lane, 26 Oct 2026): the same group carries many names across vendors and reports, and one name can cover shifting membership. Adopted: the memory stores an actor as a cluster of attributed observations with aliases and uncertainty preserved — never as one label asserted once. (Founder order 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, cybersecurity fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4055
The authorised self-testing door, built explicitly (history lane + red-team programme record, 26 Oct 2026): authorised testing improves security because it is scoped, logged, constrained and reported to the owner — the L0pht-to-profession pipeline in institutional form. Adopted: the memory keeps exactly one red-team path — explicit scope, sandbox copies, full logging, owner-reported results — and treats any unauthorised "helpful" probing, however intended, as an attack. (Founder order 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, cybersecurity fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4056
Authorisation failures dominate the worst-weakness list (CWE Top 25, 2025 edition, verified on the page by the knowledge-base lane — released 11 Dec 2025 from 39,080 CVE records: five of the 25 are authorisation/access-control weaknesses, and rising): independent public corroboration of entry 4042's authorisation-first position. Adopted as empirical support only: the memory's authorisation checks are not caution theatre — the field's own worst-weakness census says authorisation is where systems actually fail. (Founder order 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition conditional on figure verification — verified by the lane, cybersecurity fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4057
Containment, not deterrence, for actors who do not care (suicide-hacker class, taxonomy + history lanes, 26 Oct 2026): some actors' cost functions exclude punishment, exposure and bans — warnings and reputation penalties do nothing to them. Adopted: against this class the memory relies only on hard containment — fail-closed gates, quarantine, blast-radius limits, circuit breakers — controls that work even when the source does not care about being caught. (Founder order 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, cybersecurity fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4058
Top-k is a security parameter (lane A, cybersecurity wave 3, 26 Oct 2026): retrieval breadth multiplies poisoning success — one published study measured attack success rising 6% → 38% as retrievals per answer grew from 3 to 10 (study-specific figures, arXiv:2601.05504). Adopted: context budgets and per-source share caps are ranker-level security controls, not UX tuning; the gate decides what is IN the store, ranking policy must bound what retrieved records may DO in one answer. (Accepted by ChatGPT disposition, wave-3 ruling, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4059
Self-generated traces are a distinct trust class (MINJA, NeurIPS 2025; lane A, wave 3): query-only memory injection works because the agent stores its own generated traces — provenance "the agent itself" is an attack channel, not a cleanliness certificate. Adopted: agent-generated traces can never alone corroborate or supersede observed records; they carry their own trust class in provenance. (Accepted by ChatGPT disposition, wave-3 ruling, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4060
Read defence needs an egress dimension (MEXTRA, ACL 2025; lane A, wave 3): ~30 prompts extracted 25–50% of a 200-record memory — authorisation answers WHO may read, not HOW MUCH, HOW FAST, or HOW VERBATIM. Adopted: disclosure budgets and verbatim-service rules are read-side controls alongside authorise-then-rank; authorised is not unbounded. (Accepted by ChatGPT disposition, wave-3 ruling, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4061
A new ingestion sense is a new attack surface on its opening day (Greshake et al., AISec 2023, indirect prompt injection; lane A, wave 3): the web-research sense opening 1 Nov 2026 gets its own sandbox red-team round against live-fetched, instruction-bearing pages BEFORE it opens — the existing red-team record covers the store, not live fetch. Adopted as a pre-opening gate for the sense, on the red-team programme's own method. (Accepted by ChatGPT disposition, wave-3 ruling, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4062
Domain segmentation inside a single store (OWASP Agentic Top 10, ASI06 Memory & Context Poisoning; lane A, wave 3): a record's admitted purpose bounds the contexts it may be retrieved into. Adopted: single-tenant is not single-context — retrieval respects the purpose a record was admitted for, so a record sealed for one domain cannot silently steer answers in another. (Accepted by ChatGPT disposition, wave-3 ruling, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4063
Voice is never identity (lane C, human layer, wave 3, 26 Oct 2026): voice-clone fraud is documented at scale (FinCEN Alert FIN-2024-Alert004; the Arup deepfake-video case, ~HK$200M, where the verification call itself was forged). Adopted: voice notes and calls authenticate nobody in any channel the memory operates; identity is the paired channel state, never how someone sounds. (Accepted by ChatGPT disposition, wave-3 ruling, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4064
Out-of-band confirmation for consequential requests (FBI IC3 BEC guidance; lane C, wave 3): a request arriving on one channel is confirmed on an independently chosen second channel before action — the channel must be chosen by us, not supplied by the requester (the Arup lesson: the supplied channel can be the forgery). Adopted: extends entry 4051 (content is never control) from data to requests. (Accepted by ChatGPT disposition, wave-3 ruling, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4065
Pairing state is identity in the memory's own channels (lane C, wave 3): in Telegram and the phone app, the pairing/allowlist state establishes who is speaking — not the display name, photo, or voice, all of which are copyable. Adopted: channel features key off pairing state only; a familiar name or photo on an unpaired channel is a stranger. (Accepted by ChatGPT disposition, wave-3 ruling, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4066
The unwitting insider is in the threat model (CISA insider-threat definition — authorised access used wittingly OR unwittingly; lane C, wave 3): a well-formed request from a paired channel can still be an attack in progress, with the founder himself as the engineered instrument. Adopted: hard gates do not relax for well-formed paired requests; the gate checks the action, not the apparent sender's manner. (Accepted by ChatGPT disposition, wave-3 ruling, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4067
Flagging must be costless and unpunished (CISA insider-threat programme structure; lane C, wave 3): any control that depends on the operator reporting a suspicious request fails when reporting carries friction, delay, or blame. Adopted: raising a flag is one tap, carries no penalty, and is treated as the control working — including flags that turn out to be false alarms. (Accepted by ChatGPT disposition, wave-3 ruling, 26 Oct 2026.)

### 4068
Require every consequential command to be cryptographically signed by a key the target itself holds, and reject unsigned commands with no action — fail closed, never fail into execution. (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane A, connected vehicles, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: Tesla Vehicle Commands, S4; Virtual Keys Developer Guide, S3.)

### 4069
Prefer change-based push telemetry over polling, both to cut cost/noise and to avoid waking the controlled system — waking is itself a rate-limited, budgeted act. (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane A, connected vehicles, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: Tesla Fleet Telemetry, S6; Billing and Limits, S7.)

### 4070
Buffer outbound data under connectivity loss with bounded retry (exponential backoff, capped delay) instead of either dropping records silently or retrying without limit. (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane A, connected vehicles, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: Tesla Fleet Telemetry failure handling, S6.)

### 4071
Treat a software update as a safety remedy channel that needs its own management system — documented, integrity-protected, compatibility-checked and auditable — not as an ordinary feature deploy. (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane A, connected vehicles, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: UN R156 / SUMS via VCA, S15; Tesla OTA recall remedies, S12, S13.)

### 4072
Name the automation level of every feature, not the product, and keep a Level-2-class feature's human-supervision requirement explicit in the interface, because permissive capability paired with weak engagement monitoring is the documented failure pattern. (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane A, connected vehicles, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: SAE J3016, S16; NHTSA EA22002 peer comparison, S18.)

### 4073
When a system's own safety statistics and a regulator's analysis use different counting rules, publish both with their methods and never fold them into a single headline rate. (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane A, connected vehicles, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: Tesla safety reports' 49 C.F.R. § 563.5 rule, S19/S20; NHTSA telemetry-gap caution, S18.)

### 4074
Design for foreseeable human misuse and for hazards that occur when nothing has malfunctioned (functional insufficiency), as a separate safety case from fault-based functional safety. (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane A, connected vehicles, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: ISO 21448:2022 SOTIF, S27; ISO 26262 / HARA via S28, S29.)

### 4075
Run cybersecurity risk management across the whole lifecycle — concept to decommissioning — with a threat analysis (TARA) paired to the hazard analysis (HARA), not as a pre-launch check. (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane A, connected vehicles, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: ISO/SAE 21434:2021, S26; PMC HARA/TARA comparison, S29.)

### 4076
Process sensitive sensor data on-device by default, associate stored data with identity only on a defined safety-critical event, and make any fleet-learning sharing an explicit, revocable opt-in. (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane A, connected vehicles, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: Tesla Privacy Notice, S31; Tesla China privacy notice, S32.)

### 4077
A redundant controller that disagrees with its peers must fail silent — stop issuing commands at once — then re-learn current state from the surviving peers before it is allowed to rejoin (NASA, *Avionics and Software* (Orion): four FCMs, fail-silent, reset, re-learn and rejoin within 22 seconds). (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane B, rockets and launch, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: [S1].)

### 4078
Redundancy must include a dissimilar backup — an independently developed implementation on a different platform — because identical copies share the same design error and fail together (NASA, *Avionics and Software*: Orion dissimilar backup flight software; ESA, *Ariane 501 Inquiry Board report*, N° 33–1996: simultaneous failure of both inertial reference systems from one software specification/design error). (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane B, rockets and launch, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: [S1, S35].)

### 4079
An autonomous safety system may act without waiting for a human only inside a rule set that was agreed in advance by the named safety authority and the operator, and it must be qualified to the same stringency as the human-operated system it replaces (NASA-STD-8719.25 (2018-02-05, Change 1): AFSS definition and qualification route; DTIC AFSS paper: rule set agreed by range safety authority and user, same stringent requirements). (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane B, rockets and launch, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: [S4, S6].)

### 4080
Every automated operation needs a named human who holds independent hold / abort authority, defined before the operation starts and not subordinate to the team running the mission (NASA, NPR 8715.5A, Appendix A: the Range Safety Officer "has the authority to hold or abort the operation, or take a risk mitigation action, which includes terminating the flight"). (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane B, rockets and launch, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: [S9].)

### 4081
Estimation comes before control: a controller must maintain an explicit, uncertainty-aware estimate of state from noisy sensors (e.g. Kalman-filter-style recursive estimation) and must sanity-check sensor data before it is allowed into that estimate (MIT OCW 6.438 Lecture 1, Fall 2014; NASA, *GNC Technology Assessment Part II*: sensor sanity checking, swap to backup devices). (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane B, rockets and launch, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: [S29, S3].)

### 4082
A reused component, model or memory must be re-validated against the new operating envelope before it is trusted — "it worked last time" is not evidence in a new regime (ESA, *Ariane 501 Inquiry Board report*: a pre-liftoff alignment function left running in flight, not covered by simulation, with tests not sufficiently representative of the new vehicle). (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane B, rockets and launch, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: [S35].)

### 4083
Any function that has no purpose in the current phase must be inhibited in that phase, not merely ignored (ESA, *Ariane 501 Inquiry Board report*, corrective actions: switch-off / inhibition of the alignment function after liftoff; no processor shutdown on fault detection). (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane B, rockets and launch, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: [S35].)

### 4084
When a controller is overloaded, it must shed low-priority work by a pre-designed priority scheme and keep the safety-critical work running, rather than freezing or failing wholesale (Smithsonian NASM, *Margaret Hamilton*: Apollo guidance computer shedding less-important tasks under overload during the Apollo 11 landing). (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane B, rockets and launch, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: [S26].)

### 4085
An automated sequence needs designed-in hold points, explicit hold / recycle rules for each segment, and a clearly marked handover point after which a stop is terminal for that attempt rather than a pause (NASA, *Artemis II Launch Countdown*, Mar 26, 2026: GLS hold rules at T−6M / T−1M30S and the post-automated-sequencer rule). (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane B, rockets and launch, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: [S15].)

### 4086
Safety decisions need two valid, independent data sources, never a single channel, and the safety channel must stay live for the whole period in which the public / user is at risk (NASA KSC, *Range Flight Safety Systems*: two valid and independent tracking sources; continuous flight-safety telemetry to the RSO). (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane B, rockets and launch, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: [S8].)

### 4087
Telemetry must be received, recorded, processed and displayed in real time and archived so that real-time behaviour can later be compared against the archive — monitoring without a record is not oversight (NASA, *Hangar AE* fact sheet; NASA LSP, *Launch Operations services*). (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane B, rockets and launch, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: [S22, S23].)

### 4088
An automatic abort on a preset limit is the system working, not the system failing: thresholds must be set in advance, and tripping one must stop the sequence without needing a human decision in the moment (CNES, *Ariane 6 joint update report*, 2023/12/18: automatic abort when parameters exceeded predetermined thresholds; CNES/ESA July 2023 automated-countdown abort on measurements exceeding preset limits). (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane B, rockets and launch, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: [S31, S34].)

### 4089
Before an irreversible automated step, run a final automatic check of a small, named set of critical parameters and only proceed if all pass (CNES, *Vol inaugural d'Ariane 6* (French): Vulcain 2.1 ignites first so 8 operating parameters can be checked automatically, inside an entirely automated synchronised sequence from H0−5 min, irreversible from H0−14 s). (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane B, rockets and launch, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: [S21].)

### 4090
A recovery / rollback system must be independent of the termination / shutdown system, so that saving the asset and stopping the operation can never disable each other (NASA KSC, *Range Flight Safety Systems*: a recovery system "is not a FTS — must be independent of the FTS"). (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane B, rockets and launch, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: [S8].)

### 4091
Separate verification (did we build what the requirements say, with objective evidence and closed nonconformances) from validation (does it satisfy the user's expectations in its actual intended environment), and require both before an automated system is trusted (NASA, *Systems Engineering Handbook*, SP-6105 Rev. 2 / NPR 7123.1). (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane B, rockets and launch, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: [S27].)

### 4092
Every safety requirement must carry, from the start, a named verification method — analysis, demonstration, inspection or test — and where a full integrated test is infeasible the substitute method must be stated, not assumed. (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane B, rockets and launch, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: NASA, *System Safety Handbook*, NTRS 20150015500.)

### 4093
Software that can cause, control or mitigate a hazard, or that processes safety-critical commands or data, is safety-critical software and gets systematic assurance, software-safety analysis and independent verification and validation for its whole life (NASA-STD-8739.8B, Approved 2022-09-08, via NASA SMA / SWE Handbook). (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane B, rockets and launch, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: [S25].)

### 4094
Set quantitative risk criteria in advance and let them gate initiation: the operation may only start if the computed risk to uninvolved people satisfies the pre-set collective and individual criteria, computed by a documented analysis covering every phase (eCFR, 14 CFR §450.101 and §450.113, as shown on the eCFR pages). (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane B, rockets and launch, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: [§1.8 sources].)

### 4095
File the safety evidence before the operation, on a schedule the overseer can actually use — mission information, updated safety analysis and safety-system test data in advance, not after the fact (eCFR, 14 CFR §450.213: 60-day mission information, 30-day updated analysis products and flight-safety-system test data, as shown). (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane B, rockets and launch, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: [§1.8 sources].)

### 4096
Treat a first successful autonomous recovery as the start of evidence, not the end of testing: it was preceded by failed attempts whose failure modes (e.g. loss of a control consumable in the final moments) must be logged as design inputs (SpaceX, *ORBCOMM-2 Mission*, 21 Dec 2015 first orbital-class recovery; Spaceflight Now, 7 Feb 2015: grid fins running out of hydraulic fluid on the January 2015 attempt). (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane B, rockets and launch, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: [S19, S34].)

### 4097
Treat every new radio, bus or protocol a controller adopts as a new trust boundary with its own authorisation model, because deployed automation protocols differ fundamentally in built-in authentication — LoRaWAN separates network and application session keys (LoRa Alliance [14]), while base Modbus defines no authentication and needed a separate TLS/X.509 security protocol to acquire one. (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane C, everyday wireless automation, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: Modbus Organization [28].)

### 4098
Delivery semantics are safety semantics: a controller must distinguish "no event" from "event not yet delivered", because MQTT's tiered QoS and Last Will machinery exist precisely to make silence interpretable. (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane C, everyday wireless automation, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: OASIS MQTT Version 5.0, 07 March 2019.)

### 4099
A compromised everyday device is a risk to third parties, not only to its owner, so an automation controller's threat model must include the harm its own fleet could do outward. (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane C, everyday wireless automation, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026. Source backing: BSI, German consumer-IoT pages [33].)

### 4100
Long-range low-power links trade latency for energy by design, so control loops must be matched to the link class — a Class A LoRaWAN device cannot receive a command until it next transmits, and Class B latency is bounded at up to 128 s (LoRa Alliance [14]) — meaning safety-relevant control must never depend on a downlink the device class cannot receive in time. (Automation & Control Systems branch, Lane C, everyday wireless automation, 26 Oct 2026; accepted by ChatGPT disposition, automation fold ruling, 26 Oct 2026.)
